### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 5:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/5:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/5:16:1)


ומלת "וחטאת" פועל עבר, והוי"ו השיבו לעתיד כמשפט כי היא כמו "וְחָטְאָה" וכאשר העלימו האל"ף כאשר הוא במלת חטא ולא יוכלו לשום נעלם אחר אל"ף על כן החליפו הה"א בתי"ו ואין צורך לשום דגש בטי"ת, וכמוהו "וקראת אתכם הרעה" (דבר' לא כט), והעם במקום הזה לשון נקבה כמו "העם אשר בקרבה יושבת לבטח" (שופ' יח ז) "מדוע שובבה העם הזה" (ירמי' ה ה), והטעם כי החטא יהיה עליך, וכנו דרך מוסר, כי החטא יהיה על שמו וכמוהו "והייתי אני ובני שלמה חטאים" (מ"א א כא), "ואויבינו ילעגו למו" (תה' פ' ז) וימירו את כבודם (שם קו כ):


BUT THE FAULT IS IN THINE OWN PEOPLE. The word *ve-chatat* (but the fault is)⁹⁴, meaning to sin. is a verb in the perfect.⁹⁵ (but the fault is in thine own people) is to be rendered, but thy people will sin. However, the *vav* changes it into an imperfect in accordance with the rules of grammar.⁹⁶ is a perfect, *ve-chatat* is an imperfect, for its *vav* is a conversive *vav*. The word is similar to *ve-chate’ah*.⁹⁷ in the perfect and *ve-chate’ah* in the imperfect. *Chatat* corresponds to *chate’ah* and *ve-chatat* to *ve-chate’ah*. Now when the *alef* was silenced, as it is in the word *chata*,⁹⁸ it was not possible to place a *heh* after the *alef*.⁹⁹. Two silent letters cannot be placed back to back. They therefore substituted a *tav* for the *heh*.¹⁰⁰ is the usual third person feminine suffix. However, if it were used here the *alef* could not be silent, as two silent letters cannot follow each other. Hence a *tav* was substituted for a *heh*. There is no need to place a *dagesh*¹⁰¹ follows a *pattach*. If *chatat* was vocalized with a *pattach* (rather than a *kamatz*) beneath the *chet*, then *chatat* would be a noun rather than a verb, in the *tet*.¹⁰² a noun. Cf. Rashi: “And this thing brings sin (*chatat* with a *dagesh* in the *tet*) upon your people.” The word *ve-karat* (will befall)¹⁰³. in *and evil will befall you* (Deut. 31:29) is similar.¹⁰⁴ in the feminine and *kara/ve-kara* in the masculine. The forms *karat / ve-karat* arose for the same reason that *chatat / ve-chatat* came into being. The word *am* (people) is here a feminine.¹⁰⁵ is usually masculine. However, here the verb governing it, *viz., ve-chatat*, is feminine. Hence it too must be feminine. Compare, *ha-am* (the people) in *the people that were therein, how they dwelt*¹⁰⁶ (dwelt), which governs *am*, is feminine. *in security* (Jud. 18:7) and *ha-am* (the people) in *Why is this people of Jerusalem slidden back*¹⁰⁷ (slidden back), which governs *am*, is feminine. (Jer. 8:5). Its meaning is,¹⁰⁸. See note 95. but the sin will be upon you. Moses out of respect alluded to Pharaoh by saying that the sin would be on his people.¹⁰⁹. However, he really meant the former. *That I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders* (I Kings 1:21),¹¹⁰ *And our enemies mock us as they please* (Ps. 80:7),¹¹¹ was substituted for “You” out of respect for the Deity. and *Thus they exchanged their glory* (Ps. 106:20)¹¹² was substituted out of respect for God. are similar.

**וישב משה.** הנה שאלה אחר שהשם הודיע למשה ואמר לו "ואני ידעתי כי לא יתן אתכם מלך מצרים להלוך" (למעלה ג יט) עד שיעשה כל האותות אשר צוהו, אם כן למה יתרעם משה לומר למה זה שלחתני, והצל לא הצלת, התשובה, חשב משה כי מעת דברו אל פרעה יקל מעליהם עולם, והנה הוא הכביד העבודה עליהם, וטעם למה הרעותה, הפך מה שאמרת "ראה ראיתי את עני" (למעלה ג ז) וארד להצילו מיד מצרים (שם שם ה) ולמה זה שלחתני להרע לישראל והנה לא מצאתי תשובה להשיב לשוטרים:

Now a question: Why did Moses complain and say, *Why is it that thou hast sent me?* and *Neither hast thou delivered Thy people at all* after God told him, *And I know that the king of Egypt will not give you leave to go* (Ex. 3:19) until he performed all the signs that God commanded him? The answer is, Moses thought that Pharaoh would lighten Israel’s yoke as soon as he spoke to him. However, Pharaoh placed a heavier workload upon them.¹³⁸ [WHEREFORE HAST THOU DEALT ILL WITH THIS PEOPLE?] Contrary to Your words, *I have surely seen the affliction of My people* (Ex. 3:7); *And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians* (*Ibid.*). [WHY IS IT THAT THOU HAST SENT ME] To harm Israel. Behold,¹³⁹ I have not found an answer to give the officers.¹⁴⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 6:2:1

**וידבר.** הכתוב אמר "ויאמן העם" (למעלה ד לא) ולא כל העם, והכל מודים באלהים אפילו פרעה כאשר אפרש עוד על כן אמר "ויאמר אליו אני ד'" לכן אמור לבני ישראל אני ד' (פ' ו) "וידעתם כי אני ה' אלהיכם המוציא אתכם" (פ' ז):


AND GOD SPOKE. Scripture reads, *And the people believed* (Ex. 4:31). The latter implies that not all of the people believed. Everyone including Pharaoh, as I will yet explain,² admitted to the existence of God.³ Scripture therefore says, *And God spoke unto Moses, and said unto him: I am the Lord* (v. 2); *Wherefore say unto the children of Israel: I am the Lord* (v. 6); *and ye shall know that I am the Lord your God* (v. 7).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 6:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:2)


מלת "שדי" קשה בפירוש, והגאון אמר כי השי"ן נוסף כשי"ן "שאתה מדבר עמי" (שופ' ו יז) והטעם שאמר לעולם די, ולא אדע טעם לפי' זה, כי איך יקרא שם אשר די רק להיותו תואר כמו "טוב וסלח" (תה' פו ה) "עלי לבי דַוָי" (ירמי' ה יה) והנגיד רב שמואל פי' בו בלשון ערבי אלקהאר, ופי' מנצח ותקיף והיו"ד תחת אות הכפל כיו"ד "דַלְיוֹ שֹּׁקַיִם מִפִסֵח" (משלי כו ז) ואל"ף "אשר בזאו נהרים" (ישעי' יח ב) וכמוהו "כקול שדי" (יחז' א כד), "והיה שדי בצריך" איוב כב כה) ויפה פירש:


[ALMIGHTY.] It is difficult to explain the word *Shaddai* (Almighty).⁵ Saadiah Gaon says that the *shin* of *Shaddai* is a preposition, like the *shin* prefixed to *she-attah* (that it is thou) in *that it is thou that talkest with me* (Jud. 6:17). The meaning of *Shaddai* is: Who said to the world, enough.⁶ is composed of two words, *she-dai* (who is enough). He further explained that *she-dai* is short for *she-amar le’olam dai*. Saadiah Gaon apparently interprets *Shaddai* as meaning the one who controls or sets a limit on nature. See *Hagigah* 12a, “What is the meaning of *ani El Shaddai* (Gen. 17:1)? Its meaning is: I am (*ani*) the God (*El*) who said to my world *dai* (enough). Resh Lakish said: When the Holy One created the sea, it went spreading on until the Holy One rebuked it and made it dry (i.e., said to it, enough).” However, I cannot see any meaning in this interpretation. How can God be called by the name “Who is enough?”⁷) (Krinsky). *Shaddai* therefore can only be taken as an adjective, like the words *tov* (good) and *sallach* (ready to pardon) in *good, and ready to pardon* (Ps. 86:5) and *davvai* (faint)⁸ in *Shaddai* is not a prefix but an integral part of the word, like the *dalet* in *davvai* and the *samekh* in *sallach*. in *My heart is faint within me* (Jer. 8:18). Now Rabbi Samuel the Nagid explains *Shaddai* with the Arabic word *al kahar*, which means victorious and mighty. He further notes that the *yod* in *Shaddai* is in place of the double letter,⁹ is *shin, dalet, dalet*. (Cf. I.E. on Gen. 17:1 and the notes thereto.) *Shaddai* is spelled *shin, dalet, yod*. Thus one *dalet* is missing. Rabbi Samuel says that the *yod* takes the place of the *dalet*. like the *yod* in *dalyu* (hang limp)¹⁰. A *lamed* is missing in *dalyu* and is made up by the *yod*. in *The legs hang limp from the lame* (Prov. 26:7) and the *alef* in *baze’u* (divide)¹¹ is *bet, zayin, zayin*. A *zayin* is missing in *baze’u* and is made up by the *alef*. in *Whose land the rivers divide* (Is. 18:2). *Shaddai* (mighty) in *like a mighty voice* (Ezek. 1:24)¹² and *Shaddai* (mighty) in *And mighty shall he thy silver* (Job 22:25)¹³ are similar. The Nagid explained it well.¹⁴ means mighty or the Almighty.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 6:3:3

ומלת נודעתי מבנין נפעל, ואיננו כמו הודעתי כדברי מנחם:


[I MADE ME NOT KNOWN TO THEM.] The word *nodati* (I made Me known) is in the *nifal*.¹⁵ It is not like *hodati* (I made known)¹⁶. According to Menachem ben Saruk, a tenth-century Sephardic philologist, the meaning of our clause is: but My name *YHVH* I made not known to them. See note 18. as Menachem maintains.¹⁷. However, there are many verses that show that the patriarchs were aware of this divine name. Cf. Gen. 15:2; 22:14.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 6:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:4)


ורבי מרינוס אמר, כי ושמי ד' שבועה כי בלשון ערבי יש וי"ו לשבועה, וטעם לא נודעתי להם כמו שנודעתי לך וכוי"ו הזה לא מצאנו בלה"ק וככה דקדוקו, יש מלות מושכות עצמן ואחרות עמם, גם כן אותיות כמ"ם "מאל אביך ויעזרך, ואת שדי" (ברא' מט כה) שהוא מאת שדי וככה בי"ת באל שדי, כאילו כתוב ובשמי ד' לא נודעתי להם:


[BUT BY MY NAME YHVH.] Rabbi Merinus says that *u-shemi YHVH* (But by my name YHVH)¹⁸ I made Me not known to them. The latter is grammatically incorrect, as it lacks the preposition “by” before “My name,” and it presents a problem for it implies that the patriarchs were not aware of the name *YHVH*. However, it is clear from the book of Genesis that Abraham and Jacob were acquainted with this name. The commentaries which follow try each in his own way to solve this problem. is an oath, as in Arabic there is a *vav* which indicates an oath.¹⁹ can be interpreted as an oath, its meaning being: I swear by My name *YHVH*. Rabbi Merinus explains the meaning of *I made Me not known to them* as: I made Me not known to them as I made Me known to you.²⁰. The meaning of the entire verse is: I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty, and I swear by My name *YHVH* that I made Me not known to them as I made Me known to you. However, we never find a *vav* with this meaning in Scripture.²¹ indicating an oath. Thus we can’t interpret *u-shemi YHVH* as: I swear by My name *YHVH*. This then is its grammatical explanation.²². There are words that are to be read as if written twice.²³ The same applies to letters.²⁴ For example, the *mem* prefaced to *me’el* (From the God) in *From the God of thy father, who shall help thee, and the* (ve-et) *Almighty, who shall bless thee* (Gen. 49: 25)²⁵ is also to be placed before *ve-et* (and the) and be read as if written *u-me’et* (and from the).²⁶ Similarly the *bet* of *be’el Shaddai* (as God Almighty).²⁷. Our phrase is thus to be read as if written: *but by My name YHVH* (u-vi-shemi) *I made Me not known to them*.²⁸ I made Me not known to them. I.E. will later elaborate on his explanation. See note 40.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 6:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:5)


אמר רב סעדיה הגאון כי תחסר באחרונה מלת לבדו, כאילו אמר ובשמי ד' לבדו לא נודעתי להם, רק פעם באל שדי ופעם בשם ד' וכמוהו לפי דעתי לא יעקב לבדו יאמר עוד שמך כי אם ישראל משתתף עמו, ואין צורך לתקון הזה, כי ידענו כי אל שדי הוא הש"י הנכבד, ואין ביניהם הפרש, רק ששם שדי הוא תואר והשם הנכבד פעם שם עצם ופעם שם תואר כאשר פירשתי והנה מצאנו כתוב באברהם "אני ד' אשר הוצאתיך מאור כשדים" (ברא' טו ז), וביעקב אני ד' אלהי אברהם אביך (שם כח יג), ור' ישועה אמר כי אברהם ויעקב לא ידעו זה השם, רק משה כתב ככה, ולא דבר ר' ישועה נכונה, כי איך יכתוב משה שם לא הזכירו השם, ואין ספק כי האבות ידעו זה השם שהוא שם העצם רק זה השם הוא התואר לא ידעו:


Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the word *le-vado* (only) has been omitted from the end of our clause. Our text should be read as if written: but I made Me not known to them only by My name *YHVH*.²⁹ should be interpreted as if written, *u-vi-shemi YHVH le-vado*. On the contrary, I at times appeared to them with the name *El Shaddai* (God Almighty) and at other times with the name *YHVH*. In my opinion, thy name shall not be called any more only Jacob, but Israel shall be used with it (Gen. 35:10)³⁰. is similar.³¹, although missing, is implied in the text. Really, there is no need for Saadiah Gaon’s reconstruction³². because we know that *El Shaddai* and the blessed and glorious Lord are one and the same,³³ and *El Shaddai*. So what sign of divine favor is there in God telling Moses that He appears to him only as *YHVH* while He appeared to the patriarchs sometimes as *El Shaddai* and sometimes as *YHVH?* As to the question raised by our verse, I.E. answers it at the end of his comment. except that the term *El Shaddai* is an adjective and the glorious and revered name³⁴. is, as I have explained,³⁵ sometimes a noun and sometimes an adjective. Now we find it written with regard to Abraham, *I am the Lord* (YHVH) *that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it* (Gen. 15:7). We similarly find with regard to Jacob, *I am the Lord* (YHVH), *the God of Abraham thy father* (Gen. 28:13).³⁶. Rabbi Joshua says that Abraham and Jacob did not know the name *YHVH*.³⁷ literally. Moses used it when writing the Torah.³⁸ However, Rabbi Joshua is incorrect, for how would Moses dare to write a name that God did not utter.³⁹ who brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees,” would Moses deliberately dare to write, “I am *YHVH* that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees” (Gen. 15:7). There is no doubt that the patriarchs knew the name *YHVH* as a proper name. However, they did not know it as an adjective.⁴⁰ means, they did not know the adjectival meaning of *YHVH*; that is, they did not experience the adjectival meaning of My name *YHVH, viz.*, My suspending the laws of nature (Krinsky).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 6:3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/6:3:6)


ועתה אגלה לך קצת סוד אל שדי, ידענו כי השם ברא ג' עולמות שהזכרתי והעולם השפל יקבל כח מעולם התיכון כל אחד מהפרטים כפי מערכת העליונה, ובעבור כי נשמת האדם גבוה מן העולם האמצעי, אם היתה הנפש חכמה והכירה מעשה השם שהם בלא אמצעי וע"י אמצעי והניחה תאות העולם השפל, והתבודדה לדבקה בשם הנכבד, אם יש במערכת הככבים בעת ההריון רעה שתבא עליו ביום ידוע, השם שדבק בו יסבב סבות להצילו מרעתו, וככה אם יש במערכה שיהיה עָקר, השם יתקן לו כח תולדתו ויוליד, על כן אמרו חז"ל שהשם אמר לאברהם צא מאצטגנינות שלך וקרוב מזה הטעם אין מזל לישראל, ועוד אבאר זה בפ' כי תשא על כן אמר השם לאברהם קודם וארבה את זרעך "אני אל שדי" (ברא' יז א) שפירושו מנצח המערכות העליונות, לא שהמערכה תשחת רק שידע הדבק בשמו שיחדש לו טוב שלא יהיה במערכתו על כן אמר יעקב "המלאך הגואל אותי מכל רע" (שם מח) שהיה נכון לבא עלי, וזה הוא סוד כל התורה כאשר אפרש עוד, והנה האבות לא הגיעה מעלתם לדבקה בשם כמשה אשר ידעו השם פנים בפנים, על כן היה יכול משה לשנות תולדות עולם השפל, ולחדש אותות ומופתים שלא יכלו האבות לחדשם, והנה משה אמר שני דברים האחד "למה זה שלחתני" (למעלה ה כב) והשני "והצל לא הצלת את עמך" (שם שם כג), והשיב על האחרון "עתה תראה אשר אעשה לפרעה" (למעלה ו א), ועל הראשון ויאמר אליו אני ד' (למעלה ו ב) והטעם כי על ידי האבות נודע שמי שהוא אל שדי ועל ידך יודע שמי ד' הנכבד בעולם כאשר אמר לכן אמור לבני ישראל אני ד', והנה שלחתיך להודיע זה השם:


I will now reveal to you part of the secret meaning of the name *El Shaddai*. We know that God created the three worlds that I have previously noted.⁴¹ Everything in the lowest world receives power from the middle world according to the arrangements⁴² in the higher world. Due to the fact that man’s soul comes from above the middle world, if it is wise and recognizes the works of God, both those done without an intermediary⁴³ and those done via an intermediary⁴⁴ and if the soul forsakes the pleasures of this lowest world and separates itself from them to cleave to God the glorious, should there be at the time of the birth of such a person an arrangement of the stars indicating that evil will befall this man on a certain day, the God to whom this man cleaves will set the chain of events in such a way that this man is saved from the evil that was destined to befall him. Similarly, if it is in the arrangement of the stars that this man be sterile God will make him virile and he will sire children. Therefore our sages said that God told Abraham, “Leave your astrological calculations.”⁴⁵ 156a, “Abraham said before the Holy One Blessed Be He…I have searched my constellation and have found that I am incapable of having a son. Leave your astrological calculations, said the Lord to him, for Israel has no star.” Also see *Nedarim* 32a and Rashi on Gen. 15:5. The statement “Israel has no star” is close in meaning to the latter.⁴⁶ I will yet explain this in the Torah portion *Ki Tissa*.⁴⁷ Therefore, before God said to Abraham, *and I will multiply thy seed*, he told him, *I am God Almighty* (El Shaddai) (Gen. 17:1), the meaning of which is: I overcome the upper arrangements. The aforementioned does not mean that the arrangements are destroyed. It rather means that the one who cleaves to God knows that God creates good things for him that are not in keeping with what the stars have determined for him.⁴⁸ Jacob therefore said, *the angel who hath redeemed me from all evil* (Gen. 48:16), i.e., all evil that was destined⁴⁹ to come upon me. This is, as I will explain, the secret of the whole Torah.⁵⁰ Now the patriarchs did not reach the level where they were able to cleave unto God as Moses, *whom the Lord knew face to face*,⁵¹ did. Moses was therefore able to change the laws governing the lower world⁵² and produce signs and wonders⁵³ that the patriarchs were incapable of. Now Moses said two things to the Lord. One, *why is it that Thou hast sent me* (Ex. 5:22)? Two, *neither hast Thou delivered Thy people* (Ex. 5:23). God answered the latter with, *Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh* (v. 1). He answered the former⁵⁴ with, *I am the Lord* (v. 2).⁵⁵ known in the world. The meaning⁵⁶ is that via the patriarchs My name *El Shaddai*⁵⁷ was publicized, but through you My revered name *YHVH*⁵⁸ will be known in the world. As God said, *Wherefore say unto the children of Israel: I am the Lord* (YHVH) (v. 6), the meaning of which is, behold, I have sent you to make this name known.

AND ELEAZAR. Eleazar’s wife is mentioned out of respect for Phinehas, as the priesthood was given to him eternally. Hence, logically speaking, Putiel was an Israelite.⁹⁴ (fatten) and *pittpet* (conquered). The Midrash says that Eleazar’s wife was a descendant of Jethro, “who fattened calves for idols,” and Joseph, “who conquered his passions.” See *Sotah* 43a; *Baba Batra* 109b, *San*hedrin 82b and *Shemot Rabba* 67. I.E. disagrees, for he believes Putiel is mentioned to give respect to Phinehas, and it is no honor to have a pagan ancestor. We do not know the meaning of Putiel as we do not know the meaning of Mishael and Aaron and all the other names that are mentioned. If what happened to Moses had not been recorded,⁹⁵ we would not know why he was so called.⁹⁶

**הם.** עתה מעת שדברו אל פרעה הקדים משה בעבור גודל מעלתו, והשם דבר עמו פנים אל פנים, ונגש אל הערפל אשר שם השם, ולא כן אהרן, והכתוב מעיד לא כן עבדי משה (במד' יב ז) ואהרן אמר לו פעמים בי אדוני על כן לא תמצא בכל התורה מתחלת זה הפסוק שלא יקדים משה לאהרן, וככה בנביאים, וככה בכתובים ואין טענה ממלת ואלה תולדות אהרן ומשה (במד' ג א) גם "ותלד לו את אהרן. ואת משה" (שם כו נט) כי כאשר נולדו הזכירם, והעד "תולדות" גם "ותלד":


THESE. Now from the time that they spoke to Pharaoh, Scripture mentions Moses before Aaron because of his great status. Indeed, God spoke to him face to face⁹⁸ and he alone drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.⁹⁹ This was not the case with Aaron. Scripture testifies with regard to Moses, *My servant Moses is not so* (Num. 12:7).¹⁰⁰ Furthermore, Aaron said, *oh my lord* twice.¹⁰¹, in Ex. 32:22 and in Num. 12:11. The phrase *oh my lord* is found only in the latter. You will therefore not find in the entire Pentateuch starting from this verse Moses not mentioned before Aaron. The same holds true for the Prophets and similarly for the Writings. There is no argument to the contrary from *Now these are the generations of Aaron and Moses* (Num. 3:1) or from, *and she bore unto Amram Aaron and Moses* (Num. 26:59), as Scripture lists them there in the order of their birth.¹⁰² The words *generations* and *and she bore* is proof of this.

והאומרים כי נביא מגזרת "ניב שפתים" (ישעי' נז יט) איננו נכון כי שרש ניב מהשניים, לפי דעת דעת חכמי צרפת ומעלומי העין לפי דעת חכמי ספרד ושרש נביא שלש אותיות, והעד נביאים (במד' יא כט), ויתנבאו (שם פ' כה) כי האל"ף שרש, ועוד כי ניב שפתים כמו פרי, כי הוא מגזרת תנובה (ישעי' כז ו) עוד ינובון בשיבה (תה' צב טו) והעד הנאמן, וניבו נבזה אכלו (מלאכי א יב) ועוד מה טעם השב אשת האיש כי נביא הוא (ברא' כ ז) אם פירושו דברן הוא רק פירושו הוא נביא שאגלה לו סודי כדרך כי אם גלה סודו אל עבדיו הנביאים (עמוס ג ז) והוא מתענג עלי, ע"כ ויתפלל בעדך וחיה (ברא' כ ז):


[AND AARON THY BROTHER SHALL BE THY PROPHET.] Those who say that the word *navi* (prophet) comes from the root of *niv* in *niv sefatayim* (the fruit of the lips) (Is. 57:19) err.⁷ (prophecy) refer to one who calls and preaches words of rebuke to the people. It comes from the root of *niv* in *niv sefatyim*.” *Niv* comes from a two-letter root according to the French sages and from a hidden *ayin* root according to the Spanish sages.⁸ comes from the root *nun, vav, bet*. The French sages refer to such a root as a two-letter root because the *vav* is usually dropped. For the same reason the Spanish sages refer to it as a hidden *ayin* root. However, Krinsky argues that the French sages disagree as to what the root of *niv* is. The former hold that *niv* comes from a two-letter root; i.e., its root is *nun, bet*, while the Spanish sages believe it to come from the root *nun, vav, bet*. Contemporary works on grammar refer to the latter as an *ayin vav*. However, *navi* comes from a three-letter root.⁹. That its *alef*¹⁰ is spelled *nun, bet, yod, alef*. is a root letter can be seen from the words *nevi’im* (prophets) (Num. 11:29) and *va-yitnabe’u* (they prophesied).¹¹. If the *alef* was not a root letter these words would not have an *alef* in them. Furthermore, the word *niv* in *niv sefatayim* means fruit,¹² for *niv* comes from the same root as *tenuvah* (fruitage) (Is. 27:6) and *yenuvun* (they shall bring forth fruit) in *They shall still bring forth fruit in old age* (Ps. 92:15). *Ve-nivo nivzeh okhlo* (and the fruit thereof, even the food thereof, is contemptible) (Malachi 1:12) is true proof of this. Additionally, what meaning is there to, *restore the man’s wife; for he is a prophet* (Gen. 20:7) if *navi* (prophet) means a speaker. Its only meaning¹³ (prophet) in Gen 20:7. is, he is a prophet to whom I reveal my secrets, as in *But He revealeth His counsel unto His servants the prophets* (Amos 3:7). He enjoys My presence therefore *and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live* (Gen. 20:7).

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:3:1)


**ואני אקשה.** יש לשאול אם ד' הקשה את לבו מה פשעו מה חטאתו, והתשובה, כי השם נתן חכמה לאדם ונטע בלבו שכל לקבל כח עליון, להוסיף על טובתו, או לחסר מרעתו וזה אפרש בפ' כי תשא ובפסוק מי יתן והיה לבבם זה (דבר' ה כו), והנה טעם אקשה את לבו למען רבות מופתי, ור' ישועה אמר, כי טעם אקשה את לבו לסבול את המכות ולא דבר נכונה:


AND I WILL HARDEN PHARAOH’S HEART. The question arises: “If God hardened Pharaoh’s heart what was his transgression and what was his sin?”¹⁵, our verse states that God will harden Pharaoh’s heart and punish him for not mending his ways; i.e., I will harden Pharaoh’s heart and punish him for hardening his heart by multiplying “My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.” The answer is: God granted wisdom to man and implanted in his heart the intelligence to receive power from on high to add to his good¹⁶ or to diminish his evil.¹⁷ I will explain this in the Torah portion *Ki Tissa*¹⁸ and when I comment on the verse *Oh that they had such a heart as this alway* (Deut. 5:26). Now the meaning of our verse is: I will harden his heart in order to multiply My signs and My wonders.¹⁹ Rabbi Joshua says that its meaning is: I will harden his heart so that he will be able to bear the plagues.²⁰ However, he spoke incorrectly.²¹ thus does not mean I will give Pharaoh a strong heart so that he can bear up under the pressure of the plagues, but rather that I will, so to speak, dull his brain so that he does not develop his intellectual capacity.

footnotes:
¹⁵ Prima facie
¹⁶ If good things are destined to befall an individual he can increase the amount of good that will befall him by developing his intelligence. Individual Divine Providence is extended only to those who have developed their intellectual capacities. See Introduction to Vol. 1, p. XIII.
¹⁷ A person can decrease the evil that is destined to befall him by developing his intelligence. See preceding note.
¹⁸ Ex. 31:18; 33:21.
¹⁹ God prevented Pharaoh from developing his intellectual capacities; God did this not to punish Pharaoh but so that He would have a pretext for multiplying His signs and wonders in the land of Egypt. I.E. apparently held that man has free will. However, God occasionally takes it away when it serves His purpose to do so. For other interpretations, see Weiser and Krinsky.
²⁰ Hence there is no problem as to why Pharaoh was punished for being obstinate; Pharaoh was a free agent. God; granted him the physical strength to bear His plagues. He did not take away Pharaoh’s free will.
²¹ Rabbi Joshua is wrong. Heart in Scripture refers to an individual’s mental rather than physical capacity. And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:5:1)


**וידעו.** כבר הזכיר ר' יהודה המדקדק הראשון ההפרש שיש בין וְיָדְעו ובין וְיֵדְעו, כי הקמץ בקמץ גדול הוא פועל עבר כמו שׁׂמְעו והוי"ו השיבו לעתיד כמשפט, והקמוץ בקמץ קטן, והיו"ד סימן לעתיד כמו וְיִשְׁמְרו, והנח הנעלם בין היו"ד והדלת תחת היו"ד שהוא שרש, והנה הזכיר למה הביא המכות על המצריים, כדי שיודע שמו הנכבד בעולם:


SHALL KNOW. Rabbi Judah, the first grammarian, has already noted the difference between *ve-yade’u* (shall know) and *ve-yede’u* (shall know). The word *ve-yade’u*, which is vocalized with a long *kamatz*, is a verb in the perfect. Compare, *shame’u* (they heard).²³ and *shame’u* are third person perfect forms. The *vav* prefixed to *yade’u* changes it²⁴ to an imperfect as per the grammatical rules.²⁵. On the other hand, the *yod* of the word *ve-yede’u*, which is vocalized with a *tzere*,²⁶ which literally means a small *kamatz*. is a future prefix. Compare, *ve-yishmeru* (they shall keep).²⁷ in *ve-yishmeru* (root, *shin, mem, resh*) is a future prefix. Similarly the *yod* of *ve-yede’u*. The silent *yod* between the *yod* and the *dalet* ²⁸ has the *yod* sound in it. is in place of the root *yod*. ²⁹ comes from the root *yod, dalet, ayin*. Since the *yod* in *ve-yede’u* is a prefix the root *yod* is dropped. However, it is compensated by the *tzere*, which has the *yod* sound. Thus the word is sounded *ve-yede’u*, not *ve-yide’u* as it ordinarily would be. Compare, *ve-yishmeru, ve-yishme’u*, and *ve-yikhtivu.* Behold, God noted³⁰ why He brought the plagues upon the Egyptians. He brought them so that His glorious name would be known in the world.³¹

footnotes:

²⁴ From a perfect.
²⁵ For it is a conversive vav
²⁶ In Hebrew a kamatz katan
²⁷ The yod
²⁸ The tzere
²⁹ Ve-yede’u
³⁰ In this verse.
³¹ Not as a punishment for Pharaoh’s obstinacy. See I.E.’s comments on verse 3 and the notes thereto.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:7:1

**ומשה.** הזכיר שנותיהם, ולא מצאנו בכל המקרא נביאים שהזכירם הכתוב שהתנבאו בזקנותם רק אלה, כי מעלתם גדולה מכל הנביאים, ולהם לבדם היה מדבר השם בעמוד ענן, ואל יעלה על לבך כי שמואל עמהם, בעבור שכתוב "בעמוד ענן ידבר אליהם" כי כבר פירשתי במקומו, כי לאלה לבדם נתנה התורה, והנה על ידם ינחלו הצדיקים העולם הבא, וכל הנביאים הם נביאי תוכחות או עתידות:


AND MOSES. The Pentateuch records the ages of Moses and Aaron. Aside from these two, we do not find in all of Scripture prophets concerning whom the Bible says that they prophesied in their old age.³³, Part II, chap. XXXVI, translated by M. Friedlander, 1904). Their status was greater than that of all the other prophets, and to them alone did God speak in a pillar of cloud.³⁴ Do not think that Samuel is to be included among them because it is written, *He spoke unto them*³⁵ refers to the latter three.*in the pillar of cloud* (Ps. 99:7), since I have already explained in its proper place that the Torah was given³⁶ only to these two.³⁷ Now, behold, through Moses and Aaron the righteous shall inherit the world to come, while all the other prophets are prophets who³⁸ rebuke or predict the future.

³⁴ Ps. 99:7
³⁵ The previous verse speaks of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel. Thus prima facie, unto them

³⁷ Moses and Aaron. Hence Ps. 99:7 does not apply to Samuel but only to Moses and Aaron. See I.E. on Gen. 20:17 and on Ps. 99:7.

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:9:1)


**קח את מטך.** הוא מטה משה שנתנו לו והעד אמור אל אהרן קח את מטך ונטה ידך (פ' יט), וכתוב "וירם בַמַטֶה ויך את המים" (פ' כ), והנה הודיענו בפתחות הבי"ת שהוא המטה הידוע שאמר לו קח את מטך, ועוד "ומטך אשר הכית בו את היאור" (למטה יז ה):


TAKE THY ROD. The reference is to Moses’ rod which Moses had given to Aaron.⁴⁰ *Say unto Aaron: Take thy rod, and stretch out thy hand* (v. 19); *and he lifted up the rod* (ba-matteh), *and smote the waters* (v. 20) is proof of this.⁴¹ (Aaron’s rod) in our verse refers to the rod which Moses gave to Aaron. Now by employing a *bet* that has a *pattach* beneath it⁴² (the rod). *Ba-matteh* is short for *be-ha-matteh.* This *heh ha-yedi’ah* (the definite article) indicates a well-known object, in this case a well-known rod. Only Moses’ rod fits this description. Scripture is informing us that when He told him,⁴³ *Take thy rod*, He was referring to the well-known rod. *And thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thy hand, and go* (Ex. 17:5)⁴⁴ is additional proof of the above.⁴⁵

⁴¹ That thy rod

⁴⁵ That the rod was really Moses’ rod, as Moses never struck the Nile. Aaron did. However, since it was used to strike the water, it was as if Moses himself struck the water.

**ויבא משה.** גם זה מופת, שהמטה היה לתנין, ואינו דומה למופת שעשה לישראל כי לא נהפך רק לנחש, ויפת אמר נחש הוא תנין:

AND THE SORCERERS. Those who appear to change natural law.⁵⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:11:3)


והחרטומים, הם היודעים סוד התולדות והמלה רביעית אולי לשון מצרים הוא, או לשון כשדים, כי לא מצאנוה בכל המקרא רק בדברי שניהם, והפריש הכתוב בין מעשה משה שהיה אמת שנהפך המטה לתנין, ובין מעשה החרטומים, על כן כתוב בלטיהם והמלה השלישית מגזרת להט החרב (ברא' ג כד) אשכבה לוהטים (תה' נז ה) "ולהט אותם היום הבא" (מלאכי ג יט), והוא כמו בריקות ואש עוברת, וזאת היא אחיזת עינים:


THE MAGICIANS. Those who know the secrets of nature. *Chartumim* (magicians)⁵¹ is a quadriliteral.⁵² It might be an Egyptian or Chaldean word, as we do not find this word used in Scripture except when dealing with them.⁵³ Scripture indicates a difference between what Moses did and what the magicians did. Moses really changed the staff into a serpent. As for the magicians, Scripture reads, *with their secret arts*.⁵⁴ *Be-lahatehem* (with their secret arts) comes from a triliteral root.⁵⁵ The *heh* should be dropped as it is the result of a scribal error. Indeed, *Vat. Ebr.* 38 reads, *ve-hamillah shelishit*. Its root is *lamed, heh, tet*. It is derived from the same root as *lahat* (flame) in *the flaming sword* (Gen. 3:24) and *lohatim* (them that are aflame) in *I do lie down among them that are aflame* (Ps. 57:5) and *lihat* (ablaze) in *And the day that cometh shall set them ablaze* (Mal. 3:19). It⁵⁶. refers to an illusion of lightning and passing fire.⁵⁷

⁵⁴ That is, via chicanery.

⁵⁶ Be-latehem
⁵⁷ The magicians made the rod appear to turn into a serpent in the same way that they have lightening and fire seem to appear.

### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:14:1)


**ויאמר. כבד.** פועל עבר כמו כי זָקֵן יצחק (ברא' כז א) לו חָפֵץ ד' (שופ' יג) כאשר אָהֵב (ברא' כז ט), והיה קמץ קטן תחת מ"ם מֵאֵן שהוא שרש, שלא ידגש האל"ף ההוא אחריו כמו חרף נפשו (שופ' ה יח):


AND THE LORD SAID…PHARAOH’S HEART IS STUBBORN. *Kaved* (is stubborn) is a verb in the perfect.⁶⁴ It is like the word *zaken* (was old) in *when Isaac was old* (Gen. 27:1), *chafetz* (were pleased) in *If the Lord were pleased* (Jud. 13:23), *ahev* (he loveth) in *such as he loveth* (Gen. 27:9).⁶⁵ The *mem* of *me’en* (refuseth), which is a root letter,⁶⁶ is *mem, alef, nun*. is vocalized with a *tzere*⁶⁷. so that a *dagesh* is not placed in the *alef*⁶⁸ cannot take a *dagesh*. which follows it.⁶⁹ is a *pi’el*. The middle root letters of words in the *pi’el* have a *dagesh* in them, and their first root letter is vocalized with a *chirik* in the perfect. Compare, *dibber, shibber*. *Cheref* (jeoparded) in *jeoparded their lives* (Jud. 5:18) is similar.⁷⁰. Its *chet* is vocalized with a *tzere* in place of a *chirik* because its middle letter (a *resh*) cannot take a *dagesh*.

⁶⁸ An alef

**לך אל פרעה בבקר.** מנהג מלך מצרים עד היום לצאת בתמוז ואב כי אז יגדל היאור לראות כמה מעלות עלה וצוה השם למשה שילך בבקר, ויעמוד לפני היאור ויעש האות שהוא מכת היאור לפני פרעה, וצוהו לקחת המטה אשר נהפך לנחש על ידי משה לפני לכתו אל פרעה ויתנהו אל אהרן לנטותו על מימי מצרים שיראה פרעה בעיניו, כי מרגע שיכה אהרן במטה על היאור אז יהפך לדם:


GET THEE UNTO PHARAOH IN THE MORNING. It is the custom of the king of Egypt until this very day to go out in the months of Tamuz and Ab to see how high the water has risen. This is the time the river increases. God commanded Moses to go in the morning and stand before the river and perform the sign of the striking of the river in the presence of Pharaoh. He commanded Moses to take and then give to Aaron the rod which he had turned into a serpent before coming unto Pharaoh (Ex. 4:3) and to wave it over the waters of Egypt so that Pharaoh would see with his very eyes the river turn into blood at the moment that Aaron struck it.

**כה.** השליח ידבר על פי השולח ואמר דרך קצרה, כי תחסר מלת שלוחו, וככה הנה אנכי שלוחו מכה במטה אשר בידי:


THUS SAITH THE LORD. The messenger speaks the word of the one who sent him.⁷¹. However, as Moses is not the Lord, Moses should rather have said: In this thou shalt know that He is the Lord. Hence I.E.’s comment. Moses was brief, for the term “His messenger” has been omitted. The statement should be understood thus: *behold, I* His messenger⁷² *will smite with the rod that is in my hand*.

ונלאו. מבנין נפעל, מגזרת לאה כטעם לא יכלו:


SHALL LOATHE. *Ve-nil’u* (shall loathe) is a *nifal* from the same root as the word *la’ah* (weary).⁷⁴. Its meaning is, will be unable.⁷⁵ as *Vat. Ebr*. 38 does. According to I.E. the word *la’ah* means unable. So too Rashbam. Rashi and others translate it as: were weary and tired. According to I.E. *nil’u* means were unable. The *vav* changes it to an imperfect; hence *ve-nil’u* means will be unable.

AND THE LORD SAID. According to my opinion this is to be understood as follows. Aaron waved his hand and struck the Nile. He also waved his hand toward all the sides of Egypt to turn the waters of all the rivers in the land of Egypt, that is, in the kingdom of Egypt, into blood.⁷⁶ The term *the waters of Egypt* is a general term. *Over their rivers* is one of its particulars. The term *ye’or* (stream)⁷⁷ as river. River is a better translation as it refers to the Nile. refers exclusively to the Nile. There are other rivers in Egypt,⁷⁸ (their rivers). for the blood was over all of their country.⁷⁹

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:19:3)

THEIR POOLS. Pools of rainwater that form by themselves.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:19:4)


**אגמיהם.** מים מחוברים מעצמם ממי המטר:


AND OVER THEIR PONDS OF WATER. This refers to fountains, wells, and cisterns. Saadiah Gaon says that the word *meyeme* (water of),⁸² (of their water). which is the word *me* (water of) doubled, refers to sweet water while the word *me* refers to bitter water, as in *me ha-yam* (waters of the sea). Scripture therefore reads, *ha-kore le-me ha-yam* (that calleth for the waters of the sea) (Amos 5:8). Now the Gaon forgot that Scripture states, *me ha-yarden yikkaretun* (the waters of the Jordan shall be cut off) (Josh. 3:13).⁸³ refers also to sweet water. The word *me* is always doubled when connected to a pronoun, as in the word *memai* (my water) (I Sam. 25:11) and in *memekha* (thy water) (Ezek. 12:18). This mode comes exclusively in the plural form,⁸⁴ as it is incorrect to say *memi* (my water) and *memah* (her water).⁸⁵ We find me⁸⁶ used in the singular in *because the water of* (me) *sprinkling was not dashed* (Num. 19:13).⁸⁷ (dashed) is singular. Hence *me* too is in the singular.

### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:22:1)


**ויעשו כן.** מלת בלטיהם מגזרת "ותבא אליו בלט" (שופ' ד' כא) בדברי סתר הנעלמים מן העין ואין המלה חסרת ה"א, כי הה"א איננה מאותיות המשך באמצע המלה, ויש לשאול אם על יד אהרן נהפכו כל מימי מצרים לדם, אנה מצאו החרטומים מים והפכום, והתשובה, אהרן לא הפך רק המים שהיו על הארץ, לא המים שהיו תחת הארץ, והחרטומים חפרו והוציאו מים והראו כי נהפכו לדם ויש הפרש גדול בין מעשה אהרן ובין מעשיהם כי אהרן הפך כל היאור שהיה לפניו, וכל מים שהיה בכל גבול מצרים שלא היה רואה אותם ועוד כי הפך מים שאינם עומדים רק רצים תמיד, ומים אחרים באים ועוד כי עמדה המכה שבעת ימים, והחרטומים לא הראו שהפכו רק מים מעטים עומדים בכלי, וזה היה רגע אחד עד ששב פרעה אל ביתו:


AND THE MAGICIANS OF EGYPT DID IN LIKE MANNER WITH THEIR SECRET ARTS. The word *be-latehem* (with their secret arts) comes from the same root as *ba-lat* (stealthily)⁸⁹, meaning to envelop, to cover, i.e., to do something secretly. I.E.’s point is that *be-latehem* is not to be confused with *be-lahatehem* in verse 11. in *she approached him stealthily* (Jud. 4:21).⁹⁰ It means with secret things hidden from the eye. A *heh* has not been omitted from the word,⁹¹, for the *heh* would be implied in the *pattach* sound and *be-lahtehem* would thus be a variant of *be-lahatehem* in verse 11. for the *heh* is not an implied letter in the middle of a word.⁹² One may ask: If all the water in Egypt was turned into blood by Aaron, where did the magicians find the water to turn into blood? The answer is: Aaron turned only water that is found above ground into blood. He did not transform any water that was below ground.⁹³ The magicians dug and brought forth water from beneath the ground and openly turned it into blood. Now, there is a great difference between what Aaron did and what the magicians brought about. Aaron transformed all of the Nile that was before him plus all the water that was in all the borders of Egypt, which he did not see.⁹⁴ Furthermore, he changed water that was not standing still but was continually running, with other water taking its place, into blood. Additionally, the plague lasted for seven days. The magicians, on the other hand, were only able to transform a little water standing in a vessel, for a moment, until Pharaoh returned to his house.

⁹³ The Egyptians dug for water to drink. See verse 24.
⁹⁴ Into blood. The point is that Aaron transformed both the water that he saw (the Nile) and the water which he did not see into blood.

**ויחפרו.** רבים אומרים כי המים היו ביד המצרי אדומים כדם, ונתלבנו ביד הישראלי, א"כ למה לא נכתב אות זה בתורה, ולפי דעתי כי מכת הדם והצפרדעים והכנים היתה כוללת המצרים והעברים כי אחר הכתוב נרדוף ואלה השלש מעט הזיקו, רק מכת הערב שהיתה קשה, השם הפריש בין המצריים ובין ישראל וככה מכת הדבר והברד בעבור מקניהם ולא כן בשחין ולא בארבה כי הם יוצאים ממצרים, וכאשר חפרו המצרים כי חפרו העברים:


DIGGED. Many say that the water was as red as blood in the hands of an Egyptian and became clear in the hands of an Israelite.⁹⁷ 9:9. If this is so then why doesn’t the Torah record this sign? I believe that the plagues of blood, frogs, and gnats⁹⁸ included both Egyptians and Hebrews, for we shall follow Scripture.⁹⁹. Since Scripture does not indicate that these plagues did not affect the Israelites, we do not assume the contrary. These three plagues caused little harm. However, God differentiated between the Egyptians and the Israelites with regard to the swarms,¹⁰⁰ which was a very harmful plague. So too with regard to the plagues of murrain¹⁰¹ and hail¹⁰² because of their flocks.¹⁰³ This was not the case with the boils and locusts,¹⁰⁴ for they¹⁰⁵ left¹⁰⁶ Egypt.¹⁰⁷ Now as the Egyptians *digged*,¹⁰⁸ so did the Hebrews dig.¹⁰⁹

### Verse 27

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 7:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/7:27:1)


**ואם.** מלת מאן תאר יוצא, כמו ושבח אני את המתים (קהלת ד ב), וטעם נגף כמו משחית, וכן כתיב "וצפרדע ותשחיתם" (תה' עה מה), והמפרשים נחלקו במלת צפרדעים ורבים אמרו שהוא מין דג נמצא במצרים יקרא בלשון ערב אלתמסח, ויוצא מן הנהר וחוטף בני אדם ואחרים אמרו כי הם הנמצאים ברובי הנהרות שמשמיעים קול, והוא הנכון בעיני והוא הידוע:


AND IF. The word *ma’en* (refuse) is a transitive¹¹¹ (tired), hence I.E.’s comment. participle.¹¹² is ordinarily an infinitive, here it is used as an adjective. The normal participle form for this word in *pi’el* is *me-ma’en*. It is like the word *ve-shabbe’ach* (wherefore I praised)¹¹³ is a participle even though this form of the word is ordinarily an infinitive. The normal participle form of this word in the *pi’el* is *me-shabbe’ach*. in *Wherefore I praised the dead* (Eccles. 4:2). The meaning of *nogef* (smite) is destroy. It is thus written, *And frogs, which destroyed them* (Ps. 78:45). The commentaries are divided as to the meaning of the word *tzefarde’im* (frogs). Many say that it is a type of fish called *al-timsach*¹¹⁴ in Arabic that is found in Egypt, that arises from the river and preys upon people. Others say that it is the well-known sound-producing creature which is found in the majority of rivers.¹¹⁵ This interpretation appears to me to be correct.

Rabbi Samuel ben Hofni⁹ says that people usually pray that a plague be removed from them immediately.¹⁰ Pharaoh, however, thought that the plague of frogs resulted from an unpropitious conjunction of heavenly bodies which Moses knew about.¹¹ He thought that the time for the removal of the frogs had now come.¹² Therefore Pharaoh tested Moses by asking him to extend the plague and said, *Against tomorrow*.

### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:12:1)


**ויאמר.** דע כי על יד אהרן היו השלש המכות הראשונות, והאותות היו בשפלים, כמו שפירשתי למעלה, כי השתים היו במים, והשלישית בעפר הארץ, והמכות שהיו על יד משה במטה היו בעליונים, כמו שמעלתו עליונה ממעלת אהרן, כמו מכת הברד והארבה שהרוח הביאה והחשך שהיה באויר, גם מכת השחין היתה על ידו, רק שלש בלא מטה, והם ערוב, ודבר, ומכת בכורים, ואחת בלא מטה על ידי משה ומעט שיתוף לאהרן והיא מכת השחין:


AND THE LORD SAID. Note that the first three plagues and signs which Aaron brought about pertained to the lowest elements,¹⁵ as I have explained previously, since two were related to water and one to the dust of the earth. However, the plagues brought about by Moses with his rod related to a higher element. This was so because Moses was on a higher plane than Aaron. Thus the hail and the locusts were brought by the wind, and the darkness was in the air.¹⁶ Moses also brought about the plague of boils.¹⁷ However, three plagues came about without the use of the rod, namely, the swarms of beasts, murrain, and the death of the first-born.¹⁸ One plague, that of the boils, was brought about by Moses with Aaron’s minor participation and without the use of the rod.

footnotes:
¹⁵ For the four elements, see Vol. 1, p. 74, note 53.
¹⁶ Air (wind) was believed to be a higher element.
¹⁷ It was Moses who threw the soot of the furnace heavenward and caused boils to break out upon man and beast. See Ex. 9:10. This plague entailed the element of air.
¹⁸ These three plagues did not entail any interaction with any of the elements. Thus Aaron brought three plagues via the rod, i.e., blood, frogs, and gnats. Moses similarly brought three plagues via the use of the rod, i.e., hail, locusts, and darkness. One plague was brought jointly by Moses and Aaron without the use of the rod, i.e., the plague of boils. Three other plagues came about without any action by Moses and Aaron, i.e., the swarms of beasts, (J.P.S. renders swarms of flies), murrain, and the death of the first-born.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:12:2)


טעם והיה לכנים, כמו והיה לאבק (למטה ט ט) כאילו בעפר שיכה אהרן יעלה ויוליד כנים בכל ארץ מצרים:


[THAT IT MAY BECOME GNATS THROUGHOUT ALL THE LAND OF EGYPT.] This is similar in meaning to *And it shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt* (Ex. 9:9).¹⁹ prefixed to *kinnim* does not mean to, but for, i.e.; *le-kinnim* does not mean to gnats but for gnats, that is, so that gnats will result. Similarly, *le-afar* does not mean to dust but for dust, i.e., so that dust will result. I.E. comments thus because the *lamed* usually has the meaning of to. The dust which Aaron struck gave birth, as it were, to gnats which went up over all the land of Egypt.²⁰

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:13:1)


**ויעשו.** טעם ויעשו על משה בעבור שדבר לאהרן שיכה במטה כדרך, ומטך אשר הכית בו את היאור (למטה יז ה):

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:13:2)


**ותהי הכנם.** שם המין והמ"ם נוסף, או הוא תחת ה"א ואיננו שרש, ולפעמים הוא סימן לשון נקבות כמו צפרדעים, כי האחת, ותעל הצפרדע (למעלה פ' ב), והעד כנים, ותהיה מלת "הכנם" זרה בעבור תוספות המ"ם, כמו ריקם, חנם, ויפת אמר, כי המ"ם סימן למצריים, כי האחת כן מן "כנים" כמו פת מפתים, וזהו המלה כדרך "בתוך האהלי" (יהושע ז כא) ואל תתמה בעבור שאמר כל עפר הארץ היה כנים, בעבור שהכה במטה במקום אחד, כי כן היה דבר המים, ודבר השחין, כי הטעם הוא כי אז תחל המכה:


AND THERE WERE GNATS. *Kinnam* (gnats) is a generic name.²¹ presents a problem. The Hebrew word for gnat is *kinnah*; for gnats, *kinnim*. Hence our verse should have read *kinnim* or *kinnah* if a collective noun were employed. The *mem* of *kinnam* is either superfluous or in place of a *heh*.²² (a variant of *kinnah*), the *mem* in *kinnam* being superfluous. He then suggests that the word for gnat is *kinnah*, with a *mem* substituted for a *heh*. In any case, it is not a root letter. The *mem* sometimes serves as the sign of the feminine plural, as in the word *tzefardi’im* (frogs). This term is a feminine, for when referring to the singular Scripture reads, *va-ta’al ha-tzefarde’a* (and the frog came up) (Ex. 8:2).²³ (came up) is a feminine verb. Thus *tzefarde’a* (frog), the noun which it governs, must also be feminine. Hence *tzefardi’im* (frogs) is a feminine plural. I.E. makes note of this because a *mem* suffixed to a noun usually indicates that a word is a masculine plural. The term *kinnim* is proof of the aforementioned.²⁴ of kinnam is not a root letter, for the plural of *kinnah*. is *kinnim*, not *kinnamim* According to this interpretation the word *ha-kinnam* is irregular because of its superfluous *mem*.²⁵. It is similar to the word *rekam* (empty) and *chinnam* (gratuitous).²⁶ However, Yefet says that the *mem* of *kinnam* is a pronominal suffix relating to the Egyptians.²⁷ (gnats) means their gnats, for *kinnam* is a combination of the noun *ken* (gnat) and the pronoun *she-lahem* (their). He claims that the singular of *kinnim* (gnats) is *kan*, in the same way that the singular of *pittim* (morsels) is *pat* (morsel). He also says that the word *ha-kinnam* is similar to the word *ha-oholi* (my tent) (Josh. 7:21).²⁸) prefixed to it. Thus *prima facie, ha-kinnam* cannot mean their gnats. Hence Yefet points out that we occasionally do find the definite article prefixed to a noun combined with a pronoun, as in the word *ha-oholi*. Do not be amazed that Scripture records that after one spot was struck, *all the dust of the earth became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt*.²⁹ Its meaning is that the plague then started.³⁰ did not turn to gnats the moment Aaron struck the earth. The same is true regarding the plagues of the water³¹ (Ex. 7:20). and the boils.³²

### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:15:1)


**ויאמרו.** בעבור שראו שעשו כמעשה אהרן בדבר התנין, גם במכת הדם הצפרדע, ולא יכלו עתה לעשות כאשר עשה אהרן אמרו לפרעה לא באה זאת המכה בעבור ישראל לשלחם, רק מכת אלהים היא כפי מערכת הכוכבים על מזל ארץ מצרים, כי כבר פירשתי כי פרעה לא כחש הבורא, רק השם שהזכיר לו משה, וזה כדרך "כי לא ידו נגעה בנו, מקרה הוא היה לנו" (ש"א ו ט) מן השמים, על כן חזק לב פרעה, ואשר יחזק זה הפי', שאמרו אצבע אלהים היא, ולא אמרו אצבע ד' שהוא אלהי ישראל, כאשר אמר פרעה במכת הצפרדעים, העתירו אל ד' (למעלה פ' ד') וזה השם הזכיר במכות האחרונות, ועוד כי משה אמר לפרעה דבר מכת היאור לפני היותה, וככה מכת הצפרדעים, ולא הזכיר לו בתחלה מכת הכנים:


THEN THE MAGICIANS SAID. When the magicians saw that unlike the changing of the rod into a serpent and the plague of blood and frogs where they were able to duplicate Aaron’s actions they were now unable to imitate what Aaron had done, they said to Pharaoh that this plague did not come to liberate Israel but was a disaster sent by God in keeping with the arrangements of the stars dealing with Egypt’s fortune. I have previously explained that Pharaoh did not deny the existence of a Creator.³³ He only denied the existence of the God which Moses revealed to him. Our verse is explained by, *it is not His hand that smote us; it was a chance that happened to us* (I Sam. 6:9) from heaven. Hence Pharaoh’s heart was hardened. Our interpretation is supported by the fact that the magicians said, *This is the finger of God*, and not, this is the finger of the Lord, meaning the God of Israel, as Pharaoh did when he exclaimed, *Entreat the Lord*, with regard to the plague of frogs and then similarly used this term for God in the latter plagues.³⁴) rather than *Elohim* (God) for the Deity. *Adonai* is the Lord’s proper name. *Elohim* is a generic name and in the Bible often refers to idols. Furthermore, Moses told Pharaoh that the Nile would be stricken before it was actually plagued, and he likewise informed him that the land would be inundated by frogs before they appeared. However, Moses did not inform Pharaoh that a plague of gnats was about to strike.³⁵

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:18:1)


**והפליתי.** יש אומרים שהוא חסר אל"ף, והנכון שהוא מבעלי הה"א וטעמו וְאַפְרֵשׁ, ומדרך הסברא עתה החל פרעה להקל מעבודת ישראל, כאשר ראה שהפריש השם בין ישראל ובין מצרים פחד לעשות להם רעה כי צורך יש לו לשלחם לזבוח פן יפגענו בדבר, הלא תראה כי עתה נתן להם רשות לזבוח בארץ:


AND I WILL SET APART. Some say that the word *ve-hifleti* (and I will set apart) is missing an *alef*.³⁸. There is no *alef* in *ve-hifleti*, hence I.E.’s comment. However, I believe that it comes from a root ending in a *heh*.³⁹ Hence there is no *alef* in *ve-hifleti*. The meaning of *ve-hifleti* is, and I will set apart. It is logical to assume that Pharaoh now started to lighten Israel’s burden. When he saw that the Lord put a division between Israel and Egypt he feared to harm them. He now saw the need to send them to offer sacrifices to the Lord, *lest he fall upon us with pestilence* (Ex. 5:3).⁴⁰ was first uttered by the Israelites. However, it also referred to Pharaoh. See I.E.’s comment on Ex. 5:3. Don’t you see that he now gave them permission to sacrifice to the Lord in the land of Egypt?⁴¹

³⁹ Its root is peh, lamed, heh.
⁴⁰ Lest he fall upon us with pestilence
⁴¹ Which shows that Pharaoh now started to make concessions.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:18:2)


וטעם כי אני ד' בקרב הארץ, דרך משל כמנהג המלכים לעמוד באמצע מלכותם להיות קרוב אל הקצוות כאשר ברא השם לב האדם, שהוא מלך על כל הגוף באמצע ורוח האדם באמצע הגוף, ככתוב "ויוצר רוח אדם בקרבו" (זכרי' יב א) ועל זה ראיות רבות מן התולדות, על כן כתוב "מציון מכלל יופי אלהים הופיע" (תה' נ, ב) כי הוא באמצע היישוב ומלכות השם תראה ביישוב:


[THAT I AM THE LORD IN THE MIDST OF THE EARTH.] This is a metaphor. It is the manner of kings to establish their residences in the middle of their kingdoms so as to be equidistant to their borders. The Lord similarly placed the heart, which is “king” over man’s body, in the center of the human corporeal frame. Man’s spirit too is located in the center of the body, as it is written, *And (the Lord) formed the spirit of man in the midst of him* (Zech. 12:1).⁴² There are many proofs from nature that this is so. Scripture states, *Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined forth* (Ps. 50:2) because Zion is in the center of the inhabited world and God’s presence is seen in the inhabited world.⁴³

footnotes:
⁴² I.E. believed that man’s soul is located in the heart, which is in the center of the body. He held that Zech. 12:1 supports this contention.
⁴³ See I.E. on Gen. 1:1.

### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:22:1)


**ויאמר.** אמר ר' ישועה, כי פי' תועבת מצרים, משה כתב כן לגנות ע"ז כי לא אמר לפרעה רק אלהי מצרים, והוא אמר כי היה אלהיהם על צורת טלה, כי היו חושבים על מזל טלה שהוא מושל בארצם, ובעבור זה לא היו אוכלים בשר ואילו היה כן, למה לא יאכלו בשר שור או בשר גדיים, ולפי דעתי כי אנשי מצרים בימי משה היו על דעת אנשי לנדיא"ה שהם יותר מחצי העולם, וכולם הם בני חם ואינם אוכלים בשר עד היום, גם דם וחלב ודג ובצים, והכלל כל דבר שיצא מן החי, והם מתעבים מי שיאכל אותם ומלאכה נמאסה בעיניהם לרעות הצאן, וכן כתוב "כי תועבת מצרים כל רועה צאן" (ברא' מו לד), ועד היום לא יניחו אדם שיאכל בשר בארצם, ואם אחד מהם יבא בארץ נכריה, יברח מכל מקום שיאכלו בו בשר, ולא יאכל כל דבר שיגע בו אוכל בשר, וכליו טמאים בעיניהם, וכן כתוב כי לא יוכלון המצרים לאכול את העברים לחם (ברא' מג לב) והנה יוסף כאשר היה בבית פוטיפר המשילו על הכל לבד על הלחם אשר הוא אוכל כי לא יגע בו בעבור שהוא עברי, ואין טעם לשאול אם כן למה היה להם מקנה, כי כן יש לאנשי לנדיא"ה, כי הסוסים והחמורים והגמלים למשא ולרכוב, והבקר לחרוש, והצאן לצמר, ועוד אדבר על זה בפסח מצרים, אמר יפת, כי תחסר ה"א ממלת "ולא יסקלונו" כי הטעם והלא יסקלונו? ולפי דעתי, כי מלת הן נזבח כה"א התימה, והנה הוא כך, הנזבח את תועבת מצרים לעיניהם ולא יסקלונו כמוהו הן היתה כזאת (ירמי' ב י):


AND MOSES SAID. Rabbi Joshua says that the clause *the abomination of the Egyptians* was written to disparage idol worship. What Moses actually said to Pharaoh was, “the god of the Egyptians.” Rabbi Joshua further states that the god of Egypt was shaped like a lamb because the Egyptians believed that the constellation of the lamb ruled over their land. It is because of this that the Egyptians did not eat meat. However, if the reason for the Egyptians not eating meat was their worship of the lamb why did they also abstain from ox and goat meat? I believe that the ancient Egyptians in the time of Moses had the same belief currently held by the people of India, who make up more than half of the world. All of them are descendants of Ham.⁴⁷ They do not eat meat until this very day. These people also do not drink milk or blood or eat fish or eggs. In other words, they do not eat anything coming from a living creature. Furthermore, they abhor any person who eats any of the aforementioned. They consider shepherding to be an especially disgusting type of work. It is similarly written, *for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians* (Gen. 47:34). They also do not allow any meat-eating person in their country. If any of them goes to a foreign country he will flee from any place where flesh is eaten. They will not eat anything which a meat-eater has handled. They consider his very garments unclean. It is thus written, *because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews* (Gen. 43:32). Behold, Potiphar placed everything with the exception of the food which he ate under the care of Joseph, who was then living in his house. Potiphar would not permit him to touch his food because Joseph was a Hebrew. There is no reason to ask, “If this is so, then why did the Egyptians keep cattle?”⁴⁸ We find the same to be the case in contemporary India. Horses, asses, and camels were used to carry burdens and for riding. Cattle served to pull the plow and sheep were kept for their wool. I will yet speak on this when I discuss the Passover observed in Egypt.⁴⁹ Yefet says that an interrogative *heh* is missing in the phrase *ve-lo yiskelunu*,⁵⁰ (will they not stone us) literally means: and they will not stone us. For the clause to mean “(and) will they not stone us” it should read: *ve-ha-lo yiskelunu*; i e., an interrogative *heh* should be placed before the word *lo*. for its meaning is, will they not stone us.⁵¹ However, I believe that the word *hen* (lo) in *hen nizbach* (lo, we sacrifice)⁵² before the word *hen* (lo). J.P.S. translates: lo, if we sacrifice. has the same meaning as the interrogative *heh.* The meaning of our verse thus is: if we sacrifice (*hen nizbach*) the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us? The word *hen* in *hen hayetah ka-zot* (if there hath been such a thing) (Jer. 2:10) is identical.⁵³ is in place of the interrogative *heh*, for the meaning of *hen hayetah* is: if there had been, not lo, there had been. The word *hen* can mean lo, behold, or if.

⁵¹ The context implies that it is to be so translated.
⁵² Hence there is no need to place an interrogative heh

**ויאמר.** מלת העתירו בעדי היתה ראויה להקדים, כי הטעם העתירו בעדי ותסור זו המכה, ואז אשלח אתכם לזבוח במדבר כאשר אמרתם רק על תנאי שלא תרחיקו ללכת יותר מהשלשה ימים:

### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:25:1)


**ויאמר.** התל. זה השורש משונה, כי היה ראוי להיות התי"ו בדגש, כי הה"א שרש, כמו "הנה לא ידעתי דַבֵּר" (ירמי' א ו), וככה התל תהתלו בי, והנכון "וַיְהַתֵּל בהם אליהו" (מ"א יח כז) ואמר לו משה כן, בעבור שאמר במכת הצפרדעים לשלח את העם ולא שלח:


AND MOSES SAID…ONLY LET NOT PHARAOH DEAL DECEITFULLY. The word *hetel* (deal deceitfully) is irregular. A *dagesh* should have been placed in the *tav*, for its *heh* is a root letter. It should have been vocalized like the word *dabber* (speak) in *behold, I cannot speak* (Jer. 1:6).⁵⁵ is a *pi’el*. Hence it should follow the paradigm of *dabber*, which is a *pi’el* and should be vocalized *hattel*. Since the word is not so vocalized it is irregular. We find the same irregularity in *hatel tehatellu vo* (mock, will ye mock him) (Job 13:9).⁵⁶? Cf. Krinsky. The correct vocalization of this word is found in the clause *va-yehattel ba-hem eliyahu* (that Elijah mocked them) (I Kings 18:27).⁵⁷ form *va-yehattel*. Compare, *va-yedabber*. Moses said, *only let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more*, because he had promised to let the people go during the plague of the frogs and then didn’t.

### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:26:1)


**ויצא.** יש מלות בלשון הקדש שהן שוות בטעם, והם משני בנינים מהקל ומהכבד, כמו, ויעתר אל ד' והעתרתי אל ד' (פ' כה), וכמוהו אשר אנכי מורה (ש"א כ לו), והוא ירה החצי (שם), ואלה המלות שהן ככה, מועטות הן במספר:


AND MOSES WENT OUT. There are words in Hebrew that have the same meaning in the *kal* and *hifil.* These words come in two forms with one meaning. Examples are: *va-yetar* (and entreated) in *and entreated the Lord* and *ve-hatarti* (and I will entreat) in *and I will entreat the Lord* (v. 25).⁵⁸ is a *kal; ve-hatarti* is a *hifil*. Similarly *moreh* (shoot) and *yarah* (shot) in *which I shoot* and *he shot an arrow* (I Sam. 20:36).⁵⁹ is a *hifil*. *Yarah* is a *kal*. However, such words are rare.

⁵⁹ Moreh



### Verse 27

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 8:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/8:27:1)


**ויעש.** מלת וַיָסַר זרה בדקדוק, כי הפעלים השניים לעולם האות הראשון קמוץ, כמו וַיָשִׁב וַיָקָם ואם היה האות האחרון ח' או ע' או ר' שלא ידגשו יהיה האות הראשון בפתח גדול כמו ויַנַח ביום השביעי (למטה כ יא) וַיָנַע לבבו (ישעי' ז ב) וַיָסַר אליה (שופ' ד) ואלה מהבנין הקל, כי מהבנין הכבד יהיה האות הראשון בפתח קטן אם לא היה האות האחרון אחת מהאותיות הנזכרות כמו וַיָשֶׁב את כל הרכוש (ברא' יד טז), והנה בא וַיָסַר תחת וַיָסֶר, כמו וַיָסַר את אופן מרכבותיו (למטה יד כה), ונכון הוא להיות ויסר הערוב מהבנין הקל כמו, וסר הערוב (פ' כה):


AND THE LORD DID. The word *va-yasar* (and he removed) is grammatically irregular. Roots having a *vav* as their middle letter⁶⁰ is *samekh, vav, resh*. are vocalized with a *kamatz* beneath their first stem letter, i.e., *va-yashav* (and he returned)⁶¹ is *shin, vav, bet*. and *va-yakam* (and he got up).⁶² is *kof, vav, mem*. However, in cases where the last letter of the root cannot receive a *dagesh*, i.e., if it is a *chet, ayin*, or *resh*, then the first root letter is vocalized with a *pattach*,⁶³. as in *va-yanach* (and rested)⁶⁴. in *and rested on the seventh day* (Ex. 20:11); *va-yana* (was moved)⁶⁵. in *and his heart was moved* (Is. 7:2); *va-yasar* (and he turned) in *And he turned in unto her* (Jud. 4:18). All of the aforementioned applies to words in the *kal*, because in the *hifil* roots having a *vav* as their middle letter are vocalized with a *segol* beneath their first stem letters in cases where their roots do not end in the letters mentioned above.⁶⁶, or *resh*. An example of the aforementioned is *va-yashev* (and he brought back) in *And he brought back all the goods* (Gen. 14:16). Now *and he removed* is written *va-yasar* rather than *va-yaser*.⁶⁷. It is so written because its final root letter is a *resh.* Thus the *hifil* and the *kal* of this root are spelled in the same way, hence the grammatical irregularity of this root. It is like *va-yasar* (and he took off) in *And he took off their chariot wheels* (Ex. 14:25). However, it appears that *va-yasar* is a *kal* and that *va-yasar he-arov* (and He removed the swarms of flies) means: and the swarms of flies departed.⁶⁸ to be a *hifil* its meaning is, and he removed. If we interpret it as a *kal* its meaning is, and he (it) departed.

**ויכבד פרעה.** הוא חזק לבו כאשר עשה בצפרדעים שכתוב שם והכבד את לבו (למעלה פ' יא):


AND PHARAOH HARDENED HIS HEART. He hardened his heart as he did at the plague of the frogs wherein it is written: *he hardened his heart* (v. 11).



## Chapter 9


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:1:1)


**בא אל פרעה.** אל הארמון שלו, א"ר יהודה הלוי שתים מכות היו במים, האחת שהתאדמו ומתה הדגה, והשנית, שעלו הצפרדעים מהם, ובארץ שתים, אחת מהכנים, והשנית מהערוב, והן חיות מעורבות, וכתיב, ותוצא הארץ נפש חיה (ברא' א כד) ושתים באויר, כי הדבר איננו רק חם או קר, משונה מן המנהג, וברגע אחד מתים אין להם מספר בעבור כי רוח כל החיים שהיא בלב תלויה באויר והשנית, מכת שחין, כי הכתוב יקרא הרקיע אשר על ראשם שמים, והמכה השביעית מעורבת מגלגל הסערה ומגלגל האש, וכן כתוב ואש מתלקחת בתוך הברד (שמות ט כד) והשמינית מכת הארבה שבאה מרחוק ע"י הרוח והתשיעית היתה מכה נפלאה שנעדר אור שני המאורות והככבים מארץ מצרים, והעשירית רדת המשחית מגלגלי הכבוד להרוג הבכורים:


GO IN UNTO PHARAOH. To his palace. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi says that two plagues were in the water: one, that it turned red and the fish died; two, that frogs arose from it.¹ Two plagues were on the earth:² one of gnats and the second the swarms, which were an assortment of wild animals. And it is written, *Let the earth bring forth the living creature* (Gen. 1:24).³ There were likewise two plagues in the air.⁴ Murrain⁵ is nothing but a change from the normal in the air’s heat or cold. This change causes an untold number to die in an instant, as the spirit of life which resides in the heart depends on the air.⁶ The second plague⁷ was the boils. Scripture refers to the firmament which is above their heads as the heaven.⁸ (Ex. 9:10) it means “and let Moses throw it up to the air,” as the air above is called the firmament. See I.E. on Gen. 1:6 where he writes, “The firmament is the air.” The seventh plague⁹ was a mixture of the sphere of the whirlwind¹⁰ and the sphere of fire.¹¹ It is thus written, *and fire flashing up amidst the hail* (v. 24). The eighth was the plague of locusts which the wind brought from afar. The ninth was a wonderful plague in that the light from the two great luminaries and the stars was absent from above the land of Egypt.¹² The tenth was the descent of the destroyer from the spheres of the glory¹³. I.E. refers to a large shining star as a *kavod* (a glory). See Y. Klatzkin, *Otzar Ha-Munachim Ha-Filosfim*, Vol. II, Berlin, 1928, p. 62. to kill the first-born.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹ The first two plagues came about through Egypt’s waters.
² The next two plagues came about via the earth.
³ The plague of wild animals can thus be considered as a plague from the ground.
⁴ The next two plagues came about through the air.
⁵ Or pestilence. I.E. did not know that germs are the cause of pestilence.
⁶ See I.E. on Gen. 2:7.
⁷ To strike through the air.
⁸ When Scripture states, Take to you handfuls of soot…and let Moses throw it heavenward
⁹ The plague of hail.
¹⁰ A layer of wind surrounding the earth.
¹¹ A layer of fire surrounding the earth. Medieval man believed in four elements: earth, water, air, and fire. I.E. explains that all the earthly elements plus some heavenly elements were involved in bringing about the plagues. That is, two blows came from the water, two from the earth, two from the air, one from a combination of air and fire, two more from the air (locusts and darkness), and one from the heavens. Earth is the heaviest element. We therefore would imagine that it would be the first element involved in the plague. However, I.E. notes in Gen. 1:6 that it is the nature of water to be below the earth. Hence the first plague came from the waters, and succeeding plagues moved upward to the heavens.
¹² This too came about from the air, in that the air was clouded (Krinsky). See I.E on Ex. 10:22.
¹³ Hebrew, galgale ha-kavod
¹⁴ I.E. apparently believes that an evil conjugation of the stars caused the first-born to die.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:2:1)


**ועודך מחזיק.** חסר יד או הדומה כמו, מחזיק באזני כלב (משלי כו יז):


AND WILL HOLD THEM STILL. The word hand or something similar¹⁵ has been omitted.¹⁶ (hold them) is a *hifil*, a causative. It literally means causes to hold. Hence, whenever this form is encountered, the word hand or something similar is implied although not always stated. Our phrase literally reads: and will still cause to hold them. I.E. interprets this to mean: and will still cause your hand (or something similar) to hold them (Filwarg). *One that holdeth*¹⁷. J.P.S. translates as *taketh*. *a dog by the ears* (Prov. 26:17) is similar.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁵ Perhaps teeth (Weiser).
¹⁶ The word machazik
¹⁷ Hebrew, machazik
¹⁸ This too should be read as: one that causeth his hand to hold a dog by the ears. It literally reads: one that causeth to hold a dog by the ears.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:3:1)


**הנה יד ד' הויה.** הנה מצאנו שיתחלף היו"ד בוי"ו, ואתה הוה להם למלך (נחמיה ו ו) והפך זה שוי"ו אשר לא יבושו קוָֹי (ישעי' מט כג) יתחלף ביו"ד וקוֵֹי ד' יחליפו כח (שם מ לא) :


BEHOLD, THE HAND OF THE LORD IS UPON. Observe, we find that a *yod* interchanges with a *vav*,¹⁹ (is). as elsewhere we read, *and thou wouldest be* (hoveh) *their king* (Neh. 6:6).²⁰ is the usual form. Hence in *hoyah* a *yod* has been interchanged with a *vav*. The opposite is the case with the *vav* of *kovai* (that wait for me)²¹. in *For they shall not be ashamed that wait for Me* (Is. 49:23) which interchanges with a *yod* in the word *ve-kove* (but they that wait)²² is spelled *kof, vav, yod*. This comment presents a problem. *Prima facie*, no *yod* has been interchanged for a *vav* in *kove*, because this is the normal construct form of the word. Compare, *love* (*lamed, vav, heh*) and *shave* (*shin, vav, heh*). We must assume that I.E. read *koye* rather than *kove* (same vocalization but different spelling). See Rabbi David Kimchi and S. Kraus, *Sefer Yeshayahu*, edited by A. Kahanah, on Is. 40:31. in *But they that wait for the Lord shall renew their strength* (Is. 40:31).

footnotes:
¹⁹ In our verse, in the word hoyah
²⁰ Hoveh
²¹ From the root kof, vav, heh
²² The word kove


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:3:2)


ומלת דֶבֶר שם כלל לא מצאנוהו בפעלים רק במקום אחד, ותדבר את כל זרע המלוכה (דה"ב כב י), ובס' מלכים כתוב, ותאבד (מ"ב יא א) והפי' רחוק רק לא ידענו טוב ממנו:


The word *dever* (murrain) is a collective noun.²³ Its verbal form²⁴ is found employed only once, in *va-tedabber* (she destroyed) in *she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah* (II Chron. 22:10). The book of Kings²⁵ reads, *va-te’abed*²⁶ is parallel to *va-te’abed*. As *va-te’abed* means: and she destroyed, *va-tedabber* means: and she destroyed. (and she destroyed) (II Kings 11:1). This interpretation is far-fetched.²⁷ means and she destroyed. Perhaps it means she plotted against, or she waylaid, as in its Arabic cognate *dabbra*. However, we know of no better one.²⁸ means the same as *va-te’abed*.

footnotes:
²³ For pestilence. It does not refer to any particular disease (Weiser).
²⁴ Hebrew nouns have verbal forms.
²⁵ II Kings 11:1 and II Chron. 22:10 relate the same events in slightly different words.
²⁶ Va-tedabber
²⁷ That is, that va- tedabber
²⁸ We must accept the reading of the parallel verse as its meaning, i.e., that va-tedabber



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:4:1)


**והפלה.** דָבָר. יאמר על ענין דברים מחוברים כמו הדבר אשר דבר ד' (ירמי' מו יג), גם יאמר על יש כמו זה וכמוהו לא חסרת דבר (דבר' ב ז):


AND THE LORD SHALL MAKE A DIVISION…NOTHING. The word *davar* (nothing)²⁹ is used in reference to many words joined together, as in *ha-davar* (the word)³⁰, as in *eleh ha-devarim* (these are the words) (Deut. 1:1). Thus I.E. explains that *davar* can refer to many words. in *The word that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah* (Jer. 46:13). It is also used in reference to a thing, as in our verse. *Davar* in *thou hast not lacked a thing* is similar (Deut. 2:7).

footnotes:
²⁹ Literally, a thing.
³⁰ God spoke many words to Jeremiah. Thus Scripture should have read, ha-devarim

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:6:1)


**ויעש ד'.** ופי' וימת כל מקנה מצרים רובו, כי הנה כתוב, שלח העז את מקנך (פ' יט) וככה תמצא בברד את כל עשב השדה (פ' כה), והעד מכת הארבה, ואכל את יתר הפליטה (למטה י ה):


AND THE LORD DID. The meaning of *and all* (kol) *the cattle of Egypt died* is, that most of the cattle of Egypt died. For behold, it is written,³² *Now therefore send, hasten in thy cattle* (v. 19).³³ We find the same with regard to the plague of hail.³⁴ (all or every) but means most. Scripture reads, *and the hail smote every herb of the field* (v. 25). The plague of locusts concerning which it is written, *and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail* (Ex. 10:5) is proof of this.³⁵

footnotes:
³² With regard to the hail.
³³ If all the cattle died from murrain, what cattle were left to be struck by the hail?
³⁴ That Scripture uses the term kol
³⁵ If the hail destroyed every herb of the field, what was left for the locusts to eat?



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:7:1)


**עד אחד.** אפילו אחד, כאשר אפרש בשירה, וטעם זה הפסוק ואפילו ששלח וראה כי השם אוהב ישראל, ובעבורם הכה מקנהו, לא חשש מהמקנה בזאת המכה לשלח עמו, אולי לא עמדה הרבה:


SO MUCH AS ONE. *Ad echad*³⁶ means, as I will explain in the song of Moses,³⁷ *so much as one*. The meaning of our verse is: even though Pharaoh sent agents and saw that God loves Israel and on their account smote his flocks,³⁸ he was not so bothered by the death of the flocks during this plague as to let Israel go. Perhaps the plague did not last a long time.³⁹

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:9:1)


**והיה.** זה מעשה נס, שזה הפיח שהוא מעט נעשה אבק על כל ארץ מצרים ולא הפריש ישראל:


AND IT SHALL BECOME. This was miraculous, that this small amount of soot turned into dust all over the land of Egypt. This plague did not separate out the Israelites.⁴⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:9:2)


**אבעבעת.** האל"ף נוסף, כי הוא מגזרת מים תבעה אש (ישעי' סד) והמלה כפולה כמו, תשעשעו (שם סו יב) תשגשגי (שם יז יא):


BLAINS. The *alef* of *avabu’ot* (blains) is superfluous, as *avabu’ot* comes from the same root as *tiveh* (to boil)⁴¹. in *And the fire causeth the waters to boil* (Is. 64:1). The word is doubled⁴² drops out and the *bet and ayin* are doubled, forming the apparently quadriliteral *avabu’ot*. like the words *teshasha’u* (shall be dandled)⁴³. However, the *heh* drops out and the *shin* and *ayin* are doubled, forming the apparently quadriliteral *teshasha’u*. (Is. 66:12) and *tesagsegi*⁴⁴. However, the *heh* drops out and the *sin* and *gimel* are doubled, forming the quadriliteral root *sin, gimel, sin, gimel* (Krinsky). (thou didst make it to grow) (Is. 17:11).

⁴¹ Its root is bet, ayin, heh
⁴² The heh
⁴³ Its root is shin, ayin, heh
⁴⁴ Its original root is sin, gimel, heh



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:10:1)


**ויקחו את פיח הכבשן.** מלא חפניהם כאשר הזכיר ומשה זרק הכל יתכן שהחרטומים לא לקו במכת הצפרדעים והערוב, בעבור חכמתם בקשו דרך בחכמת התולדות להרויח להם מעט ועתה נבערה חכמתם על כן הזכיר זה, ובעבור שלא עמדה המכה הרבה לא בקש פרעה שיעתירו, ובעבור שהמכה הראשונה עמדה ז' ימים, לא נלמוד ממנה על דרך הפשט שככה עמדה כל מכה, ועוד אחר הכתוב נרדוף, וידוע כי מכת הדבר היתה שעה אחת, ומכת החשך ג' ימים, על כן אין לנו דרך לדעת באיזו חדש בא משה והתחילו המכות, רק אם היתה קבלה ביד חכמינו הקדושים קבלנו ושמענו:


AND THEY TOOK THE SOOT OF THE FURNACE. Each as earlier noted took handfuls of soot and Moses threw all of it heavenward.⁴⁵ It is possible that the magicians were not smitten with the plague of frogs and swarms. Through their wisdom and their knowledge of natural law they searched for a way to gain a small respite.⁴⁶ However, their knowledge now failed them, as Scripture tells us.⁴⁷ (v. 11). Pharaoh did not ask Moses and Aaron to entreat the Lord⁴⁸ because the plague did not last long. We cannot conclude from the plain meaning of the text that since the first plague lasted for seven days all the other plagues did so too. Additionally, we shall pursue the text of Scripture. It is known that the plague of murrain lasted for one hour⁴⁹ and the plague of darkness for three days. There is no way to ascertain in which month Moses came and the plagues commenced.⁵⁰ 2:10, “the judgment of the Egyptians endured twelve months.” Similarly *Seder Olam*, 3. Also, according to the rabbis, since Israel was delivered in Nisan and the plagues lasted a year they had to commence in Iyar (*Seder Olam* 3). It is possible to further interpret the rabbinic statement that the judgment of the Egyptians lasted for one year to mean that it lasted for one year from the time that Moses first appeared before Pharaoh. If we assume the aforementioned then Moses first appeared before Israel and Pharaoh in the month of Iyar. Furthermore, if we accept the fact that the judgment of the Egyptians lasted for a year then each of the ten plagues struck a little over a month apart (Tiferet Israel on *Eduyot* 3:10). Cf. *Shemot Rabba* 9:12, “Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Nehemiah: One says Moses warned them for 24 days before (he plague struck and the plague ravaged them for seven days. The other one says he warned them for seven days and the plague ravaged them for 24 days.” However, if our holy sages received this via tradition we accept and abide by it.⁵¹

⁴⁸ As he did in the case of the frogs (Ex. 8:4).
⁴⁹ That is, a very short time, for death by pestilence is immediate.
⁵⁰ According to the rabbis the plagues lasted for an entire year. See Eduyot
⁵¹ That is, that the plagues ravaged seven days, that a new one struck each month, that the plagues lasted for a year, and that Moses appeared in the month of Iyar. See note above.

### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:15:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 9:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/9:15:2)


וטעם בדבר הידוע, שבו הרגתי המקנה שלכם הייתי הורג כלכם עמהם:
