AND MOSES TOOK THE BONES OF JOSEPH. Scripture mentions above that *the children of Israel* who were alive in that generation *went up out of the land of Egypt*. Scripture now notes that the children of Israel also brought up with them the most honored one of them, the one through whom they came down to Egypt. The latter had made them swear before his death that they would tell their children, and their children would instruct their children about this.¹⁰² Now Moses busied himself with fulfilling the oath so that no guilt would fall upon Israel. For we see that the princes of Israel swore an oath to the Gibeonites.¹⁰³ Now they only took this oath on condition that the Gibeonites came from a distant place as they claimed.¹⁰⁴ After it was found that the Gibeonites came from close by¹⁰⁵ it was fitting that they not keep their oath so that they and all Israel not violate the injunction, *thou shalt save alive nothing* (Deut. 20:16). However, they kept their oath out of regard for God’s glory so that they not desecrate it.¹⁰⁶ Many years later God punished the children of Israel¹⁰⁷ because Saul permitted the Gibeonites who were in Nob, the city of the priests, to be put to death.¹⁰⁸

וטעם ללכת יומם ולילה, בעבור כי המחנה היה גדול, ולא יכלו ללכת רק מסע מעט, על כן היו הולכים מקצת יום גם מקצת לילה, ואלה השנים עמודים היו לפניהם עד שבאו אל הים כאשר אפרש:


[THAT THEY MIGHT GO BY DAY AND BY NIGHT.] Scripture reads, *that they might go by day and by night* because the camp was large and they could only journey a short distance.¹¹⁶ They therefore journeyed part of the day¹¹⁷ and also part of the night.¹¹⁸ These two pillars were, as I shall explain,¹¹⁹ before the Israelites until they came to the sea.

DEPARTED NOT. *Yamish* (departed) is a transitive verb.¹²⁰ (the pillar of cloud departed not) means: God did not cause the pillar of cloud to depart. For God mentioned above¹²¹ did not cause the pillars to depart from before the people.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/13:22:2)


ומלת יומם לא תמצא בכל המקרא רק על עת היות השמש על הארץ, כי יום ימצא בתורה ובנביאים ובכתובים והוא לילה כי כתוב ביום הכותי כל בכור (במד' ה יז) וזה היה לילה, וכתוב היום הזה יום בשורה הוא (מ"ב ז ט) והוא היה לילה, כי שם כתוב, וחכינו עד אור הבקר (שם) וכתוב יום צעקתי בלילה נגדך (תה' פה ב):


[BY DAY.] The word *yomam* (by day) is not found employed in Scripture except for the time when the sun shines upon the earth. The word *yom* (day) found in the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings refers also to nighttime, for it is written, *on the day* (yom) *that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt* (Num. 8:17). Now the slaying of the first-born took place at night.¹²² It is also written, *this day* (ha-yom) *is a day* (yom) *of good tidings* (II Kings 7:9). Now it was then night, for we read there, *if we tarry till the morning light* (*Ibid.*). Scripture also reads, *The day* (yom) *I cry in the night before Thee* (Ps. 88:2).¹²³

¹²² Ex. 12:29.

### Verse 1

**וידבר.** מדרך האמת אין ראוי למשכיל לחשוב על מעשה השם למה עשה כן, כי כל מעשיו בחכמה, וחכמת האדם כאין נגדו, והזכרתי זה, בעבור שתראה בזו הפרשה שצוה השם שישובו אחורנית דרך ערמה, כדי שיצא פרעה וירדוף אחריהם, ויטבע בים, ומחשבות השם עמוקות:


AND THE LORD SPOKE. It is truly not proper for an intelligent person to scrutinize God’s actions and ask, why did the Lord act thus?¹ For all of God’s actions are done wisely. Man’s wisdom is as nothing before God.² I mention this because you will read in this Torah portion that God³ guilefully commanded the Israelites to turn back⁴ so that Pharaoh would go out and pursue them, and drown in the sea.⁵ God’s thoughts are very deep.⁶

¹ In other words, truthfully speaking one can not always fathom God’s will.
² Cf. Ps. 39:6.
³ Acting like the general of an army.

⁵ Compare, verse 4.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:2:1)


**פי החירות.** הוא הנקרא פני החירות (במד' לג ה), ונקרא כן בעבור שהפה בפנים, והוא שם מקום:


PI-HAHIROTH. *Pi-hahiroth* is elsewhere called *Pene-hahiroth* (Num. 33:8). It is so called⁷ because the mouth (*peh*) is on the face (*panim*).⁸ (mouth of) and *pene* (face of) interchange. It is the name of a place.

**לפני בעל צפון.** אמרו כי חרטומי מצרים עשו בדבר המזלות צורות נחושת וזהו בעל צפון שלא יוכל עבד לברוח ממצרים לעבור הצורה, ובעבור זה כתוב כי ברח העם ולפי דעתי בעבור שאמר משה לפרעה דרך שלשת ימים נלך במדבר (למעלה ח כג) נראה לפרעה מדבריו כי ידע משה הדרך אשר ילכו בה אל המקום אשר יזבחו שם, וכאשר שמע פרעה שישראל החלו ללכת דרך המדבר, ואחר שהרחיקו שבו אחורנית ללכת דרך אחרת אז חשב פרעה, כי כל מה שדבר משה בערמה היה, כי אין דעתו לזבוח, כי אם לברוח, כי הבורח ישתבש עליו הדרך ולא ידע איזה דרך ילך:


BEFORE BAAL-ZEPHON. Some say that the Egyptian magicians made bronze images which drew power from the stars, and that Baal-zephon was a statue that no slave fleeing Egypt was able to pass by.⁹ It is because of this that Scripture reads, *that the people were fled* (v. 5).¹⁰ However, in my opinion because Moses said to Pharaoh, *We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness* (Ex. 8:23), it appeared to Pharaoh from these words that Moses knew the road that they would take to the place where they intended to sacrifice. Thus when Pharaoh heard that the Israelites started to go by way of the wilderness,¹¹ and when they had traveled some distance¹² backtracked to go in another way, Pharaoh surmised that everything that Moses had told him was said in guile, that he did not intend to sacrifice but to flee. For one who flees becomes confused on the way and does not know which road to take.

footnotes:
⁹ They held that Baal-zephon was an image on the border of Egypt which supernaturally prevented fleeing slaves from crossing it.
¹⁰ Once the Israelites passed Baal-zephon the Egyptians realized that the statue was ineffective against Israel and that the Israelites had fled.
¹¹ To the place where they were going to offer sacrifices.
¹² Into the desert away from Egypt.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:2:3)


**נכחו.** באה זו המלה בחירק, כמו אחרי נִפְלו (ש"ב א י) ורבים ככה:


OVER AGAINST IT. The word *nikhcho* (over against it) is vocalized with a *chirik*.¹³. The word *nikhcho* consists of the word *nokhach* (against) plus the pronominal suffix. In such cases the *cholam* changes to a *kamatz katan*. Thus we would expect *nokhcho* rather than *nikhcho*, hence I.E.’s comment. It is similar to the word *niflo* (was fallen)¹⁴, for *niflo* consists of the word *nofel* plus the pronominal suffix. in *after that he was fallen* (II Sam. 1:10). There are many other such instances.¹⁵ comes in place of a *kamatz katan* where a word vocalized with a *cholam* is combined with a pronominal suffix.

¹⁴ Which should have been vocalized noflo
¹⁵ In which the chirik



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:3:1)


**ואמר פרעה לבני ישראל.** כמו אמרי לי (ברא' כ יג):


AND PHARAOH WILL SAY OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. This is similar to *say of me* (Gen. 20:13).¹⁶ (say of me); literally, say to me. I.E.’s point is that there are instances in which the *lamed* is to be interpreted to mean of, concerning, about. Thus *li-vene yisrael* does not mean to the children of Israel but of the children of Israel.

¹⁶ Hebrew, imri li


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:3:2)


**נבוכים.** בשורק תחת חולם כמו לא תעבורי מזה (רות ב) כי הוא מבנין נפעל כמו נכונים (למטה יט יא) והנה נבוכו (יואל א יח), גם והעיר שושן נבוכה (אסתר ג טו) כמו והממלכה נכונה (מ"א ב מו) והטעם כאדם שלא ימצא עצה ולא ידע מה יעשה, ונו"ן נִבְכֵּי ים (איוב לח טז) שרש, ופירושו מעמקי ים, ואין לו טעם במקום הזה:


ENTANGLED. *Nevukhim* (entangled) is vocalized with a *shuruk* in place of a *cholam*.¹⁷ is *navokh*. Thus we would expect to see *nevokhim* rather than *nevukhim*. Compare, *nakhon, nekhonim, navon, nevonim*. It is similar to the word *ta’avuri* (pass)¹⁸ comes in place of a *sheva*. The usual form of the *kal* feminine imperfect is *ta’avri*. in *neither pass from hence* (Ruth 2:8), for *nevukhim* is a *nifal* as the word *nekhonim* (ready) (Ex. 19:11) is.¹⁹ Now *navokhu* (perplexed) (Joel 1:18) and also *navokhah* (perplexed) in *but the city of Shushan was perplexed* (Est. 3:15) are like *nakhonah* (established)²⁰ and follow the same paradigm. Similarly *nevukhim* despite its irregular vocalization. in *And the kingdom was established* (I Kings 2:46). Its meaning is, they are like a person who cannot find anyone to advise him and does not know what to do.²¹ means perplexed. The *nun* in *nivkhe* (depths of) in *the depths of the sea* (Job 38:16)²² is a root letter.²³ of *nevukhim* is not a root letter but the nun of the *nifal* form. The root of *nevukhim* is *bet, vav, kaf* and the root of *nivkhe* is *nun, bet, kaf*. The meaning of *nivkhe yam* (the springs of the sea) is the depths of the sea. *Nivkhe* has no place here.²⁴ and *nivkhe*. Rashi comments, “*Nevukhim* means enclosed and sunk deep, as in *nivkhe yam*.”

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:9:1)


**וירדפו.** מנהג הלשון לומר ככה, כמו וכל העם רואים וגו' וירא העם וינועו (למטה כ טו) והטעם כאשר ראו כן נעו ועמדו מרחוק, וככה כתוב וירדוף אחרי בני ישראל (למעלה פ' ה), והנה טעם וירדפו, כאשר רדפו אחריהם השיגם שהיו חונים על הים:


AND THE EGYPTIANS PURSUED AFTER THEM. This is in keeping with linguistical style.³³. It is similar to *and the people saw*,³⁴. *and they trembled and stood far off*³⁵ (Ex. 20:15), the meaning of which is, when they saw this,³⁶ (and they saw) is to be rendered: and when they saw. Otherwise Scripture would be literally repeating itself. they trembled and stood far off. The meaning of *and the Egyptians pursued after them* thus is: when the Egyptians pursued them,³⁷ (and they pursued) is to be rendered: and when they pursued. Thus Scripture does not literally repeat itself. they overtook them as they were encamping by the sea.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:11:1)

STAND STILL, AND SEE THE SALVATION OF THE LORD. For you will not wage war but you shall see the salvation which the Lord will work for you this day. One may ask: How is it that a large camp comprising six hundred thousand armed men were afraid of those who pursued them? Why did they not stand and fight for their own and their children’s lives? The answer is: The Egyptians were masters over Israel. The generation that left Egypt were trained from their youth to bear the yoke of the Egyptians. They were of humble spirit. How then could they now wage war against their masters? The Israelites were lazy and not learned in war. Can you not see that were it not for the prayers of Moses, the Amalekites, who came⁴⁹ with a small number of men, would have defeated Israel. God alone, *Who doeth great things* (Job 5:9); *And by Him actions are weighed* (I Sam. 2:3), so arranged events that all Israelite males⁵⁰ who left Egypt died out,⁵¹ for they had no spirit to fight the Canaanites; and a new generation with a noble spirit, who had never tasted exile, arose after the generation of the wilderness.⁵² I have noted the aforementioned in the account of Moses recorded in the Torah portion *Ve-Eleh Shemot*.⁵³

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:14:1)


**ה' ילחם לכם.** בעבורכם וככה כל מלחמה שאחריה למ"ד היא לעזר, על כן פי' ר' משה הכהן, כי רבים לוחמים לי מרום (תה' נו ג) בשבילי, וטעם מרום, מלחמת מרום כמשפט כל היושבים:


THE LORD WILL FIGHT FOR YOU. *Lakhem* means for you.⁵⁴ Similarly, whenever the word war (*milchamah*) is followed by a *lamed* it indicates aid. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen therefore explains *li* (me) in *For there are many that fight* (lochamim) *me* (li) *on high*⁵⁵ (Ps. 56:3) to mean for me.⁵⁶ follows the word war (*lochamim*.) According to Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen, Ps. 56:3 should be translated: For there are many that fight on high for me. The meaning of *on high* is, a war on high, as is the case with all that sit.⁵⁷ (that sit) to *ha-chashuvim* (that are important), the idea being that important people have others who fight for them. The verse thus states: For there are many that fight for me on high as is the case with all important people. However, in I.E.’s short commentary the reading is *ha-moshekhim*, which is a technical term for words that are to be read as if written twice. In this case our verse is to be read as follows: For there are many that fight for me, that fight for me on high, the reference being to angels who fight on his behalf. See I.E. on Ps. 56:3. In this case the last line of I.E. should be interpreted as: The meaning of on high is a war on high, as our verse belongs to those verses in which there is a word that is to be read as if written twice.

I have already showed you many such instances.⁷² Now because these three verses⁷³ are connected to each other and each one has seventy-two letters we find in them, as stated in the books,⁷⁴ on Ex. 14; Responsa of R. Hai Gaon. Also see *Ozer Ha-Geonim, Hagigah*, p. 23. The Talmud speaks of the 72-letter name of God. See *Sukkah* 45a. Those who see the 72-letter name of God in these verses do so in one of the following two ways. They arrange the three verses on top of each other and arrive at God’s name by reading down, i.e., *vav, vav, vav; yod, yod, yod; samekh, bet, tet*, etc. Or they invert verse 20 and arrange the three verses as above and read down, i.e., *vav, heh, vav; yod, lamed, yod; samekh, alef, tet*, and so on. The reason they invert the middle verse is that it states, *and the one did not come near the other all the night*; i.e., one is not to combine the letters of this verse in their normal fashion but they are to be read backwards as the word *ha-laylah* (the night) is. For *ha-laylah* reads the same whether from left to right or right to left (Krinsky). the sign of the secret of God’s explicit name. However, in my opinion it is so written⁷⁵) whose might delivered Israel. because, as I will explain in the Torah portion *Ki Tissa*,⁷⁶),which when calculated as follows, *Y* (10) *YH* (15) *YHV* (21) *YHVH* (26), comes to 72. Cf. I.E.’s *Sefer Ha-Shem* 5. the numerical value of God’s glorious name comes to seventy-two. The *Book of Raziel*⁷⁷ states that one who wants to query the heavenly powers in a dream should read the verse, *Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year*, etc. (Ezek. 1:1), for it contains seventy-two letters.⁷⁸, and apparently also in I.E’s version of Scripture, the words *ha-golah* and *marot* in Ezek. 1:1 were spelled without a *vav*. Otherwise the number of letters in Ezek 1:1 comes to 74 as they do in our editions of the Prophets. Cf. *Minchat Shai* on Ezek. 1:1.

When this angel, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them, the pillar of cloud moved with him. Let the one who identifies the angel of God with the cloud show us where we find the pillar of cloud called the angel of God. Furthermore, if the angel and the pillar are one and the same, why is *and the pillar of cloud removed from before them* repeated? If he should answer that Scripture repeats the same idea in different words,⁸⁰ then we respond that it is not the manner of Scripture to repeat itself except in prophecy⁸¹ or reproof.⁸² Moreover, it is unfit to repeat oneself when reporting how something happened.⁸³

Furthermore, we find, *On the light of the fourteenth day*⁸⁷ 2a. The meaning of which is, on the night of the fourteenth day, i.e., the night preceding the fourteenth day. We thus see that the word light can refer to night or darkness. in rabbinic literature. However, the one who interprets thus turns darkness into light and light into darkness, for it is impossible in any language for a word to mean both a thing and its opposite unless it is euphemistically used, as in *Naboth did bless God and the king* (I Kings 21:13).⁸⁸. The word light in *shall be light about me* refers to the light itself, as I have explained.⁸⁹ Similarly, the sages said⁹⁰ 3a. that *On the light of the fourteenth* is a refined language,⁹¹ which is similar to a euphemism. Furthermore, what reason was there for Scripture to say, *and he darkened the night*? It is dark every night. The only meaning of *va-ya’er et ha-laylah* is that he⁹² lit up the night⁹³ means: and he lit up the night. as he did from the day that Israel went out of Egypt, for the pillar of fire was seen every night. Now if Israel had no light how did they cross the sea?⁹⁴ For behold, by the time Pharaoh came into the sea and the Lord looked forth upon him in the morning watch, most of the Israelites had already crossed.⁹⁵

⁸⁸ Translated literally. Its meaning is, as J.P.S. translates, Naboth did curse God and the king

⁹⁰ Pesachim

**נסים לקראתו.** פרשתיו שהם חושבים בנוסם שהם חוזרין ליבשה, והם הולכים לקראתו ישתחקו עצמות חוי הכלבי שאמר כי משה ידע עת מיעוט הים ברדתו, ועת רבותו בעלותו בהמשכו, והוא העביר עמו במיעוט המים כמשפטו, ופרעה לא ידע מנהג הים על כן טבע, ואלה דברי שגעון, כי מנהג הים ברדתו לא ייבש מקום וישארו חומות מים מימינו ומשמאלו, כי הכל ייבש, ועוד כי לא יתברר סוף רדת הים ותחלת עלותו רק אחר שעות, ועוד לא השלימו ישראל לעבור עד שטבע פרעה וחילו:


FLED AGAINST IT. I have already explained¹²⁸ that the Egyptians in fleeing thought that they were returning to dry land when in actuality they were going toward the sea. May the bones of Chivi¹²⁹ the dog¹³⁰ (the dog). be crushed. Chivi said that Moses knew the time of low tide, when the level of the sea goes down, and the time of high tide, when the sea comes in and its level rises, and so brought his people across the sea when the tide was normally low. However, Pharaoh did not know the manner of the sea and therefore drowned. This interpretation is sheer madness, as the sea is not normally dry in any place when its level goes down. However, all was dry.¹³¹ Neither do walls of water remain on the right or the left.¹³² Furthermore, the end of low tide and the beginning of high tide do not become clear until some hours have passed.¹³³ Moreover, the Israelites had not yet finished crossing before Pharaoh and his army drowned.¹³⁴

¹³⁰ A play on Ha-Balkhi. By inverting the letters of Ha-Balkhi from Balakh, we get ha-kalbi
¹³¹ According to verse 29 Israel crossed on dry land.
¹³² When the sea retreats at low tide.
¹³³ It takes some hours before the effects of high and low tide are perceptible. Thus it would take quite a while for the waters to have enveloped the Egyptians. However, it appears from Scripture that the waters overwhelmed the Egyptians in a short period of time.
¹³⁴ If it was low tide why did Pharaoh and his army drown?

### Verse 29

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 14:29:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:29:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/14:29:1)


**ובני ישראל.** טעם להזכיר זה פעם אחר כי פרעה היה טובע ועוד נשארו אנשים מישראל בים עוברים וזה היה פלא בתוך פלא, כי במקום שהיו ישראל עוברים בים, היה שם רוח קדים מייבש, ובמקום פרעה וחילו הביא השם רוח אחרת להמס המים שנקרשו ונעשו חומות, והנה שתי רוחות בים ושני המקומות קרובים, והעד הנאמן על זה הפירוש שכתוב בשירה, וברוח אפך נערמו מים (למטה טו ח), וזאת הרוח היתה עם ישראל וכתוב נשפת ברוחך כסמו ים (שם פ' י) וזו היא שטבעה המצריים, על כן כתוב בסוף השירה וישב ה' עליהם את מי הים, ובני ישראל הלכו ביבשה בתוך הים (שם פ' יט), ואל תתמה איך יכלו לעבור כל הלילה, וכי שש מאות אלף רגלי לא היה רביעית המחנה, אולי על דרך אחר עברו, או נקרע לי"ב קרעים כאשר אמרו חז"ל וישראל לא עברו הים כנגד הרוחב, רק נכנסו באורך ויצאו אל מדבר שור אשר נכנסו משם כאשר אפרש:


BUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The reason this is noted a second time¹³⁹ is that there remained some Israelites who were still crossing the sea while Pharaoh was drowning. This was a miracle within a miracle, for in the place where the Israelites were crossing the sea there was a strong east wind drying¹⁴⁰ and where Pharaoh and his host were, God brought another wind to melt the waters that were frozen and formed walls. There were thus two winds in two places in the sea close to one another.¹⁴¹ True proof that this interpretation is correct is offered by the statement in the Song of Moses, *And with the blast of Thy nostrils the waters were piled up* (Ex. 15:8), which speaks of the wind that blew for Israel; and the statement, *Thou didst blow with Thy wind, the sea covered them* (Ex. 15:10), which speaks of the wind that caused the Egyptians to drown. It is because of this that the end of the song reads, *and the Lord brought back the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea* (Ex. 15:19). Do not ask, how could all of Israel cross in one night? Did not the six hundred thousand men on foot¹⁴² make up only a quarter of the camp?¹⁴³. 38 is: For the six hundred thousand men on foot did not make up even a quarter of the camp. Perhaps they passed over some other way.¹⁴⁴ Or perhaps the sea split into twelve parts, as the sages of blessed memory say.¹⁴⁵ 42; *Tanchuma, Be-Shallach* 10; *Mekhilta, Be-Shallach* 4. Now the Israelites did not cross the width of the sea.¹⁴⁶ On the contrary, they moved along its length and came out in the wilderness of Shur from wherein, as I will explain, they entered the sea.¹⁴⁷

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:1:1)


**אז ישיר משה.** משפט לה"ק לומר לשון עתיד תחת עבר עם מלת אז אז יבנה שלמה (מ"א יא ז) אז ידבר יהושע (יהושע י יב) אז יבדיל משה (דבר' ד מא) וככה בלשון ישמעאל משה לבדו חבר השירה ולמדוה ישראל ושורר כל אחד ואומר אשירה לה' וכמוהו ויצו משה וזקני ישראל (דבר' כז א) כי המצוה משה לבדו אמרה, וזקני ישראל אמרוה לכל:


THEN SANG MOSES. It is Hebrew style to employ an imperfect preceded by the word *az* (then) in place of a perfect.¹ (then sang Moses) literally means: then Moses will sing. I.E. points out that an imperfect preceded by the word *az* occasionally has the meaning of a perfect. Similarly, in the next three verses cited by I.E. verbs that are in the imperfect are to be translated as perfects, for the imperfects are preceded by the word *az*. Compare, *Az yivneh shelomoh* (then did Solomon build) (I Kings 11:7);² is an imperfect that means will build. Thus *az yivneh shelomoh* literally means: then will Solomon build. *az yedabber yehoshu’a* (then spoke Joshua) (Josh. 10:12);³ is an imperfect that means will speak. Therefore *az yedabber yehoshu’a* literally means: then will Joshua speak. az *yavdil mosheh* (then Moses separated) (Deut. 4:41).⁴ is an imperfect that means will separate. Thus *az yavdil mosheh* means: then Moses will separate. The same is true in Arabic. Moses composed the song by himself. He then taught it to all of Israel, each one of whom then sang and said, *I will sing unto the Lord*.⁵ (and spoke), which literally means: and they spoke. *Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song* may be interpreted to mean that Moses and Israel simultaneously broke into song. However, this interpretation is untenable, as it is impossible for a whole nation to know the contents of a song without first being taught its words. Hence I.E.’s comment. *And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people* (Deut. 27:1) is similar. The commandment was first spoken only by Moses. The elders of Israel then repeated it to everyone.⁶

**עזי.** אמר רבינו שלמה ז"ל כי יש הפרש בין עזי בקמץ חטף ובין עֻזי בקבוץ על כן אמר כי יו"ד עזי וזמרת יה נוסף ולא הראה לנו אחר כמוהו, ואמר כי וזמרת יה סמוך כאילו כתוב עז וזמרת יה היה לי לישועה כי חשב כי כמוהו ויהי ביום השלישי וישא אברהם את עיניו (ברא' כב ד), ומי שיבין בלשון ישמעאל ידע ההפרש שיש ביניהם, כי לומר עזי וזמרת יה ויהי לי לישועה איננו משפט לשון הקדש ולא לשון ישמעאל, ואין הפרש בין עזי בקמץ חטף, ובין היותו בקבוץ, כי אמר הטריפני חֻקי (משלי ל ה) נאמר ממנו. כי חָקךָ וְחָק בניך (ויקרא י יג), והנה בשירה הזאת, נהלת בעָזךָ (פ' יג) בקמץ חטף, וכמוהו ה' בעזך ישמח מלך (תה' כא ב), והנה היו"ד סימן המדבר א"ר משה הכהן, בעבור ריש וזמרָת קמוץ, כי הוא וזמרתי יה, אם אתן שנת לעיני (תה' קלב ד) קמוץ, כמו שנתי, והנה נַחְלָת שפרי עלי (שם טז ו) קמוץ כמו נחלתי (רות ד, ו) ה' מנת חלקי וכסי (שם טז) קמוץ, כמו מנתי, והנה מה יעשה במלת ומנָת המלך (דה"ב לא ג) שהוא קמוץ והוא סמוך, וככה ים המלח (במד' לד ג) יָם כנרת (שם לד יא), ומי שהשיב לומר אלה זרות הן נאמר לו שים עמהם עָזי וזמרָת יה", ולפי דעתי שמלת עזי מושכת עצמה ואחרת עמה, כמשפט לשון הקדש, כאלו כתוב, עזי וזמרת עזי יה, והטעם בעבור שהזכיר למעלה סוס ורוכבו רמה בים, הודה כי לא היה זה בגאותו ועזו, רק עזי ותפארת עזי הוא השם לבדו שהוא יה, וזהו אחד משלשה שמות העצם אשר פירשתי ושלשתם מגזרה אחת, ובעבור כי מלת אהיה ידועה בלשון הוצרך להחליף היו"ד בוי"ו בשם הנכבד, ומלת יה ידועה, ובעבור אות הגרון נפתח היו"ד, והיו"ד הנעלם הסירוהו כי יש לו סוד אחר מדרך המספר ומצאנו השם מחובר עם השם הנכבד, והוא כמו עזי וזמרת יה ה' וכבר פירשתי כי השם פעם הוא שם העצם, ופעם הוא שם תואר:


THE LORD IS MY STRENGTH AND SONG. Rabbi Solomon⁹ of blessed memory says that there is a difference between *ozzi* (my strength), which is vocalized with a furtive *kamatz*, and *uzzi*, which is vocalized with a *kubbutz*. He therefore says that the *yod* in *ozzi* (my strength) in *the Lord is my strength and song* is superfluous.¹⁰ of *ozzi* is not a first person pronominal suffix. The word *ozzi* has the same meaning as the word *oz*. It means strength. Cf. Rashi’s comment on this verse. However, Rabbi Solomon does not offer another such instance.¹¹ (enthroned) and *shokheni* (dwelt), the *yods* of both of which are superfluous. Cf. Filwarg. If this is what I.E. meant then he must have quoted Rashi from memory and erred. However, it is possible that what I.E. means is that Rashi offered no other instance of two words ending in a *yod* coming from the same root, one word vocalized with a *kubbutz,* the other with a *kamatz,* with the *yod* of one superfluous and the *yod* of the other a first person pronominal suffix. Rabbi Solomon goes on to say that *ve-zimrat* (and song) is in the construct with *Yah* (the Lord). He interprets our verse as if it read: The strength and vengeance¹² (and song) is to be rendered, and vengeance. Rashi connects *ve-zimrat* to *zamar,* which means to prune or cut. God, as it were, pruned Israel’s enemies. of the Lord became my salvation.¹³ (and he is become), which usually opens a new clause. Hence Rashi points out that *va-yehi* at times has the meaning of *hayah,* which continues a thought rather than starting a new clause. Rabbi Solomon thought that our verse is similar to *va-yehi ba-yom ha-shelishi va-yissa avraham et enav* (on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes) (Gen. 22:4).¹⁴ (lifted up), which is grammatically similar to *va-yehi,* does not begin a new clause but rather continues a thought. However, one who knows Arabic knows the difference between the two verses.¹⁵ or *va-yissa* can be used with the meaning of *hayah* or *nasa* and when it cannot, for Hebrew and Arabic are sister languages. It is neither correct Hebrew nor Arabic form to say *ozzi ve-zimrat Yah va-yehi li li-shu’ah*.¹⁶ cannot mean: became my salvation, but rather, *And He is become my salvation.* There is no difference between *ozzi* vocalized with a furtive *kamatz* and the same word vocalized with a *kubbutz*.¹⁷ and *uzzi* mean the same. For while Scripture reads, *chukki* (mine allotted)¹⁸ in *Feed me with mine allotted bread* (Prov. 30:8) it elsewhere reads, *chokkha*¹⁹ *ve-chok ba-nekha* (thy due, and thy son’s due) (Lev. 10:13). Now we find the word *ve-ozzekha* (in Thy strength) (v. 13) vocalized with a furtive *kamatz,* later on in this song and similarly in *O Lord, in Thy strength* (be-ozzekha) *the king re-joiceth* (Ps. 21:2).²⁰ is the word *oz* plus the second person pronominal suffix. Similarly, *ozzi* is the word *oz* plus the first person pronominal suffix. This contra Rashi, who maintains that the *yod* of *ozzi* is superfluous. The *yod* of *ozzi* is thus a first person suffix. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the meaning of *ve-zimrat Yah* is, the Lord is my song,²¹ (and song) is short for *ve-zimrati* (and my song). for the *resh* of *ve-zimrat* (and song) is vocalized with a *kamatz*.²² cannot be in the construct with *Yah,* for if *ve-zimrat* were in the construct with *Yah* it would be vocalized with a *pattach* rather than with a *kamatz.* Similarly,²³ the meaning of *shenat* in *I will not give sleep* (shenat) *to mine eyes* (Ps. 132:4) is, my sleep,²⁴ is short for *shenati* (my sleep). as *shenat* is vocalized with a *kamatz*.²⁵ If *shenat* were vocalized with a *pattach* it would be in the construct. Likewise, the meaning of *nachalat,* which is vocalized with a *kamatz*²⁶ in *Yea, I have a goodly heritage* (nachalat) (Ps. 16:6) is my heritage.²⁷ is short for *nachalati* (my heritage). Similarly,²⁸ the meaning of *menat,* which is vocalized with a *kamatz*²⁹ in, *O Lord, the portion* (menat) *of mine inheritance and of my cup* (Ps. 16:5), is my portion.³⁰ is short for *menati* (my portion). However, what will Rabbi Moses do with the word *menat* (portion) in *the king’s portion* (II Chron. 31:3) in which *menat* is vocalized with a *kamatz* and is in the construct. It is the same case with the word *yam* (sea) in *the salt sea* (Num. 34:3) and in *the sea* (yam) *of Chinnereth* (Num. 34:11). Should one respond that the latter are irregular, we would tell him to place *ozzi ve-zimrat Yah* among them.³¹ is occasionally in the construct it is possible to interpret *ve-zimrat* as being in the construct with *Yah.* Hence there is no need for the novel interpretation that *ve-zimrat* is short for *ve-zimrati.* I believe that the word *ozzi* (my strength) is, as is the style of the Hebrew language, to be read as if written twice.³² Our clause is to be read as if written, *ozzi, ve-zimrat ozzi*³³ is in the construct with *ozzi,* which is carried over from the first part of the verse. Yah (The Lord is my strength and the song of my strength).³⁴ The reason behind this verse is that Moses earlier mentioned, *The horse and his rider hath He thrown into the sea* (v. 4). Moses now states that this was not through his own majesty and strength. On the contrary, he confesses, my strength and the glory of my strength³⁵ to mean: the glory of my strength. is *Yah* alone who is the Lord. *Yah* is, as I have explained,³⁶ one of the three proper names of God. All three³⁷ come from one root.³⁸ Since the word *eheyeh*³⁹ is frequently employed in speech it was necessary to substitute a *vav* for a *yod* in God’s glorious name.⁴⁰ the form *YHVH* was used for God’s name rather than *YHYH,* which means he will be, and is frequently employed in speech. Filwarg suggests emending our textto read: since the word *yihyeh* is frequently employed in speech it was necessary for a *vav* to be substituted for a *yod* in God’s glorious name. The word *Yah*⁴¹ What I.E. means by *Yah* are the letters *yod heh.* is likewise known.⁴² is short for *yehi* (let there be) (Filwarg). Filwarg suggests emending to: The word *yehi* is likewise frequently employed. Its *yod* was vocalized with a *pattach* because of the guttural⁴³ and the silent *yod*⁴⁴ is short for *YHVH,* its shortened form should be *YHY* (yehi), as *YHVH* is really *YHYH* (which stands for *yehiyeh*), the *vav* being substituted for a *heh.* Hence I.E.’s comment. For I.E.’s explanation of the divine name see I.E. on Ex. 3:15. was dropped⁴⁵ was not substituted for it as in the full name of God (Filwarg). because it has another secret numerical meaning.⁴⁶ are spelled out and then computed they come to 26. The latter is the same as the numerical equivalent of the letters making up the divine name *YHVH*. *Yah* is spelled *yod heh*. *Yod heh* spelled out = 26. That is, *yod* spelled out comes to 20: *yod* (10), *vav* (6), *dalet* (4). *Heh,* which is spelled *heh* (5), *alef* (1), comes to 6. The full name of God, *Y* (10) *H* (5) *V* (6) *H* (5), comes to 26. Thus *Yah* = *YHVH.* We find *Yah* combined with God’s glorious name in *ki ozzi ve-zimrat Yah YHVH* (for God the Lord is my strength and song) (Is. 12:2). I have already explained that the name *YHVH* is at times a proper name and at times an adjective.⁴⁷

THE LORD IS A MAN OF WAR. The Lord supports those who love Him and cleave unto Him and He is a man of war to their enemies.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:3:2)


ופי' איש כעצם הדבר, והנה בכוכבים איש לא נעדר (ישעי' מ כו), ובחיות "איש אל עבר פניו ילכו" (יחז' א ט), ובמלאכים, והאיש גבריאל (דניאל ט כא), והנה איש מלחמה כמו בעל מלחמה כמו איש אמונים (משלי כ ו) איש שבו אמונים:


[MAN.] The word *ish* (man) means a being.⁵¹ as a being obviously eliminates an anthropomorphism. Scripture thus states in reference to the stars, *ish lo nedar* (not one faileth) (Is. 40:26); and in reference to the living creatures, *ish el ever panav yelekhu* (they went every one straight forward) (Ezek. 1:9); and in reference to the angels, *ve-ha-ish gavriel* (the man Gabriel) (Dan. 9:21). The meaning of *ish milchamah* (a man of war) thus is, a being who wages war. It is similar to the term *ish emunim* (a faithful man) (Prov. 20:6), the meaning of which is, a being⁵² imbued with faith.

footnotes:
⁵¹ Or an entity. I.E. makes a similar point in his comments on Gen 15:10. Translating ish
⁵² Cf. Krinsky and Weiser.

**ה' שמו.** עתה יודע שמו, כמו הקורא למי הים ה' שמו (עמוס ח ה) לבדו העושה ככה:


THE LORD IS HIS NAME. His name will now be known. Compare, *That calleth for the waters of the sea, And poureth them out upon the face of the earth; The Lord is His name* (Amos 5:8). He alone can do such a thing.⁵³

[THE RED SEA.] Yefet⁵⁵ says that *suf* in *yam suf* (the Red Sea) has the same meaning as the word *suf* (flags) in *The reeds and flags shall wither* (Is. 19:6) and the word *suf* in *and laid it in the flags* (Ex. 2:3). For reeds and rushes grow around the *yam suf*,⁵⁶ is the Sea of Flags or the Sea of Reeds. and not around other seas.⁵⁷ However, Rabbi Joshua says that *suf* is the name of a city.⁵⁸ is the Sea of Suf. It is like *yam kinneret* (the sea of Chinnereth) (Josh. 13:27).⁵⁹ 6a) because the city of Tiberias is situated on it shores.

ואמר פעמים ימינך ה', כטעם כי הנה אויביך ה' (תה' צב י), נשאו נהרות (שם צג ג) והטעם כי פעם אחרי פעם, פעמים אין להם מספר תעשה ככה שתרעץ ימינך האויב:


[THY RIGHT HAND.] The repetition of the phrase *Thy right hand, O Lord* indicates the same as the repetition of *For, lo, Thine enemies, O Lord* (Ps. 92:10)⁶⁶ and *The floods have lifted up* (Ps. 93:3).⁶⁷ It indicates time and time again. ### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:9:1)


**אמר אויב.** הוא פרעה:


THE ENEMY SAID. The reference is to Pharaoh.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:9:2)


ומלת תמלאמו קשה ורבי מרינוס אמר תהיה מלאה נפשי מהם לקחת כל ממונם כדרך בני יצאוני (ירמי' י כ) והטעם דבק עם אחלק שלל, ואחרים אומרים מגזרת אשר מלאו לבו (אסתר ז ה):


[SHALL BE SATISFIED UPON THEM.] The word *timla’emo* (shall be satisfied upon them) is difficult.⁷³ in *timla’emo* means them. Hence our verse literally reads, My soul will fill them (or satisfy them). However, this was not Pharaoh’s intention. Pharaoh’s intention was to be full of their wealth. Hence our text should have read: My soul will be full of them; i.e., I will be full of their wealth. Rabbi Merinus explains that *timla’emo nafshi* (my lust shall be satisfied upon them) means: my person⁷⁴ (my lust) may also be translated as, my person or my soul. shall be full of them;⁷⁵ means them we can interpret it to mean from them or of them. We can thus interpret *timla’emo* to mean full of them rather than will fill them. i.e., I will take all of their wealth. The term *timla’emo* is to be understood like the term *yetza’uni* (gone forth of me)⁷⁶ means me. Thus *yetza’uni* literally means: gone forth me. However, this is not the meaning of the word in the context of the verse. Its meaning is, gone forth of me. We thus see that Scripture sometimes employs a direct object suffix with the meaning of an indirect object. The same is true of *timla’emo.* in *My children are gone forth of me* (Jer. 10:20). Its meaning⁷⁷ is connected to *I will divide the spoil*.⁷⁸ Others say that *timla’emo* is used in the same sense as the word *me’lo’o* (presume)⁷⁹ doesn’t only mean to fill. It also means to presume. In our verse it is used in the latter sense. in *that durst presume in his heart* (Esth. 7:5).⁸⁰ means: will carry out my intentions. Hence *timla’emo nafshi* means: I will carry out my intentions upon them or, according to J.P.S., *my lust shall be satisfied upon them.*

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:10:1)


**נשפת ברוחך.** מגזרת נשף כי בנשף הבאת רוח שהטביע אותם:


THOU DIDST BLOW WITH THY WIND. *Nashafta* (Thou didst blow) comes from the same root as *neshef* (night). The meaning of *nashafta ve-ruchakha* (Thou didst blow with Thy wind) is: You brought a wind at night that drowned them.⁸⁴ literally means: you “nighted” with a wind.

footnotes:
⁸⁴ Thus nashafta ve-ruchakha


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:10:2)


צללו. מגזרת מצולות כמו לקול צללו שפתי (חבקוק ג טז):


THEY SANK. *Tzalelu* (they sank) comes from the same root as *metzolot* (depths). Compare, *My lips quivered* (tzalelu) *at the voice* (Hab. 3:16).⁸⁵ is the verbal form of *metzolot* (depths) then its meaning is, they sank. This being the case, what connection is there between *tzalelu* in our verse and *tzalelu* in Hab. 3:16, which means quivered? Krinsky suggests reading *metzilot* (bells, cymbals) (Zech. 14:20) rather than *metzolot* (depths). Indeed, I.E. connects *tzalelu* in Hab. 3:16 to *metziltayim* (cymbals). According to Krinsky we should read, “*Tzalelu* (they sank) comes from the same root as *metzilot* (bells, cymbals).” In other words, *tzalelu* means they tingled, and the meaning of our verse is, they tingled like lead in the mighty waters; i.e., they cried and shrieked as they drowned as if they were lead cymbals. The point is, they did not die quietly.

This refers to Edom and Moab even though Canaan is mentioned above.¹⁰⁸ *He spoke unto them in a pillar of cloud* (Ps. 99:79) is, as I have explained, similar.¹⁰⁹ refers only to Moses and Aaron even though Samuel is also mentioned in the verse. Moses repeated *Till Thy people pass* because they circled Mount Seir for many days.¹¹⁵

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:17:3)


וטעם פעלת ה', שאתה כוננת מקדש מכון לך, כי המקום הנזכר הוא כנגד המקום הנכבד מהעליון כי מקומות הארץ משתנים כנגד הכוכב העומד על ראשם, וחכמי המזלות יבינו זה:


[WHICH THOU HAST MADE.] Its meaning is: which Thou hast prepared as a place for a sanctuary for Thyself.¹¹⁹ The place mentioned lies opposite the glorious celestial place,¹²⁰ Ex. 10, “The Sanctuary below is directly opposite the Throne above.” Also see Jerusalem Talmud *Berakhot* 4:5 and Rashi. for the places on earth vary in accordance with the star that is over them.¹²¹ Those who are versed in the science that deals with the constellations will understand this.¹²²

footnotes:
¹¹⁹ The verse literally reads, a place for a dwelling Thou hast made. I.E. thus explains that the word order has to be rearranged. He then interprets the rearranged word order.
¹²⁰ See Mekhilta
¹²¹ I.E.’s interpretation of the rabbinic text quoted in the previous note. According to I.E. the greater the star, the more important the place under it (Krinsky).
¹²² The greater the star over a place, the greater the importance of the place (Weiser). I.E. believed that the Temple was under the influence of the sphere wherein all the stars are embedded. Hence its site was the most important place on earth (Krinsky).


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:17:4)


ומלת מִקּדָש כמו מִקְדָּש, וכמוהו "הִשְׁבַתָ מִטֳּהָרו" (תה' פט מה) כי הדגש בטי"ת נוסף כדגש קו"ף מִקְדָש, ובעבור שהיה בקו"ף שוא נע נרפה הדל"ת כי אין מנהג בכל המקרא דגש אחר שוא נע חוץ מגזרת שְׁתַּיִם, וכבר הזכרתי דקדוקו:


[THE SANCTUARY.] The word *mikkedash* (sanctuary)¹²³ in the *kof.* has the same meaning as *mikdash* (sanctuary).¹²⁴ in the *kof* but has one in the *dalet*. *Mikdash* is the form for sanctuary used throughout Scripture. The form *mikkedash* is found only here. The word *mittoharo* (his brightness) in *Thou hast made his brightness to cease* (Ps. 89:45) is similar, as the *dagesh* in the *tet* is superfluous, like the *dagesh* in the *kof* of *mikkedash*.¹²⁵ in *mittoharo,* like the *mem* of *mikkedash,* is a form *mem* and not a prepositional *mem.* Hence the *dagesh* following it, like the *dagesh* which follows the *mem* in *mikdash,* is superfluous. If the *mem* of *mittoharo* or *mikkedash* was a preposition then the *dagesh* following it would not be superfluous, for it would be in place of a *nun.* For the prepositional *mem* is in place of the word *min* (from). The *dalet*¹²⁶ does not receive a *dagesh*¹²⁷ as does the *dalet* of *mikdash.* because the *kof*¹²⁸ is vocalized with a mobile *sheva*.¹²⁹ A *dagesh kal* follows a *sheva nach* (quiescent *sheva*). It does not follow a mobile *sheva* (*sheva na*). Hence *mikdash,* which is vocalized with a quiescent *sheva,* has a *dagesh* in its *dalet* whereas *mikkedash,* which is vocalized with a mobile *sheva,* does not. With the exception of the form *shetayim* we do not find it to be the way of Scripture to place a *dagesh* in a word which follows a mobile *sheva.* I have already noted its grammatical uniqueness.¹³⁰ in the *Sefer Ha-Tzachot,* I.E. notes that *shetayim* is the only word in Hebrew in which a *sheva na* is followed by a word with a *dagesh.*

¹²⁴ Which does not have a dagesh
¹²⁵ The mem
¹²⁶ In mikkedash.
¹²⁷ A dagesh kal,
¹²⁸ Of mikkedash.
¹²⁹ Because of its dagesh.
¹³⁰ In his commentary on the letter nun,

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:18:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:18:2)


וטעם לעולם ועד על דרך קצרה, כי הוא לעולם ועַד עולם ואל תתמה בעבור מלת "עד" שאינה סמוכה כי כתוב שוכן עד וקדוש שמו (ישעי' נז טו) ומשפט לשון הקדש בהיות התנועה באות הבא אחר וי"ו יפתחוהו, כמו שור וכשב וָעֵז (ויקרא ז כג) ובעבור זה נפתה ועד, והנה אמר ואֹכַל מכל (ברא' כז לג) ובסוף הפסוק, הנחש השיאני וָאֹכֵל (שם ג יג) על כן אמרו לעלם ועד:


[FOR EVER AND EVER.] *Le-olam va-ed* (for ever and ever)¹³³ is an abridgment. The full form is *le-olam ve-ad*¹³⁴ is a variant of *ve-ad.* *olam* (for ever and until ever). Do not be amazed that the word *ed*¹³⁵ is not in the construct,¹³⁶ for we find, *shokhen ad*¹³⁷ a variant of *ed,* is not in the construct.*ve-kadosh shemo* (That inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy) (Is. 57:15). It is the custom of Hebrew to vocalize a *vav* with a *pattach*¹³⁸ I.E. occasionally refers to the *kamatz* as a *pattach* (Krinsky). when the syllable which follows it is accented.¹³⁹ rather than *ve-ed.* Compare, *va-ez* (or goat) in *of ox, or sheep, or goat* (Lev. 7:23). It is for this reason that *va-ed* is vocalized with a *pattach*.¹⁴⁰ Now Scripture reads, *va-okhal*¹⁴¹ *mi-kol* (I have eaten of all) (Gen. 27:33). However, at the end of a verse it reads, *ha-nachash hishi’ani va-okhel*¹⁴² In other words, the *pattach* changes to a *tzere* at the end of a sentence. Similarly, the word *ad* is vocalized *ed* at the end of a sentence. (the serpent beguiled me, and I did eat) (Gen. 3:13). Hence the statement, *le-olam va-ed*.¹⁴³

¹³⁸ That is, a kamatz.
¹³⁹ Hence the word reads va-ed
¹⁴⁰ That is, a kamatz.
¹⁴¹ Vocalized with a pattach.
¹⁴² Vocalized with a tzere.

### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:22:1)


**ויסע.** לפי דעתי כי עמוד הענן שהיה הולך לפניהם בצאתם ממצרים, ועמוד האש ככה לילה ללכת יומם ולילה (למעלה יג כא), ואחר שטבע פרעה וחילו אין להם פחד ולא יסעו בלילה, והנה לא תמצא בפ' בהעלותך שבלילה נסעו, והנה הסיעם משה על פי השם ואינם רק ששה מסעות עד הר סיני, והם פחותים מארבעים יום, והאויר טוב לא לח ולא קר, ומי שאין לו אהל יוכל לעמוד באויר ולא יזיקנו, ובבואם אל מדבר סיני עשו כולם סוכות כי שם יתעכבו עד שיעשו המשכן כי בעבור זה הוציא עצי שטים ממצרים כאשר אפרש, ולהיות זכר לסוכות שעשו שם היה חג הסוכות, כי הכתוב אמר כי בסכות הושבתי את בנ"י (ויקרא כג מג) ואיך ישבו בעננים? כי הסכות אינם דומים לעננים, ועוד אפרש למה חג הסוכות בחדש השביעי, וכאשר נעשה המשכן ירד השם בעמוד ענן עליו כי כן כתוב ואש תהיה לילה בו (למטה מ לח), ובנסוע הענן יסעו בני ישראל, ובעבור זה כתוב ובעמוד ענן אתה הולך לפניהם יומם (במד' יד יד), והנה שנים עמודים הם שמתחלפים על המשכן, ואם קבלה ששבעה ענני כבוד היו נניח סברתינו ונסמוך על הקבלה:


AND MOSES LED. I believe that the pillar of cloud, and likewise the pillar of fire, that went before the people when they left Egypt was to ensure that Israel was able to *go by day and by night* (Ex. 13:21). After Pharaoh and his hosts drowned, Israel was no longer frightened and did not travel at night.¹⁴⁹ Indeed, we do not find it recorded in the Torah portion *Be-Halotekha*¹⁵⁰ that Israel journeyed at night. Behold, Moses now led the people according to God’s command.¹⁵¹ There are only six journeys from the Red Sea until Mount Sinai¹⁵² lasting less than forty days.¹⁵³ The air¹⁵⁴ is then good. It is neither humid nor cold. He who does not have a tent can live outdoors¹⁵⁵ without harm. When Israel came to the wilderness of Sinai they all erected booths,¹⁵⁶ as they camped there for about year. Moses informed them that they would tarry there until they constructed the Tabernacle. It was for this reason that, as I will explain,¹⁵⁷ Israel brought out acacia wood from Egypt. The festival of booths was established in commemoration of the booths that Israel made there, for Scripture states, *that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt* (Lev. 23:43). How can one maintain that Israel dwelt in clouds?¹⁵⁸ 34:4. I.E. disagrees. For the booths do not resemble clouds.¹⁵⁹ I will yet explain why the festival of Sukkot is observed in the seventh month.¹⁶⁰ When the Tabernacle was erected God descended upon it in a pillar of cloud, as it is clearly written, *and there was fire therein by night* (Ex. 40:38). When the cloud journeyed the children of Israel went onward (Ex. 40:36). It is because of this that Scripture reads, *and thou goest before them, in a pillar of cloud by day* (Num. 14:14). There were thus two interchanging pillars¹⁶¹ over the Tabernacle. If the statement to the effect that there were seven interchanging pillars over the Tabernacle¹⁶² 1. is based on tradition, then we will rely on tradition and set aside our own opinions.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:22:2)


אל מדבר שור. הוא מדבר איתם בעצמו אולי שתי ערים היו במדבר שנקראו כן או יש למדבר שני שמות, והעד שאמר וילכו שלשת ימים במדבר הוא מדבר שור, על כן בהודעה נפתח בי"ת במדבר: ולא מצאו מים:


INTO THE WILDERNESS OF SHUR. This is the very wilderness of Etham.¹⁶³ (Israel) *passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness; and they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham, and pitched in Marah.* See I.E.’s comments on verse 23. Perhaps there were two cities in the wilderness that were so called.¹⁶⁴ Or the wilderness had two names.¹⁶⁵ *And they went three days in the wilderness,* the reference being to the wilderness of Shur, is proof of this.¹⁶⁶ (of Shur) is parallel to *and they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham* (Num. 33:8). Therefore to indicate this¹⁶⁷ the *bet* of *ba-midbar* (in the wilderness), which precedes *and found no water,* was vocalized for emphasis with a *pattach*.¹⁶⁸ 38.

### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:23:1)


**ויבאו מרתה.** וכתוב ויסעו מים סוף (במד' לג יא) כמו ויסע משה את ישראל מים סוף וילכו דרך שלשת ימים במדבר איתם ויחנו במרה (שם שם ה):


AND WHEN THEY CAME TO MARAH. It is elsewhere written, *And they journeyed from the Red Sea* (Num. 33:11). The latter is similar to *And Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea*,¹⁶⁹ (*and they went out into the wilderness of Shur and came to Marah*) (v. 22). We similarly find, *and they went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham, and pitched in Marah* (Num. 33:8).¹⁷⁰

footnotes:
¹⁶⁹ In other words, Num. 33:11 and Ex. 15:22 refer to the same event.
¹⁷⁰ Thus the wilderness of Shur is to be identified with the wilderness of Etham.

### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:24:1)


**וילנו.** מבנין נפעל, כמו וְיִכֹּנו (משלי טז ג) מן נכונו (שם יט כט) מהפעלים השניים או מעלומי העין, ואילו היה מבעלי הנו"ן היה על משקל וַיִגָשׁו:


AND THE PEOPLE MURMURED. *Va-yillonu* (murmured) is a *nifal.* It is similar to *ve-yikkonu* (shall be established)¹⁷⁴ and is similarly vocalized. in *And thy thoughts shall be established* (Prov. 16:3), which comes from the same root as *nakhonu* (prepared) (Prov. 19:29).¹⁷⁵ Similarly, the root of *va-yillonu* is *lamed, vav, nun.* It comes from a double root¹⁷⁶ However, the *vav* is usually dropped in the conjugation. Hence it appears to have only two letters (Weiser, Krinsky). or from a root in which the middle letter is missing.¹⁷⁷ If it came from a root which begins with a *nun*¹⁷⁸ I.E. makes this point because there is a *dagesh* in the *lamed.* Now one might argue that the *dagesh* in the *lamed* is not the *dagesh* of the *nifal* conjugation but rather a *dagesh* that compensates for a missing *nun,* as in *va-yippelu* from the root *nun, peh, lamed.* it would have followed the paradigm of *va-yiggashu* (came near) (Gen. 45:4).¹⁷⁹ However, it is not. Hence it has to be taken as an *ayin vav* in the *nifal.*

footnotes:
¹⁷⁴ Which is a nifal
¹⁷⁵ The root of which is kaf, vav, nun.
¹⁷⁶ A two-letter root. That is, its root is lamed, vav, nun.
¹⁷⁷ That is, its root may be described as a double root or as a root in which the middle letter is dropped.
¹⁷⁸ Nun, lamed, nun.
¹⁷⁹ That is, it would have been conjugated as a root whose first letter is a nun.

AND HE CRIED UNTO THE LORD; AND THE LORD SHOWED HIM A TREE. We do not know what type of tree this was.¹⁸⁰ 1; *Yalkut Shimoni* on Ex. 15:25. What happened can only be described as a miracle. וטעם ושב נסהו. על דרך כי מנסה ה' אלהיכם אתכם לדעת הישכם אוהבים (דבר' יג ד), וככה ויענך וירעיבך (שם ה ג) ולמען נסותך להטיבך באחריתך (שם שם טז), להטיב הסובלים שלא הלינו על משה:


[AND THERE HE PROVED THEM.] This is to be understood in the manner of *for the Lord your God putteth you to proof, to know whether ye do love the Lord your God with all you heart and with all your soul* (Deut. 13:4). Scripture similarly states, *And He afflicted thee,*¹⁸⁵ *and suffered thee to hunger* (Deut. 8:3); *and that He might prove thee, to do thee good at thy latter end* (Deut. 8:16),¹⁸⁶ that is, to do good to those who did not murmur against Moses.¹⁸⁷

### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:26:1)


**ויאמר אם שמוע תשמע.** כבר הזכרתי כי כל שמיעה שאחריה למ"ד או בי"ת אין פי' לשמוע הדבר רק להבין טעם הענין הנושא הדבר והנה זו השמיעה שיבין מה מצוה לעשות:


AND HE SAID: IF THOU WILT DILIGENTLY HEARKEN. I have already noted that when the word *shema* (hearken) is followed by a *lamed*¹⁸⁸ (to the voice of) follows *shamo’a tishma* (diligently hearken). or a *bet* it does not mean to hear the words being spoken but rather to understand the subject which is being verbalized. *Shema* in our verse thus means to understand what the Lord commands us to do.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:26:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:26:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:26:5)


וטעם המחלה. יש לך לזכור כי בעיניך ראית המחלה והנגעים והמכות אשר שמתי במצרים בעבור שמרדו בי ואם תשמע חקי תמלט מהם, שלא אעשה לך כאשר עשיתי להם, ועוד כי אני ה' אהיה רופאיך מכל מחלה שגזרתי להיותם על הארץ, אין לך צורך לרופא, כאשר רפאתי המים המרים שאין יכולת ברופאים לרפאם, והנה דבר מרה הפך המכה הראשונה כי מימי היו מתוקים ולא יכלו לשתות מהם, וכאן המים המרים שבו מתוקים, והנה השם עשה הדבר והפכו על יש לך להשמר שלא תמר בו, ולאהוב אותו כי הוא ייטיב לך:


[NONE OF THE DISEASES.] Its meaning is, the diseases you should remember. For you saw with your own eyes the diseases, the strokes, and the plagues which I put upon the Egyptians because they rebelled against Me. Now if you will hearken to My statutes you will be saved from these plagues, for I will not do to you what I did to them. Additionally, you have no need of a physician for I am the Lord that healeth thee from all disease which I have decreed to be upon the earth. I will heal you as I healed the bitter waters which no physician has the ability to heal. Behold, what happened at Marah was the opposite of what occurred when the first plague struck, for the waters of the Nile were sweet but the Egyptians could not drink from them.¹⁹¹ However, here¹⁹² the bitter waters turned sweet. You should therefore love the Lord and keep yourself from rebelling against Him, for He will do good for you.

¹⁹² At Marah.



### Verse 27

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 15:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/15:27:1)


**ויבאו.** אמר הגאון שבעים מיני תמרים היו ואחרים הוסיפו לכל שבט ושבט ואחרים אמרו לכל איש ואיש, ואין צורך לדברים האלה, כי המעינות שהיו י"ב, ושבעים תמרים לא נבראו עתה בשביל ישראל, ואין זה זמן בשול תמרים, ולפי דעתי כי ישראל לא ישבו במרה רק יום אחד, והתעכבו באלים כמו כ' יום על כן אמר הכתוב, ויחנו שם על המים על כן אמר בפסוק הבא אחריו, כי בחמשה עשר יום לחדש השני נסעו מאלים והנה בט"ו ימים חנו בד' מקומות, ואלה הם מדבר סיני ודפקה, ואלוש, ורפידים, כי תחילת החדש השלישי באו מדבר סיני, והזכיר התמרים להודיע כי המים מתוקים הפך מי מרה, כי התמרים לא יצליחו בארץ שמימיה מרים:


AND THEY CAME TO ELIM. Saadiah Gaon says there were seventy species of palm trees there.¹⁹³ Others added, for each and every tribe.¹⁹⁴ Others said, for each and every person.¹⁹⁵ However, there is no need for these interpretations, for the springs of water, of which there were twelve, and the seventy palm trees did not come into being now because of Israel.¹⁹⁶ Additionally, this was not the time for the ripening of palms.¹⁹⁷ I believe that Israel tarried in Marah for only one day¹⁹⁸ and that they stayed in Elim for about twenty days.¹⁹⁹ Scripture therefore says, *and they encamped there by the waters*.²⁰⁰ The next verse therefore informs us that Israel journeyed from Elim on the fifteenth day of the second month.²⁰¹ Now Israel camped in the following four places²⁰² in fifteen days:²⁰³ the wilderness of Sinai,²⁰⁴ Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, for they came to the desert of Sinai at the beginning of the third month.²⁰⁵ Scripture mentions the palm trees to let us know that contrary to the waters of Marah the waters here were sweet, for palm trees cannot flourish in a land of bitter waters.²⁰⁶

¹⁹⁶ There is thus no reason to assume that Israel found a forest of palm trees in the wilderness vast enough to feed a large nation.
¹⁹⁷ In other words, there are no dates on the palm trees in the month of Iyyar. Thus Scripture does not imply that Israel ate from the palm trees. Hence there is no reason to exaggerate their number.

¹⁹⁹ Israel journeyed from Elim on the 15th of Iyyar (16:1). There are 24 days from the 21st of Nisan, when Israel crossed the Red Sea, to the 15th of Iyyar. Israel journeyed for three days without water (v. 22) and spent one day at Marah. Hence they spent about 20 days at Elim.
²⁰⁰ To emphasize that their main camp at this time was at Elim.

## Chapter 16


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:1:1)


**ויסעו.** אמר הגאון רב סעדיה, כי טעם להזכיר בחמשה עשר לחדש השני, להודיע כי יום חמישי בשבוע יצאו ישראל ממצרים, והנה יום ראשון לחדש ניסן היה יום חמישי, ואייר יום ששי ושבת והנה ביום השבת באו אל מדבר סין והתרעמו בחנותם ואמר להם משה כי בערב תאכלו בשר, ובבקר ירד המן, והנה ראוי להיותו יום ראשון בעבור שאמר והיה ביום הששי (פ' ה), כי היה יום ששי והיה ששי לירידת המן, ומה שאמר הגאון נקבלהו בעבור הקבלה ולא בעבור פירושו, כי מי הגיד לו כי ממחרת בואם אל מדבר סין ירד המן, אולי עמדו שם ארבעה ימים או יותר, והחל המן לרדת ביום ראשון כי מיום רדתו נחל לספור, כי כל האומות סומכין על ישראל במספר הזה והנה הערלים קראו שמות ימות השבוע על שמות המשרתים ויום שבת לא כן ובלשון ערבי קראו חמשה ימים על דרך המספר ויום ששי אלגומ"ע על שם חבורם כי הוא להם היום הנכבד בשבוע, ויום שבת קראו אותו סב"ת, כי השי"ן והסמ"ך מתחלפים בכתיבתם, ואלה מישראל למדו, כי הנה אנשי הודו שאינם מודים במעשה בראשית תחלת ימי השבוע להם יום רביעי, בעבור כי כוכב היום הוא כוכב חמה ויש לו שלטון עליהם כפי דבריהם:


AND THEY TOOK THEIR JOURNEY. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the reason Scripture mentions *the fifteenth day of the second month* is to inform us that Israel left Egypt on the fifth day of the week.¹ Now, the first day of Nisan fell on a Thursday² and Iyyar on a Friday and on a Sabbath.³ (new moon) Iyyar fell on Friday and Saturday, as it does whenever the 15th of Nisan falls on a Thursday. Friday was the 30th of Nisan and Saturday the first day of Iyyar. Israel came to the wilderness of Sin⁴ on a Sabbath⁵ and complained⁶ upon camping. Moses then told them that they would eat meat at even⁷ and that manna would come down in the morning.⁸ Now it is logical to assume that the manna first came down on a Sunday because Scripture states, *And it shall come to pass on the sixth day* (v. 5), the reference being to the sixth day of the week and the sixth day from the day on which the manna began to descend.⁹ (v. 5) it means: and it shall come to pass on the sixth day from the day that the manna begins to fall. For after creation, with the exception of the Sabbath, Scripture does not refer to days of the week (Filwarg). It so happened that the sixth day fell on a Friday (see v. 23). We will accept that which the Gaon says because of tradition,¹⁰ 87b. not because of his explanation, for who told the Gaon that the manna came down on the morning following the coming of the Israelites to the wilderness of Sin?¹¹ The Israelites may have camped there for four or more days¹² but the manna started to come down on Sunday. The latter is so because we start the count¹³ from the day that the manna began to fall,¹⁴ for all the nations rely on Israel with regard to this numeration.¹⁵ Observe, the Christians named the days of the week after the stars.¹⁶ However, they did not do the same with the Sabbath day. The first five days of the week in Arabic are numbered. The sixth day is called *al juma*¹⁷ because it is the most honored day of the week for the Arabs and they congregate on this day. The Arabs refer to the day of *shabbat* as *sabbat* because the *shin* and *samekh* interchange in their script. They learned this¹⁸ from the Israelites. Behold, the natives of India, who do not have the belief of six days of creation, begin the week on Wednesday because the sun is the star of that day and according to their beliefs it rules over them.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:2:1)


**וילונו.** במי מרה הלינו על משה לבדו, כי הוא לבדו הסיעם וכל ישראל לא התרעמו רק קצתם, על כן כתוב, וילונו העם (למעלה טו כד) ועתה במדבר סין וילונו כל עדת ישראל על משה ועל אהרן כי שניהם הוציאום, ובמרה התרעמו על המים ועתה מתרעמים על הבשר והלחם שכבר אכלו רוב מקניהם, וקול גדול כמוהו לא ימצאו לחם לקנות כי אם ביוקר, כי שלשים יום היה להם מיום צאתם:


AND THE WHOLE CONGREGATION OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL MURMURED. The Israelites murmured only against Moses at the waters of Marah (Ex. 15:23)¹⁹ because it was he alone who led Israel onward.²⁰ Only a part of Israel and not the whole nation complained.²¹ Scripture therefore reads, *And the people*²² *murmured against Moses* (Ex. 15:24). However, in the wilderness of Sin we find that Scripture states, *And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron* because both of them had brought them out of the land of Egypt. In Marah they complained because of the water. However, they now complained about a lack of bread and meat because they had already consumed most of their cattle, for thirty days had passed since they left Egypt. A congregation as large as Israel could only buy food at very great expense.²³

**ויאמר.** טעם כי ה' הוציא אתכם בעבור שאמרתם כי הוצאתם אותנו והנה שני אותות נעשה לכם שתדעו כי הוא הוציא אתכם, האחד בערב זה היום, ושני למחרתו בבקר. והיה ראוי שיהיה ערב ובקר וידעתם, כי איננו דבק ובקר עם וראיתם את כבוד ה', כי ביום עצמו ראו את הכבוד כאשר יפרש:


AND MOSES AND AARON SAID. Moses and Aaron said, *then shall ye know that the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt* because the Israelites charged, *for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness* (v. 3). They answered, “Observe, we will perform two signs for you, one at the evening of this very day²⁵ and one on the morning of the morrow²⁶ so that you will know that *the Lord hath brought you out from the land of Egypt*.” Scripture should have read: at even and in the morning ye shall know²⁷ because *and in the morning*²⁸ is not connected to *then ye shall see the glory of the Lord*.²⁹ For as Scripture goes on to say,³⁰ Israel saw God’s glory on that very day.

**שכבת הטל.** כמו, ונבלי שמים מי ישכיב (איוב לח לז) טעם ירידה ובמקום אחר כתוב וברדת הטל (במד' יא ט), ירקב שם חוי שאמר, כי המן הוא הנקרא בלשון פרסי תרנגבי"ן, ובלשון ערבי מ"ן ובלשון לע"ז מנ"א, כי קושיות רבות עמדו עליו, האחת כי איננו יורד היום במדבר סיני, כי ההר ידוע, ואני ראיתי זה הדומה למן במלכות אלצכי"ר והוא יורד בניסן ובאייר ולא בחדשים אחרים, ועוד אם תשימהו לשמש לא ימס, ועוד כי בלילה לא יבאש, ועוד כי איננו חזק, ואין צורך שידוכנו אדם במדוכה שיעשה ממנו עוגות, ועוד כאשר יושם בלשון ימס, ועוד כי איננו משביע שיולד דם טוב רק הוא נכנס ברפואות, ועוד כי ביום הששי היה יורד משנה ועוד כי לא היה יורד בשבת, ועוד כי ירד לכל מקום שיחנו ועוד כי עבר עמהם את הירדן, ולא שבת עד חצי ניסן על דרך הפשט:


A LAYER OF DEW. *Shikhvat* (a layer) is similar to *yashkiv* (bring down) in *Or who can bring down* (yashkiv) *the bottles of heaven* (Job 38:37).⁴⁷ It means a descent.⁴⁸ (a layer of dew) means a dew fall. Scripture elsewhere writes, *u-veredet ha-tal* (And when the dew descended)⁴⁹ (Num. 11:9). May the name of Chivi⁵⁰ rot for saying that the manna is to be identified with what is known in the Persian tongue as *tarnagbin,* in Arabic as *man,* and in the vernacular as manna. There are many questions raised against him. First of all, no manna falls today in the wilderness of Sinai,⁵¹ for we know the location of the mountain.⁵² Now I have seen that which resembles manna in the kingdom of Al tzakir,⁵³ and it only comes down in Nisan and Iyyar and in no other months.⁵⁴ Additionally, if you place it in the sun it does not melt.⁵⁵ Furthermore, it does not rot in the evening.⁵⁶ Moreover, it is not very hard and one does not have to grind it in a pestle⁵⁷ if one wants to make cakes out of it. Furthermore, it melts when placed upon the tongue.⁵⁸ In addition, it does not satisfy⁵⁹ because it does not produce good blood. It is only used as a medical ingredient.⁶⁰ Furthermore, a double portion of manna came down on Friday.⁶¹ Moreover, the manna did not come down on the Sabbath. Furthermore, the manna came down wherever Israel camped.⁶² In addition, the manna crossed over the Jordan with the Israelites and did not cease to descend, according to the plain meaning of Scripture, until half the month of Nisan,⁶³ had passed.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:14:1

**ותעל.** הטעם שנפסקה כמו, אז חללת יצועי עלה (ברא' מט ד) כי הטעם מעת שחללת, יצועי נסתלק מעלי ונפסק וכמוהו "אֹמַר אלי אל תעלי בחצי ימי" (תה' קב כד) והטל היה יורד בתחלה לטהר הארץ ובהסתלק הטל יורד המן וכן כתוב, וברדת הטל על המחנה לילה ירד המן עליו (במד' יא ט):


AND WHEN THE LAYER OF DEW WAS GONE UP. The meaning of *va-ta’al* (was gone up)⁶⁴ (to go up). is ceased.⁶⁵ is, went up, hence I.E.’s comment. It is similar to *alah* (went up) in *Then defiledst thou it* — *my couch went up* (alah) (Gen. 49:4).⁶⁶ The meaning of the latter verse is: from the time that you defiled my couch it was removed from me and ceased to function.⁶⁷ *Ta’aleni* (take me away)⁶⁸ in *O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days* (Ps. 102:25) is similar. The dew came down first to clean the earth. When the dew was gone the manna descended. The latter⁶⁹ is clearly written,⁷⁰ viz., *And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell upon it* (Num. 11:9).

**דק מחוספס.** כמו עגול ואין לו חבר, והאומר שהוא כמו מחשוף (ברא' ל לז) שהוא בשי"ן אינו נכון כי משפט הלשון שיכפלו הפ"א והעי"ן כמו יפיפית (תה' מה ג) או העי"ן והלמ"ד, כמו, ירקרק (ויקרא יג מט) או הלמ"ד לבדה כמו סגריר (משלי כז טו) רק העי"ן לבדו לא מצאנו כי אם בעלומי הה"א, כמו הגיגי (תה' ה ב) כי אחר שחסר הה"א נראה הגימ"ל כלמ"ד פעל, על כן כפלוהו רק באותיות נראות לא מצאנו העי"ן כפול:


A FINE, SCALE-LIKE THING. *Mechuspas* (scale-like thing) means round shaped. It has no cognate.⁷¹ The one who says⁷² means uncovered; that is, the manna was similar to a peeled seed (Ralbag). that *mechuspas* is similar to *machsof* (uncovering) (Gen. 30:37),⁷³ which is spelled with a *sin*,⁷⁴ is spelled with a *samekh.* However, the latter presents no problem, for the *sin* and the *samekh* interchange. is incorrect. For it is the manner of Hebrew to double the first and second root letters,⁷⁵ as in the word *yafyafita* (thou art fairer)⁷⁶, *feh, heh.* (Ps. 45:3), or to double the second and third stem letters, as in the word *yerakrak* (greenish)⁷⁷ (Lev. 13:49), or to double only the third stem letter, as in *sagrir* (a very rainy day)⁷⁸ (Prov. 27:15). However, we never find the second root letter⁷⁹ doubled⁸⁰ came from the same root as *machsof,* for the root of *machsof* is *chet, sin, feh.* except for instances when the *heh*⁸¹ is silent, as in *hagigi* (my meditation)⁸² (Ps. 5:2) in which the *gimel* appears to be a third root letter after the *heh* is dropped.⁸³ it appears to come from the root *heh, gimel, gimel,* not *heh, gimel, heh* with the *gimel* doubled. Hence it was doubled. However, we do not find the middle root letters to be doubled in words where all root letters are sounded.⁸⁴ Hence *mechuspas* cannot be derived from that root.

**ויראו.** אמר רבינו שלמה כי בלשון ישמעאל תרגום מה הוא מן הוא והמגיד לו ככה לא דבר נכון כי תרגום מה הוא בלשון ישמעאל מה הוי, רק מן הוא תרגומו מי היא כי איננו נופל מן בלשונם כי אם על אדם, כי פי' מן הוא מגזרת, אשר מנה את מאכלכם (דניאל א, י):


AND WHEN THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SAW IT. Rabbi Solomon⁸⁵ says that the meaning of *man hu* (what is it) in Arabic is, *what is it*? However, someone misinformed him, because the Arabic phrase for “what is it” is *mah huwi,* as the term *man* is used in Arabic exclusively in reference to people. The way to explain *man* is to note that it comes from the same root as *minnah* (appointed) in *who hath appointed your food and your drink* (Dan. 1:10).⁸⁶ means: it is something appointed (for us); it is a food allotment set aside for us.

[AND MOSES SAID UNTO THEM.] Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that we know that the Torah is not written in chronological order. There are many similar instances.⁸⁸ introduces a pluperfect. See I.E. on Gen. 1:9. Indeed, we find that Scripture states in this very portion, *and it bred worms and rotted,* the meaning of which is: and it bred worms and had previously rotted.⁸⁹ Indeed, Scripture states, *and it did not rot, neither was there any worm in it* (v. 24).⁹⁰ Scripture delayed reporting the words of Moses⁹¹ is out of sequence. See note 87. because it had to elaborate and go on to say, *This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded,* etc. (v. 16).⁹²

When one of the *tavs*¹¹⁶ was dropped the *bet* was vocalized with a *kamatz*¹¹⁷ I.E. refers to the *kamatz* as a *pattach* a number of times in his commentary on Exodus. See I.E. on Ex. 15:18. to indicate that the word is feminine. It is the same, as I will explain, with the word *achat* (one).¹¹⁸ 4.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:25:1)


**ויאמר.** רבים חסרי אמונה השתבשו בעבור זה הפסוק ואמרו כי חייב אדם לשמור יום השבת והלילה הבא אחריו, כי משה אמר כי שבת היום לה', ולא הלילה שעבר, גם אמר מחר ופירשו "ויהי ערב ויהי בקר" (ברא' א ה) כרצונם, כי יום ראשון לא השלים עד בקר יום שני ולא דברו נכונה, כי משה לא דבר לישראל רק כנגד מנהגם כאשר הזכרתי לך, כי מנהג ארצות ערלים אינם כמנהג ארץ ישראל במאכלם ובמלבושם ובנינם וענינם, כי אין מנהג שיאפה אדם או יבשל בקיץ ובחורף ולא לעשות מלאכה רק ביום על כן אמר מחר, ועתה שים לבך להבין טפשות המפרשים ויהי ערב ויהי בקר אשר הזכרתי, כי הכתוב אומר ויקרא אלהים לאור יום (ברא' א ה) והוא מעת זרוח השמש עד שקעו, ולחשך קרא לילה (שם) מעת שקוע השמש עד זרחו, והנה הלילה הפך היום, כמו שחשך הפך אור, אם כן איך יקרא מעת ערב שהוא עריבת השמש עד בקר יום והנה הוא לילה, והנה כתוב על אלה לילה ליום ישימו, ודע כי היום בלשון הקדש על שני דרכים, האחת כאשר הזכרתי, כל זמן שאור השמש עומד על הארץ כנגד כל מקום, על כן כתוב לילה ויום (אסתר ד טז) ויום ולילה (ברא' ח כב) שלשה ימים ושלשה לילות (יונה ב א), כי אילו היתה מדת היום כוללת עמו לילה, למה יזכיר לילה, וזה לא יתכן בראייה גמורה מחכמת הדבור, ששם דבר יהיה כולל שני דברים שהאחד הפך כנגדו והדרך השנית שמלת יום נופל על זמן קרוב או רחוק, ביום הכותי כל בכור (במד' ג יג) אתה עובר היום (דבר' ט א) אל ארץ אחרת כיום הזה (שם כט כז), והיה ביום ההוא (ישעי' ז כא) ורבים ככה והנה נניח כל אלה הדברים ונבקש יום התורה כאשר אמרתי כי שנותינו אינם קבועים במהלך החמה והלבנה רק בקביעות בית דין, והנה מצינו שאמר שבעת ימים מצות תאכלו (למעלה יב טו) ופירש כי זה המספר מארבעה עשר לחדש בערב (שם שם יח), וכתוב, מערב עד ערב תשבתו שבתכם (ויקרא כג לב) ועוד מי שאירע לו קרי בלילה או ביום, כי כן כתוב מקרה לילה (דבר' כג יא), והנה לא יטהר עד בא השמש שהוא סוף היום הראשון, ואלו כן שהוא עד בקר יום שני, היה ראוי שירחץ בבקר, כי הם אומרים כי היום והלילה שהוא אחריו יקרא יום, הנה יהיה חצי היום טמא וחציו טהור, ואשר יארע לו קרי בתחלת הלילה, חצי היום שעבר טמא, גם חצי יום הבא ואלה דברי התועים, וכבר פירשתי ויהי ערב ויהי בקר במקומו:


AND MOSES SAID. Many lacking in faith erred because of this verse and said that a person is obligated to keep the Sabbath day plus the night which follows it,¹²⁵ I.E. composed his *Sefer Ha-Shabbat* to refute this view. See Introduction to Vol. 1, p. XIX. because Moses said, *for to-day* and not the night before *is a sabbath unto the Lord.* Additionally, Moses said, *Tomorrow is a solemn rest* (v. 23).¹²⁶ They interpreted, in accordance with their view, *And there was evening and there was morning one day* (Gen. 1:5) to mean that the first day was not finished until the morning of the second day.¹²⁷ However, they spoke incorrectly. As I have already made mention to you, Moses spoke to Israel only in accordance with their practice. Now the manner of the land of the uncircumcised¹²⁸ with regard to their food, their dress, their buildings, and affairs is not the same as that of the Land of Israel. It is the practice in the Land of Israel that no one bakes, cooks, or does any other work, both in summer or winter, at any time but during the day.¹²⁹ Hence Moses said, *Tomorrow is a solemn rest*.¹³⁰ Now pay close attention to understand the stupidity of those who explain *and there was evening and there was morning* in the manner which I noted above. For Scripture says, *And God called the light day* (Gen. 1:8), the reference being from the time that the sun rises until the time that it sets; *and to the darkness He called night,* the reference being from the time that the sun sets until the time that it rises. The night is thus the opposite of day, as the darkness is the opposite of the light. This being the case, how can Scripture refer to the evening, which commences at the time that the sun sets and lasts until the morning, as “day” when it is then night? Behold, concerning such people Scripture states, *They change the night into day* (Job 17:12). Now note that the word day is used in Hebrew in two ways. I have already mentioned one of them, viz., as long as the light of the sun is over any place on the earth. Therefore Scripture states, *three days, night and day* (Esth. 4:16) and, *and night and day* (Gen. 8:22). Now if the measure of the day includes the night in it, why mention night?¹³¹ It is also incorrect from the point of view of the science of linguistics¹³² for a noun to refer to two things which are the opposite of each other.¹³³ The word day is used secondarily in the sense of close or far-off time, as in *on the day that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt* (Num. 3:13); *thou art to pass over the Jordan this day* (Deut. 9:1); *and cast them into another land, as it is this day* (Deut. 29:27); *And it shall come to pass in that day* (Is. 7:21). There are many other similar instances. Now let us leave all these things aside and seek, as I have said, only after the day of the Torah,¹³⁴ for our years are not established according to the movement of the sun and moon but rather according to what the Bet Din decrees.¹³⁵ Now we find that Scripture states, *Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread* (Ex. 12:15). Scripture then goes on to explain that this number¹³⁶ begins on the evening of the fourteenth of the first month (Ex. 12:18). Scripture also states, *from even unto even, shall ye keep your sabbath* (Lev. 23:32).¹³⁷ Furthermore, a man who has a seminal emission during the night or day, for it is so written, viz., *that which chanceth him by night* (Deut. 23:11), does not become “clean” until sunset, which is the end of the first day.¹³⁸ Now if it were so,¹³⁹ namely, that the first day ends on the morning of the next day,¹⁴⁰ then it is only fit for the one who experienced an emission to immerse himself in the morning.¹⁴¹ For if we say that the day and the night which follows it make up one day then the one who experienced an emission¹⁴² will be “unclean” for half a day¹⁴³ and clean for half a day.¹⁴⁴ And one who experienced an emission at the beginning of the night will be unclean for half of a day that passed¹⁴⁵ and also for half of the coming day.¹⁴⁶ This is the opinion of those who err.¹⁴⁷ I have already explained to you the meaning of *and there was evening and there was morning* (Gen. 1:5) in its place.¹⁴⁸ not as meaning that the day came to a close at morning, but rather as meaning that the evening and the morning of the first day came.

**ויאמר.** עתה פירש מה יעשו בעודף המונח וגלה להם סודו כי לא ימצאוהו היום כי לא ירד:


AND MOSES SAID. Moses now explained to them what they should do with the additional manna which was laid up, and he revealed to them its secret, that they would not find it this day because it did not come down.

SIX DAYS SHALL YE GATHER IT. It shall always be as it is now for as long as you are in the wilderness; that is, ye shall gather it for six days but on the seventh no manna shall come down.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:28:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:28:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/16:28:3)


וטעם, ותורתי שהשם הורה להם טעם השבת על כן לקטו לחם משנה, וטעם לשון רבים, מצותי ותורתי כי כל המצוות והתורות הם אמת בלי ספק כמשמעם, ויש להם סודות בדברי הנשמה ולא יבינום רק המשכילים, ועל כן כל מצוה היא שתים:


[MY LAWS.]¹⁵³ For God taught them the reason for the Sabbath.¹⁵⁴ to mean my teachings, that is, my teachings concerning the Sabbath, namely, that it is God’s day and manna would not fall on it. They therefore gathered twice as much bread on the sixth day. There is a reason why Scripture employs the plural, namely, *My commandments and My laws*.¹⁵⁵ All the commandments and laws are, beyond any doubt, to be taken literally. However, they have secret meanings pertaining to the soul that only the enlightened can understand. Thus every commandment has two meanings.¹⁵⁶

footnotes:
¹⁵³ Hebrew, torotai.
¹⁵⁴ I.E. explains torotai
¹⁵⁵ When in reality one command and one teaching were violated.
¹⁵⁶ Thus when one violates a commandment one disregards its obvious meaning plus its secret meaning, hence the use of the plural commandments and laws in our verse.



### Verse 29

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 16:29:1

**ראו.** הטעם ראו זה המופת שיתן לכם השם, שיתברר לכם, כי הוא צוה שתשבתו כאשר שבת במעשה בראשית על כן הוא נותן שירד המן היום כפלים ממנהגו בכל יום:


SEE. Its meaning is: see the wonder that the Lord will perform for you so that it shall become clear to you that God commanded you to rest as He rested when He made all things in the beginning. God is therefore permitting twice as much manna to come down today as normally comes down every day.
