**ועשית.** ראיתי ספרים שבדקום חכמי טבריה ונשבעו חמשה עשר מזקניהם ששלש פעמים הסתכלו כל מלה וכל נקודה, וכל מלא וכל חסר והנה כתיב יו"ד במלת **תיעשה** ולא מצאתי ככה בספרי ספרד וצרפת ומעבר לים, והקדמונים דרשו, כי תוספת היו"ד רמז לעשרה מנורות שיעשה שלמה והכלל אם יש שם יו"ד היא מלה זרה ובדרש כי נעשית מאליה והטעם שכל רואיה היו תמהים איך יכול אדם לעשותה, כי הנה כתוב ויעש מנורת, כן עשה את המנורה (במד' ח ד) והנה על מחבת בשמן תֵעָשֶׂה מורבכת תביאנה (ויקרא ו יד), והנה מקשה כמו הכתוב בכרובים:


AND THOU SHALT MAKE A CANDLESTICK. I have seen copies of Scripture which the wise men of Tiberias have examined. Behold, I found the word *te’aseh* (be made) spelled with a *yod*.²⁴² Fifteen of their wise men²⁴³). The Ben Asher and Ben Naphtali families were active there. In fact, Maimonides recommended the Torah Scroll written by Aaron ben Asher in 930 C.E. as a model for all Torah scrolls. swore that they checked every word, vowel, full and deficient spelling, three times. I did not find this to be the case with the books of Scripture in Spain, France, and on the other side of the sea.²⁴⁴ Our sages said that the additional *yod* in *te’aseh* alludes to the ten²⁴⁵ is numerically equivalent to 10. candlesticks which Solomon would make. Let me generalize. If there is a *yod* in *te’aseh*, then *te’aseh* is irregular.²⁴⁶ is normally spelled without a *yod*. The Midrash tells us that the menorah made itself.²⁴⁷ 8; *Be-halotekha* 3. Also see Rashi. The meaning of this midrash is that all who saw the menorah marveled and asked, “How could a human being make it?”²⁴⁸ Look! Scripture states, *and he*²⁴⁹ *made candlesticks*²⁵⁰ and *so he made the candlestick* (Num. 8:4).²⁵¹ Behold, Scripture writes, *On a griddle it shall be made* (te’aseh) *with oil*;²⁵² does not imply made by itself. No one can interpret Lev. 6:14 as meaning that the meal offering made itself. *when it is soaked, thou shalt bring it in* (Lev. 6:14). Observe, the word *miksheh* (of beaten work) here has the same meaning as the word *miksheh* which is written in connection with the cherubim.²⁵³

מלת מָרְאָה זרה ואיננה כדרך, מושלך (ש"ב כ כא) כי אין פעול למלת ראה כי אם נראה לבדה והיה כן בעבור כי הרואה אינו פועל רק מקבל דמות, ובעל התולדות יבין זה, ולפני שאדבר על המשכן שגם הוא היה יריעות כרובים אתן לך עיקר שתסמוך עליו:


[WHICH IS BEING SHOWN.] The word *moreh* (being shown)²⁶⁰ is a *hofal*. is irregular.²⁶¹ normally is, for nothing happens to the person to whom an object is shown. Hence Scripture should have read *ro’eh ba-har*, rather than *morah ba-har*. This is Krinsky’s interpretation. For another interpretation see Weiser. It is not employed in the same way that the word *mushlakh* (be thrown) (II Sam. 20:21) is,²⁶² (rosho) *shall be thrown* (mushlakh) *to thee over the wall*. In this verse *mushlakh* refers to the object being thrown, viz., his head. for the verb *ra’ah* (saw) does not come in the *pa’ul*.²⁶³ is the passive *kal* form. All *kal* transitive verbs come in the *pa’ul*, i.e., *katav/katuv, akhal/akhul, shavar/shavur*. However, *ra’ah* does not have a *pa’ul* form. Only the term *nireh* (seen)²⁶⁴ participle form. According to I.E. the word *nireh* does not imply that anything is happening to the object being seen, whereas the *pa’ul* form does. is employed.²⁶⁵ is not employed. This is so because one who sees is not acting on anything. He merely perceives an image. Those who are versed in the sciences will understand this.²⁶⁶ I wish to lay down a fundamental principle to you before I speak on the tabernacle, which also²⁶⁷ was made out of curtains [decorated] with cherubim.²⁶⁸

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 25:40:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/25:40:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/25:40:3)


**אמר אברהם המחבר** כל יש על שני דרכים, האחד שהוא גוף שיש לו אורך ורוחב ועומק והנה שש פאות, מהאורך יבאו פנים ואחור, ומהרוחב ימין ושמאל, ומהגבוה מעלה ומטה, ויש יש שאינו גוף, והם מלאכי השם הקדושים, גם נשמת האדם, ואלה השנים דרכים השם בראם לבדו, ואין יכולת בנברא לברוא עצם שיהיה גוף אף יש שאיננו גוף והוא נכבד יותר, גם אין בו כח להכחידו עד שיעדר ולא יהיה יש ויש דבר סמוך על יש ונשען עליו ולא ימצא לבדו והיא הצורה גם היא על שני דרכים, האחת עומדת ולא תסור כצורת הקדושים, והחכמה בנשמה, גם בגופות כחום האש וליחות המים, והדרך האחר מקרים, אינם עומדים, רק מתהפכים ונחלפים וסרים ונעדרים וכאלה יכול האדם לעשות על כן השם הנכבד לא יתכן שיהיה לו דמות ותמונה לא עומדת ולא נעדרת, כי השם ברא עצם כל דבר, כי כל צורה עומדת או מקרה, ואתן לך משל אחד קדרות הלבנה כשנכנס צל הארץ בינה השמש בראש התלי או בזנבו, ואתן לך משל אחר ידענו כי כח הנשמה בכל הגוף ויש מקומות בגוף האדם שיש בהם מהחבלים היוצאים מן המוח שירגישו יותר מהאחרים, כמו העינים והאזנים, כי העצמות גם הכבד לא ירגישו והנה הלב קבל כח הנשמה יותר מכל איברי הגוף, על כן היו איברים רבים משרתים לו, וככה השם הנכבד, ידענו כי כבודו מלא כל העולם, רק יש מקומות שיראה כח השם בו יותר ממקומות אחרים, ובעבור שני דברים האחד כפי מתכונות תולדות המקבל, והשני כפי כח עליון שהוא על ראש המקבל, על כן נבחר מקום בית המקדש, ואם נתן לך השם חכמה בלבך תבין סוד הארון והכפורת והכרובים שהם פורשי כנפים ומחוץ לפרוכת דבר המנורה ומזבח הקטרת והשלחן ומחוץ לפתח המשכן מזבח העולה ואת כל כליו, ואת הכיור ואת כנו, ואלה הדברים הם כבוד אלהים ובעבור זה רמזתי לך, כי יש בדורנו אנשים חכמים בעיניהם אולי יהתלו על דברי, והיודע סוד נשמתו ומתכונת גופו, יוכל לדעת דברי העולם העליון כי האדם דמות עולם קטן, והוא היה סוף בריאתו בארץ, וסימן לדבר בגדול החל ובקטן כלה והגאון הזכיר כי שמונה עשר דברים הם במשכן שהוא עולם אמצעי וכמוהם בעולם העליון, וככה העולם הקטן, הנה הכלל כל כרוב, נעשה לקבל כח העליון, גם בעבור שילמוד המשכיל ואין צורך להאריך:


Abraham the author says: All that exists, exists in one of the following two ways. One, it exists as a body that has length, width, and depth. The aforementioned results in six sides. From the length of an object comes front and back, from its width right and left, and from its height²⁶⁹ up and down. There are also incorporeal beings, namely, God’s holy angels and man’s soul. These two types of beings²⁷⁰ were created by God alone. It is not in the power of any created being to create a corporeal being. It is certainly beyond the power of any being to create an incorporeal being, for incorporeal beings are more important than corporeal beings.²⁷¹ It is also beyond the power of any created being to totally annihilate another being ²⁷² There is something which comes very close to existence and is tied to existence but does not exist independently.²⁷³ This thing is called form.²⁷⁴, ed. by Dagobert D. Runes, Littlefield, Adams and Co., 1959). Form also comes in two ways. One type of form is permanent and does not pass away, namely, the form of the holy angels and the wisdom which is in the soul.²⁷⁵ Form is also found in corporeal elements. The heat of fire and the wetness of water are examples. The accidents²⁷⁶). are the second way in which form manifests itself. The accidents are not permanent. They come and go. They change. They turn and disappear. Man is able to produce accidents.²⁷⁷ It is impossible for the glorious God to have a permanent or unchanging²⁷⁸ image or picture because God created the essence of all things.²⁷⁹ Now, all forms are either permanent or accidents.²⁸⁰ Let me give you one example.²⁸¹ The moon is eclipsed²⁸² when the earth’s shadow enters between the moon and the sun at the head or tail of the dragon.²⁸³ I will give you another example.²⁸⁴ We know that the power of the soul is all over the body. However, there are places in the human body such as the eyes or the nose that are more sensitive than others because of the nerves that go out from the brain. The bones and liver are devoid of sensation. Now the heart is more receptive to the power of the soul than are all other organs of the body. Many organs therefore serve it. Similarly with the glorious God. We know that God’s glory fills the world. However, there are places where God’s power is more manifest than in other places. This is so for the following two reasons. Divine manifestation varies in accordance with the natural makeup of the recipient and in accordance with the upper power that is above the receiver.²⁸⁵. Therefore, the place of the holy temple [Mount Moriah] was chosen.²⁸⁶ If God will give you wisdom, then you will understand the secret of the ark, the ark covering, and the cherubim which spread their wings.²⁸⁷ You will also understand the secret of the objects which were placed outside of the curtain,²⁸⁸ namely, the menorah, the incense altar, and the table.²⁸⁹ You will also comprehend the secret of the objects placed outside of the opening of the tabernacle, namely, the altar of the burnt offering and its utensils and the basin and its base. These objects served to honor God. I gave you these hints because there are many people in our generations who think they are wise. Perhaps they will mock my words. He who knows the secret of his soul and the makeup of his body is able to understand the workings of the upper world. This is so because man is a microcosm. Man was the last thing created by God when he created the earth. Let this serve as a sign: *He began with the largest*²⁹⁰ *and finished with the youngest*²⁹¹ (Gen. 44:12).²⁹² Saadiah Gaon notes that there are eighteen objects in the tabernacle which serves as the intermediary world.²⁹³ The same number of objects is found in the upper word²⁹⁴ and also in the microcosm.²⁹⁵ Here is a general rule. Each cherub was made to receive power from above. It was also made so that the intelligent will learn.²⁹⁶ There is no need to go on.

## Chapter 26


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 26:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:1:1)


**ואת המשכן.** כאשר הודיעו בתחלה את תבנית המשכן:


MOREOVER THOU SHALT MAKE THE TABERNACLE. As you were first told, namely, *the pattern of the tabernacle* (Ex. 25:9).¹ (the tabernacle), i.e., the earlier-noted tabernacle, rather than tabernacle (Krinsky).

footnotes:
¹ Moses was told to make the tabernacle according to the pattern which he had been shown earlier. I.E. comments thus because Scripture reads, ha-mishkan


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 26:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:1:2)


**מעשה חשב.** אמרו חכמים כי מעשה חשב שנים פרצופים, ורוקם פרצוף אחד ונכון הוא, ועל דרך הפשט מעשה חושב אינו רוקם ולא אורג, רק על דרך שעושין היום בגדי משי, כי הצורה שעלתה בלב היא חשבון, ומחשבתה, ויציירנה בלוח וישים שני חוטין בחשבון למשוך מרחוק:


THE WORK OF THE SKILLFUL WORKMAN. Our sages said that *ma’aseh choshev* (the work of the skillful workman) refers to two faces, and [*ma’aseh*] *rokem* (the work of the weaver) (v. 36)² 72:b: “It was taught in the name of Rabbi Nehemiah *rokem* (weaving) is needlework, therefore it has only one face. *Choshev* is weaving work, therefore it has two faces.” According to Rashi, one face means the same image on both sides of the curtain. Two faces means a different image on each side of the curtain, e.g., “a lion on one side, and an eagle on the other side.” Also see Rashi on *Yoma* 72b. to one image. What they said is correct. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, *ma’aseh choshev* is neither needle-work nor weaving.³, which literally means the work of an artist. It refers rather to a process employed today in making silk garments. The image that arises in the heart comes from insight and thought.⁴ (and its thought). Meijler suggests emending to *machashavah*. The artist draws it upon a tablet. He then places two threads upon the image which he thought up in order to draw it from a distance.⁵, Israel, 1991) comments, “I was not worthy to understand his (I.E.’s) holy words. One has to be an expert silk worker to understand his words.” According to Weiser, I.E. is describing the transfer of an image from a wooden tablet to silk. This is done by holding the tablet over the silk by two threads (or chords) and then dropping it, thus imprinting it upon the screen.

footnotes:
² See Yoma
³ According to I.E. needlework or weaving did not entail artistic skill. Hence it could not be considered ma’aseh choshev
⁴ Literally, and its thought. Hebrew, machashvtah
⁵ It isn’t clear what I.E. had in mind. Meijler suggests that some words might be missing from our texts. Rabbi Isaac Sarim (Be’er Yitzchak



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 26:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:2:1)


**ארך.** חסרי דעת אמרו, כי מדת כ"ח בעבור כ"ח מחנות הלבנה והנכון כי היו עשר יריעות על דרך נוטה שמים כיריעה (תה' קד) על כן היה מקום קדש הקדשים בחשבון מעוקב:


THE LENGTH. The uninformed say that the curtains were twenty-eight cubits in length because of the twenty-eight stages⁶ of the moon. However, actually there were ten curtains over the tabernacle to correspond with *Who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain* (Ps. 104:2).⁷ The place of the Holy of Holies therefore was a cube in measure.⁸

footnotes:
⁶ Literally, camps. The moon has a slightly different appearance each night of the month. According to Meijler, I.E. rejected this opinion because the curtains were 28 cubits in length merely in order to cover the width of the tabernacle and its sideboards down to the sockets.
⁷ In other words, the ten curtains of the tabernacle corresponded to the heavens which contain the ten spheres. The tabernacle was, as it were, God’s dwelling place. See I.E. on Ex. 25:40.
⁸ The Holy of Holies was 10 cubits wide, 10 cubits in length, and 10 cubits height. These measurements corresponded to the ten spheres.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 26:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/26:3:1)


**חברת.** כדמות תואר או יהיה כדמות פועל שזאת חוברות זאת, והעד חבור עצבים אפרים הנח לו (הושע ד יז) שהוא פעול:


COUPLED. *Choverot* (coupled) is an adjective.⁹ is an adjective, then our verse reads: five curtains coupled together, one to another. On the other hand, it might be a verb¹⁰ is a verb, then our verse should be translated: five curtains coupling one another. meaning that this curtain coupled the other curtain. *Ephraim is joined* (chavur) *to idols* (Hos. 4:17), wherein *chavur* is a *pu’al*,¹¹. is proof of the aforementioned.¹² is a verb. If a verb is found in the passive, it must have an active counterpart. It should be noted that *choveret* is the feminine form of *chover*.

והנה עשר יריעות הוא המשכן, והמשכן קראו אחד כולל הכל, כי כל גוף אינו דבר אחד, רק הוא מחובר מאחדים, וככה השם הנכבד שהוא אחד כולל הכל ונקרא אחד, וכן העולם הקטן והגדול:


[THAT THE TABERNACLE MAY BE ONE WHOLE.] Look, the term tabernacle refers to the ten curtains. The tabernacle is called one, and it encompass all ten [curtains] for all physical entities are made of various elements. Similarly God the revered, who is One. God includes everything and is called One.²⁴ The same is true with the microcosm²⁵ and the macrocosm.²⁶

**ארך, האחת.** מלת אחת זרה, כי היתה ראויה להיות אחדת כי הדל"ת אינה מאותיות המשרתים, רק בעבור שהתחברו שנים דל"ת ותי"ו שהם ממוצא אחד, יכבד על הלשון על דרך משָרַת את המלך (מ"א א, טו) וחסרו הדל"ת:


THE LENGTH OF EACH CURTAIN. The word *achat* (each) is irregular. The word should have read *achedet*,³⁰. The feminine form thus should be *achedet*. for the *dalet* is not a letter that serves as a prefix or a suffix.³¹ However, the *dalet* was dropped because it is very hard to sound a *dalet* and a *tav*, both of which are dentals, back to back. It³² was dropped for the same reason that the *tav* in *mesharat*³³. (ministered) in *ministered unto the king* (II Kings 1:15) was dropped.

**חמש.** בשו"א ופת"ח דרך קצרה, כמו שלש סאים (ברא' יח ו):


FIVE. The word *chamesh* (five) is vocalized with a *sheva*³⁴. and a *pattach*.³⁵. I.E.’s point is that the word *chamesh* is in the construct. It is an abridged form,³⁶, (vocalized with a *kamatz* beneath the *chet*), rather than *chamesh* (vocalized with a *chataf pattach* beneath the *chet) ha-yeri’ot*, for the construct indicates possession. Thus *chayyat ha-sadeh* (animals of the field) is short for *chayyot shel hasadeh* (animals of the field). However, since a number cannot be possessed, it is incorrect to say *chamesh shel ha-yeri’ot*. Thus *chamesh ha-yeriyot* is not short for *chamesh shel ha-yeri’ot*. Hence is not a true construct form. It is merely a quicker way of saying *chamesh* (vocalized with a *kamatz* beneath the *chet) ha-yeri’ot*. like the word *shelosh*³⁷ is in the construct with *se’im*. (three) in *shelosh se’im* (three measures) (Gen. 18:6).³⁸ (vocalized with a *kamatz* beneath the *shin) ha-se’im* rather than *shelosh* (vocalized with a *sheva* beneath the *shin*) *se’im*.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 26:16:1

**עשר אמות.** אמות המשכן לא ידענו אם הם כאמות יחזקאל שהם אצילה ובדרך סברא אמות הבית הראשון כן היו בעבור שמצאנו בדברי הימים כתוב במדה אחרונה:


TEN CUBITS. We do not know whether the cubits of the tabernacle were measured from the armpits⁶⁹ (where the arm joins the shoulder) (Krinsky). An alternate interpretation is: we do not know whether the cubits of the tabernacle’s “noble cubits” are like Ezekiel’s cubits. A “noble cubit” is a cubit that is larger then the ordinary cubit (Krinsky). like Ezekiel’s cubits.⁷⁰ Logically, the cubits of the first temple were of such cubits,⁷¹, it appears that I.E. means that they were the same type of cubits as those spoken of by Ezekiel. However, this cannot be so because I.E. goes on to quote II Chron. 3:3 to the effect that the earlier cubits, i.e., the smaller cubits, were employed in the temple. We must thus interpret “of such cubits” as referring to the cubits of the tabernacle. See Sarim. For alternate interpretations see Meijler and Krinsky. as we find that the Book Of Chronicles⁷² speaks of the earlier⁷³. 38. The printed editions have *middah acharonah* (the later measure). This appears to be an error, for II Chron. 3:3 explicitly reads, *ba-middah ha-rishonah* (the earlier or the ancient measure). The earlier measure refers to the measure employed in the tabernacle. It is possible that the reading of the later measure occurred because of the problem pointed out in note 70. On the other hand, it is possible that I.E. quoted from memory and erred, and that the printed texts rather than *Vat. Ebr*. 38 preserve the original reading. In this case, “were of such cubits” refers to Ezekiel’s cubits. measure.⁷⁴

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 26:18:1

**ועשית.** הנה לא נכתב כמה עובי הקרש, והראשונים אמרו שהיה אמה א"כ הוא כותל הדרומי היה שלשים אמות וככה הצפוני, והנה לא נשאר בכותל המערבי רק רחב שמונה אמות, וצריכים אנו לשום שם שמונה קרשים אולי הוצרכו לאמה, כי היה העובי אמה בעבור הבריח התיכון הנכנס בתוך הקרש, ועל דעת רבינו שלמה כי במעשה נס היה עומד כי על דרך הפשט שלשה בריחים תיכונים הם, וככה כתוב מן הקצה אל הקצה לא אל הקצות ואם קבלה היא שהעובי היה כך נשמע ונקבל, ואם דרך סברא יש תיקון אחר, כי השנים הבריחים הם עליונים, גם השפלים הם עד חצי הקיר והבריח התיכון שהובא בתוך הקרשים יהיה מבריח מן הקצה אל הקצה וכמוהו לעשות בתוך התכלת ובתוך הארגמן (למטה לט ג) וכן הפעמונים בתוך הרמונים (שם שם כה) ולולי זה לא היו מצפים הבריחים התיכונים זהב, ואם נאמר כי לא ידענו כמה עובי הקרש יש לנו לתקן המערב איך היתה, והנה בתחלה היו מתקנים פאת מערב, כי השנים הקרשים שהם למקצועות המשכן שפירושו כמו זויות וככה היה חצי מקצוע החצר כי היה כצורת מרובע ארוך, והנה יש לנו מקצעות, ואלה השנים הקרשים לבדם שהם במקצעות אינם כמדת הקרשים הנזכרים על כן הבדילם הכתוב, ואמר כן יהיה לשניהם לבדם לא הקרשים האחרים, ובאלה שנים קרשים הם מקימין המשכן, והיו הששה קרשים באמצע, והנה רוחב המשכן עשר אמות ולא ידענו אם היו קרשי המקצעות מרובעות או עגולות כי אין לנו רק אמה אחת, ועל הדרך שאמר רבינו שלמה לא תהיינה אלה הקרשים בטור שוה, כי חצי אמה יהיה בפנים כי קרש הוא ואינו בגד, ואחר כן ישימו קרשי צפון ודרום והנה יצא חוץ מן המשכן כפי עובי הקרש על כן יהיה כנגד עמוד פתח המשכן, ובחצי יריעות עזים יהיה התיקון:


AND THOU SHALT MAKE. Observe! Scripture does not record the thickness of the boards. The ancients⁷⁵ 98b. said that each board was a cubit thick. If this is the case⁷⁶ then the southern wall, which was thirty cubits, [was a cubit thick]. This was also the case with the northern wall.⁷⁷ Thus a space measuring eight cubits in width⁷⁸ was left for the western wall.⁷⁹ However, eight boards⁸⁰ had to be placed there.⁸¹ It is possible that the ancients were compelled to say that the boards were a cubit thick. They were compelled to say that the boards were a cubit thick because of the middle bar⁸² which was inserted into the boards.⁸³ According to Rabbi Solomon⁸⁴ the bar could only lay there by a miracle.⁸⁵ 98b, “It (the middle bar) lay there by miracle” (Soncino translation). Rashi in his comments on the Talmud explains that one long middle bar was placed into one of the boards and it miraculously snaked around all three sides of the tabernacle. This comment is not in our editions of Rashi on the Pentateuch. In our editions, Rashi merely notes that a separate middle bar was inserted into each of the three sides of the tabernacle. I.E. probably quoted Rashi from memory and attributed to him here what he wrote in his commentary on the Talmud. According to the plain meaning of the text there were three middle bars.⁸⁶ Scripture similarly writes, *from end to end* (v. 28).⁸⁷ It does not state⁸⁸ from end⁸⁹ to the ends.⁹⁰ Now if the sages received a tradition that the boards were a cubit in thickness, then we will accept their tradition. However, if they arrived at this measurement by reasoning, then we can explain it differently. The two bars, namely, the upper two bars, and likewise the two lower bars,⁹¹ reached half of the wall.⁹² The middle bar that was placed *in the midst* (be-tokh) *of the boards* (v. 28) passed through from end to end.⁹³ *To work it in the midst* (be-tokh) *of the blue, and in the midst of the purple*⁹⁴ (Ex. 39:3) is similar,⁹⁵ (in the midst) does not always literally mean in the midst of an object’s very body. It can be taken to mean midpoint or between. Thus in Ex. 39:3, *be-tokh* (in the midst) means among. Similarly, in verse 28 *be-tokh ha-kerahsim* does not mean in the very midst of the board’s body but rather at the midpoint of the board’s outer surface. as is *and put the bells in the midst* (be-tokh) *of the pomegranates*⁹⁶ (Ex. 39:25). The middle bars would not have been covered with gold⁹⁷ if they were not placed on the surface of the boards.⁹⁸ If we admit that we do not know the thickness of each board, then we can explain the structure of the western wall. Now, they first set up the western wall. For two boards were set aside to serve as corners⁹⁹ of the tabernacle,¹⁰⁰ as the meaning of *mekutzot*¹⁰¹ is corners. The same was true of half of the corners of the courtyard,¹⁰² for the courtyard¹⁰³ was in the form of a parallelogram. We thus have two corners. Now these two corner boards were not the same size as the other boards mentioned in Scripture.¹⁰⁴ Scripture therefore separates these boards¹⁰⁵ and says, *thus shall it be for them both* (v. 24), that is, only for them and not for any of the other boards. The tabernacle was erected by utilizing these two boards. The remaining six boards¹⁰⁶ were placed in the middle.¹⁰⁷ The width of the tabernacle was thus ten cubits.¹⁰⁸ We do not know if the corner boards were square or round,¹⁰⁹ for we have only one remaining cubit.¹¹⁰ According to Rabbi Solomon’s explanation, these boards did not stand in a straight line¹¹¹ because half a cubit was inside the tabernacle.¹¹² We are dealing with boards, not with garments.¹¹³ They then¹¹⁴ set up the boards on the northern and southern sides. Now an amount equivalent to the thickness of the boards¹¹⁵ protruded¹¹⁶ from the tabernacle.¹¹⁷ The pillar¹¹⁸. See verse 36. of the opening of the tabernacle was therefore opposite it.¹¹⁹ stood at the very entrance to the tent. The half a curtain of goatskin¹²⁰ fixed it.¹²¹

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 27:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/27:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/27:9:1)


**ועשית.** מצאנו כתוב קדמה מזרחה (למטה פ' יג), וידענו כי ראשי המזרחים שלשה, האחת כנגד נקודת ראש מזל גדי, שהוא סוף נטות השמש בפאת דרום והשני כנגד הקו השוה שהוא ראש טלה ומאזנים והשלישי כנגד ראש סרטן שהוא סוף נטות השמש לצפון, וככה נגבה תימנה דרום:


AND THOU SHALT MAKE. We find that Scripture says, *kedemah mizrachah* (on the east side eastward) (v. 13).²⁹. Now since both *kedem* and *mizrach* mean east, Scripture should have read *kedemah* or *mizrachah*. The question thus arises, why did Scripture employ the phrase *kedemah mizrachah*? I.E. brings up this issue here since Scripture uses the phrase *negev temanah* (south…southwards). Here too the question arises, why employ the phrase *negev temanah* when both *negev* and *teman* mean south? We know that there are three “heads” to the east.³⁰ The first is opposite the point of the head of Capricorn,³¹ which is the furthermost southern position of the sun. The second³² is opposite the celestial equator, which is the head of Aries and Libra.³³ The third is opposite the head of Cancer, which is the sun’s furthermost northern position.³⁴ refers to the middle portion of the eastern sky. So Krinsky. I.E. comments thus because in his opinion the tabernacle corresponded to the heavens. Thus *kedemah mizrachah* corresponded to a certain portion of the heavens. Weiser claims that *kedemah mizrachah* refers to the entire eastern side. The same applies to the phrase *negbah temanah* (south…southward)³⁵. I.E. used the term *negbah temanah* because verse 18 reads *kedemah mizrachah*. in the south.³⁶ refers to the middle portion of the southern sky. So Krinsky. For other interpretations see Weiser.

The southern sky consists of Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. Capricorn is located in the southwestern section of the heavens. Aries lies in the southeastern part of the sky. The first “head” of the east begins at a point in the southeastern sky directly opposite the constellation of Capricorn.

### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 27:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/27:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/27:12:1)


**ורחב.** הנה הרוחב חצי האורך, והמפרשים אמרו כי המשכן הושם במרחק חמשים במערב והנה רחבו חמשים, וזהו **ורחב חמשים בחמשים,** ולפי דעתי כי הטעם שהוא מרוב אורך זויותיו נצבות, כי רחבו בכל צד חמשים ואין טעם להיות פי' חמשים בחמשים מצד החצר, כי לא כפל האורך על הרוחב כמשפט:


AND FOR THE BREADTH…FIFTY CUBITS. The width of the courtyard was thus half of its length.⁴⁰ The commentaries tell us that the tabernacle was placed fifty cubits westward.⁴¹ 23b. “He placed the tabernacle (which measured 30 by 20 cubits) at the edge of fifty cubits (i.e., 50 cubits inwards) so that there was fifty cubits in front of the tabernacle and twenty cubits around the sides.” Now its width was fifty cubits. This is what *and the breadth fifty every where* (v. 18) means. However, I believe that the meaning of *the breadth fifty every where* is that the courtyard was a right-angled parallelogram,⁴². Literally, because of its many long right angles. In other words, the courtyard was a parallelogram that measured 50 cubits in width. Such a structure is 50 cubits in breadth *every where*, i.e., all along its width. Meijler suggests emending *me-rov orekh zavyotav nitzavot* (because of the length of its many angles) to *meruva orekh zavyotav nitzavot* (a right-angled parallelogram). *Vat. Ebr*. 38 reads: *merchav arokh zeviyot*, which means a right-angled parallelogram. This reading seems to be the most correct. Be that as it may, according to I.E. the import of our verse is that the tabernacle courtyard was not tapered but measured 100 by 50 cubits. and its width was fifty cubits on all sides.⁴³ is that its width did not vary. There is no necessity to explain *the breadth fifty every where* as referring to the side of the courtyard,⁴⁴ as Scripture does not repeat the dimensions length by width as it normally does.⁴⁵ (fifty every where). If Scripture were speaking of a square it would read, *chamishim al chamishim* (fifty by fifty) (Filwarg). Also see Weiser.

**ואתה תצוה.** אזכיר בתחלה טעם לדבק הפרשה, כי כאשר השלים לספר כל כלי הקדש, והפרוכת והמשכן והאהל והמכסה ומזבח העולה והחצר והמסך החל לפרש משרת המשכן, ומה היא עבודתם בעצמם אין זר אתם, והחל שיעלו נרות בשמן זית, לא בשמן זר, ואלה המשרתים ראוים להיות נכרים ונבדלים במשפחותם, גם במלבושיהם והזכיר הכתוב זה אחר זה, ואחר כן הזכיר שהם חייבים ללמד שבעת ימי המלואים שילמדם משה וירגילם, ואחר כן ישרתו ויעלו עולות התמיד על מזבח העולה, לא על מזבח הזהב, רק שיקטירו עליו ויכפרו על קרנותיו אחת בשנה:


AND THOU SHALT COMMAND. I will first note the reason for the position of this Torah portion.⁴⁹ follows the Torah portion *Terumah*. After God finished enumerating all the holy utensils, the veil, the tabernacle, the tent, the cover, the altar of the burnt offering, the courtyard, and the screen,⁵⁰. He commenced⁵¹. to deal with those who ministered in the tabernacle.⁵², the priests. He explained the service which they alone were to perform. No stranger was permitted to perform the service alongside them. God opened⁵³ with the command that they⁵⁴ cause a lamp to burn using pure olive oil. They were not to employ any other oil. It is only fitting that those who ministered in the tabernacle were to be distinguished and set apart, both in family and in dress.⁵⁵ Scripture lists the garments one after the other.⁵⁶ Scripture then mentions that those who served in the tabernacle were obligated to learn the service during the seven days of consecration. Moses was to teach and train them. After this, the priests would serve in the tabernacle. They would offer the daily burnt offering on the altar of the burnt offering. They were not to offer it upon the golden altar. The priests were to offer only incense upon the golden altar and to make atonement upon its horns once a year.⁵⁷

**וטעם ואתה תצוה.** שהיא מצוה עולמית על הצבור לתת תמיד שמן זית להעלות נר תמיד, ואל תשתומם בעבור השמן שהביאו הנשיאים, כי הוא היה שמן המשחה, רק שמן למאור חיוב הצבור, ויש מנהג במקומות ששם זיתים, שיבחרו הזית הזך, והטעם הגרגרים שאין בהם עפוש, או שלא נאכלה קצתם, וממנו יעשו שמן למאכל המלכים, על כן הזכיר הכתוב זך לפני כתית:


*And thou shalt command* ⁵⁸. means that there is an eternal command upon the congregation to continually provide olive oil to kindle a perpetual light. Do not be troubled by the oil which the princes⁵⁹ brought.⁶⁰ It was anointing oil.⁶¹ (Ex. 35:28). Krinsky explains that only the princes had pure olive oil in the desert (see I.E. on Ex. 35:27). Hence after the princes donated the oil to be used for anointing oil, some of it was utilized for the light. The congregation, on the other hand, was obligated to bring oil for the light. There is a practice in countries where olives grow to choose pure olives, that is, olives that do not have any rot on them or olives that have not been partially eaten. These olives are then used to make oil for the king’s food. This is the reason that Scripture mentions *pure*⁶² before *beaten*.

**אשר על העדות.** דרך קצרה על ארון העדות, אמר יפת, כי יערוך כמו כערכך הכהן (ויקרא כז יב) שיערוך שמן שיספיק להיות הנרות מאירים מערב ועד בקר, וככה נרות המערכה (למטה לט לז), ונכון הוא להיות טעם יערוך בעבור היות הנרות כחצי עגול, ועוד אדבר על זה:


WHICH IS BEFORE THE TESTIMONY. *The testimony* is short for the ark of testimony. Yefet says that *ya’arokh* (shall set)⁷¹. This root can mean to estimate or to arrange. Hence the two interpretations of *ya’arokh* (shall set). is similar in meaning to *ke-erkekha* (as thou valuest it)⁷² in *as thou the priest valuest it* (Lev. 27:12). It means that the priest shall estimate the amount of oil that will be sufficient for the lamps to give light from evening till morning.⁷³ (shall set) means shall estimate. The same applies to the phrase *nerot ha-ma’arakha* (even the lamps to be set in order) (Ex. 39:37).⁷⁴ (even the lamps to be set in order) as: the lamps to be estimated; that is, the lamps whose oil has to be estimated. *Ya’arokh* may also be properly interpreted as meaning shall set, for the lamps were set in a semicircle.⁷⁵ I will yet speak on this.

### Verse 1

**ואתה.** בעבור היות משה כהן הכהנים בתחלה על כן טעם הקרב אליך, וכבר רמזתי לך למה נבחר אהרן להקדישו לשם בעבור כבוד משפחת נחשון שיהיו הכהנים מכפרים על בני ישראל, ואין לדבר על משה אדונינו כי בורח היה, ומי יתן לו עברית, ועוד כי טורח כל ישראל על משה ללמדם המצות, ולדון כל דבר קשה.


AND BRING THOU. Scripture says, *And bring thou near unto thee* [*Aaron thy brother, and his sons…that they may minister unto me*] because at first Moses was the high priest.¹ I have already hinted² at why Aaron³ was chosen to be sanctified to the Lord so that the priests⁴ would make atonement for Israel. Aaron was chosen because of the importance of Nahshon’s family.⁵ We cannot find fault with Moses,⁶ our master, as Moses was a fugitive.⁷ Who would have given him a Hebrew woman?⁸ Furthermore, the burden of all of Israel was upon Moses.⁹ Moses had to teach Israel the commandments. He also had to judge all difficult cases.¹⁰

וי"ו **לכהנו לי.** נוסף כוי"ו חיתו שדי (תה' קד יא) בנו בעור (במד' כד ג), ופי' שמות בני אהרן אולי בנים אחרים היו לו חוץ מאלה, ואין ספק כי רבתה למעלה במדבר משפחת אהרן, על כן נתנו להם ישראל ערים רבות הכתוב בס' יהושע:


[THAT THEY MAY MINISTER UNTO ME.] The *vav* in *lekhahano* (that they minister) in *that they may minister unto me* is superfluous.¹¹ in *le-khahano* is not a pronominal suffix, and *le-khahano* has the same meaning as *le-khahen*. It is like the *vav* in *chayeto* (beast)¹² has the same meaning as *chayat*. The *vav* in *chayeto* is not a pronominal suffix. in *every beast of the field* (Ps. 104:11) and *beno* (son of)¹³ has the same meaning as *ben*, for the *vav* in *beno* is not a pronominal suffix. in *the son of Beor* (Num. 24:3). Our verse lists the sons of Aaron. It is possible that Aaron had other sons besides these.¹⁴ There is no doubt that Aaron’s family increased greatly in the wilderness. Hence they were given the many cities enumerated in the Book of Joshua.¹⁵

**ואתה.** וי"ו **מלאתיו** שב אל לב:


AND THOU SHALT. The *vav* in *milletiv* (I have filled)¹⁹ refers to *lev* ²⁰ (hearted).²¹ (wise-hearted) precedes *milletiv* (I have filled it). Since *chakhme* is plural, Scripture should have read *milletim*. Hence I.E.’s comment that *milletiv* refers to *lev*, which is singular.

### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 28:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/28:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/28:4:1)


**ואלה הבגדים.** הזכיר בתחלה החשן שהי' למעלה מהאפוד שהוא למעלה מהמעיל, ואחר כן הכתונת והאבנט החוגר אותו והמצנפת על ראשו וכן היה כאשר רחץ אהרן במים ולבש מכנסי בד, ואין צורך להזכירם עתה, ולא בשעת מעשה כי מנהג כל אדם ללבוש מכנסים והנה משה הלבישו הכתונת, ואחר כן שם המצנפת על ראשו ושם על המצנפת ציץ נזר הקדש ולא הזכיר בפסוק הזה שהוא סופר בגדי כהונה את ציץ נזר הקדש כי אינו בגד וקדמונינו הזכירו בעבור הרבים שמונה בגדי כהונה, ואין האורים והתומים בגדים ולא אבנים ולא קלפים, ואחר כן חגר אותו באבנט, ואחר כן הלבישו המעיל, ואח"כ האפוד, ויאפד לו בו כי החשב מהאפוד ובעבור החשב נקרא אפוד, והנה על הסדר שהוא בפסוק הזה, ואל תשתומם שתמצא כתוב באחרונה במעשה וישם את המצנפת על ראשו (ויקרא ח ט) כי פירושו וכבר שם המצנפת עם ציץ הזהב בלבשו הכתנת, וכמוהו וילבישוהו בגדים (זכריה ג ה) וכבר הלבישוהו כי בתחלה כתיב וישימו הצניף הטהור על ראשו (שם):


AND THESE ARE THE GARMENTS. Scripture first mentions the breastplate, which was worn over the ephod, which was worn over the robe.²² It then mentions the tunic and the girdle²³ which went around it²⁴ after the mitre was placed on Aaron’s head. This is what happened²⁵, etc. when Aaron washed²⁶ and put on linen breeches.²⁷ However, there was no reason to mention the breeches here nor in the description of the actual investiture of Aaron,²⁸ for it is the manner of all men to wear breeches. Now Moses put the tunic upon Aaron.²⁹ He then placed the mitre upon Aaron’s head,³⁰ and He placed “the plate of the holy crown”³¹. upon the mitre.³² Our verse, which enumerates the priestly garments, does not mention “the plate of the holy crown” because “the plate of the holy crown” was not a garment. However, our sages mentioned the holy plate among the priestly garments³³ 71b. because most of the objects worn by the high priest were garments. Hence the sages speak of the eight garments worn by the high priest. The Urim and Thummim³⁴ were not garments.³⁵ Neither were the stones,³⁶ nor the cards.³⁷ After this³⁸ Moses encircled Aaron with the girdle. Moses then placed the robe upon Aaron. He then placed the ephod upon the robe and *put the ephod upon him, and he girded him with the skilfully woven band of the ephod and bound it unto him therewith* (Lev. 8:7).³⁹ The skillfully woven band was part of the ephod.⁴⁰ [the ephod] *unto him* [Aaron] *therewith*. The ephod was so called because of the skillfully woven band.⁴¹ Moses dressed Aaron according to the order described in our verse. Do not be bothered by the fact that Scripture later states, regarding the actual investiture of Aaron, *And he set the mitre upon his head* (Lev. 8:9).⁴² Its meaning is, he had already placed the mitre with the golden plate on Aaron’s head when he dressed him in the tunic.⁴³ (and he set) has a pluperfect meaning: and he had set. See Vol. 1, p. xvi, item 4. The meaning of *and clothed him with garments* (Zech. 3:5) is similar; i.e., they had already clothed him. For Scripture previously states, *So they set a fair mitre upon his head* (*Ibid*.).⁴⁴. The aforementioned shows that the mitre was donned following the robes. However, when Scripture describes what actually happened it says, *So they seta fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments* (Zech. 3:5). The latter implies that the mitre was put on before the garments. Hence I.E.’s interpretation that *and clothed him with garments* (*Ibid*.) means, and they had already clothed him.

רק בעבור האורים שהם עליו, ועוד שאלה אחרת, כי לא נוכל לומר כי האורים הם עצמם התומים, כי כתוב לאורים ותומים (עזרא ו סה), ועוד מלת לאורים גם תומים לשון רבים, והנה דברים רבים הם, ורבינו שלמה אמר, כי האורים והתומים היו כתבי שם המפורש, ואלו ראה תשובת רבינו האי לא אמר ככה, וסוד עמוק הוא דבר האפוד והחשן, רק ארמוז קצת הסוד אולי יבינהו מי שהוא ידע דעת עליון, והפתח שיוכל לבא אל הסוד, שתי העבותות הנתונות גמורות מהעליון והשפל, והמשכיל יבין, והנה אפודים רבים היו עם הכהנים, ויש להם חשב, רק כי אין שם חשן ולא אורים, ואשר היה רגיל בדברי האורים והתומים שהיו על חשן המשפט יוכל להשיב לשואל מדמיון האפוד לבדו רק לא בכל עת, ואלו הואלתי לגלות זה הסוד לא יכולתי לכתבו כפי המכתב שחברתי בפי' הספר כלו, כי לא יביננו מי שלא למד ספר המדות, וסוד מלאכת שמים, ואין צורך להאריך בצורת האפוד והחשן והטבעות:


AND THEY SHALL MAKE THE EPHOD. Scripture starts with the ephod⁴⁶ because it was larger than the breastplate. The Torah tells us *that the breastplate be not loosed from* the skilfully woven band of *the ephod* (v. 28).⁴⁷ There are some very difficult questions relating to the ephod and the breastplate. Moses only made one ephod.⁴⁸ However, Scripture states, *that he*⁴⁹ *came down with an ephod in his hand* (I Sam. 23:6). The latter does not refer to the ephod made by Moses,⁵⁰ for Scripture does not read “the ephod,”⁵¹ ephod,” not “*the* ephod in his hand.” the meaning of which is, the well-known ephod,⁵² as it does when it states, *“Bring hither the ephod”* (I Sam. 23:9).⁵³ Furthermore, why does Scripture state, *he came down*, but it does not say he brought down? It thus appears that the ephod was accidentally among his possessions.⁵⁴ implies that Abiathar happened to have an ephod which he brought down, whereas if Scripture had read: that he brought down the ephod in his hand, it would have implied that Abiathar deliberately brought down *the* ephod. In the latter case, the reference would be to the ephod made by Moses. Additionally, Scripture there states, *fourscore persons*⁵⁵. If it is not a scribal error, then I.E. quoted from memory and erred. *that did wear a linen* (bad) *ephod* (I Sam. 22:18).⁵⁶ Many commentaries explain this verse as meaning that the *persons*⁵⁷ were fit to wear the ephod.⁵⁸ means fourscore and five persons who were fit to wear a linen ephod. In other words, they did not actually wear an ephod but were worthy of wearing the ephod made by Moses. However, they did not bother to learn the truth.⁵⁹ A *bad* (linen) ephod is an ephod made from a type of flax. However, the ephod made by Moses was not made of *bad* (linen).⁶⁰ It was made of gold, blue wool, purple wool, and scarlet, with *shesh* (linen)⁶¹ is a high quality linen. intertwined with all of the aforementioned.⁶² They only inquired of the breastplate of judgment which had the Urim and Thummim upon it.⁶³ Scripture similarly writes, *by the judgment of the Urim before the Lord* (Num. 27:21). *Bring hither the ephod* (I Sam. 23:9)⁶⁴ [Saul’s] *hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard?* (I Sam. 23:11). does not present a counterargument⁶⁵, this verse implies that the ephod itself served as the instrument by which God’s will was divined. because the breastplate was connected to it. The Urim⁶⁶ went along with the breastplate.⁶⁷ We similarly read, *till there stood up a priest with Urim and Thummim* (Neh. 7:65). Scripture likewise states, *Thy Thummim and Thy Urim* (Deut. 33:8). Now, Scripture tells us⁶⁸ that God answered David through Abiathar’s ephod.⁶⁹ However, we also read that when Saul went to war he inquired of the Urim (I Sam. 28:6). These were the very Urim that were placed in the breastplate of judgment which was with the ephod⁷⁰ and the ark.⁷¹ However, David inquired of Abiathar’s ephod in Ziklag. Abiathar’s ephod was thus not Moses’ ephod.⁷² The following problem is even more difficult.⁷³ It is clear that the Urim do not refer to the stones of the breastplate,⁷⁴ 73b). Rashi explains that the stones on the breastplate of judgment served as the instrument of divination by lighting up. See Rashi on verse 30. Also see note 88. However, Rashi does not identify the stones on the breastplate with the Urim and Thummim. Other commentaries taking the Talmud at face value did. It is with these commentaries that I.E. takes issue. as Scripture openly states, *And thou shalt set in it settings of stones* (v. 17). The setting of the stones was the work of a stonecutter and not the work of Moses. God then told Moses,⁷⁵ *And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim* (v. 30).⁷⁶ Scripture, in describing the making of the breastplate,⁷⁷. 38. The latter reads: “Scripture in describing its making,” the reference being to the making of the previously mentioned breastplate. tells us, *And they set in it four rows of stones* (Ex. 39:10). Scripture then describes the four rows of stones.⁷⁸ Scripture tells us that Moses placed the breastplate upon Aaron *and in the breastplate he put the Urim and the Thummim* (Lev. 8:8). Now according to the plain meaning of the text the stones were not the objects that enlightened or fulfilled,⁷⁹ because inquiries were made of the Urim and Thummim. We do not know what they were. The explanation that the names of the tribes⁸⁰ was not inscribed on any of the stones.” For none of the tribes has a *tzadi* in their names. The Talmud responds, “Rabbi Samuel ben Isaac says, ‘The names of Abraham, Isaac (Hebrew, *yod, tzadi. chet, kof*), and Jacob were also inscribed upon the stones’” (*Yoma* 73b). and the patriarchs⁸¹ was not inscribed on the stones.” The words *shivte yeshurun* (the tribes of Jeshurun) were similarly inscribed on the stones” (*Yoma* 72b). were inscribed on the breastplate is of no help,⁸² for the breastplate of judgment was so called only because of the Urim that were on it.⁸³ There is an additional question: we cannot identify the Urim with the Thummim,⁸⁴ for Scripture states, *with Urim and Thummim* (Neh. 7:65). Furthermore, the words *with Urim* and *Thummim* are in the plural. They thus consisted of many objects.⁸⁵ Rabbi Solomon says that the Urim and Thummim consisted of an inscription of God’s explicit name.⁸⁶ However, he would not have said this had he seen the responsa of Rabbi Hai Gaon.⁸⁷). There is a very deep secret behind the ephod and the breastplate. I will allude only to a part of this secret. Perhaps he who knows the mind of the Most High will understand it. The following are the keys to the secret of the ephod.⁸⁸ The two wreathen chains on the two rings [represent the head of Aries and Libra].⁸⁹ The band of the ephod represents the celestial equator.⁹⁰ Hence six names were inscribed on the stone which was on the other shoulder.⁹¹ Now these things⁹² can only be grasped by the mind. Hence six names were inscribed on one stone⁹³ in accordance with the number, names, and order of birth of the tribes of the children of Israel.⁹⁴ Six names were similarly inscribed on the second stone.⁹⁵ On the other hand, the names on the breastplate were not divided in the same manner as they are grasped by the mind.⁹⁶ They were divided in a way that could be perceived by the eye.⁹⁷ Scripture states, *And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a thread of blue* (v. 28) to prevent the breastplate from moving to the side.⁹⁸ The breastplate was folded, for the Urim and Thummim were kept there until such time as they were needed. They were then placed outside of the breastplate.⁹⁹ Note, the stones of the ephod were like each other.¹⁰⁰ They were of one color.¹⁰¹ This was not the case with the stones of the breastplate,¹⁰² for the sapphire stones¹⁰³ served as a memorial,¹⁰⁴ while the judgment of the children of Israel was upon the stones of the breastplate.¹⁰⁵ The word Urim is related to the word *ur* (fire) in *I am warm, I have seen the fire* (Is. 44:16).¹⁰⁶ is a variation of *or* and should thus be translated as light. Hence, according to I.E., Is. 44:16 should be rendered: *I am warm, I have seen the light* (Krinsky). It should be noted that Nahmanides’ text of I.E. reads: “The Urim and Thummim were made out of gold.” The Thummim are so called because they are whole.¹⁰⁷ (thummim) is *taf, mem, mem*. The Urim were of gold and silver. This was not the case with the Thummim.¹⁰⁸ The [importance of the] number [twelve] has been established by irrefutable proof from the upper and lower worlds.¹⁰⁹ The intelligent will understand what I say.¹¹⁰ Now the priests had many ephodim. They all had bands. However, they lacked the breastplate and the Urim. A priest who was an expert in using the Urim and Thummim was able to respond to an inquirer because the ephod at hand resembled [the ephod made by Moses].¹¹¹ However, the priest did not always get an answer.¹¹² Now if I wanted to even begin to reveal this secret¹¹³ it would take up more space than the entire commentary which I have composed on this book. For only an individual who has studied works on geometry and the secret of the way the sky works can understand the secret of the ephod. There is no need to expand on the form of the ephod, the breastplate, and the rings.

**ואבן השהם.** לבנה, ובארמית בורלא ולשון ישמעאל בלאור ואין לנו דרך בבירור לדעת אבני המלואים כי הגאון תרגמם כרצונו, כי אין לו קבלה שיסמוך עליה כי הנה ראינו שתרגם ספיר לבן, ואינו רק אדום, ואין טענה מאודם הכתוב בראשונה כי ידוע כי חמש הם גווני העינים, הלבן וברקת, ואדום וירוק ושחור והנה בעבור היות האדום האמצעי ימצא על מינים רבים ותרגום נופך כדמות שחור בעבור ותשם בפיך עיניה (מ"ב ט ט), וזה לא יתכן שלא יהיה נו"ן נופך שרש, כי הוא על משקל אודם, וחכם גדול ספרדי אמר כי יהלום הוא הנקרא אלמם שהוא שובר כל האבנים, ונוקב הבדולח מגזרת הולם פעם (ישעי' מא ז), והיו"ד נוסף כיו"ד יצהר, גם אחלמה, אל חלמה, והוא אבן שכל מי שהאבן ההיא באצבעו לעולם יראה חלומות, ואין לתמוה על זה, כי כח ימצא בתולדת כל אבן ואבן, כי יש אבן שמושכת את הברזל, והמעמדת את הדם והבורחת מהחומץ, והנשברת לעולם על משולש:


ONYX STONES. The *avne shoham* (onyx stones) were white. They are called *burla* in Aramaic and *balor* in Arabic. We have no way to positively identify the stones that were set in the breastplate. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon translated them¹¹⁴ as he saw fit, as he had no tradition to rely upon.¹¹⁵ We read the Gaon’s translation and noticed that he rendered *sappir* (sapphire) as white.¹¹⁶ to as a white stone. See I.E. on Ex. 24:10. However, this is not the case. *Sappir* is red.¹¹⁷ is a red stone. As noted before, sapphire is usually blue, sometimes white, hardly ever red. See chapter 24, note 3. The fact that the first stone¹¹⁸ mentioned by the Torah was a carnelian¹¹⁹ (a red stone). does not refute this,¹²⁰ is a red stone. In other words, one should not assume that there was only one red stone on the breastplate. for there are five visible colors: white, lightning,¹²¹ red, green, and black. Now since red is the middle color¹²² it comes in various shades. Saadiah Gaon renders *nofekh* (carbuncle) as black on the basis of *and she painted* (ba-pukh)¹²³ is *peh, vav, kaf*. *her eyes* (II Kings 9:30).¹²⁴ is a “black mineral powder, for increasing brilliance of eyes by darkening edges of lids.” (*Hebrew and English Lexicon of the Old Testament*, edited by Brown, Driver, Briggs, Oxford University Press, Oxford). However, the *nun* in *nofekh* is undoubtedly a root letter,¹²⁵ is *nun, peh, kaf*. Hence *nofekh* and *pukh* are two different words. for *nofekh* follows the paradigm of *odem* (carnelian).¹²⁶ A great Sephardic scholar said that *yahalom* (emerald) is a diamond.¹²⁷ in Arabic. This stone has the ability to break up all other stones and to bore through bdellium. *Yahalom* is related to the word *holem* (smiteth) in *smiteth the anvil* (Is. 41:7). The *yod* of *yahalom* is not a root letter.¹²⁸. The *yod* of *yahalom* is a form letter. It is like the *yod* of *yitzhar* (oil).¹²⁹ is *tzadi, heh, resh*. Also *achlamah* (amethyst) is to be identified with the dream stone.¹³⁰ in Arabic. This is a stone that always induces dreams in the person who wears it.¹³¹. One should not be surprised at this,¹³² as every stone has a specific power placed in it by nature. Thus there is a stone that attracts iron.¹³³ There is likewise a stone that stops bleeding. Another stone is repelled by vinegar. There is also a stone whose pieces always form a triangle when broken.

**ומלת שרשרות.** כפול העי"ן, ואם לא יכפלוהו שוה, הוא שרשת גבלת (פ' כב), ולפרש בלשון הקדש מלת גבלות, ומלות רבות, במעשה החשן, גם מלת חשן קשה:


CHAINS. The middle root letter has been doubled in *sharsherot* (chains).¹³⁴ is *shin, resh, shin*. However, the *resh* was doubled and a new quadriliteral root, *shin, resh, shin, resh*, formed. The latter is the root of *sharsherot*. However, the word has the same meaning when the middle root letter is not doubled. Compare, *sharshot*¹³⁵ is *shin, resh, shin*.*gavlut* (plaited chains) (v. 22). It is very difficult to explain the meaning of *gavlut* (plaited) in Hebrew.¹³⁶, and some of the other terms used by Scripture in relation to the *choshen* are not Hebrew words. We consequently do not know their meaning. The same applies to many of the words employed by Scripture that refer to the making of the breastplate as well as to the word *choshen* (breastplate) itself.

AND THOU SHALT MAKE A PLATE. The Gaon renders *tzitz* (plate) *atzabah*. It¹⁴³ is masculine but I.E. uses the feminine pronoun (*hi*) because he is referring to *atzabah*, the Arabic equivalent of *tzitz*. was placed on the mitre. It was not shaped like a crown, as the plate¹⁴⁴. It is rather strange that I.E. first employs pronouns which refer to the Arabic form of the word and then employs a pronoun which refers to the Hebrew form of the word. It should be noted that *Vat. Ebr*. 38 has a totally different reading. It reads: “The Gaon renders *tzitz* (plate) *atzabah*. It is placed on the mitre. The mitre does not have the shape of head-tires, for the head-tires are similar to the high hats which men in this and surrounding countries place upon their heads as a head covering. However, the mitres are made out of long thin material which is twisted only around the head.” There is no inconsistency in the tenses in this reading. was placed only on the forehead.¹⁴⁵ According to the plain meaning of the text, the *migba’ot* (head-tires) (Lev. 8:13)¹⁴⁶ (mitre) worn by the high priest. were not shaped like the mitre (*mitznefet*). The head-tires are similar to the high hats which men in this and surrounding countries place upon their heads as a head covering. [37.] THE MITRE. The mitre¹⁴⁷ is made from long thin material which is twisted only around the head.¹⁴⁸ The turbans worn by women in these areas are somewhat similar. In Spain, Africa, Egypt, Babylonia, and Baghdad and in the land of the Ishmaelites, only men of respect, not the women, wear turbans on their heads.¹⁴⁹ The important officials place a golden plate on the turban over the forehead. I have already noted that the ornaments in the Land of Israel and the customs practiced there differ from those in these areas. Rabbi Solomon¹⁵⁰ found it necessary to harmonize Scripture¹⁵¹ (the plate) *on a thread of blue*. However, it goes on to say, *and it* (the plate) *shall be upon the mitre*. This implies that the plate was on the mitre, not upon the thread. Furthermore, Ex. 39:31 states, *And they tied unto it* [the plate] a *thread of blue*. In other words, verse 37 implies that the plate was placed upon the thread, but Ex. 39:31 implies that the thread was placed on top of the plate. by explaining that three blue threads were attached to the plate.¹⁵² top.” The first refers to the threads on the outer side of the plate, the second to the threads on the inner side of the plate, and the third to the threads that passed through the middle perforation. However, according to the plain meaning of the text only one blue thread¹⁵³ was necessary to keep the plate, which was on the face of the mitre on the forehead, in place.

**וטעם ושמת אותו על פתיל תכלת.** עם פתיל תכלת, שהיה הציץ קשור משני צדדין, ואין ספק כי פני המצנפת הוא על מקום המצח לא על הראש, ובמקום אחר כתוב ויתנו עליו פתיל תכלת (למטה לט לא) לתת על המצנפת מקום המצח ואל תתמה על מלת על כי כמוהו ויבואו האנשים על הנשים (למטה לה כב) על לחם הבכורים תנופה לפני ה' (ויקרא כג, כ) על שני כבשים (שם שם) את החלב על החזה (שם ז, ל) ורבים ככה, והנה לא תמצא לעולם, כי המצנפת היתה רק לאהרן לבדו, והמגבעות לבניו, וי"א כי מגבעות מגזרת גבעות (ברא' מט, כו) כי המצנפת עוטרת הראש ועוטה אותו, וכן כתוב צנוף יצנפך צנפה (ישעי' כב, יח) ועוטך עטה (שם שם יז), והיודע דרך צנוף המצנפת, ידע פי', לא זאת השפלה הַגְבֵהַ, וְהַגָבֹהַ השפיל (יחז' כא לא), כי אומנות היא, והנה כתוב ושמת המצנפת על ראשו, ונתת את נזר הקדש על המצנפת (למטה כט ו) והנה הציץ נקרא נזר, וכמוהו ועליו יציץ נזרו (תה' קלב יח) אולי הכל מגזרת ציץ דבר נראה, וככה מציץ מן החרכים (ש"ה ב ט), ודע כי בשנים הנקבים שהם במוח על המצח, שם יתחבר כח החמש הרגשות, ושם כח הדמות ושם תחל המחשבה ע"כ כתוב על הציץ לשאת את עון הקדשים אולי לא היתה מחשבת המקדשים כהוגן:


AND THOU SHALT PUT IT ON A THREAD OF BLUE. The meaning of *al petil techelt* (on a thread of blue) is, with¹⁵⁴ here means with. Hence verse 37 does not contradict Ex. 39:31. See note 152. Also see note 153. a thread of blue,¹⁵⁵ as the thread was tied to the plate on two sides.¹⁵⁶ There is no doubt that the front of the mitre was placed over the forehead.¹⁵⁷ [the plate] *shall be* means that the plate shall be on the forehead. It¹⁵⁸ was not placed over the head. Scripture elsewhere states, *And they tied unto it a thread of blue, to fasten it upon the mitre* (Ex. 39:31), that is, upon the forehead.¹⁵⁹ does not mean on the mitre per se, as Rashi says (see note 152) but upon the forehead. Hence Ex. 39:31 does not contradict Ex. 28:37. Do not be surprised that Scripture uses the term *al*.¹⁶⁰ usually has the meaning of on. Hence I.E.’s comment. We find the same¹⁶¹ used in the sense of with. in the following, *And they came, both men with* (al) *women* (Ex. 35:22);¹⁶²*And the priest shall wave them with* (al) *the bread of the first-fruits for a wave-offering before the Lord* (Lev. 23:20); *with* (al) *the two lambs* (*Ibid*.); *the fat with* (al) *the breast* (Lev. 7:30). There are many similar instances in Scripture. Now you will never find [the mitre and the head-tires interchanging].¹⁶³ For the mitre was set aside only for Aaron, and the head-tires for his children. Some say that the word *migba’ot* (head-tires) is related to the word *givot* (hills) (Gen. 49:26).¹⁶⁴ had the shape of a high hat. The mitre¹⁶⁵. surrounded and wrapped the head.¹⁶⁶. We similarly read, *He will violently roll* (tzanof) *and toss thee Like a ball* (yitznofkha tzenefah) (Is. 22:18); *Yea, He will wind thee round and round* (ve-otekha ato) (Is. 22:17). The one who knows how the mitre is wrapped knows the meaning of [*The mitre shall be removed…*] *this shall be no more the same: that which is low shall be exalted, and that which is high abased* (Ezek. 21:31).¹⁶⁷ shall no longer be wound about the head. It takes a special skill to wind a mitre around the head. Now Scripture states, *And thou shalt set the mitre upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the mitre* (Ex. 29:6). The *tzitz* (plate) (v. 36) is thus called a *nezer* (crown).¹⁶⁸ (crown), as the *keter* covers the entire head. *But upon himself shall his crown* (nizro) *shine* (yatzitz) is similar (Ps. 132:18).¹⁶⁹ is used in connection with *nezer*. Perhaps they all¹⁷⁰ in our chapter and the word *yatzitz* in Ps. 132:18. are used in the sense of *tzitz*, meaning something seen. The same is true with the word *metzitz* (peereth) in *He peereth through the lattice* (Cant. 2:9). Note that the five senses come together in the two cavities which are in that part of the brain which is behind the forehead. This is where the imaginative power is located. Furthermore, all thoughts begin there. It is for this reason that Scripture writes, regarding the plate, that Aaron shall bear the iniquity *committed in the holy things* (v. 38). It is possible that those who hallowed holy things unto the Lord did so while thinking improper thoughts.¹⁷¹

ואמר הכתוב על כתנת אהרן בתחלה וכתונת תשבץ (למעלה פ' ד) שהיא משובצת לבדה ולא כן כתונת בניו, והתשבץ עשוי לכבוד אהרן, וככה אמר במעשה ויתן עליו הכתונת (ויקרא ח ז) הידוע, שהיא המשובצת, ועל בניו וילבישם כתנות (שם פ' יג), כמו ולבני אהרן תעשה כתנות (למטה פ' מ), ורב סעדיה תרגם ושבצת תעיין והוא כדמות צורת המטבע מרובע עשוי בתוך העגול:


AND THOU SHALT WEAVE THE TUNIC IN CHEQUER WORK. When Scripture first mentions Aaron’s tunic it says, a *tunic of chequer work* (v. 4). Only Aaron’s tunic was chequered. His sons’ tunics were not. The tunic was chequered to dignify Aaron. Scripture similar reads, *And he put upon him the tunic* (Lev. 8:7) when it describes Aaron’s investiture. It reads, *the tunic*,¹⁷², with the definite article. the reference being to the chequered tunic. However, concerning Aaron’s children we read, *and clothed them with tunics* (Lev. 8:13).¹⁷³ The latter is similar to *And for Aaron’s sons thou shalt make tunics* (v. 40).¹⁷⁴ Rabbi Saadiah Gaon translated *ve-shibatzta* (and thou shalt weave…in chequer work) as: you shall weave eye-like [designs].¹⁷⁵ as: you shall make the tunic eye-like (Weiser); that is, the tunic shall consist of eye-like designs. It is a coin-like design, that is, a square within a circle.¹⁷⁶

[Of FINE WHEATEN FLOUR.] The word *solet* (fine flour) refers to flour made from wheat cleansed of all impurities. It is called *samid* in Arabic.¹⁸ It is produced in the land of the Ishmaelites. There is no better bread than bread made from it.¹⁹ Many connect the word *solet* to the word *salita*²⁰. (thou hast trodden)²¹ in *Thou hast trodden light all them that err from Thy statutes* (Ps. 119:118);²² and to *sillah* (trodden) in *The Lord hath trodden All my mighty men in the midst of me* (Lam. 1:15).²³ means trodden grain, that is, grain that has been broken up into pieces (Krinsky). Kimchi accepted this definition of *solet*. They say that *makkolet* (food) in *food to your household* (I Kings 5:25)²⁴. is similar.²⁵ is connected to *salita* and *sillah*, then where does the *tav* in *solet* come from? For both *salita* and *sillah* come from the root *samekh, lamed, heh*. These commentaries therefore point out that we find something similar with the word *makkolet*. *Makkolet* comes from the root *kaf, lamed, heh* (Meijler). However, a form *tav* is added to it in its normal form. The same is true of the *tav* in *solet*. See Weiser and Meijler. Others say that *solet* means ground.²⁶

**ומלאת.** דעת המתרגם ארמית כמו ומלאו יָדָו (יחז' מג כו) רק מה נעשה במלת מלאו ידכם היום (למטה לב כט) והגאון פי' יד חיוב, ואחרים אמרו כי מלואים להיותם שלמים מלאים ורגילים והנה מה יעשו במלת ומלאו יָדָו (יחז' מג כו):


AND THOU SHALT CONSECRATE. The one who translated the Torah into Aramaic⁴⁴ is of the opinion that *u-milleta yad* (and thou shalt consecrate)⁴⁵ is similar to *u-milu yadav* (so shall they consecrate it)⁴⁶ on this verse. (Ezek. 43:26).⁴⁷ as *u-tekarev kurbana de-aharon ve-kurbana di-venohi* (and you shall offer the sacrifice of Aaron and the sacrifice of his children). However, what shall we do with *milu yedkhem ha-yom*⁴⁸ (consecrate yourselves today to the Lord) (Ex. 32:29)?⁴⁹ Saadiah Gaon explains the word *yad* to mean obligation.⁵⁰ means: see to it that Aaron and his sons fulfill their obligation. Thus according to the Gaon, to fill the hand means to do one’s duty. Others say that the term *melu’im* (consecration)⁵¹ is used because it indicates that they are complete, full, and trained.⁵² the priest learned…to train his hands in the service.” However, what will they do with *u-mile’u yadav* (so shall they consecrate it⁵³) (Ezek. 43:26)?⁵⁴

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:10:1)


**והקרבת.** כבר הזכיר זה והנה הטעם כאשר תקריב את הפר, יסמוך אהרן ובניו עליו, ויש אומרים, כי טעם וסמך אהרן לבדו, ואחר כן בניו, ועל האיל כתוב וסמכו אהרן ובניו (פ' טו) והנה הטעם כאשר היה שיסמכו יחדיו לא זה לפני זה:


AND THOU SHALT BRING THE BULLOCK. This has already been mentioned.⁵⁵ Its meaning is as follows. When you shall bring the bullock,⁵⁶ (and thou shalt bring) is to be rendered, when thou shalt bring. Hence Scripture is not being redundant. See note 57. Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon it.⁵⁷ Some say that the meaning of *and Aaron shall lay*⁵⁸ (shall lay) is in the singular. Hence the interpretation quoted by I.E. is: Aaron alone shall first lay his hands upon the head of the bullock. His sons shall then do the same. Now with regard to the ram, Scripture later states, *and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram* (v. 15). Scripture thus describes exactly what happened. They should lay their hands together, not one after the other.⁵⁹ (shall lay). *Ve-samekhu* is in the plural. The commentaries on I.E. differ over how to interpret this comment. Some take it to mean that I.E. indicates there was no difference in procedure between the laying of the hands upon the bullock and the laying of the hands upon the rams; in both cases Aaron and his sons put their hands upon the sacrificial animals in unison (Krinsky). Meijler is of the opinion that I.E. believes that in contrast to the laying of the hands upon the rams, Aaron first laid his hands upon the bullock and then his sons did the same. The difference of opinion revolves around how we interpret “Scripture thus describes exactly what happened.” Krinsky takes it to refer to both instances, while Meijler takes it to refer only to the second instance. For further elucidation, see Filwarg.

⁵⁷ This is not mentioned in verse 3.
⁵⁸ The text literally reads: and Aaron shall lay and his sons their hands on the head of the bullock. Ve-samakh
⁵⁹ For the text reads, ve-samekhu

### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:12:1)


**ישפוך.** הכהן השופך:


HE SHALL POUR OUT.⁶². In our text of the Pentateuch the reading is: Thou shalt pour out (*tishpokh*). Meijler and Krinsky believe that I.E.’s version of the Pentateuch reads *yishpokh* (he shall pour out). However, Weiser believes that the reading of *yishpokh* is due to a copyist’s error. According to Weiser, I.E. also reads *tishpokh* (thou shalt pour out), and I.E. commented thereupon: *Yishpokh ha-kohen ha-shofekh* (The priest who pours shall pour out). In other words, I.E. explained, that *Thou shalt pour* is not to be taken literally, for Moses was not commanded to personally pour out the blood. He was told to appoint a priest to carry out this task. Some copyist then dropped the word *tishpokh* from the heading and made *yishpokh* into a heading. Hence our reading. The priest who pours shall pour out.⁶³

footnotes:
⁶² Yishpokh
⁶³ All the remaining blood at the base of the altar. See note 63.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:13:2

וי"א כי נקראו כליות מגזרת נכספה וגם כלתה נפשי (תה' פד ג) כי שם כח התאוה למשגל:


[KIDNEYS.] Some say that *kelayot* (kidneys) are so called because the word *kelayot* is related to the word *kaletah* (pineth) in *My soul yearneth, yea even pineth for the courts of the Lord* (Ps. 84:3). For the power of sexual desire is located in the kidneys.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:14:1)


**ואת בשר.** כולל הראש והנתחים:


BUT THE FLESH OF THE BULLOCK. Flesh takes in the head and the pieces of the bullock.


###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Exodus/r/29:14:2)


**ופרשו.** דרך סברא ירחצוהו ואח"כ ישרפוהו והקטיר האמורים:


AND ITS DUNG.⁶⁵ 38. Also see Meijler. Logically speaking,⁶⁶ it⁶⁷ was to be washed and then it⁶⁸ is: and the place where the dung collected thou shalt burn. was to be burned.⁶⁹ (and its dung) to *u-lefi*. He interprets *But the flesh of the bullock* as follows: Flesh takes in the head and the pieces of the bullock. Now logically speaking, it was to be washed and then it was to be burned; i.e., the bullock was to be washed in the same manner that the ram (v. 17) was. See Weiser, Sarim, and Filwarg.. AND HE SHALL MAKE THEM SMOKE (*ve-hiktir*).⁷⁰ (and he shall make them smoke) does not appear in our verse. Weiser suggests that it has been transposed from verse 13. However, verse 13 reads *ve-hiktarta* (and make them smoke). Weiser explains that the original comment on verse 13 reads as follows: *Ve-hiktarta* (and [thou shalt] make them smoke). Commenting on this, I.E. writes: *Ve-hiktir* (and he shall make them smoke). That is, Moses himself was not commanded to personally place the organs on the fire; another priest would do as well. For some reason, a copyist left out the heading *ve-hiktarta* and the word *ve-hiktir* was transposed to verse 14. Meijler, on the other hand, claims that the word *ve-hiktir* should not be read as a heading but rather as the continuation of the previous sentence. The latter should read: Logically speaking, it was washed and then it was burned. After this, the priest smoked the enumerated organs. The reference is to the enumerated organs.⁷¹

**ומלת חטאת.** בעבור שהיא קרבה לכפר החטאת נקראת כן, וככה האשם על כן וחטאו את המזבח (יחז' מג כב) יסירו חטא מעליו:


[SIN-OFFERING.] A sin offering is called a *chatat* ⁷² because it is brought to atone for a sin. The same applies to the *asham* (guilt-offering).⁷³ Hence the meaning of *ve-chitte’u et ha-mizbe’ach* (they shall purify the altar)⁷⁴ is: they shall remove the sin from the altar.

THE GREAT TOE. The plural of *bohen* (great toe) is *behonot* (Jud. 1:6). This is grammatically inconsistent.⁸⁶ is *behanot*, not *behonot*. Compare, *goren, geranot*. The singular of *bahon* is *behonot* (Weiser). This noun is thus vocalized according to two paradigms.⁸⁷ There are many such nouns.

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:22:2

**שוק.** הצד הימין, והחזה נלקחו מאיל המלואים, והשוק והחזה יהיו מהיום נתונים לאהרן ולבניו מזבחי שלמי בני ישראל, רק החזה מאיל המלואים משה לבדו יאכלנו, כי הוא כהן הכהנים:


THE RIGHT THIGH. The thigh that is on the right side⁹³ (thigh) is feminine. Hence our verse should have read, *shok ha-yeminit*, rather than *shok ha-yamin* (the right side). Hence I.E. points out that *shok ha-yamin* is short for *shok tzad ha-yamin* (the thigh that is on the right side). *Tzad* is masculine. Hence the use of the masculine form *yamin*. and the breast were taken from the ram of consecration. From that day on, the thigh and the breast of peace offerings were to be given to Aaron and his sons.⁹⁴ However, Moses alone ate the breast of the ram of consecration because he was a high priest.⁹⁵

###### Ibn Ezra on Exodus 29:39:1

**את הכבש.** ה"א הכבש בעבור ה"א אחרת, כאלו הוא את הכבש האחד ור' משה הכהן אמר כי את הכבש כבש אחד:


THE ONE LAMB. The *heh* prefixed to the word *keves* (lamb) also serves as a prefix to the word *echad* (one).¹³¹ is ungrammatical. Hence I.E.’s comment. The phrase is to be read as if written, *et ha-keves ha-echad* (the one lamb).¹³². There too I.E. comments that the *heh* prefixed to the word *keves* also serves as a prefix to the word *echad* and that the phrase is to be read as if written *ha-keves ha-echad*. I.E. might have been commenting from memory and confused the two sections. However, Shadal, Meijler, and Filwarg believe that I.E. had a version of the Pentateuch in which Ex. 29:39 read: *et ha-keves echad*. Rabbi Moses Ha-Kohen says that the meaning of *et ha-keves echad* is, the lamb, one lamb.¹³³ is to be read as if written twice, that is, *et ha-keves, keves echad*. This comment is also repeated in Num. 28:4.

**עלת תמיד לדרתיכם.** יעשו ככה בבואם אל ארץ כנען כי לא הקריבו עולות רק חמשים יום במדבר סיני, וזהו עולת תמיד העשויה בהר סיני (במד' כח ו) כי המשכן הושם בתחתית ההר בקצה המחנה, כי מעורבים היו השבטים כי באחד לחדש השני החלו לדעת מספר כל שבט ושבט לעשותם דגלים, ואחר שנסעו דרך שלשת ימים מהר סיני היה הארון נוסע בתוך המחנות, ועל דרך הסברא לא הקריבו ישראל עולות וזבחים רק בסיני לבדו, ויום הכפורים בשנה השנית, כי כן כתוב על עבודת אהרן, ויעש כאשר צוה ד' את משה (ויקרא טז לד) וכן כתוב הזבחים ומנחה הגשתם לי בית ישראל ארבעים שנה במדבר (עמוס ה כה) כי ישראל עמדו במדבר בתהו יליל ישימון כמו שמונה ושלשים שנה, ומאין היה להם בכל יום חצי הין שמן זית, ג"כ יין, ואיך יוליכו עמהם כמו ארבעה עשר אלף הין, ומאין היה להם שני כבשים בני שנה בכל יום, ותוספת בשבת ובמועדים, ואין טענה ממלת אנחנו ובעירנו (במד' כ) כי בקדש היה, ושם בישוב קנו, ובזאת השנה שללו מדין וארץ סיחון ועוג, ויהי לכלם מקנה רב:


IT SHALL BE A CONTINUAL BURNT-OFFERING THROUGHOUT YOUR GENERATIONS. They shall bring these offerings when they enter the land of Canaan. For the Israelites offered burnt offerings only for fifty days in the desert of Sinai. This is what Scripture means by *It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai* (Num. 28:6). The tabernacle was placed at the edge of the camp at the bottom of the mount,¹³⁷ as the tribes were intermingled.¹³⁸ On the first day of the second month¹³⁹ they began to know the number of each tribe and to make standards (Num. 1 and 2).¹⁴⁰ After they traveled a distance of a three-day journey from Mount Sinai, the ark journeyed¹⁴¹ in the midst of the camps (Num. 10:33).¹⁴² (Num. 10:33). After that, it journeyed in their midst. See I.E. on Num. 10:31. Be that as it may, I.E.’s point is that after 50 days at Sinai, the ark was no longer in the tabernacle and thus no sacrifices were offered. See Filwarg. Logically speaking, the Israelites offered burnt offerings and sacrifices only at Sinai and on Yom Kippur in the second year. This is what Scripture states regarding Aaron’s service.¹⁴³ The Torah there writes, *And he* [Aaron] *did as the Lord commanded Moses* (Lev. 16:34).¹⁴⁴ Scripture similarly states, *Did ye bring unto Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel?* (Amos 5:25). Israel spent about thirty-eight years in a wasteland, in *a howling wilderness* (Deut. 32:10). Where did they get half a *hin* of olive oil and a half *hin* of wine daily?¹⁴⁵ How could they carry almost fourteen thousand *hin* around with them?¹⁴⁶ Where did they get two lambs daily in the first year? Where did they get the animals for the additional sacrifices on the Sabbath and the festivals? The statement *we and our cattle* (Num. 20:4)¹⁴⁷ does not refute our contention, for Israel was then at Kadesh,¹⁴⁸ and they bought cattle from the settled population. Furthermore, they looted the Midianites and the lands of Sihon and Og in that year. They thus had an abundance of cattle.¹⁴⁹

¹³⁸ The Israelites formed an amorphous mass. The only open space available for the tabernacle was at the edge of the camp.
¹³⁹ Of the second year following the Exodus.
¹⁴⁰ That is, it was only on the first day of the second month of the second year that the Israelites were organized into separate groups with their own place around standards, with the tabernacle in the center of the camp.
¹⁴¹ It is unlikely that Israel would offer sacrifices while the ark journeyed (Filwarg).
¹⁴² Of the 12 tribes of Israel. It is I.E.’s opinion that for the first three days of their journey from Sinai, the ark traveled before the camp
¹⁴³ That is, regarding the service which Aaron was to perform on Yom Kippur.

¹⁴⁷ Which shows that the Israelites had cattle.

**לכם.** לישראל, וככה קריאת העדה:


WITH YOU. Israel.¹⁵² (with you) is a plural. Hence I.E.’s comment. We find this to be the case when the congregation was called together.¹⁵³. So Meijler and Filwarg. According to Weiser its meaning is: Scripture uses the word *ve-no’adu* (shall gather themselves), which comes from the same root as *mo’ed* when it describes the gathering of the congregation. We thus see that the term *mo’ed* means gathering or meeting.

**ושכנתי.** יספר איך ישכון הכבוד בתוך בני ישראל בהקים הדגלים, כי ארבעת הדגלים היו בארבע הפאות, ומחיצה בין מחנה לויה למחנה ישראל כי גם הם היו לארבע הפאות ואחר כן מחיצה, ושם האהל בתוך בני ישראל, והנה בעל קרי לא יצא ממחנה ישראל גם יד לא היה להם לשבת חוץ לתחום, רק המצוה באה על מחנה ישראל בצאתו למלחמה על האויב, וכן כי תצא מחנה (דבר' כג, י) לא ידבר על מחנה כל ישראל אנשים נשים וטף, כי היוצאים למלחמה הם זכרים ומעטים, והנה בנשאם הארון עמהם כאשר עשה פנחס לא יכלו לעשות מחיצה למקום הארון:


AND I WILL DWELL. Scripture describes how God’s glory will dwell among the children of Israel when the standards will be set up.¹⁶³ Four standards were set up on the four sides.¹⁶⁴ Additionally, there was a separation between the camp of the Levites and the camp of the Israelites¹⁶⁵ because they too camped on all four sides,¹⁶⁶ There was another barrier beyond this barrier where the tent of meeting was placed amidst the children of Israel. Now a person who experienced a seminal emission did not have to leave the camp of Israel.¹⁶⁷ Neither was there a place set aside beyond the border of the camp for a person to sit down [and relieve himself].¹⁶⁸ The commandment for a person who experienced a seminal emission to leave the camp¹⁶⁹ applied only to the camp of Israel when it went to war against the enemy.¹⁷⁰ The commandment *When thou goest forth in camp against thine enemies* (Deut. 23:10) similarly does not speak of the entire camp of Israel, men, women, and children. It is only males, and then only a small number of them, who sally out to wage war. Now when the soldiers of Israel carried the ark with them as Phineas did,¹⁷¹ they were unable to set up a barrier between themselves and the place of the ark.¹⁷²
