###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 5:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:3:2)


**כי אתנו אנחנו.** והטעם כי גם אתנו כמו לא יקרא שמך עוד יעקב. או טעמו לא כרת עם אבותינו שהיו במצרים רק אתנו כרת הברית כי רבים יש במחנ' ששמעו הברית מפי השם על כן אמר אנחנו אלה שהם פה והם חיים והעד על יושר זה הפירוש שאמר עמכם וביניכם:


BUT WITH US, EVEN US. The meaning of *ittanu*⁵ (even us) is, but also with us.⁶). I.E. believes that this should be interpreted: The Lord made not this covenant with our fathers alone, but also with us. In other words, *ittanu* (us) should be interpreted as if written *gam* (also) *ittanu*. It is similar to *thy name shall not be called any more Jacob* (Gen. 35:10).⁷ should be read as if written, Thy name shall not be called any more only Jacob. See I.E. on Gen. 35:10 (Vol. 1, p. 332). Or it means the Lord did not make a covenant with our fathers who were in Egypt but only with us,⁸ for there were many in the camp who heard the covenant from the mouth of God.⁹ Moses therefore said even us, those who are here, and are alive. Moses’ words, *with you* (v. 4) and [*I stood*] *between* [*the Lord*] *and you* (v. 5) is proof of the correctness of this interpretation.

ומלת **לאמר.** דבקה עם דבר ה' עמכם בהר מתוך האש לאמר ויתכן להיות פירוש אנכי עומד בין ה' אחר מעמד הר סיני והטעם שהוא דבר עמכם פנים בפנים ומאותו היום הייתי אני עומד בין ה' וביניכם כי יראתם כאשר יפרש:


[SAYING.] The word *saying* is connected to the previous verse. Its meaning is, *The Lord spoke with you face to face…out of the midst of the fire* (v. 4) *saying*.¹³, etc. It is possible that *I stood between the Lord and you* means I stood between the Lord and you after the revelation at Sinai. Its meaning is, God spoke with you face to face [at Sinai] and from that day on I stood between the Lord and you because you were afraid,¹⁴ as Moses goes on to explain.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 5:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:5:4)


**ולא עליתם בהר.** כאשר עליתי אני ומשה נגש אל הערפל ואל תשים אל לבך בעבור היות מלת לאמר רחוקה כי כן רבים והמדבר לא הפסיק הפסוקי' ולא הפרשיות גם אל תשית לב אל המלות כי הם כגופות והטעמים כרוחות והכורת בשני כלים זה כמו זה במעשה מעשה אחד הוא על כן שוא ושקר כי הם אחים וכל שקר שוא וכבר פירשתי זכור שהוא כמו שמור. והוסיף כאשר צוך ה' אלהיך והטעם במעמד הר סיני:


AND WENT NOT UP INTO THE MOUNT. When I went up. Compare, *but Moses drew near unto the thick darkness* (Ex. 20:18). Do not pay attention to the fact that the word *saying* is far removed [from the end of verse 4],¹⁵ for there are many such instances.¹⁶ The speaker¹⁷ did not separate the verses and sections.¹⁸ Also do not pay attention to the words,¹⁹ for they are like bodies and their meanings are like souls.²⁰ One who cuts with two similar tools produces the same result. Scripture therefore interchanges *shav* (false)²¹ (v. 17) and *sheker* (false) (Ex. 20:13),²² (ed shaker). Deut. 5:17 reads: *Neither shalt thou bear* false/vain *witness* (ed shav). as these terms are brothers.²³ All lies are vanity. I have already explained that the word *zakhor* (remember) (v. 8) means the same as *shamor* (keep).²⁴ (zakhor) *the sabbath day to keep it holy*. Deut. 5:12 reads: *Remember* (shamor) *the sabbath day to keep it holy*. Hence I.E.’s comment. Moses adds,²⁵ is not found in Exodus. Hence I.E.’s comment. *as the Lord thy God commanded thee* (v. 12). It means, when you stood around Mount Sinai.²⁶ is keep the Sabbath as God commanded you at Sinai when he revealed the Decalogue.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 5:16:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 5:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:16:2)


**ימיך.** באר שיהיו טובים. דע כי דעת כל הקדמונים כי הדבור הראשון הוא אנכי ואם יש לשאול למה הפסיק המפסיק לא יהיה לך וכבר פיר' עשרת הדברים כי סמכתי על דעתם רק הישר בעיני שמלת אנכי איננ' מהעשר' כי דבור אנכי הוא המצוה ועיקר המצות כאשר פירשתי כבר:


THY DAYS. Scripture goes on to explain that they will be good days.³⁸ elaborates on *that thy days may be long*; i.e., your long days will be good days. Know that all the early sages are of the opinion that *I am* (v. 6) is the first statement³⁹ even though there is room to ask why the one who separated the statements did not separate *Thou shalt have no other gods* (v. 7).⁴⁰. The Decalogue is divided into ten sections in the massoretic edition of the Torah. Each of these sections is devoted to a particular statement. Now, if *I am* is an independent statement, it should form an independent section. However, it does not. Hence *I am* seems to be an introduction to that which follows. We have followed *Vat. Ebr*. 38 which reads *lo hifsik*. I have already explained the Ten Statements,⁴¹ is the first of the Ten Statements. See I.E.’s comments on Ex. 20:1 in both the long and the short commentary. See Vol. 2, pp. 401-404. relying on their opinion.⁴² However, I believe that the statement *I am* is not part of the Ten Statements, for the meaning of *I am* is, I am the one who commands. *I am* is the basis of the commandments, as I have explained previously.⁴³ includes all precepts directed at the heart, tongue, and human deeds. For one who does not believe in his heart that God exists has no reason to be obligated to observe any commandments” (I.E., Vol. 2, p. 415).

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 5:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/5:18:1)


ומלת **חמד** בלשון הקדש מתפרשת לשני טעמים האחד גזל ועושק וקחת של אחרים בחזקה ובאונס וכך ולא יחמוד איש את ארצך כי אם אין פירושו כן הנה תהיה הארץ רעה ולא בא הכתוב אלא לשבח והטעם השני לשון תאוה בלב ולא תצא לפועל. והנה לא תחמוד בית רעך. הדבור התשיעי. ולא תחמוד אשת רעך הדבור העשירי. ויהיה בית רעך ואשת רעך נדבקים זה עם זה או בית רעך כלל והעד שאמר משה בספר הזה שבאר את התורה תחת לא תחמוד אמר לא תתאוה. ורבים אמרו כי אין עון במחשבת הלב ואין עליהם שכר ועונש ויש ראיות רבות להשיב עליהן ולא אאריך רק אראה להם לב חורש מחשבות און הטיבות כי היה עם לבבך ולישרים בלבותם ומשה אמר בסוף בפיך ובלבבך לעשותו. ועיקר כל המצות ליישר הלב, ורובם זכר והמזיד והשוגג יוכיחו:


The word *chamad* (coveted) has two meanings in Hebrew.⁴⁴ (neither shalt thou covet). One is to rob, to extort, to take someone’s property by force and compulsion. This is the meaning of the word in *neither shall any man covet* (yachmod) *thy land*⁴⁵ (yachmod) *thy land* means no one shall desire your land, then the Land of Israel would be an undesirable land. Hence the meaning of *neither shall any man covet* (yachmod) *thy land* must be no one will take your land. (Ex. 34:24). For if this is not its meaning, then the land is bad. But Scripture only comes to praise the land. The second meeting is to desire in the heart without acting.⁴⁶ Now, *Neither shalt thou covet thy neighbor’s house* (Ex. 20:14) is the ninth statement, and *thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife* (*Ibid.*) is the tenth statement.⁴⁷ as the first statement of the Decalogue. Therefore, it counts *Neither shalt thou covet thy neighbor’s house* and *thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife* as two separate statements. According to this interpretation, *thy neighbor’s house* and *thy neighbor’s wife* are connected to each other.⁴⁸ precedes *thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife*, while the reverse is true in Deuteronomy (Weiser). On the other hand, *thy neighbor’s house* might be a general rule.⁴⁹ is the tenth statement. Scripture first states the general rule and then goes into detail; that is, *Neither…thy neighbor’s house* includes your neighbor’s wife, servant, ox, ass, and all that he owns. According to this interpretation, *I am* is the first statement and *Neither shalt thou covet thy neighbor’s house* is the tenth. The fact that Moses in this book [Deuteronomy] in which he explains the Torah, employs *ve-lo*⁵⁰. *titavveh* (neither shalt thou covet) (v. 18) in place of *lo tachmod* (thou shalt not covet) (Ex. 20:14) is proof of this.⁵¹ is a general statement, for Moses explains it by using a different term in Deuteronomy. Many say that one cannot sin with one’s thoughts and there is no reward and punishment for what one thinks. However, one can refute them by quoting many verses. I will not prolong my argument. I will merely point to the following: *A heart that deviseth wicked thoughts* (Prov. 6:18); *thou didst well that it was in thy heart* (II Chron. 6:8); *And to them that are upright in their hearts* (Ps. 125:4). Moses at the end⁵² said, *in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it* (Deut. 30:14). The main purpose of the *mitzvot* is to perfect the heart. Most of them serve as a memorial.⁵³, translated by H. Norman Strickman, Jason Aaronson, 1995, p. 78: “Some commandments serve as reminders of the fundamental precepts. For example, the Sabbath commemorates creation. Likewise, not permitting one’s slave to work on the Sabbath recalls the Exodus from Egypt. Similarly, the Pascal lamb, the *matzot*, the bitter herbs, the *sukkah*, the *mezuzah*, and the *tefillin* worn on the hand and head. Likewise, the *tzitzit.”* The distinction made between a sin committed deliberately and one committed inadvertently should convince them.⁵⁴

**מי יתן.** אין הכתוב או' מי יתן לי רק מי יתן להם ע״‎כ נכתב להם אחר והיה לבבם זה ודע כי שורש כל המעשים והתנועות גזרות השם וכל הנמצאים תחת השמים כחם ותולדותם כפי המערכ' העליונה עם השרשים למטה וכן עם המורכבים וכן כפי תנועתם יום יום ועת ועת כי לעולם יהיה שנוי כאשר פירש בעל ספר יצירה והחלקים יקבלו מהכללים כפי תולדותם ובעבור כח הכללים יוכלו לשנות מעט בתולדת וזה טעם ויחזק ה' את לב פרעה ובמקום אחר ויכבד לבו הוא ועבדיו והכל אמת על כן אומר ידעתי ה' כי לא לאדם דרכו ואומר למה תתענו ה' מדרכך ומשה אמר ובחרת בחיים ואחר שהשם לא ימנע טוב הנה הוא אוהב להיטיב ואמר הכתוב כלשון בני אדם מי יתן:


OH THAT. Scripture does not say *mi yitten li* (oh that I) but rather *mi yitten la-hem* (oh that they).⁶⁵ is Israel not God. The word *la-hem* (they) thus follows *ve-hayah levavam zeh* (such a heart as this).⁶⁶ (oh that they). This literally reads, Oh that such a heart as this to them. I.E. believes that this should be read as if written, *mi yitten la-hem ve-hayah levavam zeh lahem* (oh that they had such a heart as this). Note, God’s decrees are the source of all actions and movements.⁶⁷ The power and nature of all that is found beneath the heavens is determined by the arrangement of the heavenly bodies. These are connected to the roots below.⁶⁸ The same applies to the compounds.⁶⁹ All things similarly depend on the movements of the heavenly bodies day by day and time by time, for there is always a change,⁷⁰, p. 173). as the author of the *Sefer Yetizrah* explained.⁷¹ is a mystical work composed between the third and sixth centuries either in the Land of Israel or in Babylonia. The parts⁷² receive⁷³ from the categories⁷⁴ according to their nature.⁷⁵ It is due to the power of the “categories” that they⁷⁶ can make some small changes in nature.⁷⁷ This is the meaning of *and the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart* (Ex. 11:10).⁷⁸ In another place, Scripture states, *and hardened his heart, he and his servants* (Ex. 9:34).⁷⁹ It is all true. Scripture therefore states, *O Lord, I know that man’s way is not his own* (Jer. 10:23). It similarly states, *O Lord, why dost Thou make us to err from Thy ways* (Jer. 63:17). Moses said, *therefore choose life* (Deut. 30:19).⁸⁰ Now, since God does not withhold good,⁸¹ He loves to do good. Scripture employs human language when it says, *Oh that*.⁸²

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 6:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:4:1)


ומה שהעתיקו קדמונינו ז״‎ל על ק״‎ש הוא האמת ואין צורך לחפש דע כי זה השם הנכבד הוא שם העצם ואם כן מה טעם לאמרו פעם שנית והתשובה כי אדם שם עצם ושם מקרה שאיננו כן ואם הוא נקרא מעצם האדמה וכן זה והעד השם שהוא סמוך אל צבאות או העיקר הוא אלהינו ונכפל כמו כן לומר אחד והטעם לבדו וראיות עד אין חקר יש כי השם אחד והפסוק שאמר ביום ההוא יהיה ה' אחד על מחשבות בני אדם והנכון בעיני שהוא דבק עם מלך כי כן כתוב והיה ה' למלך על כל הארץ ביום ההוא יהיה ה' מלך אחד ושמו אחד כטעם כי אז אהפוך אל עמים שפה ברורה והנה כל העולם ידברו שפה אחת על כן יהיה שם ה' אחד:


HEAR O ISRAEL: THE LORD (*YHVH*) OUR GOD, THE LORD (*YHVH*) IS ONE.] That which the ancients, of blessed memory, transmitted regarding the reading of the *shema* is true,⁵ (shema), *O Israel*, morning and evening. and there is no need for further investigation. Note that the glorious name (*YHVH*) is a noun.⁶ This being the case, why is it said a second time?⁷) our God is one. It should be noted that I.E. comments elsewhere that it is biblical style to repeat nouns in the same verse. See I.E. on Gen. 19:24, (Vol. 1, p. 208) and on Ps. 1:2. The answer is that Adam is a noun. Adam is also an adjective, and not a noun,⁸ even though⁹). he was called after the very earth. The same is true of the name *YHVH*.¹⁰ The fact that *YHVH* is connected to *tzeva’ot* (hosts)¹¹ (the Lord of hosts) (Is. 1:9). is proof.¹² is in the construct with *tzeva’ot*, whereas a proper name cannot come in the construct. See I.E. on Ex. 3:15 (Vol. 2, p. 65). On the other hand, the term *Elohenu* (our God) might be the object.¹³ is our God. The name *YHVH* was repeated in order to state *YHVH echad* (the Lord is one) the meaning of which is, only *YHVH*.¹⁴ is our God, it goes on to say that only *YHVH* is our God. There are many proofs that *YHVH* alone is God.¹⁵ The verse that states, *In that day shall the Lord be One* (echad)¹⁶ (Zech. 14:9), speaks of men’s thoughts.¹⁷ In my opinion, the word one¹⁸ is connected to the word king, for Scripture writes: *And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; In that day shall the Lord* alone be King *and His name one* (Zech. 14:9).¹⁹. I.E.’s interpretation eliminates the implication that today there are more gods than *YHVH*, for it speaks of all people recognizing one king, i.e., the Lord. The latter is similar in meaning to *For then will I turn to the peoples, A pure language, That they may all call upon the name of the Lord* (Zeph. 3:9}. Behold, all the nations will speak one language. The name of the Lord will therefore be one.

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 6:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:6:1)


**והיו הדברים האלה.** אמרו המכחשים על עשרת הדברות ועליהם נאמר וכתבתם על מזוזות ביתך והאמת כל המצות:


AND THESE WORDS…SHALL BE. Those who deny the Rabbinic tradition²⁸ say that the reference is to the Decalogue, and that it is in reference to the Decalogue that Scripture states, *And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts* (v. 9). However, the truth is that *and these words…shall be* refers to all of the commandments.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 6:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:7:1)


**ושננתם.** מגזרת חץ שנון. וידוע איך ישונן החץ הנה נרא' כי עיקר כל האדם עבודת השם ועבודתו להכיר פעליו והמעתיקי' העתיקו שעת ק״‎ש וכלנו נסמוך עליהם:


AND THOU SHALT TEACH THEM. *Ve-shinantam* (and thou shalt teach them) is related to the word *shanun* (sharp) in *and a sharp arrow* (Prov. 25:18). The method of sharpening an arrow is well known.²⁹ Observe. Our verse teaches that the main purpose of man is to serve God.³⁰ God’s service consists in recognizing God’s works.³¹, the reference is to the study of the Torah (see Weiser). However, it should be noted that in I.E., study of God’s works usually refers to the study of the sciences. Thus I.E. writes: “When one masters astronomy and the circuits of the [sun and. moon], he comes to know the works of God the glorious” (*The Secret of the Torah*, p. 21). Perhaps I.E. is alluding here to his belief that the Torah cannot be fully understood unless it is interpreted in light of the studies of science (see *The Secret of the Torah*, pp. 33,34). However, the transmitters of tradition taught that [our verse] refers to the time of reading the *shema*.³² means that we should read the *shema* at night, and *when thou risest up* refers to the reading of the *shema* in the morning. See chapter 1 of *Mishnah Berakhot*. We all rely on them.

### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 6:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/6:25:1)


**וצדקה תהיה לנו.** י״‎א מכאן רמז לשכר המצות לעוה״‎ב ולפי הפשט כי מדרך הצדקה חייבים אנחנו לשמור את רצונו כי הוא אדוננו והנכון בעיני כי כל הגוים יראו שאנחנו צדיקים בשמרנו מצותיו וחקיו שהם צדיקים כי כן כתוב:


AND IT SHALL BE RIGHTEOUSNESS UNTO US. Some say that this verse hints at the reward in the world to come for the observance of the commandments.⁵⁰. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, our verse teaches that following God’s will is the righteous thing to do, for He is our Master. I believe that the correct meaning is, all the nations shall see that we are righteous when we keep God’s commandments and statutes, which Scripture clearly states are righteous.⁵¹

**אל פניו.** הטעם לעצמו. וי״‎א כמו בפניו בכעסו והטעם כי ישלם לשונאיו בעבור ששנאו האמת:


TO THEIR FACE. *Be-fanav* (to their face) means to him.²² Others say that *el panav* (their face) has the meaning of *befanav*, that is, because of His anger.²³ is to be rendered His anger. See I.E. on Deut. 4:37. Its means that God will repay the wicked because they hated the truth.²⁴

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 7:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/7:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/7:10:3)


**להאבידו לא יאחר לשונאו.** י״‎א כי הטעם ישלם לרשע גמול טוב שעשה בעוה״‎ז ולא יאחר לתת לו בעוה״‎ב והנכון בעיני שהוא כנגד אוהביו שהם עומדים לאלף דור שונאיו יאבדו והוסיף לא יאחר שיחשוב שיעמוד בנו או בן בנו כטעם על שלשים ועל רבעים:


TO DESTROY THEM; HE WILL NOT BE SLACK TO HIM THAT HATETH HIM. Some say that the meaning of our verse is that God rewards the wicked for his good deeds in this world and does not wait to reward him in the world to come.²⁵, 22a; Onkelos and Rashi. However, it appears to me that our verse contrasts the righteous²⁶ who will exist²⁷ for a thousand generations with the wicked²⁸ who will be destroyed. Scripture reads, *He will not be slack* because the wicked person thinks that his son or grandson shall live,²⁹ as in [*visiting the iniquity of the fathers*] *upon the children, and upon the children’s children* (Ex. 33:7).³⁰

²⁶ Literally, ones who love God.
²⁷ By living on through their children.
²⁸ Literally, ones who hate Him.
²⁹ And receive the punishment due him.
³⁰ Hence the Torah states that the wicked themselves shall receive the punishment due them.

**עקב.** כמו לעולם עקב שכר באחרונה וטעם הפסוק הראשון שומר הברית ששמר ברית אברהם ואתם אם תהיו מאוהביו ישמור עוד הברית ואם היית מאוהביו ואהבך וברכך והרבך זה פירוש הברית והחסד:


BECAUSE. *Ekev* (because) has the same meaning as *ekev* (reward) in *For ever, reward*³¹ (Ps. 119:112). It means the reward which will be given at the end. The meaning of *who keepeth covenant* in the previous verse (v. 9) is that God kept the covenant with Abraham. If you will be among those that love Him, then He will continue to keep the covenant.³² in our verse is, God will continue to keep the covenant if you love him. If you will be among those who love Him, then *He will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee* (v. 13). This is the meaning of *the covenant and the mercy* (v. 12).

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 7:13:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/7:13:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/7:13:5)


**ועשתרות.** כמו עדרים ומפרש גדול היה בספרד והוציא טעם למה קראו העברים הבקר בשם אלף והצאן בעשתרות וכן היה מפרש הבעלים ועשתרות בעל המזל הצומח והעשירי ועוד לא די שיברך פרי בטנך כי לא יהיה בך עקר שאין זרעו מוליד וכן בבהמתך כי עוד תהיה בריא מכל מין חולי ידוע להיות כמנהג העולם **וכל מדוי.** שהיו חוץ המנהג:


AND THE YOUNG OF. *Ashterot* (and the young of) means and the flocks of. There was a great commentator in Spain³⁷ who explained why the Hebrews referred to cattle as *alef*³⁸ (thy kine) and in *alufenu* (oxen). and to sheep and goats as *ashterot*. He similarly explained the *ba’alim* and the *ashtaroth* (Jud. 10:6) as referring to the lord of the flowering constellation³⁹, p. 202). This constellation is the first (*alef*) in the sky and its ruling planet, its lord (*ba’al*) was believed to have a powerful affect on fertility. and that of the tenth.⁴⁰, and *adar* when most of the sheep and cattle are born. Scripture goes on to say God will not only bless the fruit of your body but there will not be a barren male, that is, one whose seed is infertile, among you or among your cattle. Furthermore, you will be healthy and avoid all sorts of well-known illnesses which normally befall people. You will similarly avoid abnormal, evil diseases.⁴¹

³⁷ I.E. does not identify the commentator.
³⁸ As in alafekha
³⁹ The planet which rules over “the ascent, the zodiacal sign appearing on the eastern horizon at a certain moment” (I. Efros, Studies in Medieval Jewish Philosophy
⁴⁰ The tenth constellation, Capricorn, which rules during the months of tevet, shevat
⁴¹ Hence the mention of the diseases of Egypt.

### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 7:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/7:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/7:24:1)


**השמדך.** שם הפעל ואם הוא בחירק יתכן היות כמוהו השאיר לו שריד והעד אותם שהוא הפעול:


THOU HAST DESTROYED THEM. *Hishmidekha* (thou has destroyed them) is an infinitive even though it is vocalized with a *chirik*.⁴⁵ beneath the *heh. Hishmidekha* is a *hifil*. In such cases the *heh* is normally vocalized with a *pattach* in the infinitive. Compare, *hashmid*. The word *hishir*⁴⁶ (left him remaining) in *until there was none left him remaining* (Num. 22:35) is most likely similar to it. The word *otam* (them), which is the object,⁴⁷. proves that *hishmidekha* is an infinitive.⁴⁸ is a third person (*hishmid*) plus the second person pronoun. Its meaning is, he destroyed you. However, with the word *otam* following, it is an infinitive, meaning you destroy them.

⁴⁶ Which is a hifil.

⁴⁸ Hishmidekha

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 8:3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/8:3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/8:3:6)


**מוצא פי ה'.** כמו מה שגזר כמו הדבר יצא מפי המלך והטעם כי על הלחם לבדו לא יחיה האדם רק הכח או עם הכח הבא מהעליונים במצות השם וזה פי' מוצא פי ה' והעד שלא אכלתם לחם וחייתם:


EVERY THING THAT PROCEEDETH OUT OF THE MOUTH OF THE LORD. It means that which God has decreed. Compare, *As the word went out of the king’s mouth* (Esth. 7:8). The meaning of our verse is, man does not live by bread alone but by the power,¹¹ or with the power, which comes from on high¹² refers to the power to nourish which God placed in all foodstuffs. According to the second interpretation the verse refers to divine providence. The latter was demonstrated by the manna which came from on high. by the command of God. This is the meaning of *that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord*. The fact that you did not eat bread and you lived is proof of this.

footnotes:
¹¹ In the nature of the food. In other words, God created the world in such a way that man can exist on all types of food. For I.E.’s use of the word “power” in the sense of nature, see I.E. on Deut. 5:26.
¹² See I.E. on Deut. 5:26: “The power and nature of all that is found beneath the heavens is determined by the upper arrangement.” According to I.E.’s first comment, everything that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 9:22:1

**ובתבערה.** יתכן להיותו שם מקום ולא חנו שם כי אם יום א' על כן לא הזכירום באלה מסעי והוא א' משלשה מסעים שנסעו מהד סיני עד קברות התאו' כאשר פירשתי. וטעם לחבר תבערה עם מסה כי היו העם מתאוננים כמו מנסים לשם והזכיר תבערה קודם מסה כי במסה לא אירע להם כלום וי״‎א כי בא עמלק בעבור שנסו השם ועל כן הזכיר בעירת אש השם בהם וזנוב עמלק ומכת המתאוים הזכיר בתחלה הקשה וי״‎א כי תבערה היא מסה כמו מראש שניר וחרמון והנכון מה שפירשתי:


AND AT TABERAH. Taberah is probably the name of a place. Israel camped there for but one day. Therefore Scripture does not mention it¹⁵. 38. The printed texts read “them,” in place of “it.” in the Torah portion *Elleh Mase* (These Are the Stages) (Num. 33:1).¹⁶ It is one of the thirty journeys that Israel traveled from Mount Sinai until they came to Kibroth-hattaavah (Num. 33:17),¹⁷ as I explained.¹⁸ The reason Scripture connects Taberah with Massah¹⁹ is that the people *were as murmurers* (Num. 11:1);²⁰ that is, they tested God.²¹ Scripture mentions Taberah before Massah²² because nothing happened to Israel at Massah.²³ Some say that Amalek came²⁴ because Israel tested God.²⁵ Scripture therefore mentions²⁶ the burning of God’s fire among them,²⁷ Amalek’s smiting of Israel’s hindmost,²⁸ and the smiting of those who lusted.²⁹ Scripture mentions the most severe punishments first.³⁰ Some say that Taberah and Massah are one and the same place.³¹ (These Are the Stages) (Num. 33:1). It is like *From the top of Senir and Hermon* (Cant. 4:8).³² However, my interpretation is correct.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 10:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/10:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/10:1:2)


**ארון עץ.** אמרו המעתיקים ז״‎ל כי ארון אחר עשה משה בתחלה והעד ואעש ארון ואח״‎כ אמר ואפסול ואמר ואשים את הלוחות בארון אשר עשיתי ודעתם רחבה מדעתנו כי היה נראה לנו כי וישכון כבוד ה' דבק עם הכבוד שראו הזקנים ולא נדע מתי עלה משה כי היה נראה בדרך הפשט כי משה לא נתענה כי אם שמונים יום כי פי' אנכי עמדתי בהר כימים הראשונים הוא שנוי והטעם כאשר עמדתי בהר אותם הארבעים יום שמע ה' אלי ואמר לך למסע וזהו לך נחה את העם והנה יהי' ארון עץ בצווי והוא הארון שעשה בצלאל:


AN ARK OF WOOD. The transmitters of tradition,² of blessed memory, said that Moses first³, Ex. 1:10, and Rashi. made another ark.⁴ Proof of the latter is, *So I made an ark* (v. 3), which is followed by *and hewed two tables of stone* (v. 3) *and put the tables in the ark which I had made* (v. 5). Now their minds are superior to our minds, for it appears to us⁵ that *And the glory of the Lord abode* (Ex. 24:16) is connected with the glory which the elders saw (Ex. 24:10).⁶ cloud…*And Moses entered in the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount; and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights*. According to the rabbis this verse relates to the giving of Torah (see Rashi on Ex. 24:16). Also, according to the rabbis, the forty days which this verse states Moses spent on the mountain starts with the seventh of Sivan. There are 120 days between that day and Yom Kippur when, according to Rabbinic tradition, Moses descended with the second pair of tablets. Moses thus spent 120 days on Mount Sinai. See *Pirke de-Rabbi Eliezer*, chapter 46. I.E. disagrees. He believes that the plain meaning of the text does not allow one to conclude that Moses spent 120 days on Mount Sinai. The text merely says that the elders of Israel ascended Mount Sinai and had a vision of God (Ex. 24:1-12). It does not say which day they descended. Following this vision the cloud covered the mountain for seven days, after which God called Moses to ascend the mountain for 40 days. We thus do no know what day Moses ascended the mountain, and therefore, cannot calculate 120 days between revelation and Yom Kippur. Thus Moses did not necessarily spend 120 days on Mount Sinai. We do not know when Moses ascended,⁷ for according to the plain meaning of the text it appears that Moses fasted for only eighty days,⁸ is not a repetition of Deut. 9:25 but speaks of an additional 40 days. Furthermore, *as the first time forty days and forty nights* indicates that as he fasted the first time, so did he now. for the meaning of *Now I stayed in the mount* (v. 10) repeats what was said earlier.⁹ It means when I stayed on the mountain during those forty days¹⁰ God listened to me and said, *Arise, go before the people* (v. 11), the reference being to *And now go, lead the people* (Ex. 32:34). The making of the ark of wood (v. 3) was thus by command.¹¹ is to be interpreted, I commanded that an ark of wood be made. It refers to the ark made by Bezalel.¹²

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 10:3:1

**ואעש ארון.** בצווי ויהיה פי' ויקהל משה וכבר הקהיל משה וכבר הראיתיך רבים כן וכל זה בעבור שאמר ויהיו שם כאשר צוני ה' וזהו ונתת אל הארון את העדות גם יתכן להיות פירושו על ועשית לך ארון עץ והקבלה תנצח:

By command.¹³ The meaning of *And Moses assembled* (Ex. 35:1) should be interpreted, and Moses had assembled.¹⁴ as And Moses had assembled Israel; that is, Moses gathered Israel and commanded them to make the tabernacle before he ascended Mount Sinai a second time to receive the second tablets. I have already shown you many such instances.¹⁵ All of this is necessitated¹⁶ by Scripture’s statement, *and there they are, as the Lord commanded me* (v. 5).¹⁷ This¹⁸. is what *And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony* (Ex. 25:16) refers to. It is also possible that it¹⁹ (v. 5). refers to *and make thee an ark of wood*.²⁰ The tradition of the sages shall triumph.

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 10:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/10:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/10:6:1)


**ובני ישראל נסעו מבארות בני יעקב מוסרה.** נכנס זה הפסוק במקום הזה בעבור שאמר ואתפלל גם בעד אהרן בעת ההיא ואמר כי לא מת אהרן רק בשנת הארבעים והעד שכן פירושו שאמר בעת ההיא הבדיל ה' את שבט לוי וזה היה בהר סיני כאשר פירשתי בפרשת וידבר וקדמונינו אמרו שנסעו לאחור ומה נעש' במלת שם מת אהרן ויקבר שם ור' יצחק אבן גיאת ז״‎ל הספרדי פי' שם כמו אז וכמוהו משם רוע' ואין צורך רק לפי דעתי כי מבארות בני יעקן איננו בני יעקן גם מוסרה איננו מוסרות רק קדש יקרא בארות בני יעקן ושם מדבר הר ההר מוסרה ורבים כן הלא תראה הכתוב אמר מדבר שור ובפסוק אחר מדבר איתם:


AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL JOURNEYED FROM BEEROTH-BENEJAAKAN TO MOSERAH; THERE AARON DIED. This verse is placed here²¹ because Moses said, *And I prayed for Aaron also the same time* (Deut. 9:20).²², Moses indicated that Aaron did not go along with those who worshipped the calf. Moses indicated that Aaron did not die until the fortieth year (Num. 33:38).²³ Moses’ statement, *At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi* (v. 8), which took place at Mount Sinai²⁴ as I explained in the Torah portion which opens with *And The Lord Spoke* (Num. 1:1),²⁵ is proof that this is its meaning.²⁶ The early authorities²⁷ tell us that Israel backtracked.²⁸, chapter 1, Hal. 10; *Yoma*, Chap 1, Hal. 1; *Seder Olam*, chapter 9. However, what shall we do with the clause, *there Aaron died, and there he was buried*?²⁹ Rabbi Isaac ibn Giat the Spaniard,³⁰ of blessed memory, says that the meaning of *sham* (there) is then.³¹ He says that *mi-sham* (from thence) in *misham ro’eh* (from thence, from the shepherd) (Gen. 49:24) is similar. There is no need for this interpretation. On the contrary, I believe that Beeroth-benejaakan is not to be identified with Bene-jaakkan; neither is Moserah the same as Moserot (Num. 33:31).³² In reality Kadesh³³ is called the wilderness of Beeroth-benejaakan, and the wilderness of Mount Hor is called Moserah.³⁴ There are many such examples.³⁵ Do you not see that Scripture says the wilderness of Shur (Ex. 15:22)? However, in another place Scripture refers to it as the wilderness of Etam (Num. 33:18).³⁶

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 10:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/10:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/10:7:2)


ו**יטבתה** הוא המקום הנקרא באר כי כן כתוב ומשם בארה וזה טעם **ארץ נחלי מים** כי במשענותם כרו הנדיבים ויצאו המים וזה הפסוק שהוא ומשם נסעו הגדגדה דבק עם ויכהן אלעזר והנה פירשתי לך כי ישראל לא הקריבו זבחים אחר נסעם מהר סיני ויתכן שהקריבום בבואם אל צלמונה ופונן והיתה תחלת כהונת אלעזר בכהונה גדולה באותם המקומות בראש השנה ושמש במקום הנקרא באר ביום הכפורים והנה הפירוש כן ויכהן אלעזר כאשר נסעו אל מקום פלוני ולמה כהן אלעזר כי השם הבדיל בעת עבודת העגל את שבט הלוי לשאת את הארון לעמוד לפני השם:


[TO JOTBAH.] Jotbah is the place that is also called Beer,³⁹ (well). It is not to be identified with Jotbah in Num. 33:33 to which Israel journeyed from Hor-haggidgad. for Scripture reads, *And from thence to Beer* (Num. 21:16). This is what a *land of brooks of water* (v. 7) refers to, for the nobles of the people dug it with their staves and water came forth (Num. 21:18). This verse, namely, *From thence they journeyed unto Gudgod* is connected to *and Eleazar…ministered* (v. 6).⁴⁰ Now, I have already explained to you that Israel did not offer sacrifices after they journeyed from Mount Sinai.⁴¹ It is possible that they offered them when they came to Zalmonah⁴² is connected to *and Eleazar…* it follows that Eleazar started to serve as high priest there. and Punon and that the beginning of Eleazar’s service as high priest started in those places on Rosh Ha-Shanah.⁴³ (high priest). He ministered in a place called Beer⁴⁴ on Yom Kippur.⁴⁵. In other words, verses 6 and 7 are to be interpreted, and Eleazar ministered in Gudgod and in Jotbah. The meaning of our verses⁴⁶ thus is, And Eleazar ministered when they came to such and such a place.⁴⁷ Why did Eleazar minister? Because when Israel worshipped the calf, God separated the tribe of Levi to carry the ark and to stand before the Lord.⁴⁸ does not refer to when Israel came to Jotbah but rather to what happened at Sinai (v. 8).

**ואדוני האדונים.** כי מעלות גבוהות הם כטעם וגבוהים עליהם ומי שיכיר אלה המדות הוא מול לב:


LORD OF LORDS. For they are on various high levels,⁵⁶ as in *and there are higher than they* (Eccles. 8:7). The one who knows these measures⁵⁷ is of circumcised heart.⁵⁸

**עושה משפט.** אע״‎פ שהוא נשגב הוא עושה משפט יתום ואלמנה שאין להם עוזר כטעם אבי יתומים וכן הגר ויכלכלהו בהשענו עליו ואחר שהשם אוהב הגר אתם חייבים שתאהבוהו:


HE DOTH EXECUTE JUSTICE. Even though He is exalted, He executes justice on behalf of the orphan and widow who have no one to help them, as in *a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows* (Ps. 68:6). He similarly loves the stranger and sustains him when he⁵⁹ relies on Him. Now, since God loves the stranger, you too are obligated to love him.

⁵⁹ The stranger.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 11:2:1

**כי לא את בניכם.** התשובה היא כי עיניכם הרואות והטעם כי אלה הנוראות אינם לעתיד שיראום בניכם רק אתם ראיתם אותם:


I SPEAK NOT WITH YOUR CHILDREN THAT HAVE NOT KNOWN. The answer is², *but your eyes have seen* (v. 7).³ It⁴ (v. 7). means these wonders are not future phenomena which your children shall see. On the contrary, you yourselves have witnessed them.

footnotes:
² The question raised by our verse is, “If God did not speak with their children, to whom was He speaking?”
³ In other words, verse 7 concludes the thought raised in our verse. I.E.’s point is that our verse is to be understood, I speak not with your children…but with you whose eyes have seen the great deeds that God wrought.
⁴ …but your eyes have seen

THAT FOLLOWED THEM. *Be-raglehem* (that followed them) means because of them.¹⁰ literally means at their feet. Hence I.E.’s comment. On the other hand, the term may be taken literally.¹¹ Since you have seen all of this,¹² take heed so that you observe God’s commandments.¹³

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 11:10:1

**כי הארץ.** הנה טעם אחר שאתם חייבים לשמור מצותיו כי הארץ איננה כארץ מצרים רק יש לה צורך אל השנה לשום השם עינו עליה והטעם בדרך משל כאדם שיראה כל מה שהיא צריכה ויתן הכל בעתו:


FOR THE LAND. Here is another reason why you are obligated to observe God’s commandments. The land is not like the land of Egypt. On the contrary, the land needs God to keep His eye on it.¹⁶ The meaning of our verse can be understood with the following parable. The Lord will act like a person who sees all that the land needs and will give everything in its time.

footnotes:
¹⁶ The land requires God’s supervision.

**מרשית.** בלא אל״‎ף ורבים כן ע״‎כ כ' והיה אם שמע תשמעו ונתתי מטר ארצכם וזהו עיני ה' אלהיך בה:


FROM THE BEGINNING. *Me-reshit* (from the beginning) is spelled without an *alef*.¹⁷ is usually spelled with an *alef*. There are many such instances.¹⁸ is dropped. Scripture therefore¹⁹ goes on to say, *And it shall come to pass* (v. 13); and *I will give the rain of your land in its season* (v. 14).²⁰ This is what Scripture means by the eyes of *the Lord are always upon it*.²¹

footnotes:
¹⁷ The world reshit
¹⁸ Where a silent alef
¹⁹ That is, because the land requires God’s supervision.
²⁰ That is, Scripture states that God will give rain in its season if Israel observes God’s laws, because the land requires God’s supervision. God will care for the land if Israel observes His commandments.
²¹ It means that God looks upon the land to see whether the inhabitants are observing His laws.

THE BLESSING, IF YE SHALL HEARKEN. For if you hearken, behold, you are blessed.³⁶ A blessing means an addition of the good.³⁷ A curse means a diminution.³⁸ The word *kelalah* (curse) is related to the word *kallah* (light).³⁹

**אבד תאבדון את כל המקומו**'. אמר רבי יונה המדקדק כי את אלהיהם חסר וי״‎ו והטעם ואת אלהיהם ולא אמר כלום רק הוא דבק עם מלת אשר עבדו שם:


YE SHALL SURELY DESTROY ALL THE PLACES…THEIR GODS. Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that *et elohehem* (their gods) is lacking a *vav*, for the meaning of the phrase is, and their gods.¹ However, he contributes nothing.² is connected to *asher avedu sham* (wherein they served). *Et elohehem* is most certainly connected to *asher avedu sham* (wherein they served).³ (their gods) not *ve-et elohehem* (and their gods). I.E. feels that there is no reason to interpret *et* as if written *ve-et*.

³ For our text reads, et elohehem

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 12:8:1

ואתם **לא תעשון ככל אשר אנחנו עושים פה.** בעבור שהיו נוסעים ממסע אל מסע ויש מי שיקריב עולה במסע שירצה אחר מות אהרן ויש מי שיתן בכור צאנו ויש מי שלא יתן כי המצוה תלויה בארץ ואין זאת דעתי רק טעמו שלא היו כולם יראי השם ובעבור שאמר אנחנו הנה שם מצות רבות כעולות תלויות בארץ כי כן כתוב:


YE SHALL NOT DO AFTER ALL THAT WE DO HERE THIS DAY. Scripture states this because they were journeying from station to station.⁸ After Aaron’s death some would sacrifice a burnt offering in any one of the stations that he desired to do so.⁹ Some would present the first-born of the flock. Others did not, for the commandment¹⁰ is contingent upon the Land of Israel.¹¹ However, this is not my opinion. Its meaning,¹². rather, is that not all of them feared God. Now, Moses said “we”¹³ because, as Scripture clearly states, he made the many commandments regarding the burnt offering contingent upon the Land of Israel.¹⁴

⁹ After Aaron’s death the bringing of sacrifices was optional. Hence some brought sacrifices; others did not.
¹⁰ To offer sacrifices. After Aaron’s death the bringing of sacrifices was optional. Hence some brought sacrifices others did not. Thus every man did whatsoever was right in his eyes.
¹¹ Hence Scripture tells the Israelites that once they enter the Land of Israel, they must offer the sacrifices that Scripture commands.
¹² The meaning of, Ye shall not do after all that we do here this day. Every man whatsoever is right in his own eyes
¹³ Even though Moses was not included among those who did not fear the Lord. The first part of the verse, where the term “we” is found, applies to the laws which Israel did not observe in the wilderness.
¹⁴ The burnt offering is representative of all laws in force only in the Land of Israel.

OR THE FIRSTLINGS OF THY HERD OR OF THY FLOCK. Moses speaks to the *kohanim*,²⁸ for the Levites and also the *kohanim* are included among the Israelites.²⁹. Compare, *And I commanded you* (Deut. 3:18) wherein Moses speaks to two and a half tribes. Similarly, Moses speaks to Israel when he says, *the first-born of man shalt thou surely redeem* (Num. 18:15), which means the one who is obligated to redeem.³⁰ Similarly, *Thou mayest not eat within thy gates*³¹ and *but thou shalt eat them before the Lord thy God* (v. 18) refer to the one who is obligated to eat.³² The heretics³³ say that there are two sorts of first-born. One is the first to break out of its mother’s womb. The second is the first-born of the flock.³⁴ There is no need to respond to their nonsense. There are also others who say that if an Israelite is in the chosen place, then he eats the first-born and the tithe. However, this is the reverse of what Scripture says.³⁵

Moses speaks to the *kohen* concerning⁴⁷ a first-born, a sin offering, a guilt offering, or the shoulder or breast.⁴⁸ If the *kohen* eats from a peace offering, the major part belongs to the Israelite.⁴⁹’s share of the peace offering consists of the shoulder, the cheeks, and the maw. See Deut. 18:3.

## Chapter 13


### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 13:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:2:1)


**כי יקום בקרבך נביא.** טעם בקרבך כי אין נביא כי אם מישראל וזאת הפרשה דבקה בעבור עכו״‎ם כי שרפת הבנים ע״‎ג. נביא שיאמר כי בהקיץ דבר השם או שלוחו עמו או בחלום ויש אומרים כי יתכן להיות הנביא ממגנבי דבר השם ופי' שאמר נביא האמת שיהי' אות כך להצדיקו ושמע השומע והגידו להיות אות לנפשו ויש אומרים כי אפילו בא האות והמופת אין להאמין בו כי הוא דבר הפך שקול הדעת ולפי דעתי שיש אות גם מופת כמו סימן והעד דברי ישעיה שאמר הנה אנכי והילדים אשר נתן לי ה' לאותות ולמופתים ואות הנביא כאשר הלך עבדי ישעיה ערום ויחף ואותות בניו שמותם על דבר המקרה שיהיה בימיהם והם עמנואל מהר שלל חש בז ושאר ישוב ובמכות והיו לך לאות ולמופת וכן רבי':


IF THERE ARISE IN THE MIDST OF THEE. Scripture reads *in the midst of thee* because there is no prophet except from among Israel.¹ This section is connected to the previous one² because they both deal with idol worship, for the burning of the children (Deut. 12:31) was an act of idol worship. Our verse deals with a prophet who claims that God, or God’s messenger, spoke to him while he was awake or in a dream. Some say that it is possible that the prophet³ was one of those who steal God’s word (Jer. 26:30). They explain that a true prophet said that a certain sign would appear to verify his word.⁴ Someone heard this and related the sign so that it should bear witness for him.⁵ Others say that even if the sign or a wonder came to pass⁶ we do not believe him,⁷ for what he says⁸ contradicts reason.⁹, Treatise III. I believe that the terms wonder¹⁰. and sign¹¹. apply also¹² (Deut. 4:34). to symbolic acts.¹³ (wonder) and *ot* (sign) usually refer to a miraculous act such as changing a rod into a serpent or water into blood. However, it may also refer to an act which illustrates what the prophet predicts will happen. According to I.E. the sign spoken of in our verse refers to the latter. Hence Scripture speaks of the sign coming to pass; i.e., the act played out by the prophet came to be. Compare, the words of the prophet Isaiah: *Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me shall be for signs and for wonders* (Is. 8:18); the sign of the prophet¹⁴ in *Like as My servant Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot* (Is. 20:3);¹⁵ the names of his children, which served as signs regarding things that would occur in their lifetime, namely, Emanuel (Is. 7:14); Maher-shalal-hash-baz (Is. 8:3); Shearjashub (Is. 7:3). Also Scripture’s statement with regard to the plagues,¹⁶ *And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder* (Deut. 28:46). There are many such instances.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹ Prophesy is found only among Israelites. I.E. considered Balaam an astrologer who claimed to be a prophet. See I.E. on Num. 22:28 (Vol. 4, p. 186). This is also the opinion of Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi. See Book I of the Kuzari.
² Deut. 12:29-31.
³ Spoken of in our verse.
⁴ The true prophet gave a sign to show that what he said was true.
⁵ The false prophet used the sign given by the true prophet for his own purposes.
⁶ By the prophet.
⁷ The prophet.
⁸ His call to serve other gods.
⁹ See Rabbi Saadiah Gaon, Sefer Ha-Emunot Ve-Ha-De’ot
¹⁰ Hebrew, mofet
¹¹ Hebrew, ot
¹² In addition to referring to supernatural events, as in Or hath God assayed to go and take Him a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders
¹³ The terms mofet
¹⁴ Isaiah gave his sons names which alluded to that which would occur in the future. Thus he named one son Immanuel (God is with us) to indicate that Judah would survive. He named another son Shear-jashub (a remnant shall return) to indicate that the remnant of Judah will repent and return to God.
¹⁵ Isaiah walked naked and barefoot in Jerusalem to indicate that the people of Judah will be led into exile barefoot and naked.
¹⁶ Which would befall Israel.
¹⁷ Where signs and wonders are used in the sense of omens.

*Sarah* is an adjective. Hence I.E. notes that the word which *sarah* is describing has been omitted. Our text is to be interpreted as if written, *ki dibber davar sarah*. I.E. interprets the latter as, for he has spoken words commanding us to turn away from the Lord. *But in the multitude of counselors established*²⁵ (Prov. 15:22) is similar.²⁶ Scripture reads *sarah* (perversion) because God commanded Israel to turn away (*la-sur*) from idolatry.²⁷ as meaning for He has spoken words urging us to turn away from the Lord. On the other hand, the word *sarah* might be related to the word *soreh*²⁸. (defiant) in *defiant*²⁹ *and rebellious* (Deut. 21:20). The latter interpretation is correct. The *resh* should have received a *dagesh*.³⁰. However, it doesn’t, for *resh* does not receive a *dagesh*.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 13:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:7:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 13:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:7:2)


וטעם **בן אמך.** שהייתם בבטן אחת והאם כגוף והאב כצורה והצורה לא יבינוה כי אם מתי מעט:


The import of *thy mother* is, you³³. This is an appellation rarely used in Scripture. The question thus arises, “Why did Scripture add *the son of thy mother*?” Furthermore, why did the Torah not describe the brother as the son of thy father? Hence I.E. comments that the matter from which a person is made comes from the mother; the father’s sperm (so I.E. believed) shapes the matter. Thus a person, biologically speaking, is closer to a brother from a mother than to a brother from a father, and probably has closer emotional ties to him. Hence Scripture states, even if your brother who is made of the same matter as you entices you, do not listen to him. were in one womb. The mother is like matter and the father is like form.³⁴ not thy father. Very few people understand the nature of form.

footnotes:
³³ And your brother were in one womb. Thus the meaning of our verse is, even if your brother who was in one womb with you entices you. Our verse speaks of thy brother, the son of thy mother
³⁴ Form gives shape to matter. Form is intangible. Different men will give different form to the matter produced by the same woman. However, all of the children will share the same matter. Hence Scripture speaks of thy mother

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 13:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/13:19:1)


וטעם **כי תשמע.** כן תעשה אם בקשת לעשות הישר בעיניו. ונסמכה פרשת בנים אתם לה'. בעבור המסיתים אח או בן או אב או אנשי עיר הנדחת ואסור להתאבל עליהם אף כי להתגודד כי הנה אסור הוא על כל מת:


WHEN THOU SHALT HEARKEN. The meaning of *When*⁴³. I.E. renders *ki* if. Thus our clause reads, if thou shalt hearken. Hence his interpretation. *thou shalt hearken* is, thus shall you do if you desire to do what is right in the eyes of God. The section which opens with *Ye are children of the Lord* (Deut. 14:1) is connected to this section because of the enticers,⁴⁴ namely, a brother, a sister, and a son or daughter (v. 7), or the inhabitants of the idol-worshipping city (v. 14). It is prohibited to mourn for them,⁴⁵ and it is certainly prohibited to cut oneself,⁴⁶ for behold, that is prohibited over any deceased.⁴⁷

You shall therefore not imitate their practices. The section opening with the words *Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing* (v. 3) follows because Scripture says, as it were, you are holy in your heart and in your mouth. You shall be separated from the nations. All who see you shall recognize you, for you will not make yourself bald for the dead and you do not eat all living creatures. If you are a holy people, then it is unfitting for you to eat that which is unclean and defiles one’s soul.

**היוצא השדה שנה שנה.** אמר רבי יהודה הלוי הספרדי נ״‎ע כי הוא דבק עם זרעך והטעם הזרע שהוצאת אל השדה ולפי דעתי שהוא כפשוטו וטעמו על התבואה מה שיוצאת השדה ואם יטעון טוען כי הכתוב אמר היוצא והוא מהפעלים שאינם יוצאים לאחרים הראינו לו העיר היוצאת אלף והעד תשאיר מאה וחז״‎ל אמרו שהוא מעשר שני ודע אם תחל ממעל הנה האחד ראש ואם ממטה הנה העשירי וזה סוד הבכור והמעשר ודע כי האחד איננו בחשבון וכן העשירי כי הוא כנגד האחד כי הוא ראש למחברת השנית וסוף למחברת הראשונה וכל שרש בחשבון סמוך אליו מפניו ומאחריו ובעבור היות האחד והעשרה עיקריים והאמצעיים חמשה וששה הם הנקראים עגולים על כן אותיות הנח הם אלה הארבעה ומהם אותיות השם הנכבד והנורא:


WHICH IS BROUGHT FORTH IN THE FIELD YEAR BY YEAR. Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi the Spaniard, who rests in Eden, said *that which is brought forth in the field* is connected to the word *seed*, and our verse is to be understood as, you shall tithe the seed which is brought into the field for planting.²⁹ (is brought forth) is intransitive. Hence his interpretation. However, I believe that we are to interpret the verse according to its plain meaning. Our clause refers to the produce which the field brings forth.³⁰ (is brought forth) is transitive. Our verse is to be understood as follows: You shall tithe the seed which the field produces. Should some dispute this and argue that Scripture reads *ha-yotze* (which is brought forth), and *yotze* (brought forth) is an intransitive verb, then we will show him *ha-ir ha-yotzet*³¹ is the feminine form of *ha-yotze*. It is transitive. We thus see that *ha-yotze* can also be transitive. *elef* (the city that sent forth a thousand) (Amos 5:3). *Shall have a hundred left* (*Ibid.*)³² proves this.³³ is transitive, for it speaks about what is left in the city. The rabbis said that the reference is to the second tithe.³⁴ Note.³⁵ If you start from the top,³⁶ then one is the first number. If you start from below,³⁷ then, behold, ten is the first number.³⁸ This is the secret of the first-born and the tithe.³⁹ Observe. The number one does not depend on a sum.⁴⁰ The number ten is similar. It is the counterpart of one because it is the beginning of the second series of numbers.⁴¹ It is also the end of the first series.⁴² All parts of sums are connected to ten in front and in back.⁴³ The numbers one and ten are the main numbers; the middle numbers, five and six, are called the round numbers.⁴⁴ These four numbers⁴⁵ therefore⁴⁶ form the silent letters.⁴⁷ (1); *heh* (5); *vav* (6), and *yod* (10). These letters are not always sounded. They are vowel letters. One of them is present whenever a word is enunciated. Without these letters, language would be impossible. They are also the letters that form the glorious and awe-inspiring name.⁴⁸ in Ex. 3:14.

AT THE END OF¹. EVERY SEVEN YEARS.] Its meaning, as I have explained, is, at the beginning of the year.² means either at the end of or at the beginning of. Here it means at the beginning. ### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 15:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/15:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/15:10:1)


**בגלל.** כמו סבה לבעבור סבב כי הכל הוא בחלקי' בחלקי הכל שהוא הגוף:


THAT. *Bi-gelal* (that) means the same as *sibbah* (because of). Compare, *sabbev* (cause) in *cause to change* (II Sam. 14:20).³⁰. For the All³¹ is in the parts,³² that is, in the parts of the All, that is, the body.³³, N.Y., 1969, p. 99). In other words, the All is the nation, and the individual is a part of the nation. However, it should be noted that I.E. refers to God as the All. See I.E. on Gen. 1:26 (Vol. 1, p. 46), “God is one…He is all.” Also see I.E. on Gen. 18:21 (Vol. 1, p. 196) and Ex. 33:21 (Vol. 2, p. 695). The above-noted commentaries may have shied away from interpreting God as All here because of its pantheistic implications. It should be noted that when I.E. says that God is All, he does not intend to identify God with the world as the pantheists do. He means that God’s power and supervision hold the world together and give it continuous existence. Indeed, I.E. compares God’s relation to the world to that of speech to the speaker. As long as the speaker speaks, sounds are uttered. However, the speaker is not identified with the speech which he utters. On the other hand, I.E. was a contemporary of Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi and may be employing terminology similar to the one quoted above.

³¹ God.
³² In human beings, who are part of the whole.
³³ Thus by being kind to his fellow human being, a person is being kind to God (Weiser). Other commentaries explain that the All refers to the community of Israel and the parts to each individual Jew. Now, since all of Israel forms one body, by helping another Jew one is helping oneself (Motot and Rabbi Yosef ben Eliezer tov Elem, followed by Krinsky, Netter, and others). See Book III of the Kuzari: “Plato calls…that which is expended on behalf of the law the portion of the whole. If, however, an individual neglects ‘the portion of the whole’…of which he forms a part, he sins against the commonwealth and more against himself; for the relation of the individual to the commonwealth is as the relation of the single limb to the body…” (Isaak Heinemann translation in Three Jewish Philosophers

**העניק תעניק לו.** הטעם עשה לו תפארת מגזרת וענקים לגרגרותיך או יהיה פירוש המלה כפי המקום בלא אח:


THOU SHALT FURNISH HIM LIBERALLY. *Ha’anek ta’anik* (thou shalt furnish him liberally) means treat him gloriously. *Ta’anik* (thou shalt furnish him) is related to the word *anakim* (chains)⁴¹ in *And chains about thy neck* (Prov. 1:9).⁴² (thou shalt furnish him liberally) literally means thou shalt put ornament on him. Hence I.E.’s interpretation. On the other hand, the meaning of *ta’anik* is to be derived from its context.⁴³ (thou shalt furnish him) is not related to the word *anakim* (chains) in *And chains about thy neck* (Prov. 1:9). In this case, the word has no brother.⁴⁴

IT SHALL NOT SEEM HARD UNTO THEE. We find it written in Scripture, *three years, as the years of a hireling* (Is. 16:14). The latter proves that a person has no right to hire himself out for more than three years. The law similarly applies to the one who hires him and pays his wages.⁵²

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 15:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/15:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/15:18:2)


וזה טעם משנה כמו כפל וכן והיה משנה הוא משנה למלך שם משנה למלך תאר השם גם הוא מגזרת שנים כאשר פירשתי והנה זה הכתוב יפרש כי ובשביעית יצא לחפשי חנם בתחלת השנה גם יש ראיה משנת השמטה גם מיום השבת:


[DOUBLE.]⁵³. The following is the definition of *mishneh*. It means double. Similarly *mishneh* (twice) *in ve-hayah mishneh* (and it shall be twice as much) (Ex. 16:5). The word *mishneh* in the latter is a noun. However, *mishneh* (next) in *mishneh la-melekh* (next unto king) (Esth. 10:3) is an adjective.⁵⁴. 38. The *Mikra’ot Gedolot* reads: “The following is the definition of *mishneh*. It means double. Similarly *mishneh* (twice) in *ve-hayah mishneh* (and it shall be twice as much) (Ex. 16:5), the meaning of which is *mishneh lamelekh* (double unto the king). The word *mishneh* in the latter is a noun. However, *mishneh* (next) in *mishneh la-melekh* (next unto king) (Esth. 10:3) is an adjective.” The words “the meaning of which *mishneh lamelekh* (double unto the king)” appear to be a gloss. See Weiser and Krinsky. It⁵⁵ (next) in *mishneh la-melekh*. is also related, as I have explained,⁵⁶ to the word *shenayin* (two).⁵⁷, which means second to him” (Vol. 1, p. 382). Note, our verse explains that *and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing* (Ex. 21:2) refers to the beginning of the year.⁵⁸. If the slave did not go out at the start of the seventh year he would be serving seven not six years. There is also proof of this from the year of release (*shemitttah*)⁵⁹ as well as from the Sabbath day.⁶⁰

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 15:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/15:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/15:22:2)


**הטמא והטהור.** שב אל תאכלנו והטעם כמו קריאה אתה הטמא או הטהור והטעם בין שיהיה טמא או טהור הוא מותר לאוכלו בעבור כי בשר קודש אם אכלו טמא הוא בכרת ובעבור שהזכיר שנה בשנה הזכיר שלש פעמים ועוד בעבור הבכור שיאכל במקדש וכן הפסח יאכל במקדש ולא חוץ ממנו:


THE UNCLEAN AND THE CLEAN. The reference is to *may eat it*.⁶⁹ prefaced to the Hebrew words for clean and unclean as a vocative *heh*. Thus *ha-tame* (the unclean) means you who are unclean, and *ha-tahor* (the clean) means you who are clean. The meaning of our clause thus is, you who are unclean and you who are clean shall eat of it. Our verse is to be understood as a call: you, the clean and the unclean. Its meaning is, one is permitted to eat it whether one is clean or unclean. Scripture states this because one who is unclean and eats holy meat is punished with *karet* (excision). Scripture reads *three times in a year* (Deut. 16:16) because it here (v. 20) states year by year.⁷⁰ Additionally,⁷¹ because the firstling is to be eaten in the sanctuary.⁷² The paschal offering⁷³ 5:8. is similarly to be eaten in the sanctuary, not outside it.

### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 16:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/16:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/16:1:1)


**את חדש האביב.** נקרא כן בעבור שהיה בו אביב בצאתם ממצרים והמכחישים אמרו כי לא נעשה פסח בלא אביב וכבר השיבותי על הבליהם גם אנחנו נודה כי בית דין היה מסתכל לאביב ודע כי אין לחדשים בלשון הקדש שמות כי ניסן סיון גם כסליו גם טבת גם אדד שהם נזכרים במקרא הם לשון כשדים על כן אמר הוא חדש ניסן רק מצאנו זיו ואיתני' ובול וטעם ראשון כאשר ימצא האביב הנו חדש הראשון כי משם יחל לספור החדשי' אם היתה שנה שעברה שנים עשר חדש או שלשה עשר לא נחוש על זה וזה טעם ראשון רק קדמונינו ז״‎ל העתיקו עם האביב דברים אחרים וכל דבריהם אמת:


THE MONTH OF ABIV. It is called the month of Aviv because when the Israelites went out of the land of Egypt, the first of the barley crop (*aviv*)¹ as the first of the barley crop. Thus according to I.E. *the month of Abiv* means the month when the first of the barley crop appears in the field. appeared in the fields in that month. Those who deny the Rabbinic tradition say that Passover² is not to be observed if the first of the barley crop has not appeared.³ did not appear, then the paschal lamb was not offered that year. They do not believe that an additional month was added to the year if the *aviv* had not yet arrived. (See Meijler). I have previously responded to their nonsense.⁴ We will also admit that the Beth Din⁵ took the appearance of the first barley crop into consideration.⁶. 11a,b. Note that in Hebrew the months have no names.⁷ Nisan (Esth. 3:7; Neh. 2:1), Sivan (Esth. 8:9), and also Kislev (Neh. 1:1), Tevet (Esth. 2:16), and Adar (Esth. 3:7), which are mentioned in Scripture, are Chaldean terms. Hence Scripture states, *which is the month of Nisan* (*Ibid.*).⁸. Scripture identifies the first month by its Chaldean name because the Jews did not call the month by that name in earlier times. However, we find Ziv (I Kings 6:37),⁹ Etanim (I Kings 8:2),¹⁰ and Bul (I Kings 6:38).¹¹ The meaning of first¹². is that when you find the first barley ripe, then the first month has arrived, for one starts counting the months from it We do not care about this,¹³ whether the year that passed consisted of twelve months or thirteen months.¹⁴ This is the meaning of first.¹⁵ arrives. However, the ancients of blessed memory transmitted traditions regarding many other things along with the ripe barley grain.¹⁶. 11:a,b. All of their words are true.

OF THE FLOCK. To fulfill the obligation of the paschal sacrifice.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 16:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/16:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/16:2:2)


**ובקר.** לשלמים והעד ובקר שלשת אלפים אחר שאמר הכל לפסחים על כשבים ובני עזים וכן נתנו לפסחים חמשת אלפים ובקר חמש מאות והנה זכר הפסח קודם הבקר וכן אתה וביתך וי״‎א כי במצרים אמר כבש או עז ועתה בקר אם יוכל והראשון הוא הנכון:


AND THE HERD. For peace offerings.²⁰ The fact that Scripture says, *and three thousand bullocks* (II Chron. 35:7), after it says, *all of them for the passover-offerings*, with regard to the lambs and kids (*Ibid.*), is proof.²¹ refers to peace offerings, for Scripture implies that only the lambs and kids were offered as paschal sacrifices. II Chron. 35:7 states: *And Josiah gave to the children of the people, of the flock, lambs and kids, all of them for the passover-offerings, unto all that were present, to the number of thirty thousand*. It similarly tells us that they gave (unto the Levite) *for the passover-offerings five thousand small cattle, and five hundred oxen* (*Ibid.*, v. 9). Scripture thus mentions the Passover offerings before it mentions the cattle.²² It similarly states, *thou and thy household* (Deut. 14:26).²³. The former applies to the paschal offering and the latter to peace offerings. Some say that Scripture commanded that a lamb or a he-goat were to be offered in Egypt.²⁴ However, Scripture now tells us if one is able to, he may offer cattle. However, the first interpretation is correct.²⁵

AND THOU SHALT ROAST.²⁹ [literally, and you shall cook]. I have previously explained that *u-vishalta* means you shall roast in fire.³⁰. Hence I.E.’s comment. Compare, *And they roasted* (va-yevashelu)³¹ *the passover with fire* (II Chron. 35:13). Scripture reads *u-vishalta* to indicate that the Passover offering is not to be eaten raw.³² (cooked) comes from the same root as the word ripe. Thus *u-vishalta* can be taken to mean prepare (cook or roast) it to the point where it is fit to be eaten.

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 16:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/16:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/16:8:1)


**ששת ימים.** אמרו הקדמונים מהחל חרמש ויתכן להיות ביום השביעי דבק עם ששת ימים והבדילו מפאה אל פאה אחרת להזהיר לא תעשה מלאכה ולא אמר כל מלאכה והטעם כל מלאכת עבודה ובמקום שאמר כל מלאכה שם כתוב אך וכאשר הזכיר הפסח שהוא חייב לבא אל מקום הכבוד הזכיר החג השני גם השלישי ולא הזכיר יום תרועה ויום העשור כי אין הצבור מתחבר במקדש:


SIX DAYS. The ancients said six days from the lifting of the sickle.⁴⁵ This took place on the second day of Passover. See Lev. 23:9-12. Scripture prohibits eating of the new crop of grain before a measure (an omer) of new grain is cut and offered on the altar. Now, the Torah commands that matzot be eaten for seven days (v. 3). This contradicts our verse which states that matzot be eaten for six days. The Talmud (*Menachot* 66a) explains that our verse refers to matzot baked from the new crop, which could not be eaten before the second day of Passover, while the verse that tells the Israelites to eat matzot for seven days speaks of matzot made from grain from the previous year. See Rashi. It is possible that *and on the seventh day* is connected to *six days*.⁴⁶ *And on the seventh day* was separated from the first half of the verse and placed in the second half of the verse because Scripture wanted to warn against doing work.⁴⁷ refers to both the first part of the verse and to the second. Our verse is to be understood as follows: *Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread;* and [so too] on the seventh day; *and on the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly …thou shalt do no work therein*. Scripture does not say all manner of work.⁴⁸ The reason for the latter is that only servile work⁴⁹ is prohibited. Where Scripture does state all manner of work,⁵⁰ it reads, “Save” [that which every man must eat].⁵¹ When Scripture mentions that one is obligated to offer the Passover sacrifice in the glorious place, it also mentions the second festival (v. 9)⁵² and the third festival (v. 13).⁵³ It does not mention the day of *shofar* sounding⁵⁴ and the tenth day,⁵⁵ because the congregation does not gather then in the sanctuary.⁵⁶

⁴⁷ On the seventh day. The point is and on the seventh day
⁴⁸ All manner of work is prohibited on the Sabbath and Yom Kippur. However, work necessary for the preparation of food is permitted on festivals.
⁴⁹ All work except that which is necessary for the preparation of food. See Ex. 12:16.

The *samekh* of *missat* (after the measure) receives a *dagesh* to compensate for the missing *nun*.⁵⁷ from *the root nun, samekh, samekh*. *Missat* is related to the word *nes* (banner). It means the lifting of the hand.⁵⁸ (after the measure of the freewill-offering of thy hand) means the lifting of the freewill-offering of thy hand. Scripture uses the term lifting when it deals with an offering to the sanctuary. Compare the word *trumah* (offering), which literally means a lifting.

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 17:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/17:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/17:5:1)


**וסקלתם באבנים.** זה או זאת כמו באש ישרפו אותו ואתהן ובעבור שאמר והוגד לך בסתר ושמעת הדבר בגלוי הוצרך לפרש אע״‎פ שהוגד לך ושמעת לא יומתו רק ע״‎פ שנים עדים:


AND THOU SHALT STONE THEM. The man or the woman.⁸ cannot refer to both of them, for Scripture speaks of a man or a woman. It is similar to *they shall be burnt with fire*, *both he and they* (Lev. 20:14).⁹ (ethen) can’t refer to both women, for what sin did the first woman commit? It is only the second woman taken who is put to death. If he first takes the mother, then it is the daughter who is put to death. If he first takes the daughter, then it is the mother who is put to death. The meaning of *ethen* (they) thus is, one of them. Since Scripture says, *and it be told thee* (v. 4) in secret,¹⁰ and *thou hear it* (*Ibid.*) in public,¹¹ it had to explain that even though it was told to you, and you heard, they shall not be put to death except upon the testimony of two witnesses.¹²

footnotes:
⁸ Who worshipped idols. And thou shalt stone them
⁹ The verse speaks of a man who takes a mother and daughter, or a daughter and mother. They shall be burnt with fire, both he and they
¹⁰ I.E.’s elaboration of the verse.
¹¹ I.E.’s elaboration of the verse.
¹² The law of witnesses follows the law of idolatry because the punishment of idolaters requires two witnesses to the act of idol worship.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 17:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/17:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/17:6:1)


**או שלשה עדים.** מקבלים עדות שנים על דעת הגאון והנה לא פירש בתורה אם תקובל עדות השאר והאשה ועדות אויב המת ויש אומרים אם היו שני עדים מכחישים שני' עדים השלישי יכריע לזכות או לחובה ויש אומרים שנים עדים מהחכמים ושלשה מהאחרים וגם אנחנו צריכים בעל כרחנו לדברי הקבלה:


OR THREE WITNESSES. Who accept the testimony of two witnesses.¹³?” So says the Gaon.¹⁴ Look, the Torah does not state whether we accept the testimony of relatives or of a woman or the testimony of an enemy of the deceased.¹⁵ Some say that if two witnesses contradict two witnesses, then a third witnesses determines innocence or guilt.¹⁶. Others say two witnesses from among the wise men and three from the others.¹⁷ We are thus forced to rely on the words of tradition.¹⁸ is, just as two witnesses form one unit, so do three witnesses form one unit, and if one of the three is disqualified the entire unit is disqualified.

footnotes:
¹³ According to the Gaon two witnesses may testify before three witnesses. The latter may then testify as to what they heard. However, two witnesses cannot testify before two other witnesses. Thus according to the Gaon our verse should be read as follows: at the mouth of two witnesses who saw the event that they are testifying to, or at the mouth of three witnesses who heard it from two witnesses, shall he that is to die be put to death. The Gaon so interpreted our verse because he wanted to avoid the question, “If two witnesses are enough to convict a person, why does Scripture go on to say or three witnesses
¹⁴ Rabbi Saadiah Gaon.
¹⁵ We must rely on tradition in these instances. I.E. comments thus because he will soon say that we must rely on tradition regarding the understanding of our verse.
¹⁶ Hence Scripture reads, At the mouth of two…or three witnesses shall he…be put to death
¹⁷ Non-scholars.
¹⁸ In understanding our verse, as we must with regard to the testimony of relatives, or of a woman, or the testimony of an enemy of the deceased. According to the rabbis the meaning of At the mouth of two…or three witnesses

Now Israel complained about Solomon who, because of his great love of money, *made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones* (I Kings 10:27). They said [to his son], *Thy father made our yoke grievous* (I Kings 12:10). Some say that they complained because of the buildings.⁴³ However, this is not so, for strangers built the house.⁴⁴ The latter is clearly stated in Scripture.⁴⁵ Look, following Solomon’s death Adinoram, who was over the levy,⁴⁶ was stoned to death by the Israelites (I Kings 10:18).⁴⁷

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 18:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/18:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/18:1:1)


**לא יהיה לכהנים הלוים.** כאשר הזכיר משפטי המלך שהוא השופט הזכיר גם משפט הכהנים שהם מורי התורה ואחר שאמר שאין להם נחלה יקחו מאת הזובח הזרוע והלחיים והקיבה הזרוע מהגוף והלחיים שהלשון ביניהם מהראש והקיבה מהקרב ודרך דרש כי הכהן הוא שוחט השלמים הזרוע שכר זרועו בשחיטה והלחיים שכר הברכה והקיבה שכר הבדיקה ועל דרך הפשט כי אלה טובים משאר הבשר גם הזכיר דברי לוי כי גם הם יורו התורה בשערים והעד דברי הימים:


THE PRIESTS THE LEVITES, EVEN ALL THE TRIBE OF LEVI, SHALL HAVE NO PORTION. When Scripture mentions the laws of the king,¹ who is the judge,² it makes mention of the laws of the *kohanim*, who are the teachers of the Torah. After Scripture states that they have no inheritance,³ it states that they will take from the sacrificer⁴ the shoulder, the cheeks, and the maw:⁵ the shoulder from the body; the cheeks, which have the tongue between them, from the head; and the maw from the insides. There is a midrashic interpretation that since the *kohen* slaughters the peace offerings, he receives the shoulder as payment for the use of his shoulder in the slaughtering, the cheeks as payment for reciting the blessing,⁶ and the maw as payment for the investigation.⁷ checks the innards to see if they are healthy. If they are not, the animal is declared unfit and cannot be eaten. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, these⁸ are better than the rest of the meat.⁹ Scripture also mentions the laws regarding the Levites,¹⁰ for they too¹¹. will teach the Torah in the gates. The Book of Chronicles shows this to be the case.¹² (the Levites) *taught in Judah, having the hook of the Law of the Lord with them; and they went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught among the people*.

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 18:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/18:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/18:8:1)


**לבד ממכריו.** יש אומרים שהוא כמו מאת מכריהם בדרך רחוקה מעט ולא אבה הדקדוק רק הוא מגזר' וכי תמכרו ממכר והטעם כי אם מכר ביתו שירש מאבותיו כאשר כתוב ויצא ממכר בית ועיר אחוזתו וזה פירוש על האבות לא יאמר לו הנה יש לך לא תאכל עוד אלא חלק כחלק יאכלו וכאשר השלים להזכיר דבר השופט והכהן הזכיר דבר הנביא:


BESIDE THAT WHICH IS HIS DUE. Some say that *mimkarav* (which is his due) is similar to *makkarekhem*¹³. 38. The printed texts have *makkarehem*. (them that bestow it upon you)¹⁴ (which is his due) his relatives. They read our verse as, beside that which his relatives from his fathers’ houses bestow upon him. They interpret the latter as follows: if a member of a *kohen* family allows another *kohen* to sacrifice in his place, then his colleagues cannot say to him, “Since you are offering the sacrifice in place of your relative, you shall not in addition eat the sacred food with us.” See Rashbam. It should be noted that according to the commentaries, Levite in our verse refers to a *kohen* from the house of Levi. in *from them that bestow it upon you* (II Kings 12:8).¹⁵ However, they are a bit off the mark. The rules of grammar will not accede to it.¹⁶ comes from the root *nun, kaf, resh*, while *mimkarav* comes from the root *mem, kaf, resh*. On the contrary, *mimkarav* is related to *timkeru mimkar* (sell aught) in *and if thou sell aught* (Lev. 25:14).¹⁷. The meaning of *le-vad mimkarav al ha-avot* (beside that which is due according to the father’s house)¹⁸ is, if the *kohen* sold his house, which he inherited from his father as Scripture states, *then the house that was sold in the city of his*¹⁹. *possession, shall go out*²⁰) may sell, in a Levitical city, the house which he received as an inheritance. (Lev. 25:33). The latter explains *according to the fathers*.²¹) has inherited from his fathers. The local *kohanim* shall not say to him, Look, you have money, you shall not in addition eat the sacred food with us. On the contrary, they shall eat like portions.²² shall receive an equal share in the sacrificial meat. After Moses concludes the laws pertaining to the judge²³ and the *kohen*,²⁴ he mentions the laws regarding the prophet.²⁵

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 18:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/18:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/18:10:2)


**קוסם קסמים.** יתכן היותו שם כלל ופירושו חותכי משפט האומרים כי כן יהיה בלא ספק וכן גוזרין וקרוב ממנו קסם על שפתי מלך והפרט מעונן ומנחש ומכשף גם יתכן היותו שם פרט להוברי שמים וטעם קסמים שיש במשפטי הכוכבים הנקראים ראשונים ושניים:


ANYONE THAT USETH DIVINATION.²⁷. *Kosem* (one that useth divination) is most probably a general term. It refers to those who issue decrees and declare things will undoubtedly be so.²⁸ The term *gazerin* (magicians) is similar.²⁹ (Dan. 2:27) comes from *gazar* (to decree). Thus *gazerin* means those who decree. The word *kesem* (divine sentence) in *A divine sentence is in the lips of the king* (Prov. 16:10) is close in meaning to it. The particulars³⁰. are a *soothsayer* (me’onen), *or an enchanter* (menachesh), *or a sorcerer* (mechashef). It is also possible that *kosem* is a specific term for astrologers³¹. This is a phrase found in Is. 47:13. I.E. there defines it as astrologers. I.E. believed that the study of astrology was permitted. What was prohibited was making absolute predictions using astrology. It should be noted that I.E. believed that the *urim* and *tummim* entailed the use of astrology. Therefore I.E. probably believed that certain types of astrological predictions were prohibited, while others, i.e., those sanctioned by the Torah, were permitted. See I.E. on Ex. 28:5 (Vol. 2, pp. 595-598? and the notes thereto). See also Dov. Schwartz, *Astral Magic in Medieval Jewish Thought* (Heb.), Bar-Ilan University, Israel, 1999, pp. 62-91. and that *kesamim* (divinations) refers to divination that astrologers make based on the primary and secondary stars.³²

**ודורש אל המתים.** ההולכים אל בית הקברות ולוקחים עצם אדם מת ובעבור מחשבתו ושגיונו תראה לו דמות צורות בחלום גם בהקיץ וכל אלה תועבות השם כי האמת להיות לב האדם תמיד תמים עם בוראו וכאשר ישען על חכמתו לבקש האמת ומה שיהיה חוץ מהשם הנה לבו חסר כי הוא משובש והרוצה לדרוש ידרוש מהשם על פי הנביא על כן כתוב אחריו נביא מקרבך זה יהושע והעד שאמר אליו תשמעון וכתיב וישמעו אליו בני ישראל ועוד ראיה אחרת כי לא מצאנו נביא שנכנס עם ישראל לארץ כי אם יהושע גם כן יתכן להיות זה כלל לכל נביא שיקום אחר משה:


OR A NECROMANCER. Such as those who go to cemeteries and take the bone of a dead person and, because of their imagination and madness, see shapes⁴⁰ while they are awake⁴¹ or in a dream. All of these things⁴² are abominations to God. The truth is that a person must fully believe in his creator in his heart. When a person relies on his wisdom, and not on God, in seeking the truth and what will be in the future, his mind is deficient, for it is perverted. The person who wants to inquire,⁴³ let him inquire from God via a prophet. Scripture therefore afterward reads, *A prophet will the Lord…raise up…from the midst of thee* (v. 15). The latter refers to Joshua. *Unto him ye shall hearken* (*Ibid.*), which is later followed by *and the children of Israel hearkened unto him* (Deut. 34:9), is proof of this. The fact that we do not find any other prophet but Joshua entering Canaan⁴⁴ is additional proof of this.⁴⁵. The only one who fits that description is Joshua, for we do not find any other prophet but Joshua immediately following Moses. It is also possible that our verse lays down a general rule for each and every prophet who will arise after Moses.⁴⁶ applies not only to Moses’ successor, but to all prophets following Moses.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 19:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/19:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/19:5:4)

AND THE HEAD SLIPPETH FROM THE HELVE. *Venashal* (slippeth) is similar to *ve-nasa* (shall set forward) (Num. 2:17).⁶ It is related to the word *yishal* (shall drop off) in *for thine olives shall drop off* (Deut. 28:40). The word *ve-nashal* (and shall cast) in *and shall cast out many nations* (Deut. 7:1) is transitive. However, *ve-nashal* (slippeth) in our verse is intransitive. According to a great grammarian the same is true of the word *yasaf* (more) in *with a great voice, and it went on no more* (Deut. 5:19) and *yasaf* (added) in *For the Lord hath added sorrow* (Jer. 45:3).⁷ is intransitive in Deut. 5:19 and intransitive in Jer. 45:3. However, I believe that they are both transitive.

והטוען כי חברו הסיג גבולו יביא עדים על כן **לא יקום עד אחד.** בין לרוצח בין למכה בין למסיג בין לכל דבר רק ע״‎פ שני עדים דרך קצרה כי במקום אחר ע״‎פ שנים עדים:
