Scripture therefore goes on to state, following this, *Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth* (v. 21). The one who claims that his neighbor removed his landmark must bring witnesses. Hence, Scripture reads, *one witness shall not rise up*, which means that two witnesses are required in cases involving murder, assault, landmark removal, or any matter.²⁰ S*hene edim* (two witnesses) is an abridged phrase,²¹ is short for *shenaim*. for Scripture elsewhere reads, *shenayim edim* (two witnesses) (Deut. 17:6).

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 20:7:1

**ארש אשה ולא לקחה.** בנשואין והנה זה הכתוב לאות כי יש מי שימות בבא יומו רק המת במלחמה מת בלא יומו על כן אמר דוד או במלחמה ירד ונספה:


AND WHAT MAN IS THERE THAT HATH BETROTHED A WIFE, AND HATH NOT TAKEN HER? In marriage.⁹ (betrothal) and *nesu’in* (marriage). In the first stage the woman, though married, still lived in her father’s house. In the second stage she went to live with her husband. The marriage was not consummated till the second stage. Look, this verse is a sign that there are people who die when their time comes.¹⁰ However, the one who dies in battle dies before his time. Hence David said, *or he shall go down into battle, and be swept away* (I Sam. 26:10).¹¹.

¹⁰ Thus the man who has married a woman but has not consummated the marriage is exempt from the army because his time to die has probably not yet come. He will therefore be able to consummate his marriage if he does not go forth to war.
¹¹ The entire clause reads: or his day shall come to die; or he shall go down into battle, and be swept away

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 20:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/20:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/20:19:1)


**כי האדם עץ השדה.** כבר ביארתי בספר היסוד כי יתכן בכל לשון לקצר לאחוז דרך קצרה כמו חמור לחם רק מלת לא לא יתכן להיותה נחסרת כי הטעם יהיה להפך ומדקדק גדול ספרדי אמר כי חסר ה״‎א וכן הוא הכי האדם עץ השדה וזה הטעם איננו נכון בעיני כי מה טעם לאמר לא תשחית עץ פרי כי איננו כבני אדם שיוכל לברוח מפניך ולפי דעתי שאין לנו צורך לכל זה וזה פירושו כי ממנו תאכל ואותו לא תכרות כי האדם עץ השדה והטעם כי חיי בן אדם הוא עץ השדה וכמוהו כי נפש הוא חובל כי חיי נפש הוא חובל:


FOR IS THE TREE OF THE FIELD MAN.¹⁸. The latter literally means for man is a tree of the field. This, as I.E. goes on to say, does not make sense. Hence the interpretations which follow. I have previously explained in the *Sefer Ha-Yesod*¹⁹ that it is possible in all languages to be brief and to apply an abbreviated style, as in “an ass bread”²⁰ (I Sam. 16:20).²¹. However, it is impossible to leave out the word *lo* (no, not),²² for in this case the meaning would be reversed.²³ as if written *ki ha-adam lo etz ha-sadeh* (for the tree of the field is not a man). In other words, Onkelos claims that the word *lo* has been left out of the verse. I.E. disagrees. Hence his comment. A great Spanish grammarian²⁴ said that a *heh*²⁵. has been omitted.²⁶ in *ki ha-adam etz ha-sadeh*. Our clause should be interpreted as if written, *hakhi adam etz ha-sadeh* (for is the tree of the field man).²⁷. The latter literally means for man is a tree of the field. Hence the unnamed grammarian’s interpretation. Now this interpretation does not appear correct to me. Why would Scripture say that you shall not destroy fruit trees, because, unlike a human being, they cannot run away from you?²⁸ as, for is the tree of the field man. I believe there is no need for all this.²⁹ as if written *ha-khi adam etz ha-sadeh*. The following is the meaning of our clause. For thou mayest eat of them, but thou shalt not cut them down, for the tree of the field is man; that is, the life of man is supported by trees.³⁰ (for man) is short for *ki chayye ha-adam* (for the life of man). Compare, *For he taketh a life to pledge* (Deut. 24:6), which is short for, for he taketh that which sustains man’s life to pledge.

footnotes:
¹⁸ Hebrew, ki ha-adam etz ha-sadeh
¹⁹ A Hebrew grammar composed by I.E. The book survives only in fragments.
²⁰ Translated literally.
²¹ An ass bread is short for an ass laden with bread
²² If one wants to employ an abbreviated style.
²³ Onkelos renders ki ha-adam etz ha-sadeh

**ואותו לא תכרות.** דבק עם לבא מפניך במצור הנה לא תשחית עץ פרי שהוא חיים לבן אדם רק מותר שתאכל ממנו ואסור לך להשחיתו כדי שתבא העיר מפניך במצור והעד על זה הפירוש שהוא נכון שאמר וכרת ובנית מצור:


BUT THOU SHALT NOT CUT THEM DOWN. This is connected to *that it should he besieged of thee*.³¹ Look, do not destroy a fruit tree, which is a source of sustenance for human life. Be that as it may, you are permitted to eat of it but you are prohibited from destroying it so that the city will be besieged because of you. The fact that Scripture then states *thou mayest destroy and cut down*,³² *that thou mayest build bulwarks* (v. 20), is proof of this.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 21:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:7:1)


ה״‎א **שפכה.** תחת סימן הרבים כמו שפכה אשורי ועל דרך הדרש שישוב לאחת כי היד לשון נקבה ברוב:


[SHED.] The *heh* in *shafekhu* (shed) indicates the plural.⁹ is usually used to indicate the third person plural perfect. In our verse a *heh* is used in place of the *vav*. It is like the *heh* in *shafekhu ashurai* (my steps slipped) (Ps. 73:2).¹⁰ is spelled with a *heh* in place of a *vav*. However, interpreting it midrashically, the *heh* refers to each one of the hands, for the word *yad* (hand) is in most cases feminine.¹¹ is the third person perfect feminine. In this case our verse reads: *yadenu shafekhah* (our hands it has spilled). According to I.E. a combination of the plural with the singular refers to each one of the plural. See I.E. on Gen. 49:22 (Vol. 1, p. 441).

footnotes:
⁹ A vav
¹⁰ Here too the word shafekhu
¹¹ If we ignore the vowels, then our word reads shafekhah. Shafekhah

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 21:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:9:1)


**ואתה תבער הדם הנקי.** פירושו עונש הדם הנקי או יהיה הדם דם הנקי ויש אומרים אתה חייב לבער שפיכות דמים והנכון בעיני הוא אשר הזכרתי כי לא ישפך דם נקי בארצך אם תעשה הישר בעיני ה' כסוד שכר עבירה עבירה ושכר מצוה מצוה:


SO SHALT THOU PUT AWAY THE INNOCENT BLOOD. The meaning of *the innocent blood* is, the punishment for the shedding of the innocent blood.²⁰ (ha-dam hanaki) *from the midst of thee*. The question arises, “What does this clause mean?” The innocent blood has already been shed, i.e., put away. Hence I.E. points out that *ha-dam ha-naki* is short for *onesh ha-dam ha-naki* (the punishment for the innocent blood), and our verse teaches that by performing this ritual you remove from your midst the punishment for the shedding of innocent blood. See Meijler. On the other hand, the word *ha-dam ha-naki* (the innocent blood) is short for *ha-dam, dam ha-naki* (the blood, the innocent blood).²¹, the spiller of innocent blood. That is, if after the ritual is performed the murderer is discovered, you shall put away the shedder of blood, of innocent blood. Some say that the meaning of *so shalt thou put away the innocent blood* is, you must eradicate the shedding of blood. However, in my opinion, and I have mentioned this before, it means no innocent blood will be shed in your land if you do what is right in the eyes of God. The latter is in keeping with the secret that the reward of sin is sin, and the reward of a commandment is the commandment.²² 2:1. If innocent blood was shed near the city it was because the people of the city committed a similar crime. Thus the wages of sin is more sin.

footnotes:
²⁰ Our verse reads, So shalt thou put away the innocent blood
²¹ According to Meijler our verse is interpreted as if written shofekh hadam, dam ha-naki
²² Avot

**את אביה ואת אמה.** אם קרוב י״‎א כי זה הבכי על אביה ועל אמה שלא התיהדו ולפי דעתי שחייב כל אדם בשקול הדעת לכבד את אביו ואת אמו בחיים ובמות:


HER FATHER AND HER MOTHER. If close by.⁴⁴. 38 reads, if he (her captor) killed them. Some say that she bewails her father and mother because they did not convert to Judaism.⁴⁵ However, I believe that reason teaches us that every person is obligated to honor his father and his mother while they live and also after their deaths.

footnotes:
⁴⁴ If her parents were recently killed, that is, if they were killed in the war. Weiser believes that the reference is to her parents’ residence. If the place of their residence is close by, then the captive woman can ascertain the fate of her parents. Vat. Ebr
⁴⁵ In this case she bewails her parents even they are still alive.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 21:13:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:13:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:13:8)


וטעם **ובכתה.** שתתאבל עליהם כמשפט ישראלית כי היא מתייהדת אם נהרגו כאשר נשבת ואין צריך להזכיר תרחץ כי היא צריכה למי נדה כי כבר נכתב אתם ושביכם:


The meaning of *and bewail…* is, she shall mourn her parents if they were killed while she was taken captive in the same manner that an Israelite women mourns, for she is converting to Judaism. Scripture had no need to mention that she shall bathe,⁴⁶, a pool of water which purifies the impure. All converts have to immerse themselves in a *mikveh*. for it is necessary for her to be purified by the waters of sprinkling,⁴⁷. According to Rabbinic interpretation the reference is to a *mikveh*. as Scripture earlier states, *ye and your captives* (Num. 31:19).⁴⁸

footnotes:
⁴⁶ In a mikveh
⁴⁷ Hebrew, me niddah
⁴⁸ Shall purify yourselves in the “waters of sprinkling.”


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 21:13:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:13:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:13:9)


וחז״‎ל אמרו עד שלשה חדשים ואע״‎פ שאין צורך לחזוק הנה העד ויהי כמשלש חדשים והוא הזמן שיחל הולד להתנועע ואסור לשכב עם אשה בספק אם היא הרה בעבור הולד כי יש מי שיולד בחסרון שנים חדשים כמנהג ג״‎כ ביתרון רק הוא המעט:


[AND AFTER THAT THOU MAYEST GO INTO HER, AND BE HER HUSBAND.] Our rabbis, of blessed memory, said that he has to wait three months.⁴⁹ on this verse. Even though the words of our sages need no support⁵⁰ I offer the following *as* proof, *And it came to pass about three months after* (Gen. 38:24).⁵¹ The latter is the time when the fetus begins to move. It is prohibited to have sexual relations with a women when one is in doubt as to whether she is pregnant or not, because of the uncertain paternity of the fetus; for some women give birth two months short of the normal term.⁵² Others give birth later than the normal term.⁵³ However, the latter rarely occurs.⁵⁴

footnotes:
⁴⁹ Before marrying the captive woman, in order to ascertain the paternity of the child that she might be carrying. See Sifre
⁵⁰ That it takes three months before one is certain as to whether or not a woman is pregnant.
⁵¹ Three months after Tamar had intercourse with Judah her pregnancy first became evident.
⁵² Thus if a woman gives birth after nine months and had intercourse with one man nine months ago, and intercourse with another man seven months ago, we do not know whether she carried for nine months and the first man is the father, or she had the child prematurely and the second man is the father.
⁵³ At 11 months it is thus possible for the captor to wait three months before taking the captive woman and for the latter to have a child 8 months later without the captor being the husband. This being the case, why did the rabbis say that the captor has to wait three months? They should have said that he should wait four months.
⁵⁴ The rabbis were not concerned with what occurs rarely.

A FULL MONTH. *Yerach yamim* (a full month) is similar to *chodesh yamim* (a whole month) (Num. 11:21).⁵⁵ I have explained this previously.⁵⁶. See I.E. on Gen. 4:4 (Vol. 1, p. 81). According to I.E., *chodesh yamim* refers to a complete cycle of the month. A month is called a *yerach*⁵⁷ means a moon. because the moon is its basis.

### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 21:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/21:23:1)


**כי קללת אלהים תלוי.** בעבור שברך השם ועל דרך הפשט כי אלהים פועל והקללה תבוא לכל מקום קרוב מהתלוי ויש לו סוד דבק בנפש על כן ולא תטמא את אדמתך ונסמכה זו הפרשה בעבור המלחמה כי בתחלה כי תצא והנה גבעון יוכיח כי משפט לא תלין איננו לכבוד המת רק לכבוד הארץ כי משפט הערלים והישראלים [איננו] (בס' מ״‎ח מ״‎ז) שוה:


FOR HE THAT IS HANGED IS A REPROACH UNTO GOD.⁸⁷. For he cursed God.⁸⁸ as, he is hanged (*taluy*) for cursing God (*ki killelat Elohim*). When people see his body they are reminded that God was cursed. The latter is a reproach to God. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, God is the subject.⁸⁹ The curse comes to all places close to the hanged.⁹⁰ as for God curses the hanged. He interprets this as meaning God curses those who are near a hanged person. It⁹¹ has a secret connected to the soul.⁹² Scripture therefore goes on to say, *that thou defile not thy land*.⁹³ This section follows because of the war,⁹⁴ for Scripture first states, *When thou goest forth to battle* (Deut. 20:1). Now the incident at Gibeon⁹⁵ shows that the purpose of the law which says that his body shall not remain upon the tree all night is not out of respect for the deceased but rather out of respect for the land,⁹⁶ for the law of the Canaanites and the law of the Israelites differ.⁹⁷. 38 and other manuscripts. Some printed editions read: for the law of the uncircumcised and the law of the Israelites are the same. According to this reading Israel did not allow non-Jews to remain hanging on the tree because the Israelites respected Canaanite practice. The *Vat. Ebr*. 38 version is to be preferred for many reasons.

footnotes:
⁸⁷ Hebrew, ki killelat Elohim taluy
⁸⁸ This intrerpretation renders ki killelat Elohim taluy
⁸⁹ And he that is hanged the object.
⁹⁰ I.E. renders ki killelat taluy
⁹¹ This law.
⁹² The area infects the soul. I.E. probably meant that the sight of a hanged person and its putrefying smell affect a person’s psyche and prevent him from concentrating on philosophical and religious studies.
⁹³ By leaving a putrefying body exposed.
⁹⁴ Dealt with in verses 10-15.
⁹⁵ In the war at Gibeon Joshua captured five Canaanite kings and hanged them. He removed their bodies before nightfall. He did not do this out of respect for the deceased, for according to Canaanite practice there was nothing wrong in allowing the bodies to rot in public. Hence he did this out of respect for the land. See Josh. 10:26,27.
⁹⁶ That it not be defiled.
⁹⁷ The Gibeonites did not allow burial of the sons of Saul whom they hanged. Their bodies remained on the tree for months. See II Sam. 21:1-14. So Vat. Ebr

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 22:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:5:1)


**לא יהיה כלי גבר.** נסמכה בעבור צאת למלחמה כי האשה לא נבראת כי אם להקים הזרע ואם היא תצא עם אנשים למלחמה תבא בדרך לידי זנות וכן לא ילבש גבר והטעם זכר שלא נתמלא זקנו יתערב עם הנשים וינאף הוא והן ואינו יודע וזה יורה כי מנהג ישראל היה וכן ברובי המלכיות להיות מלבוש האנשים איננו כמלבוש הנשים רק הפרש ביניהם וי״‎א על חוץ לדרך ואין צורך רק השם יתעב מי שישנה מעשה השם:


A WOMAN SHALL NOT WEAR THAT WHICH PERTAINETH UNTO A MAN. This law was stated here because Scripture deals with going out to war. Women were created only to have children.¹¹ If a woman joins men in going to war she will come to engage in illicit sexual relations on the way.¹² The law that states *neither shall a man put on a woman’s garment* is similar.¹³ The reason for this law is as follows. If a male who does not have a full beard¹⁴ mixes with women, then he and they will have sexual relations without anyone knowing.¹⁵, as in *Vat. Ebr*. 38. A male dressing as a female has access to women. Rashi has a similar explanation. This law indicates that the custom of Israel was for the garments of men to be unlike the garments of women. There was a definite difference between the garments.¹⁶ This is also the practice in most countries. Some say that our verse speaks of unnatural intercourse.¹⁷ However, there is no need for this interpretation.¹⁸ The fact is that God abominates the one who changes the works of the Lord.¹⁹

footnotes:
¹¹ Legitimate children.
¹² Women who march off to war with men will have relations with them and produce illegitimate children. I.E. most probably inserted “on the way” because he wanted to explain why this law follows the previous one. It does so because both deal with something happening on the way. See I.E.’s comments on verse 6 and the notes thereto.
¹³ The purpose of the law is to prevent illicit sexual intercourse.
¹⁴ A full beard is not to be taken literally. It means enough facial hair to indicate that the person is a male.
¹⁵ Reading ve-en yode’a
¹⁶ Of males and females.
¹⁷ The reference is to homosexuality.
¹⁸ Our verse should be taken in accordance with its plain meaning.
¹⁹ Which cross dressing does, for one is then unable to distinguish between male and female.

**הנופל.** נקרא על שם סופו וכן יומת המת וכן ובגדי ערומים תפשיט ויתרוצצו הבנים ומלות רבות לאין מספר נקראו על שם סופם ולא נדע אם כן דרך הלשון. או הוא דברי נבואה כמו וירדוף עד דן עד נחל אשכול על כן יעזב איש את אביו ואת אמו ואחר מצות הבית מצות הזרע והנטע כי אחר שהוא בארץ ובנה בית וזרע:


IF ANY MAN FALL.³² Scripture speaks of the end result.³³ The following are similar: *The dead shall be put to death* (Deut. 17:6);³⁴ *And stripped the naked of their garments* (Job 22:6);³⁵ *And the children*³⁶ *struggled together* (Gen. 25:22). There are an innumerable number of words that are named because of the end result. We do not know if this is linguistic style or prophetic statements, as in *and pursued as far as Dan*³⁷ (Gen. 14:14); *unto the valley of Eshcol*³⁸ (Num. 13:23); and *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother*³⁹ (Gen. 2:24). After laying down the law dealing with the house, Scripture goes on to deal with the laws of seeds and plants, for after entering the land the Israelite would build a house and then plant.

### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 22:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:12:1)


**גדלים תעשה לך.** אמרו המכחישים שהוא מצוה בפני עצמה בלילה כמו הציצית ביום על כן כתוב אשר תכסה והמעתיקי' העתיקו כי זאת מצות הציצית ביום ופירוש גדלים כמו בבנינה גדלים מעשה שרשרות. והמכחישים הוציאוה מגזרת גדולה ואנחנו מאמינים בדברי קדמונינו לבדם והזכיר זה הכתוב לבאר על ארבע כנפות ונסמך לשעטנז בעבור הציצית שהוא מותר:


THOU SHALT MAKE TWISTED CORDS. The deniers⁴⁵ say that this is a separate commandment⁴⁶ pertaining to nighttime. It is similar to the fringes that are to be worn during the day. Scripture therefore reads, *wherewith thou coverest thyself*.⁴⁷ However, the transmitters of tradition say that our verse speaks of the fringes that are to be worn during the day.⁴⁸ 43a. The meaning of *gedilim* (twisted cords) is similar to the word *gedilim* (wreaths) which is employed with regard to the building of the temple. Compare, *wreaths* (gedilim) *of chainwork* (I Kings 7:17).⁴⁹ means twisted threads, for chain-work means twisted. The deniers connect the word *gedilim* to the word *gedolah* (large).⁵⁰ means large threads. We believe only in the words of our ancestors. Scripture mentions this law a second time⁵¹ in order to add *upon the four corners*.⁵² The law mandating fringes is connected to the law prohibiting a mixture of linen and wool because the latter does not apply to fringes.

⁴⁷ To indicate that it deals with fringes that are to be worn at night.
⁴⁸ See Menachot
⁴⁹ In other words, gedilim
⁵⁰ They saw that gedilim
⁵¹ That is, in addition to mentioning it in Num. 15:37-41, it also mentions it here.

### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 22:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:21:1)


**וסקלוה.** שיתכן שאחר שארסה שכב איש אותה כי המארס לא ארם אותה רק היא אומרת שהיא בתולה ומעתיקי הדת בארו הדבר באר היטב ואלה הבתולים ימצאו עד זמן קצוב וכפי תולדת הנערות ובעבור וסקלוה נסמכה פרשת הבעולה והמאורסה:


SHALL STONE HER. Someone most likely slept with her after he betrothed her, for the one who betrothed her would not have done so unless she told him that she was a virgin. The transmitters of the law explained the matter very clearly.⁵⁹ The signs of virginity are found until a fixed time, according to the nature of young ladies.⁶⁰ 59a, “And he (the High Priest) shall take a wife in her virginity (Lev. 21:13) excludes one who is a *bogeret* (a female above the age of 12 1/2) for her virginity has ended.” I.E. took this statement literally. However, other rabbis interpret this to mean that older women bleed less than those younger than 12 1/2. See *Tosafot, Yevamot* 59a. Also see *Ketuvot* 9a,b and Rashi and *Tosafot* comments there. Also see Maimonides, *Mishneh Torah, Hilkhot Ishut* 11:12,13. The law dealing with a married women was connected to the law of the betrothed damsel because Scripture states, *and the men of the city shall stone her*.⁶¹

⁶¹ The same penalty is exacted from a woman living in the house of her husband (v. 24).



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 22:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/22:22:1)


**גם** פירושו זה כמו זה והנה פירוש זה עוד:


BOTH OF THEM. The meaning of *gam*⁶² is also. The literal meaning of *u-metu gam shenehem* (then they shall both of them die) thus is, they shall also die both of them. The word *gam* seems out of place. Hence I.E. renders *gam* as this one like that one. ### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 23:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/23:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/23:3:1)


**ממזר.** אחז״‎ל הבא מן העריות והשני ממי״‎ן נוספין כממי״‎ן נהרסו ממגורות ואחרים אמרו כי הוא שם גוי וישב ממזר באשדוד כי רחוק הוא שיקרא שם ישראל ואף כי בעת הישועה בשם גנאי והמתרגם תפש דרך קצרה ודרש:


Our rabbis, of blessed memory, said that a *mamzer* (bastard) is a child that results from a sexual act which is deemed an *uncovering of the nakedness*.¹⁶ The two *mems* of *mamzer* are superfluous.¹⁷ is a variant of *zar*, (a stranger). A *mamzer* is a child born to people who must remain strangers to each other with regard to sexual relations. They are like the *mems* in *mamgurot* (barns) in *the barns are broken down* (Joel 1:17). Others say that *mamzer* is the name of a people. Compare, *And a mamzer shall dwell in Ashdod* (Zech. 9:6), for it is far-fetched for Israel to be given a shameful name.¹⁸. It is even more unlikely for this to happen in the time of the salvation.¹⁹ refers to Israel then the prophet is saying that the bastards (Israel) shall dwell in Ashdod when the messiah comes. Therefore what the prophet says is that in the messianic era a nation called *mamzer* will dwell in Ashdod. The Aramaic translator of the Bible was brief and midrashic.²⁰ to Zech. 9:6 renders *And a mamzer shall dwell in Ashdod*, and the children of Israel shall dwell in Ashdod where they were strangers. Thus the *Targum* renders *mamzer* in Zechariah as strangers. *Vat. Ebr*. 38 says, the Aramaic translator of the Bible interpreted it midrashically. The latter reading appears correct, for the *Targum* elaborates on the text.

WHEN EVENING COMETH ON. *Li-fenot erev* (when evening cometh) is similar in meaning to *ki fanah ha-yom* (for the day declineth) (Jer. 6:4).³¹. In other words, *li-fenot erev* means when the day declines, when the shadows of evening come. According to Krinsky and others the reference is to the afternoon when the sun begins its decline. Filwarg believes the reference is to about an hour and a third before the onset of night. See I.E. on Gen. 1:18 (Vol. 1, p. 40). “Know that evening begins at sunset and lasts for one and a third hours, during which time a light-like appearance is seen before sunrise.” Also see Rashi: “He should immerse himself close before the setting of the sun” (Rosenbaun and Silberman translation). This also strengthens the opinion of the rabbis of blessed memory.³² The deniers³³ say that *li-fenot* (cometh on) means before.³⁴ refers to night. They interpret *li-fenot erev* as before night comes, i.e., after sunset. They say nothing of value. Some say³⁵ that the meaning of *li-fenot erev* (when evening cometh) is, when the evening begins to come.³⁶ Now, after Scripture employs the phrase *li-fenot erev*, it says, *and when the sun is down. Li-fenot erev* thus means before the evening.³⁷ *Li-fenot boker* (when the morning appeared) is similarly before sunrise.³⁸

ונסמכה פרשת קדשה בעבור העבד ומעתיקי הדת אמרו כי הקדש הוא הנשכב והעד מבנ״‎י. ואמר אליהוא וחיתם בקדשים כי נפשם כנגד חיתם והנה קדשים כנגד' נועד וכתוב וגם קדש היה בארץ בתי הקדשים ושם כתוב אשר הנשים אורגות שם ואני לא אבין טעם קדשה וכאשר נחפשה היטב טעם המלה אז היא ידועה שהיא מזומנת לכל עובר ושב והעד איה הקדשה א״‎כ יהיה קדש כמעשה המצרים והמבין יבין ובעבור קדשה נסמכה פרשת אתנן זונה:


[THERE SHALL BE NO HARLOT] The law of the *kedeshah* (harlot) follows because the previous section deals with a bondman.⁵⁴ The transmitters of tradition say that the term *kadesh* (sodomite) refers to the one who is slept with.⁵⁵ The phrase *of the sons of Israel* is proof of this.⁵⁶ Elihu said, [*Their soul perisheth in youth] And their life as that of the depraved* (kedeshim) (Job 36:14); *their soul* corresponds to *their life* and *kedeshim* corresponds to *in youth*.⁵⁷ Scripture also states, *And there were also sodomites* (kadesh) *in the land* (I Kings 14:24); *the house of the sodomites* (kedeshim) II Kings 23:7). Scripture there continues, *where the women*⁵⁸ *wove coverings* (*Ibid.*). I do not understand the meaning of the word *kedeshah*. (harlot). When we investigate carefully the meaning of the word we find that it refers to a woman who is known to be prepared to offer herself to all who come and go. *Where is the harlot* (kedeshah) (Gen. 38:21) is proof of this. If this is so,⁵⁹ refers to a female engaged in heterosexual intercourse, then so must the term *kadesh*, for *kadesh* is the masculine form of the noun. then the term *kadesh* refers to an Egyptian-like practice.⁶⁰. See I. E. on Haggai 2:12. The intelligent will understand.⁶¹ The law dealing with a harlot’s hire follows because our section deals with a harlot.

footnotes:
⁵⁴ Slaves were considered to be promiscuous.
⁵⁵ The one who takes the passive position in male homosexual intercourse.
⁵⁶ That the reference is to the passive partner in male homosexuality, for the term “of” implies passivity. Otherwise Scripture would have used the term “among” (Krinsky, Meijler). I.E.’s point is that “of” means belonging to. Hence within the context of our verse it alludes to the docile sex partner.
⁵⁷ I.E. renders this like youth; that is, their soul perishes like the souls of young men who are sodomites.
⁵⁸ I.E. takes this reference to be to prostitutes (Krinsky).
⁵⁹ If the term kedeshah
⁶⁰ I.E. believed that the ancient Egyptians were weak, and when they reached the age of forty they did not have the strength to deflower a virgin. They therefore had to turn to an individual who had the ability to do so on their behalf. This individual was called a kadesh
⁶¹ What I.E. is alluding to.

HIRE. The word *etnan* (hire) is similar to *mattan* (gift).⁶². The *alef*⁶³. is superfluous and the *nun*⁶⁴. is doubled⁶⁵ in its root. like the *peh* of *na’afufehah*⁶⁶. (her adulteries) (Hos. 2:4) and like the *resh* of the word *sagrir* (rainy) (Prov. 27:15). *Etnan* refers to what the harlot took, that which those who turn to her give her. [The hire of a harlot shall not be brought to the house of God] because it was given for a prohibited act.

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 23:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/23:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/23:20:1)


**לא תשיך לאחיך.** בעבור שהזכיר העבד הנכרי אע״‎פ שכתוב בו לא תוננו יש לך רשות שתשיכנו:


THOU SHALT NOT LEND UPON INTEREST TO THY BROTHER. This law is mentioned here because Scripture earlier mentions the non-Jewish bondman (v. 17). Scripture states that even though it is prohibited to wrong the latter,⁶⁸ it is permitted to take interest from him.

⁶⁸ The foreign bondman who has found refuge in Israel.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 23:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/23:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/23:20:2)


**לא תשיך לאחיך.** יש הפרש בין תשך לתשיך והטעם שלא תקבל מאחיך שיתן לך רבית גם הוא עובר על מצות רבית והנה המלה יוצאה לשנים פעולים ורבים אמרו כי תשיך כמו תשך אין הפרש ביניהם וכמו כן פעולים רבים במקרא:


THOU SHALT NOT LEND UPON INTEREST TO THY BROTHER. There is a difference between *tishokh* (you shall take interest)⁶⁹. and *tashikh* (Thou shalt lend upon interest).⁷⁰. The meaning of *lo tashikh* (Thou shalt not lend upon interest) is, you shall not accept interest from your brother when he offers it;⁷¹ is you shall not cause interest to be given. your brother also violates the law regarding interest.⁷² Notice, *tashikh* is a word governing two acts.⁷³ and refers to both you and your brother. You shall not cause your brother to give you interest, and your brother shall not give you interest. Many say that *tashikh* is similar to *tishokh*.⁷⁴ is a *hifil*, it has the meaning of a *kal*. It means you shall not take interest. There is no difference between them. There are many such verbs in Scripture.⁷⁵ with the meaning of the *kal*.

⁷⁰ Which is a hifil
⁷¹ The meaning of lo tashikh
⁷² When he gives it.
⁷³ It is a hifil
⁷⁴ In other words, even though tashikh
⁷⁵ Verbs in the hifil

### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 24:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:1:1)


**כי יקח איש אשה.** גם הוא חשובה כשרה. [ס״‎א כשדה]:


WHEN A MAN TAKETH A WIFE. She is also considered fit.¹. However, she is disliked by her husband. I.E. takes issue with Beth Shamai, which interprets *some unseemly thing* as a sexual transgression. See *Mishnah, Gitten* 9:10. Other editions read, she is also considered as a field (*ke-sadeh*). A woman, like a field, is acquired by a money transaction. See *Kedushin* 2a. Hence the law regarding a woman follows that of the field. Filwarg believes that I.E. compares a woman to a field in that both are seeded and produce fruit.

footnotes:
¹ Hebrew, kesherah


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 24:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:1:2)


**חן בעיניו.** שהיא הפך תולדתו:


FAVOR IN HIS EYES. For her nature is the reverse of his.²

footnotes:
² The reason that she did not find favor in her husband’s eyes was not due to a moral imperfection.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 24:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:1:3)


**ומצא בה.** ולא יוכל לגלות כי אין לו עדים והטעם או מצא בה כמו ומכה אביו ואמו:


AND HE HATH FOUND.³. I.E.’s reading is *And he had found*. The problem is that the verse reads *ki matza* (because he has found). Weiser suggests that *u-matza* is I.E.’s paraphrase of *ki matza*. However, I.E. goes on to prove that the *vav* prefixed to a word sometimes has the meaning of “or.” It is a bit farfetched to say that I.E. intends to say that *ki matza* should be interpreted as *u-matza*, and that *u-matza* should be interpreted as *or has found*, because a *vav* sometimes has the meaning of or. It thus appears either that I.E.’s copy of Deuteronomy had *u-matza* or that I.E. quoted from memory and committed an egregious error. And he cannot reveal it,⁴ for he has no witnesses.⁵ The meaning of *and he hath found* is, or he hath found, as in *And he that smiteth his father, or his mother* (Ex. 21:15).

footnotes:
³ Hebrew, u-matza
⁴ The moral imperfection found in her.
⁵ To the immoral act that he accuses her of.

למ״‎ד **לכל דבר.** נוסף כמו והשלישי לאבשלום:


[WITH ANY BUSINESS.] The *lamed* placed before *le-khol davar* (with any business) is superfluous.¹⁴ should be read *kol davar. Le-khol davar* literally means to any business. *Khol davar* means any business. It is like the *lamed* in *le-avshalom* (Absalom) in *the third, Absalom* (I Chron. 3:2).¹⁵. Literally, the third, to Absalom. However, the context does not permit this interpretation. Hence the *lamed* of *le-avshalom* is superfluous, and *le-avshalom* is to be read as if written *avshalom*.

footnotes:
¹⁴ Le-khol davar
¹⁵ Hebrew, ha-shelishi le-avshalom



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 24:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:6:1)


**לא יחבול רחים ורכב.** אמרו המכחישים כי נדבקה זאת הפרשה עם ושמח את אשתו כי רמז למשכב כי אסור שימנע מן המשכב וזה הבל וריק והביאו ראיה תטחן לאחר אשתי וכבר פירשתיו והאמת שהוא כמשמעו שאסור לאדם שיחבול רחים ותחסר מלת חובל כמו ויאמר ליוסף אשר ילדה אותה ללוי ורבים כן כי טעמם ויאמר לו האומר ילדה לו היולדת:


NO MAN SHALL TAKE THE MILL OR THE UPPER MILLSTONE TO PLEDGE. The deniers¹⁶ say that this section is connected to *and shall cheer his wife whom he hath taken* (v. 5),¹⁷. This can be rendered, he shall not harm (Krinsky). Thus the meaning of our verse is, one shall not harm his partner by refraining from taking the upper position (the upper millstone) or the lower position (the mill). for our verse alludes to coitus, namely, that it is forbidden to abstain from sexual intercourse. However, this is sheer nonsense. They offer as proof, *Then let my wife grind unto another* (Job 31:10). I have previously explained the latter.¹⁸ The truth is that our verse is to be taken at face value,¹⁹ that a person is prohibited from taking a mill to pledge. The word *chovel* (one who takes a pledge) is missing from our verse.²⁰. This literally means he shall not take the mill or the upper millstone to pledge. The question is: To whom does “he” refer? Hence I.E. points out that the word *chovel* (anyone that takes a pledge) has been omitted. Our verse should be read as if written, *lo yachavol chovel rechayim va-rechev* (any one that takes a pledge shall not take the mill or the upper millstone to pledge). It is similar to *and he said to Joseph* (Gen. 48:1) and to *whom she bore to Levi* (Num. 26:29), for the meaning of the former is, someone said to Joseph, and of the latter, the one who bore, bore to Levi.²¹ There are many such cases.²²

¹⁸ That intercourse is metaphorically described by the term “grinding.” See I.E. on Job 31:10.
¹⁹ Despite the fact that “grind” is used as a metaphor for sexual intercourse in Job.
²⁰ Our verse reads, lo yachavol rechayim va-rechev

**רחים.** שם שנים ולא יתכן להיותם נפרדים:


THE MILL. The word *rechayim* (mill) is in the dual form. It does not come in the singular.

THE UPPER MILLSTONE. *Rechev* (upper millstone) refers to a water mill. Others say that it refers to the wood which is placed on the mill.²³ Still others say that the *rechayim* (mill) refers to the lower millstone and *rechev* to the upper millstone.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 24:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:6:4)


**כי נפש הוא חובל.** כי בו מחית נפשות והסומכים על הסמך הפרשיות איננה טענה כי כל מצו' עומדת בפני עצמה והסמיכות כדרך דרש וזאת הפרש' דבקה כי הזכיר שלא יגזול ענבים לתת אל כליו וחרמש בקמה ולקחת אשה והיתה לו גם לאחר ויצא מרשותו והלוקח אשה שישמח בה לא יהיה עשוק שיצא בצבא וחביל' הרחים עושק וגם גונב נפש וכן נגע הצרעת שלא ישמרו משפטיה תזיק הקרובים וכן לא תעשוק העני בעבוטו והשכיר והבנים הקטנים שלא ימותו בעון אביהם והטיית משפט גר יתום וחבול בגד אלמנה ושכחה בשדה כי היא לעני וכן לא תעולל וכן פן יוסיף ונקלה וחסימת השור עשק כי יגע ולא יאכל והממאן ליבם כדמות עשק והמחזקת במבושים עושקת אבן ואבן איפה ואיפה עשק ממש גם עמלק עשק לישראל:


FOR HE TAKETH A MAN’S LIFE TO PLEDGE. For life is sustained by these instruments. Those who rely on the juxtaposition of the sections have no argument,²⁴ for each commandment stands by itself.²⁵ The explanation of their juxtapositions is midrashic.²⁶ This section²⁷ is connected to the previous ones in the following way:²⁸ the Torah mentions that one is not to steal grapes by putting them in his pots (Deut. 23:25), or to lift up a sickle upon his neighbor’s grain (Deut. 23:26); or to take a woman after she has been his and then left his house and married another (v. 1). It also states that one has to cheer the woman whom he marries (v. 5); he is not to be oppressed by going into the army (*Ibid.*). The taking of a millstone in pledge is a form of oppression.²⁹ So too is kidnapping a person. Similarly the plague of leprosy, for if he does not observe its laws then the plague will injure those in proximity to it.³⁰ Scripture similarly states, do not oppress a poor person by taking a pledge from him (v. 10). It similarly states do not oppress a hired person (v. 14) and small children should not be put to death for the sins of the fathers (v. 16). It likewise warns against perverting the justice due a stranger or the fatherless (v. 17). It prohibits the taking of a widow’s garment as a pledge (v. 17). It prohibits one from retrieving a sheaf which was forgotten in the field, for it belongs to the poor (v. 19). Similarly *Thou shalt not glean* (v. 21). Likewise *lest if he should exceed…Then thy brother should be dishonored* (Deut. 25:3).³¹ The muzzling of an ox (v. 4) is an act of oppression, for the animal toils but cannot eat of its toil. Similarly, refusing to perform levirate marriage (Deut. 25:5-10) is a form of oppression. The woman who grabs a man’s testicles (Deut. 25:11) commits an act of oppression. Employing diverse weights and diverse measures (Deut. 25:13,14) is oppression in its purest form. Furthermore, Amalek oppressed Israel (Deut. 25:17-19).³²

²⁷ The law regarding taking a mill to pledge.
²⁸ That is, if we want to connect this section midrashically to what comes before, we can so in the following manner.

³⁰ By infecting them.
³¹ Deut. 25:3 prohibits the infliction of more that 40 stripes to one being punished by lashes. Exceeding this number of stripes is a form of oppression.
³² Thus the laws in Deut. 23:25-25:19 are thematically related. Hence the law prohibiting the taking of a mill was included in this section.

Here is proof of the midrashic statement that we should not read the word *metzora* as *metzora* (a leper) but as an acronym for *motzi shem ra* (one who invents libel).³⁶ on the Torah portion *Metzora* 2. ###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 24:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/24:20:1)


**כי תחבוט.** כמו חובט חטים והוא פעל יחבט קצח בנין נפעל וכן כל אותיות אחעה״‎ר כאשר יבנה מהם בנין נפעל ואלה הם לא יאצר ולא יחסן. ולא יהרג. יעבד בו. יראה כל זכורך כי כן המשפט:


WHEN THOU BEATEST. *Tachbot* (thou beatist) is similar to *chovet* (beating) in *beating out wheat* (Jud. 6:11). It is in the *pa’al*.⁵⁶. The word *yechavet* (is beaten) in *But the black cummin is beaten* (Is. 28:27) is a *nifal*. All letters whose first root letter is an *alef, chet, heh, ayin*, or *resh* are vocalized like *yechavet* when conjugated in the *nifal*. The following are examples of each one of the aforementioned: *ye’atzer*⁵⁷. (treasured) and *yechasen*⁵⁸. (laid up) in *it shall not be treasured nor laid up* (Is. 23:18); *yehareg*⁵⁹. (killed) as in *ve-lo yehareg* (and will not be killed); *ye’aved*⁶⁰. (plowed) in *neither be plowed* (Deut. 21:4); *yera’eh*⁶¹, *alef*, *heh*. (appear) in *and they shall not appear* (Deut,. 16:16), for this is the rule.⁶², *chet*, *heh*, *ayin*, or *resh* is vocalized with a *tzere* rather than with a *chirik*, which is the usual vocalization.

⁵⁹ From the root heh, resh, gimel
⁶⁰ From the root ayin, bet, dalet
⁶¹ From the root resh
⁶² The letter prefixed to all words whose first root letter is an alef

## Chapter 25


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 25:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:1:1)


**ושפטום.** השופטים כמו לא יחבול רחים:


AND…JUDGE THEM. *U-shefatum*¹ literally means and they will judge them. The subject is omitted. Our verse literally reads, *if there be a controversy between men and they go unto judgment, and they judge them* (u-shefatum). Hence I.E. explains that “and they judge them” is short for: and the judges judge them. is to be rendered, and the judges judge them. Our verse is similar to *No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone to pledge* (Deut. 24:6).²

¹ U-shefatum
² Here too the subject is omitted, for the verse literally reads, He shall not take the mill to pledge. See I.E. on Deut. 24:6 and the notes thereto.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 25:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:2:1)


**בן הכות.** בחיר״‎ק כמו בן נון (ס״‎א בן) יקה והטעם כמו בן בליעל. וכן שבן לילה היה. והוא חייב. להכותו לפי דעתי שהכה חברו:


DESERVE TO BE BEATEN. The word *bin* (deserve) is vocalized with a *chirik*.³, i.e., *ben*. Compare, *bin nun* (son of Nun) (Josh. 1:1) and *bin yakeh* (son of Jakeh) (Prov. 30:1). *Bin hakkot* (deserve to be beaten) is similar to *ben bliyya’al* (a base fellow) (I Sam. 25:17).⁴ usually means son of. However, in *bin hakkot* and *ben bliyya’al, ben* signifies that the subject belongs to a certain group. *Bin laylah* (in a night) in *which came up in a night* (Jonah 4:10) is similar. The judge is obligated to beat him.⁵ means that the wicked falls into the category of those whom the judge is obligated to have beaten. I believe that Scripture calls the culprit wicked⁶. because he struck his neighbor.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 25:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:2:3)


**כדי רשעתו במספר.** המכות. היה נראה לנו שיש עון שיוכה עליו עשר גם עשרים ופחות ויותר והעד כדי רשעתו רק לא יוסיף על ארבעים לולי דברי הקבלה והוא לבדו האמת וי״‎א כי טעם רשעתו במכות גדולות או קטנות וכלם במספר ארבעים:


ACCORDING TO THE MEASURE OF HIS WICKEDNESS, BY NUMBER. Of blows. It would have appeared to us, were it not for the words of tradition,⁹ that there are some sins that a person is punished for with ten blows. Others are punished with twenty blows. Other sins are punished with a lesser or greater number. The clause *according to the measure of his wickedness* is proof of this. In any case,¹⁰ the blows shall not exceed forty. However, the words of tradition alone are true.¹¹ Others say that *his wickedness*¹². refers to greater or lesser blows,¹³ all of which number forty.¹⁴

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 25:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:5:1)


**כי ישבו אחים יחדו.** גם הם אמרו כי אינם אחים ממש כי אם קרובים והביאו ראיה מבועז ולא אמרו כלום כי אין שם זכר יבום כי אם גאול' ומה טעם להזכיר יחדו ואם היו במדינ' אחת או בחצר אחד או שהיו אוהבים זה את זה. ואמרו כי הנה הכתוב אמר ויבמה וזה אות כי איננה יבמה כי אם בשם כמו שבה יבמתך והנה נואלו ונסכלו כי הנה מפורש בבני יהודה ויבם אותה והוא יבמה גם יבמתך בעבור היותן לשני אחים וכל איש דעת ידע כי המצות שנתנו למשה שהם מצות לא תעשה לא היו אסורות קודם לכן ואילו היה אדם מונע עצמו מהן וקדם משה לא היה הדבר רע בעיני השם אף כי שכתב כי את כל התועבות האל עשו אנשי הארץ אשר לפניכם ולא מצאנו נביא שהזהירם והנה הכתוב אמר על אונן שלא נתן זרע לאחיו וירע בעיני ה' על כן אנחנו נסמוך על הקבל' שהם אחים ממש:


IF BRETHREN¹⁹ (brothers). DWELL TOGETHER. The deniers also say that these brethren²⁰ are not actual brothers,²¹ but are relatives. They brought proof from Boaz.²² (Ruth 4:5). However, they contribute nothing, for there is no mention of levirate marriage,²³ only of redemption.²⁴ Why mention the word *together*?²⁵ Does it matter if they were in one state or in one courtyard, or if they loved each other?²⁶ They say,²⁷. 38. *Mikra’ot Gedolot* reads: He says. look, the verse says *ve-yibbemah* (and shall perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto her).²⁸ means a brother-in-law. This shows that he is her brother-in-law in name only.²⁹ as, and be a brother-in-law to her. Now if the true brother-in-law was being addressed Scripture would not say, and be a brother-in-law to her. Hence we must interpret *ve-yibbemah* as meaning “act as a brother-in-law to her.” The upshot of all this is that a true brother-in-law is not being addressed. It is like *thy sister-in-law* (yevimtekh)³⁰ is the word *yevamah* (sister-in-law) plus the second person personal pronoun. Orpah was the wife of Ruth’s brother-in-law (*yavam*). She is referred to as a *yevamah* because she took her husband’s place. We thus see that the term *yavam* in its various forms can refer to one who acts like one’s brother-in-law. *is gone back* (Ruth 1:15). Now observe that they have become foolish and stupid, for Scripture states, with regard to the sons of Judah, *and perform the duty of a husband’s brother* (ve-yabbem) *unto her*³¹ (Gen. 38:8).³² your sister-in-law Tamar. Now he³³ was her³⁴ brother-in-law.³⁵ Also, the term *yevimtekh* (thy sister-in-law) (Ruth 1:15) was used because they were married to two brothers.³⁶ was not employed figuratively in Ruth. All intelligent people know that the negative commandments given to Moses³⁷ were not previously prohibited.³⁸ However, it would not have been evil in the eyes of God if someone abstained from them³⁹ before the law was given to Moses.⁴⁰ The fact that Scripture states, *for all these abominations have the men of the land done, that were before you* (Lev. 18:27), shows that this is certainly the case. We do not find a prophet who warned them.⁴¹ 5: “The fundamental commandments are those precepts that are implanted in the heart. They…were known by reason before the Torah was given through the agency of Moses” (Strickman translation, p. 75). Look, Scripture says of Onan, who did not give seed to his brother, *the thing which he did was evil in the sight of God* (Gen. 38:10).⁴² We will therefore rely on the tradition that they are actual brothers.

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 25:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/25:13:1)


**בכיסך.** מקום למאזנים או יוציא מן הכיס בדרך רמאות והראשון הוא נכון והעד כיס אחד יהיה לכלנו משקל אחד. ומגזרת תכוסו על השה ואם הוא משורש אחר ורבים פירשו כמו חריט ואין צורך:


IN THY BAG.⁶⁰. Where you place the scales.⁶¹ (bag) is the name of a receptacle where the scales are kept. Or, do not deceitfully take the weights from the bag.⁶² The first interpretation is correct. The proof text is, *Let us all have one hag* (kis)⁶³ (Prov. 1:14), the meaning of which is, one scale.⁶⁴ (Prov. 1:14) is, let us all have one scale, for let us all have one bag makes no sense in this context. The word *kis* (bag) is related to the word *tachossu* (ye shall make your count)⁶⁵ means you shall apportion. A person uses scales to measure the weight of portions. See I.E. on Ex. 12:4 (Vol. 2, p. 219). in *ye shall make your count for the lamb* (Ex. 12:4) even though *tachossu* comes from a different root.⁶⁶ comes from the root *caf, vav, samekh. Tachossu* comes from the root *caf, samekh, samekh*. Many explained the word *kis* to mean a pouch.⁶⁷ (a cloth into which an object is placed). In this case *kis* refers not only to a receptacle for scales but to any bag or purse. There is no need for this interpretation.

## Chapter 26


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 26:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/26:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/26:1:1)


**והיה כי תבא.** בעבור שכתוב בהניח ה' אמר השם כי יש מצות הן קודם בהניח ה' רק כאשר תבא והם הבכורים והמעשר וכתיבת התורה על האבנים ובנות מזבח והברכה והקלל' על שני ההרים:


AND IT SHALL BE, WHEN THOU ART COME. Since Scripture wrote, *Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest* (Deut. 25:19),¹ God now says that there are commandments that must be observed before He gives you rest. In fact, these commandments take effect as soon as you enter the land. They are: the first fruits,² the tithes,³ writing the Torah on the stones,⁴ building the altar,⁵, 4-6. and the blessing and the curse on the two mountains.⁶

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 26:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/26:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/26:5:2)


**אובד אבי.** מלת אובד מהפעלים שאינם יוצאים ואילו היה ארמי על לבן היה הכתוב אומר מאביד או מאבד ועוד מה טעם לאמר לבן בקש להאביד אבי וירד מצרימה ולבן לא סבב לרדת אל מצרים והקרוב שארמי הוא יעקב כאלו אמר הכ' כאשר היה אבי בארם היה אובד והטעם עני בלא ממון וכן תנו שכר לאובד והעד ישתה וישכח רישו והנה הוא ארמי אובד היה אבי והטעם כי לא ירשתי הארץ מאבי כי עני היה כאשר בא אל ארם גם גר היה במצרים והוא היה במתי מעט ואחר כן שב לגוי גדול ואתה ה' הוצאתנו מעבדות ותתן לנו ארץ טובה ואל יטעון טוען איך יקרא יעקב ארמי והנה כמוהו יתרא הישמעאלי והוא ישראלי כי כן כתוב:


A WANDERING ARAMEAN. The word *oved* (wandering) is an intransitive verb. If Aramean referred to Laban¹⁶ (a wandering Aramean was my father) is to be rendered an Aramean (Laban) sought to destroy my father (Jacob). See *Sifre*, the Passover Haggadah, and Rashi. then Scripture should have read *mavid or me’abbed*.¹⁷ Furthermore, what reason would Scripture have had for stating, *Laban sought to destroy my father and he*¹⁸ *went down to Egypt*? Laban did not cause Jacob to descend to Egypt. It thus appears to me that the term Aramean refers to Jacob. Scripture, as it were, reads, when my father was in Aram he was “perishing.” That is, he was poor, he had no money. Similarly *oved* (perish) in *Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish* (Prov. 31:6). *Let him drink, and forget his poverty* (Prov. 31:7) is proof.¹⁹ The meaning of our phrase thus is, a perishing Aramean was my father. Its import is, I did not inherit the land from my father, for my father was poor when he came to Aram.²⁰ He was also a stranger in Egypt. He was few in number.²¹ He then became a large nation.²² You O Lord took us out of slavery and gave us a good land. Let the one who disputes²³. not argue, “How could Jacob be called an Aramean?”²⁴ Look, we find the same with Ithra the Ishmaelite²⁵ who, as Scripture clearly states,²⁶ was an Israelite.²⁷

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 26:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/26:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/26:14:1)


**לא אכלתי באוני.** כמו בן אוני ולחם אונים והטעם רמזתי על לשון הקודש וטעם אוני כמו אבלי כי אם הייתי אבל לא אכלתי (קודם) [ס״‎א קודש] המעשר:


I HAVE NOT EATEN THEREOF IN MY MOURNING. The word *oni* (my mourning) is similar to the word *oni* (sorrow) in *ben-oni* (the son of my sorrow) (Gen. 35:18) and *onim* (mourners) in *bread of mourners* (Hosea 9:4). I alluded⁴⁰ to its meaning⁴¹ in Hebrew.⁴². 38. Some emend our verse to read, “in my book on the Hebrew language (*Moznayim*).” See Weiser. The meaning of *oni* is, my mourning. If I was in mourning then I did not eat of it before setting aside the tithe.⁴³. Some editions read *lo akhalti kodesh ha-ma’aser*, I did not eat the holy, the tithe. The latter is forbidden to a mourner in the time between the death and burial of a close relative.

**האמרת.** מלשון גדולה וקרוב מגזרת בראש אמיר ויאמר רבי יהודה הלוי הספרדי נ״‎ע כי המלה מגזרת ויאמר והטעם כי עשית הישר עד שיאמר שהוא יהי' אלהיך גם הוא עוש' לך עד שאמרת שתהי' לו לעם סגולה ויפה פירש והנה תהיה מלת האמרת פעל יוצא לשנים פעולים:


THOU HAST AVOUCHED. *He’emarta* (avouched) means exalted. It is close in meaning to *amir* (uppermost bough) in *In the top of the uppermost bough* (Is. 17:6). **שמור את כל המצוה.** ומה היא והקמות לך אבנים גדולו' להכיל התורה ויאמר הגאון ז״‎ל כי כתוב עליהם מספר המצות כמו הכתובות בהלכות גדולות בענין אזהרות ויפה אמר:


KEEP ALL THE COMMANDMENTS. Namely, *that thou shalt set thee up great stones* to contain the entire Torah. The Gaon,⁵ of blessed memory, said that the commandments⁶ were listed upon the stones, as in the *Halakhot Gedolot*.⁷ was the first to enumerate the 613 commandments. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon uses the *Halakhot Gedolot* as an illustration of a list of the 613 commandments, for it was the first work to provide such a list. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon interprets thus because he does not believe that the stones were large enough for the entire five books of the Torah to have been written upon. They were listed in a manner similar to the *azharot*.⁸ (exhortation) is 613. He explained well.

⁸ Liturgical poems devoted to the enumeration of the 613 commandments. The numerical value of the Hebrew letters of azharot

They then turned their faces towards Mount Ebal and opened with the curse: *Cursed is the man who maketh a graven or molten image*, and both parties respond amen.” is to say, *blessed is the man who does not make a graven or molten image*, and similarly all of them.²⁶ However, according to the plain meaning of the text, the blessing refers to *Blessed shalt thou be in the city* (Deut. 28:3).²⁷, that is, Deut. 28:3-13. וטעם להזכיר אלה י״‎א עבירות בעבור שיוכל לעשותם בסתר והעד ושם בסתר כי אם יעשה בגלוי יומת וכן מכה רעהו בסתר והחל מהעיקר שהוא בינו ובין בוראו ואחר כן בינו ובין אבותיו כי מי ידע אם יקלה אותם:


Scripture mentions these eleven sins³⁰ because an individual can commit them in secret. *And setteth it up in secret* (v. 15) is proof, for if one commits this crime³¹ in the open he is put to death.³² *He that smiteth his neighbor in secret* (v. 24) is similar. Scripture begins with the most important, namely, that which concerns a person and his creator.³³ It then speaks of a person and his parents,³⁴ for who knows if he dishonors them.³⁵

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 27:19:1

**מטה משפט גר יתום.** כי אין להם עוזר והנה גם הוא בסתר והזכיר הגר גם היתום והאלמנה כי אם יטה הדיין משפט אחרים יערערו עליו ויפרסמוהו והגר והיתום והאלמנה אין להם כח. ושוכב עם אשת אב ואחות וחותנת אינו נחשד להתייחד עמה על כן הוא דבר נסתר ואין כן שאר העבירות:


CURSED BE HE THAT PERVERTETH THE JUSTICE DUE TO THE STRANGER, FATHERLESS. For they have no one to help them. Look, this too is done in secret.³⁶ Scripture mentions the stranger as well as the orphan and the widow because if the judge perverts the justice due others, they will accuse and publicize him. The stranger, the orphan, and the widow are powerless. Sleeping with one’s father’s wife, with a sister, or with a mother-in-law is an act that is committed in secret, for one is not suspected when he is alone with any one of them. It is not so with other sins.³⁷

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 27:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/27:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/27:26:1)


**אשר לא יקים.** י״‎א על כל התורה וי״‎א על אלה הנזכרים ולא אמרו כלום בעבור שכתוב לעשות אותם והנכון בעיני כי קלל על מצות לא תעשה הנזכרים וקלל מי שלא ישמור גם בסתר מצות עשה על כן אמר לעשות אותם:


THAT CONFIRMETH NOT. Some say that the reference is to the entire Torah. Others say that it refers to the specifically mentioned sins.⁴⁰ However, what they say is meaningless, for Scripture says, *to do them*.⁴¹ However, it appears to me that Scripture cursed the violators of the precepts which are mentioned.⁴² It also cursed the one who secretly does not observe the positive commandments. Scripture therefore reads, *to do them*.

footnotes:
⁴⁰ The sins mention in verse 15-25.
⁴¹ The verse curses those who fail to observe positive practices, not only those who violate certain laws.
⁴² In verses 15-25.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:7:1)


ואחר שאמר שתהיה עליון על כל הגוים אמר כי אם יקשרו אויביך על כן אמר הקמים עליך:


[THAT RISE UP AGAINST THEE.] Since Scripture earlier stated that God will set Israel on high above the nations (v. 1), it now goes on to say that should the nations revolt against Israel [the Lord will cause thine enemies] *that rise up against thee* [to be smitten before thee].


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:7:2)


**ובשבעה.** לשון רבים בעבור שוב ימי השבוע כי הוא תלוי בעליונים:


AND…SEVEN. This means many.¹⁵ The number seven is employed because of the continuous cycle of seven days of the week.¹⁶ It¹⁷ has a set number of days because is contingent on the bodies which are on high.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁵ Seven is not to be taken literally.
¹⁶ It is the maximum number of days in the week. Scripture did not use a month because there are not the same number of days in each month.
¹⁷ The week.
¹⁸ Each day of the week is connected to one of the seven moving heavenly bodies, namely, the sun, the moon, and the five visible planets.

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:13:1

**כי תשמע.** בלב לשמור ולעשו' והכלל שלא תסו' מאחרי השם לעבוד עבודת כוכבים כי הוא עיקר כל העבירות לכפור בעיקר והפך זה יחוד השם לשמור ולעשות כי עיקר השמיר' המעש':


IF THOU SHALT HEARKEN. In your heart to observe and to do. The sum of the matter is, do not turn aside from God to serve idols, for the root of all sins is to deny God.²⁴ The reverse of the aforementioned is to affirm that the Lord is one and to hearken and to observe, for the most important aspect of hearkening is observing.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:22:2)

WITH FEVER. Each day. *Kaddachat* (fever) is related to *kadechah* (kindled) in *For a fire is kindled* (Deut. 32:22). The words *mehumah* (discomfiture), *migeret* (rebuke), *shachefet* (consumption), *kaddachat* (fever) and *dalleket* (inflammation) are adjectives.

²⁷ The usual meaning of cherev


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:22:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:22:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:22:6)


**ובשדפון.** נפיחות וכן שדופות קדים וי״‎א הפוך והטעם דקוק:


AND WITH BLASTING. *Shiddafon* (blasting) means bloating. Compare, *shedufot kadim* (blasted with the east wind)²⁸ as bloated by the east wind. (Gen. 41:23). Others say the reverse is true. Its meaning is then thin.²⁹

footnotes:
²⁸ This interpretation renders shedufot kadim
²⁹ Withered, shriveled.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:22:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:22:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:22:7)


**ובירקון.** כמשמעו בלשון קדר וי״‎א כי אלה חליים בזרע ובשדפון כמו שדופות קדים והעד הכיתי אתכם בשדפון ובירקון. על כן אחריו והיו שמיך וכן בפרשת אם בחקותי:


AND WITH MILDEW. *Yerakon* (mildew) is to be rendered according to its meaning in Arabic.³⁰ Some say that these³¹ (blasting) and *yerakon* (mildew). refer to diseases of the seed.³² *U-vashiddafon* (blasting) is similar to *shidufot* (blasted) in *blasted with the east wind* (Gen. 41:23). *I have smitten you with blasting* (shiddafon)³³ here refers to a disease of the seed, for Amos goes on to speak of gardens, vineyards, and olive trees. See Amos 4:9. *and mildew* (Amos 4:9) is proof. Therefore Scripture afterwards reads, *and thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass*. We find the same in the Torah portion *If Ye Walk in My Statutes* (Lev. 26:3).³⁴

footnotes:
³⁰ It is a disease in which the skin develops a greenish color.
³¹ Shiddafon
³² Unlike the illnesses mentioned up to this point which attack people, these attack plants.
³³ Shiddafon
³⁴ Scripture first speaks of illnesses that strike people and then of plagues that fall upon the plants.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:27:2)


**ובטחורים.** הם היוצאים במקום הנסתר על כן כתוב ובעפולים והוא מגזרת ויבא אל העופל:


AND WITH THE EMERODS. They appear in the hidden places.⁴² Scripture therefore reads *u-vafolim*⁴³. The *keri* reads *u-vatchorim*. (and with the emerods). The latter is related to the world *ofel* (hill) in *And when he came to the hill* (II Kings 5:24).⁴⁴ because they are hill-like; i.e., they consist of swellings. According to Weiser its meaning is, hemorrhoids are called *ofalim* because hills are used for hiding and hemorrhoids appear in hidden places.

footnotes:
⁴² They are swellings that appear in hidden places.
⁴³ This is the ketib
⁴⁴ Hemorrhoids are called ofalim


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:27:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:27:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:27:3)


**ובגרב.** כן בלשון ישמעאל:


AND WITH THE SCAB.⁴⁵. The same is true in Arabic.⁴⁶.

footnotes:
⁴⁵ Hebrew, garav
⁴⁶ The Arabic word for scab is jarabu


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:27:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:27:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:27:4)


**ובחרס.** י״‎א שיצטרך אל חרס כאיוב ואם הוא בסמ״‎ך וי״‎א במכת השמש. והנכון שהוא שם חולי כנזכרי' ואין לו חבר:


AND WITH THE ITCH.⁴⁷. Some say that he will need a potsherd⁴⁸. He will need a potsherd (*cheres*) to scratch himself to relieve his itching. as Job did.⁴⁹ This is so⁵⁰ because one employs a potsherd for relief if struck by this illness. even though the word *cheres* (itch) is spelled with a *samekh*.⁵¹. Others say *u-ve-chares* (and with the itch) means: and with a blow from the sun.⁵² is the sun. See Jud. 14:18. Hence this interpretation renders *u-ver-chares*, and with sunstroke. However, the correct interpretation is that *cheres* (itch) refers to the name of a disease like the ones mentioned previously. The word has no neighbor.⁵³

footnotes:
⁴⁷ Hebrew, cheres
⁴⁸ Hebrew, cheres
⁴⁹ Job used a potsherd to relief his itching. See Job 2:8.
⁵⁰ The disease is called cheres
⁵¹ While the word for potsherd is spelled with a sin
⁵² One of the meanings of the word cheres
⁵³ It is not found elsewhere in Scripture. Hence we do not know what sort of disease it refers to.

USE THE FRUIT THEREFOF. *Techallennu* (use the fruit thereof) is related to the word *chalil* (flute).⁵⁸. 38. The printed editions read *chalilah*. See I.E. on Deut. 28:6: “They were in the habit of dancing [to the tune of flutes] in the vineyards.” Hence the term *techallennu*.

### Verse 32

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:32:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:32:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:32:1)


**וכלות.** כמו נכספה וגם כלת' וכן ותכל דוד ואינו חסר נפש כאשר פירש חסר הדעת כי ותכל פועל יוצא ולא נזכר הפועל כמו אשר ילדה אותה:


AND FAIL WITH LONGING. The word *kalot* (fail with longing) is similar to the word *kaletah* (pineth) in *My soul yearneth, yea, even pineth* (Ps. 84:3) and to *va-tekhal* (failed with longing) in *va-tekhal david* (and caused David to fail with longing)⁵⁹ (II Sam. 13:39). The latter is not lacking the word “soul” as the one lacking in knowledge says,⁶⁰ is to be rendered, And David’s soul failed with longing. It should be noted that this interpretation was offered by Rashi, Radak, and the *Targum*. for the word *vatekhal* is transitive. The subject⁶¹, i.e., the one who caused David to fail in longing. is omitted,⁶² as it is in “whom she bore”⁶³ (Num. 26:59).⁶⁴

footnotes:
⁵⁹ Translated according to I.E.
⁶⁰ The “one lacking in knowledge” says, va-tekhal david
⁶¹ Of va-tekhal
⁶² According to I.E our text is to be interpreted, and caused David to fail in longing. See Radak on II Sam. 13:29. Radak quotes an interpretation which renders the verse, And the wife of David caused him to fail in longing. This apparently is the way I.E. interprets our verse (Krinsky).
⁶³ Translated according to I.E.
⁶⁴ Scripture omits the person who did the bearing.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:53:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:53:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:53:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:53:2)


**יציק לך.** כל אחד מאויבך או הוא כן בעבור היותו בסוף:


SHALL STRAITEN THEE. Each one of your enemies.⁸³ (shall straiten) is in the singular. *Oyevekha* (thine enemies) is in the plural. According to I.E. when a verb in the singular governs a noun in the plural, the verb refers to each one within the plural. Or the word *oyevekha* is so vocalized⁸⁴ rather than *oyivkha*. because it comes at the end of a verse.⁸⁵ is really a singular. Our text should thus be rendered, wherewith thine enemy shall straiten thee.

⁸⁵ In other words, oyevekha

FROM BETWEEN HER FEET. This is a euphemism.⁹⁰ Compare, *and he had neither dressed his feet* (II Sam. 19:25).⁹¹ is, he did not shave his pubic hair. Also see Talmud, *Yevamot* 103a.

### Verse 59

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:59:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:59:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/28:59:1)


**מכתך.** לשון יחיד עם רבים מורכבת וכן ועדותי זו אלמדם:


THY PLAGUES. *Makkotekha* (thy plagues) is a compound of a singular⁹² and the plural.⁹³ is a plural. We would thus expect a *yod* to follow the *tav* and the *tav* to be vocalized with a *segol* in *makkotekha*. However, the *tav* in *makkotekha* is vocalized with a *sheva*, and *makkotekha* has no *yod* in it. The latter is the spelling and vocalization of the singular. Compare, the word *edoti* (my testimony)⁹⁴ is a plural. Thus the word should read *edotai*, for “i” is a singular suffix. Thus *edoti* is a compound of a plural with a singular pronominal suffix. in *And My testimony that I shall teach them* (Ps. 132:12).

footnotes:
⁹² Suffix.
⁹³ A noun in the plural. Makkot
⁹⁴ Edot

WILL THE LORD BRING UPON. *Yalem* (will bring) is related to the word *he’elah* (brought up)⁹⁷, and means bring up. (Jer. 16:15) even though it⁹⁸ is vocalized with a *sheva. He’elah* is vocalized with a *chataf segol*. Since both words are in the *hifil* we would expect them to be vocalized similarly. Hence I.E.’s comment. is vocalized with a *sheva*. ###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 28:68:1

**והתמכרתם.** אינו כמו ונמכרתם רק פירושו אתם תבקשו למכור עצמכם אנשים ונשים ואין קונה והנה זאת הברית במצות השם בערבות מואב:


AND…YE SHALL SELL YOURSELVES. *Ve-hitmakkartem* (and ye shall sell yourselves) does not mean and you will be sold.¹⁰⁵, not in the *nifal*. (Cf. *nimkartem* in Is. 50:1.) [BUT THE LORD HATH NOT GIVEN YOU A HEART TO KNOW.] Scripture reads a *heart to know* because they tested God ten times⁶ and did not make mention of the signs which they witnessed.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 29:3:2

וטעם **נתן.** כי מאתו העלילה הראשונה ועוד כי ראו שלא הוצרכו ללחם ויין:


Scripture reads *given* because God is the first cause.⁷. Hence I.E. points out that Scripture ascribes man’s achievements to God because God is the first cause and in that sense can be said to give man *a heart to know*. Furthermore,⁸ they saw that they had no need for bread or wine.⁹

YE ARE STANDING THIS DAY. Around the ark.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 29:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:9:2)


**ראשיכם.** כמו האלה' שרה אמו והנבוא' עודד הנביא וכן הוא ראשיכ' שהם ראשי שבטיכ' כמו ונירם. והטעם כי הנשיאי' סמוכים ואחריה' הזקני' ואחריה' השוטרים ואחריה' כל איש ישראל הזכרי' ואחריה' הטף בזכרי' ואחריה' הנשים ואחריה' הגרים:


YOUR HEADS. *Roshekhem* (your heads) is similar *to ha**ohelah* (the tent) in *into the tent Sarah his mother* (Gen. 24:67)¹⁷ is short for into the tent, the tent of Sarah his mother. Similarly, *your heads* is short for your heads the heads of. See I.E. on Gen. 24:67 (Vol. 1, p. 243). and *even the prophecy, Odad the prophet*¹⁸ (II Chron. 15:8).¹⁹ is short for even the prophecy, the prophecy of Odad the prophet. See I.E. on Gen. 24:67 (Vol. 1, p. 243). *Roshekhem shivtekhem* (your heads, your tribes) is to be interpreted as your heads, who are the heads of your tribes.²⁰ is short for *roshekhem roshe shivtekhem*. *Roshekhem* (your heads) is like the word *va-niram* (we have shot at them) (Num. 21:30).²¹ (we have shot at them, Heshbon is destroyed). According to I.E. this is to be interpreted as And their king, the king of Heshbon was destroyed. See I.E. on Num. 21:30 (Vol. 4, p. 175). The word is to be so interpreted for the princes²² were closest to the ark.²³ After them came the elders, followed by the officers, after whom came all the men of Israel, that is, the males, followed by the male little ones, after whom came the women, followed by the strangers.

footnotes:
¹⁷ Translated literally. According to I. E. into the tent Sarah his mother
¹⁸ Translated literally.
¹⁹ According to I.E. even the prophecy, Odad the prophet
²⁰ Roshekhem shivtekhem
²¹ Num. 21:30 reads, va-niram avad cheshbon
²² The heads of the tribes.
²³ According to I.E. our verse records the hierarchical arrangement of the Israelites before the ark, when the covenant was made. If we take our verse literally the word “tribes” breaks up the arrangement. Hence I.E. insists that our verse reads, your heads, the heads of your tribes.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 29:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:11:1)


**לעברך.** שם הפועל. כטעם ויעברו בין בתריו. והנה מלת עבר בחסרון בי״‎ת להפך:


THAT THOU SHOULDEST ENTER INTO THE COVENANT. *Le-ovrekha* (that thou shouldest enter) is an infinitive.²⁴ It is like *va-ya’avru* (and passed) in *and passed between the parts thereof* (Jer. 34:18).²⁵ (that thou shouldest enter) means that you should pass, i.e., that you should enter the covenant, for they used to cut an animal in half when making a covenant and walk between the halves. Observe, the word *avar* (passed) minus the *bet*²⁶ has the opposite meaning.²⁷ preceding *brit* means to violate the covenant. Hence our verse reads, *le-ovrekha bi-verit*. Had our verse read, *le-ovrekha berit*, it would have meant that you should violate the covenant.

²⁴ With the pronominal suffix.
²⁵ In other words, le-ovrekha
²⁶ Following it.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 29:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:18:3)


**למען ספות.** אמר רבי יהודה הלוי נ״‎ע ל' כריתה כמו האף תספ'. כלומר שיחשוב המתברך לבטל דברי הצדיק שהוא כנוי במלת רוה עם דבר הצמא' והנה כנה הצדיק ברוה. כמו כעץ שתול על מים. והרשע בצמאה כמו כערער בערבה. ויחשוב כי גם ברכתו בלבו תפסיק הקללה ויפה פיר' לולא שמלת רוה תואר השם והיה ראוי להיות רווי את הצמא. ויאמר רבי יונה המדקדק כי טעמו בעבור שיראה שיכלה התם עם הרשע על כן יחשוב בלבו רע ואין זה נכון בעבור שלום יהיה לי. ולפי דעתי שמלת ספות לשון תוספת כמו ספות חטאת. והטעם שלום יהיה לי אע״‎פ שאלך בשרירות לבי כי בצדקת הצדיקים אחיה. כי הם רבים ואני יחיד חוטא. על כן כתוב אחריו לא יאבה ה' סלוח לו כי אז והטעם מיד יכרת גם זה הפסוק לעד על פירושי במלת ונסלח לו. והנה ספות כי הרוה תוסיף על הצמאה ומשל הצדיק ברוה כטעם כעץ שתול על פלגי מים והרשע בצמאה כטעם כערער בערבה והעד שכתוב בתחלה שרש פורה ראש ולענה והוא במקום צמא:


THAT…BE SWEPT AWAY. Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi, who rests in paradise, says that the word *sefot* (swept away) means to extirpate. Compare, *tispeh*³⁴. [thou (wilt) sweep away] in *Wilt Thou indeed sweep away* (Gen. 18:23). In other words, the one who blesses himself³⁵ wants to nullify the words of the righteous,³⁶ who are metaphorically called “the watered,” with the words of “the dry.” Look, the righteous are called watered. Compare, *For he shall be like a tree planted by the streams of water* (Jer. 17:8). The wicked are called dry. Compare, *For he shall be like a tamarisk in the desert* (*Ibid.*, v. 6). The wicked person thinks that the blessing which he utters in his heart will also stop the curse. He explained well were it not that the word *ravah* (well watered) is an adjective.³⁷ (dry). The point is that Rabbi Judah’s interpretation requires that nouns, not adjectives, be employed in our verse, for according to his interpretation the verse speaks of people. Filwarg argues that Rabbi Judah’s interpretation requires a noun because the dry and the watered are metaphors for curses and blessing, which are nouns. He interprets in this manner because later on I.E. himself interprets the dry and the watered as referring to people. The problem with Filwarg’s interpretation is that I.E. quotes Rabbi Judah as saying, “The righteous are called watered…The wicked are called dry.” Our text should have read, *ravi*³⁸ *et ha-tzama*³⁹ (the well watered…with the dry). Rabbi Jonah the grammarian⁴⁰ says that it means⁴¹. because the corrupt sees the righteous⁴² destroyed along with the wicked⁴³ he therefore thinks evil in his heart.⁴⁴. The wicked person says I might as well be wicked, for both the righteous and the wicked suffer one fate. They are both swept away. However, this is incorrect because Scripture reads, *I shall have peace*.⁴⁵ implies that he says something positive to himself. However, there is nothing positive in saying the righteous and I will be swept away. In my opinion the word *sefot* (swept) means to add. Compare, *sefot chattat* (add sin) (Is. 30:1). The added sin is the wicked person’s statement, I shall have peace even though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart. I will live because of the righteousness of the righteous, for the pious are many and I am an individual sinner.⁴⁶. A nation is judged by the majority of its people. The wicked believe that the merit of the majority, who are righteous, will protect the sinners, who are a minority. Scripture therefore afterwards reads, *The Lord will not be willing to pardon him*⁴⁷. *but then…* (v. 19). The meaning of the latter is he shall immediately be destroyed. This verse is also proof of my interpretation of *and he shall be forgiven*⁴⁸. According to I.E. the word *salach* means to delay punishment. See I.E. on Num. 14:19, “Selach refers to being slow to anger.” (Num. 15:28). The meaning of *sefot* is that the well watered will add to the dry. Scripture compares the righteous to the well watered, as in *And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water* (Ps. 1:3). It compares the wicked to the dry. Compare, *For he shall be like a tamarisk in the desert* (Jer. 17: 6). The fact that Scripture at first reads, *a root that beareth gall and wormwood* (v. 17), is proof of this.⁴⁹ It is in a dry place.⁵⁰ grows in parched land. Hence the wicked person is called the dry (Meijler, Krinsky). I.E.’s interpretation presents a problem. He interprets “the watered and the dry” as referring to people. However, earlier I.E. rejects Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi’s interpretation for this very reason. As noted above, Filwarg attempts to justify I.E.’s position. However, his interpretation is forced.

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 29:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:19:1)


**יעשן אף.** ישרפנו אש האף עד שיראה העשן והנה אם הוא יחיד ימות מיד ואם היא משפחה ורבצה בו כל האלה והטעם שתרבץ האלה במשפחה עד שימח' שמה ואם הוא שבט והבדילו ה' לרעה וכמוהו והיה לה' והעלתיהו עולה כאשר פירשתיו:


THE ANGER OF THE LORD…SHALL BE KINDLED.⁵¹ (literally, shall smoke). Our clause literally reads, the anger of the Lord…shall smoke. Hence I.E.’s interpretation. The fire of God’s anger shall bum him to the point where the smoke will be visible. Observe, if the sinner be an individual he will die immediately, and if it is a family *all the curse…shall lie upon him*. This means that the curse shall lie upon the family until its name is eradicated. If the sinner be a tribe, *the Lord shall separate him unto evil* (v. 20).⁵² refers to an individual; *and all the curse…shall lie upon him* refers to a family; *and the Lord shall separate him unto evil* refers to a tribe. Similarly *And I will offer it up for a burnt-offering* (Jud. 11:31), as I have explained.⁵³ there has the meaning of or. It appears that I.E. interpreted similarly.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 29:28:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:28:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/29:28:2)


**לה' אלהינו** והטעם כי משפטו ביד השם והוא יפרע ממנו ואם היתה בגלוי חיוב לנו ולבנינו לעשות ככתוב בתורה. וי״‎א כי הנסתרות והנגלות הם לה' ואין לנו כי אם לעשות דברי התורה וזה הפי' בלא ראש ורגל ומה טעם יש להזכיר כן במקום הזה ובעבור שאמר וישליכם אל ארץ אחרת אמר כי אם תשוב אל ה' אע״‎פ שאתה חוצה לארץ השם ישיב שבותך ועל דעת רבי יהודה המדקדק הראשון כי הוא יניח. והטעם ימצא מנוח' לנשבים ויתן להם רחמים ואחר כן ישוב ויקבץ:


BELONG UNTO THE LORD OUR GOD. Its meaning is that his punishment is in the hands of God, and the Lord will exact punishment from him. However, if the sin was committed in public there is an obligation on us and our children to do in accordance with that which is written in the Torah. Others say⁶³ that the secret and the revealed things belong to God. It is incumbent upon us only to observe the words of the Torah. Now this interpretation has no head or foot.⁶⁴ What reason is there to mention this here?⁶⁵ Scripture states that if you *return unto the Lord* (Deut. 30:2), *God will turn thy captivity* (*Ibid.*, v. 3) even though you are outside of the land because it stated earlier, *and cast them into another land* (v. 27). According to Rabbi Judah⁶⁶ the first grammarian, the meaning of *ve-shav* (then shall turn) (Deut. 30:3) means God will give rest;⁶⁷ (*Ibid.*, v. 3) as God will give rest to your captivity. that is, he will give rest to the captives and be merciful to them, and after this He will return and gather.⁶⁸ in 30:3 as will He give rest, and the second *ve-shav* as and will He return.
