### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 31:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/31:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/31:15:1)


**וירא ה' באוהל.** הידוע הטעם כי עמוד הענן היה על הפתח והשם היה נראה באהל וזהו הכבוד ודבור ואצונו זהו ויצו את יהושע בן נון במצו' השם יתברך על כן אמר אשר נשבעתי להם ואח״‎כ פרשת הנך שוכב עם אבותיך ואין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה וכן פ' ויהי ככלות משה לכתוב דבקה עם ויכתוב משה את התורה הזאת:


AND THE LORD APPEARED IN THE TENT. The specified tent.²³ (tent) has a *heh ha-yedi’ah* prefixed to it. The meaning of our verse is that the pillar of cloud was at the door of the tent and God was seen inside the tent. This²⁴ is what the glory²⁵ refers to.²⁶ The statement *that I may give him a charge* (v. 14) refers to *And he*²⁷ *gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge* (v. 23) by the command of God, may He be blessed. Scripture therefore reads, *which I swore unto them* (*Ibid.*).²⁸ After this came the passage *Behold, thou art about to sleep with thy fathers* (v. 16).²⁹ There is no chronological order in the Torah. The passage *And it came to pass, when Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law* (v. 24) is connected to³⁰ *And Moses wrote this law* (v. 9).

²⁷ Moses.

²⁹ According to I.E. the sequence of events was as follows: Verses 14,15; 23; 16-22; 9. The reason for the aforementioned is purely exegetical. It allows for a logical, sequential unfolding of events.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 31:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/31:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/31:16:3)


**אחרי אלהי נכר הארץ.** ידענו כי השם אחד והשנוי יבוא מהמקבלים והשם לא ישנה מעשיו כי כולם בחכמה. ומעבודת השם לשמור כח הקבול כפי המקום על כן כתוב את משפט אלהי הארץ על כן אמר יעקב הסירו את אלהי הנכר והפך המקום הדבק בעריות שהם שאר. והמשכיל יבין:


AFTER THE FOREIGN GODS OF THE LAND. We know that God is one.³⁴ Change comes from the recepients.³⁵ God does not change His works,³⁶ for they are executed in wisdom. It is part of the service of God to harness one’s power to receive spiritual inspiration in accordance with the place.³⁷ Scripture therefore reads, *the manner of the God of the land* (II Kings 17:26).³⁸ Jacob therefore said,³⁹ *Put away the strange gods* (Gen. 35:2).⁴⁰ The place is unlike other places with regard to engaging in sexual intercourse with women whom Scripture deems as being of close flesh.⁴¹ The intelligent will understand.⁴²

³⁴ God is unchangeable. God remains the same at all times.
³⁵ Of Divine beneficence. According to I.E. praying to God does not change God’s mind. It changes the petitioner. The person changes his fate because he becomes a different person. Thus God’s decrees remain unchangeable.

Also see Ex. 15:17.
³⁸ The reference is to the people whom the king of Assyria brought to Samaria. They wanted to learn the manner of the God of the land because they knew that if they wanted to remain in the Land of Israel, they would have to alter their ways to fit the religious requirements of the land.
³⁹ To his sons.
⁴⁰ According to I.E., Jacob told his sons, “Now that we are in the Land of Israel put away the images which you held on to while you were outside of the Land of Israel.”
⁴¹ A person is not allowed to marry a variety of close relatives. Among these are two sisters and an aunt. However, Jacob married two sisters and Amram married his aunt. According to I.E. they did so because they were outside of the Land of Israel. See I.E. on Lev. 18:26.
⁴² That the Land of Israel has special spiritual significance.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 31:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/31:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/31:16:4)


וטעם **בקרבו.** שב אל נכר כאילו אמר וזנה אחרי אלהי עם נכר שהם אלהי הארץ. והקרוב כי בקרבו שב אל הארץ כי נמצא לשון זכר כמו ולא נשא אותם הארץ. נעתם הארץ:


[AMONG THEM.] *Be-kirbo* (among them) refers to *foreign*.⁴³. I.E. does not believe that Scripture would use the term “among them” when referring to foreign gods, for such gods do not exist, and it is impossible to come among them. Hence his interpretation. Scripture, as it were, states, and go astray after the gods of a foreign people,⁴⁴ who are the gods of the land.⁴⁵ is short for “the foreign people of the gods of the land.” However, it appears that *be-kirbo* refers to the word *ha-aretz* (of the land),⁴⁶ should be translated as “in it” or “into the midst of it” and our verse rendered, and go astray after the foreign gods of the land into the midst of which they enter. for the word *eretz* is found in the masculine.⁴⁷ which is masculine, can refer to *eretz. Eretz* is usually feminine. Hence I.E.’s comment. Compare, *And the land* (ha-aretz) *was not able to bear* (nasa)⁴⁸ is masculine. *them* (Gen. 13:6); *the land* [is] *burnt up* (netam⁴⁹ is masculine. aretz) (Is. 9:18).

## Chapter 32


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:1:1)


**האזינו.** כבר פירשתי בספרי כי מלת האזינו מגזרת אזן כאילו אמר הטו אזן:


GIVE EAR. I have previously explained in my book¹ (Weiser). that the word *ha’azinu* (give ear) is related to the word *ozen* (ear). Scripture, as it were, says incline your ear.²

footnotes:
¹ The Moznayim
² I.e., pay attention.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:1:2)


וכבר הודעתיך שהגאון אמר כי טעם **השמים.** המלאכים וטעם **הארץ.** אנשי הארץ. או עדות הגשם היורד מן השמים והארץ תתן יבולה והנכון בעיני כי העיקר בעבור היותם עומדים לעולם וכן שמעו הרים גם אבן יהושע ושם כתוב כי היא שמעה וכבר רמזתי לך על נשמת האדם שהיא אמצעות בין הגבוהי' לשפלי' והיא תדמה הכל על צורת היכלה. ואף כי להבין גם היושבת בהיכל. על כן תגביה השפלי' ותשפיל הגבוהים:


I have previously informed you³ that the Gaon⁴ says that the meaning of *heavens* is the angels and the meaning of the *earth* is the people of the earth.⁵ On the other hand, its meaning might be that the rain that comes down from heaven and the fruit which the earth produces are called to bear witness.⁶. I believe that the correct interpretation is that Moses called heaven and earth to witness because they last forever.⁷ Similarly *Hear, O ye mountains* (Micah 6:2) and also Joshua’s stone.⁸ Scripture there writes that the stone heard. I have hinted to you that man’s soul is intermediary between the upper and lower worlds.⁹ The soul compares all things to its body.¹⁰ It certainly does so when speaking to other human beings.¹¹ It therefore elevates the low and lowers the high.¹² (Num. 13:29).” Also see I.E. on Ex. 19:20 (Vol. 2, pp. 388,389).

footnotes:
³ See I.E. on Deut. 3:24. However, I.E. does not there mention Rabbi Saadiah Gaon by name.
⁴ Rabbi Saadiah Gaon.
⁵ Rabbi Saadiah Gaon renders our verse: Give ear, O inhabitants of heaven, and I will speak, And let the people of the earth hear the words of my mouth.
⁶ See Rashi: “If Israel will act worthily, the witnesses will come and give them their reward…the ground will give its increase, the heavens will bestow its dew.” Rashi’s interpretation is based on the Sifre
⁷ In other words, heaven and earth do not refer to angels and people, or rain and the produce of the earth.
⁸ See Josh. 24:27: And Joshua said…‘Behold, this stone shall be a witness…for it hath heard all the words of the Lord…’
⁹ Man’s soul comes from the middle world. See I.E. on Ex. 19:20 (Vol. 2, p. 338). For the upper, middle, and lower worlds, see I.E. on Ex. 3:15 (Vol. 2, pp. 86-90).
¹⁰ Literally, its palace. The body serves as a “palace” for the soul. The mind explains reality by employing figures of speech based on the body. For example, the earth opened her mouth, etc.
¹¹ Literally, other inhabitants of the palace.
¹² See I.E. on Gen. 1:26 (Vol. 1, p. 45). “Now a human being cannot speak of things above or below without employing human terminology. Hence Scripture uses such terms as the mouth of the earth (Num. 16:30), the hand of the Jordan



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:1)


**יערף.** מגזרת יערף מזבחותם כטעם ירד:


SHALL DROP. The word *ya’arof* (shall drop) is related to the word *ya’arof* (he will break down) in *He will break down their altars* (Hos. 10:2). The meaning of *ya’arof* (shall drop) is will come down.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:2)


**לקחי.** מה שיקח אחד ממנו כטעם למוד וכן כי לקח טוב:


MY DOCTRINE. *Likchi* (My doctrine) refers to that which one will take away¹³ means took. The noun *lekech* thus means a taking. from him.¹⁴ It means a lesson. Compare, *lekech* (doctrine) in *For I give you a good doctrine* (Prov. 4:2).

¹³ The word lakach
¹⁴ Learn from Moses.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:3)


**כשעירם.** הנכון בעיני שהם דקים:


AS THE SMALL RAIN. I believe that *se’irim* (small rain) refers to light rain.¹⁵ (showers), which refers to a heavy rain.

footnotes:
¹⁵ For it stands in contrast to revivim


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:2:4)


**וכרביבים.** מגזרת רב ושניהם שמות התאר והעד כי עשב חזק מדשא. וי״‎א כי שעירים מגזרת שער ואחרים אמרו מגזרת סערת ה' ואם הוא בשי״‎ן וכן וישתער עליו כמו ויסתער עליו גם יתכן שאין לו אח במקרא והנה הטעם כפול כדרך כל הנבואות לחזוק ועיקר הטעם שהתפלל משה שיהיו דבריו כטל וכמטר שלא ישובו ריקם כי אם הרוו את הארץ כי כן כתוב והטע' שיכנסו דבריו בלבו' השומעי' כמעשה הגשם על הארץ להולידה ולהצמיחה:


AND AS THE SHOWERS. The word *revivim* (showers) is related to the word *rav* (numerous). They¹⁶ (small rain) and *revivim* (showers). are adjectives. The fact that *esev* (herb) is stronger than *deshe* (tender grass) is proof of this.¹⁷ (small rain) refers to light rain and *revivim* (showers) to a heavy rain, for Scripture speaks of *se’irim* falling on *deshe* and *revivim* on *esev*. Some say that *se’irim* (small rain) is related to *sa’ar* (hair).¹⁸ Others say that it is related to the word *sa’arat* (storm of)¹⁹ (small rain) means a rainstorm. in *storm of God* (Jer. 30:23) even though *se’irim* is spelled with a *sin*.²⁰ (storm) with a *samekh*. Similarly, the phrase *ve-yista’er alav* (shall come against him like a whirlwind) (Dan. 11:40), which is spelled with a *sin*, means the same as *ve-yista’er alav* spelled with a *samekh*.²¹. It is also possible that the word *se’irim* has no brother in Scripture.²² Our verse repeats itself²³…repeats *And the showers…* for emphasis, as is the style in all prophecies. The essence of our verse is that Moses prayed that his words be like dew and rain which, as it is written, do not return unfulfilled²⁴ but water the earth.²⁵ The meaning of the latter is that Moses’ words should enter the hearts of those who hear them in the same way that the rain affects the earth and fructifies it and causes it to produce plants.

²² Its meaning is to be ascertained from its context.

²⁵ Is. 55:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:1)


והחל **הצור תמים פעלו.** להודיע כי כל מה שאירע לישראל בעבור מעשיהם הרעים היה:


[THE ROCK, HIS WORK IS PERFECT.] Moses opens with this phrase to make it known that all that befell Israel did so because of their evil deeds.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:2)


וטעם **הצור.** שהוא עומד תמיד כצור. ואל תתמה. כי כן יאמר הכתוב כארי' ישאג כי לא יוכל המדבר לדמות מעשי השם ית' כי אם אל מעשיו. כי הכל מעשיו. וכן צור לבבי כמו משען ותוקף ועמידה. וי״‎א מלשון צורה וכן וצורם לבלות שאול. ועיקר שאין לו עצם מקבל רק הוא צור קדמון והראשון נכון בעיני:


The meaning of *The Rock* is that God, like a rock, is everlasting. Do not be amazed at this,²⁷ for Scripture similarly states, *The Lord…shall roar like a lion* (Hos. 11:10).²⁸ Scripture does this because one who speaks cannot compare God’s work to anything but His works, for everything is His work. Rock, in *But God is the rock of my heart* (Ps. 73:26), similarly means a support, might, and permanence. Others say that *tzur* (rock) is related to the word *tzurah* (image). Compare, *tzuram* (their form) in *And their form shall be for the nether-world* (Ps. 49:15). Its basic meaning is that God does not consist of matter,²⁹. which can be molded into a form.³⁰ On the contrary, He is Primary form.³¹ The first interpretation appears correct to me.

footnotes:
²⁷ That Scripture compares God to a rock.
²⁸ We thus see that Scripture compares God to mundane objects.
²⁹ Hebrew, etzem
³⁰ According to medieval philosophy everything on earth consists of matter and form.
³¹ He does not consist of matter. According to this interpretation our clause should be rendered, The Primary form, for all His ways are justice.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:3)


**תמים פעלו.** כי כל מפעל פועל חסר בעבור הצטרכו לאשר הוא למעלה ממנו לבד מפעל השם הנכבד והכל (שנים) (בם' מ״‎ח גרס שונים) חוץ מיוצר הכל:


HIS WORK IS PERFECT. All the works of an artisan are incomplete³² because the artisan needs the assistance of one greater than he.³³ The work of God alone is perfect. Everything is a duality³⁴ except for the creator of all.³⁵

footnotes:
³² A human being’s work is not perfect.
³³ The work of an artisan or an author can always be improved upon. Furthermore, most artisans need assistance. Hence what they alone produce can never be perfect.
³⁴ Matter and form. Some versions read, everything is in flux.
³⁵ God does not consist of matter and form.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:4)


**כי כל דרכיו משפט.** שלא ישתנו רק הם על משפט אחד וזו היא התהלה (התחלה) וכל הנבראים ישתנו מעשיהם כפי צרכיהם ומעשי השם (לכבודו) (בם' הנ״‎ל גרס לבדו) בגבורה כפי החכמה. ואין לטעון מעמידת השמש כי סודו ברור במלת וירח בעמק אילון כאשר פירשתי במקומו:


FOR ALL HIS WAYS ARE JUSTICE. His ways do not change.³⁶ On the contrary, they follow one law.³⁷ This is the praise of God.³⁸ (v. 3). All those who are created change their deeds in accordance with their needs.³⁹ God’s works⁴⁰. were done for His glory,⁴¹. with might⁴². and wisdom.⁴³. Some editions read: God’s works alone were done in might in accordance with wisdom. The standing still of the sun (Josh. 10:12)⁴⁴ is no argument to the contrary because, as I explained in its place,⁴⁵ its secret is clear, from the clause *And thou, Moon in the valley of Aijalon* (*Ibid.*).⁴⁶

³⁷ They are eternal.
³⁸ That God’s works are unchangeable. This is what Moses means by ascribe ye greatness unto our God

⁴¹ The world reflects God’s glory. See Ps. 19:1, The heavens declare the glory of God
⁴² Some editions read: God’s works alone were done in might. Creation was a mighty act. Compare the blessing recited upon hearing thunder: “Whose might and power fill the world.” Also see Ps. 29:1, Ascribe unto the Lord glory and strength
⁴³ Hence they are unchanging. See Job 12:13, With Him is wisdom and might

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:5)


**אל אמונה ואין עול.** הוא לבדו יש לו גבורת אמת כי כל גבורה בגבורים הוא מקרה מיד אחר. והטעם אחר שהוא אל אמונה לא יתכן שיעשה עול ויתכן להיות ואין עול בדרכיו. או מלת אל מושכת עצמה ואחרת עמה:


A GOD OF FAITHFULNESS AND WITHOUT INIQUITY. God alone has true might,⁴⁷. *El* means mighty. (See I.E. on Ex. 3:15). Hence I.E.’s comment on God’s might. for all the might of the mighty is an “accident;”⁴⁸ that is, it depends on outside sources.⁴⁹ The meaning of our clause is, it is not possible that God does iniquity because He is a God of faithfulness.⁵⁰ (and without iniquity). The literal meaning *of ve-en avel* is, and no iniquity. According to this interpretation, and no iniquity means and God does no iniquity. It is possible that *ve-en avel* (and without iniquity) means and without iniquity in His ways.⁵¹ On the other hand, it is possible that the word *El* (God) is to be read as if written twice.⁵² is to be interpreted as if written, *ve-en El avel*.

footnotes:
⁴⁷ The term used for God in our clause is El
⁴⁸ Accident in Aristotelian philosophy refers to a quality which is not part of the essence of a being. For example, color is said to be an accident, for the color of an object is not part of its essence.
⁴⁹ No king or ruler is autonomous. His power is dependent on the will of his underlings.
⁵⁰ Our verse reads ve-en avel
⁵¹ In other words, and no iniquity is short for, and no iniquity in his ways.
⁵² Our clause is to be read: A God of faithfulness, not a God of iniquity. According to this interpretation, ve-en avel


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:4:6)


**צדיק וישר הוא.** בעבור שאמר שחת לו אמר כי צדקתו שחתו עם נפתל והנה הוא לבדו ישר ויושר הישר לתקן המעות על כן טעם לו בעבור שהיו לו בתחלה:


JUST AND RIGHT IS HE. Since Scripture states *shichet lo* (is corruption His) (v. 5),⁵³ literally means he destroyed. I.E. renders *shichet lo* as He destroyed that which belonged to Him, that is Israel. it says a perverse people corrupted God’s righteousness.⁵⁴ Look, God alone is right.⁵⁵ The rightness of the right is to fix that which is crooked.⁵⁶ The word *lo* (v. 5) therefore refers to what He had at first.⁵⁷ means He destroyed what was His, that is, Israel. According to I. E. the word *lo*, which usually means him, is to be interpreted as *shelo* (his).

footnotes:
⁵³ Shichet
⁵⁴ Israel corrupted God’s righteous ways by sinning..
⁵⁵ God destroyed the perverse. Hence his act of destruction was not unjust.
⁵⁶ By punishing the wicked. Hence what God did to Israel was not unjust.
⁵⁷ In other words, shichet lo



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:5:1)


**לא בניו.** אלה שאמרו שאינם בניו וכן בנים לא אמון בם. והטעם שלא יודו שהוא בראם ואם יודו בפה לא יודו בלב והעד שלא יראו מהשם. ולמ״‎ד לו משרת עצמו ואחר עמו והוא למומם והטעם בעבור מומם שהוא דור עקש ופתלתל:


NO; HIS CHILDREN’S IS THE BLEMISH. *Lo banav* (no, his children’s) means those who say that they are not his children. Scripture similarly states, *Children in whom is no faithfulness* (v. 20). Its meaning is that they do not admit that God created them. Although they might profess their belief verbally, they do not believe it in their hearts. The fact that they do not fear God⁵⁸ is proof of their lack of belief. The *lamed* of *lo* (his) serves itself and another word along with it. It is to be prefixed to the word *mumam* (the blemish).⁵⁹ is to be read *le-mumam*. The entire clause is to be interpreted as if written, *lo banav le-mumam*. The meaning of *lemumam* is, because of their blemish, their blemish consisting in being *A generation crooked and perverse*.⁶⁰

footnotes:
⁵⁸ For Scripture declares them to be a crooked and perverse generation.
⁵⁹ Mumam
⁶⁰ According to this opinion our verse should be interpreted: God destroyed what originally belonged to Him, that is, those who, because of their blemish (which consists in their being a generation perverse and crooked), say that they are not His children.


###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:5:2)


**ופתלתל.** מתחזק ומתנצח בעקשותו וכן נפתולי אלהים. י״‎א כי טעם שחת לו כמו שחתו להם והטעם לנפש' ואל תתמה בעבור שהמלה לשון יחיד כי כן משפט הל' הלא תראה זכור ימות עולם בינו שנות דור ודור והנכון בעיני שהוא כן שחת לשם והטעם השחתת דרכי השם הנטועים והחקים שצוה כאילו אמר שחת לו דור עקש שהם לא בניו וזהו מומם והעד כי כן פירושו הבא אחריו והוא הלה' תגמלו זאת וכבר פירשתי טעם הה״‎א בספר מאזנים:


AND PERVERSE. The meaning of *u-fetaltol* (and perverse) is he grows strong and triumphant in his crookedness.⁶¹ (a crooked and perverse) as crooked and triumphant. Hence his interpretation. Compare the word *naftule* (wrestlings)⁶² (perverse) and *naftule* (wrestlings) come from the same root, *nun, peh, lamed*. in *with mighty wrestlings* (Gen. 30:8). Some say that the meaning of *shichet lo* (is corruption His) is, they corrupted themselves; that is, they corrupted their souls. Do not wonder that the singular *lo* is employed,⁶³ for this is the style of the language. Can you not see that Scripture reads, *Remember* (zekhor)⁶⁴ is singular. *the days of old, Consider* (binu)⁶⁵ is singular. *the years of many generations* (v. 7). I believe that *shichet lo* (is corruption His) means they corrupted God;⁶⁶ is, they corrupted to him. that is, they corrupted the ways of God, which are implanted in man’s mind,⁶⁷ as well as the statutes which He commanded. Scripture, as it were, says the crooked generation that is not His children corrupted Him.⁶⁸ This is their blemish. The verse that follows, namely, *Do you thus requite the Lord*, is proof that this is its interpretation.⁶⁹ I have explained the meaning of the *heh*⁷⁰. The next verse opens with an interrogative *heh*. Hence I.E.’s comment. in the book entitled *Moznayim*.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:7:4)


**ויגדך.** כמו ויגד לך. וכן כי ארץ הנגב נתתני. בני יצאוני:


AND HE WILL DECLARE UNTO THEE. *Ve-yaggedekha* means and he will declare unto thee.⁷⁸ means unto thee. The *kha* ending usually indicates the accusative (you or thee). Thus *ve-yagaddekha* would appear to mean, and He will declare you. Hence I.E. points out that here it means will declare to you. Compare, *netattani* (thou hast given to me)⁷⁹ is usually the sign of the accusative. Compare *channani* (Gen. 33:11). Thus we would ordinarily render, *netattani*, you have given me. Hence I.E. points out that here it has the meaning of you have given to me. We thus see that at times accusative suffixes are not to be rendered literally. in *for that thou hast given to me in the Southland*⁸⁰ (Josh. 15:19). And *yetzauni* (are gone forth of me) in *My children are gone forth of me* (Jer. 10:20).⁸¹ is to be rendered as gone forth of me, not gone forth me.

**בהנחל עליון גוים.** אמרו המפרשים על דור הפלגה שנפצה כל הארץ כי אז גזר השם להיות ארץ שבעה גוים לישראל והוא שתספיק למספרם על כן למספר בני ישראל:

The commentaries⁸³ say that the reference is to “the generation of the dispersion”⁸⁴ when all the earth became inhabited.⁸⁵ God at that time decreed that the land of the seven nations should belong to Israel, as this land would be large enough for them. ###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:8:2)


**יצב.** י״‎א שהוא שם הפועל כמו הנה לא ידעתי דבר. וי״‎א שהוא פועל עתיד תחת פועל עבר כמו יעשו עגל בחורב. והנכון בעיני כי שאל אביך רמז למביני' וכן זקניך והטעם כמו אשר חלק ה' אלהיך כי לכל חלק למטה חלק למעלה:


HE SET. Some say that *yatzev* (he set) is an infinitive.⁸⁷ appears to be a third person imperfect, meaning he will set. The verbs *be-hanchel* (When…gave the nations their inheritance) and *be-hafrido* (When He separated) which precede *yatzev* are infinitives. Hence this opinion that *yatzev* too is an infinitive. Compare the word *dabber* (speak)⁸⁸ in *behold, I cannot speak* (Jer. 1:6). Others say that *yatzev* (he set) is a verb in the imperfect,⁸⁹ employed as a perfect.⁹⁰ is here to be rendered he set. It is like the word *ya’asu* (they made)⁹¹ (they made) is an imperfect employed as a perfect. in *They made a calf in Horeb* (Ps. 106:19). I believe that *Ask thy father* alludes to those “who understand.”⁹² means one who knows and understands the past history of Israel (Weiser). The same applies to “thy elders.” The meaning of *the portion*⁹³. *of the Lord is His people*⁹⁴and *according to the number…* is similar to *which the Lord thy God hath allotted*⁹⁵. Deut. 4:19 reads: *which the Lord thy God hath allotted unto all the peoples under the whole heaven*. (Deut. 4:19), for every portion⁹⁶ below⁹⁷ has a portion⁹⁸ above.⁹⁹

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:8:3)


וטעם **למספר בני ישראל.** כאשר אחז״‎ל כי צורת יעקב אבינו חקוקה בכסא הכבוד והוא סוד גדול והעד כי חלק ה' עמו וזו היא המעלה הגדולה שלא עשה כן לכל גוי על כן אמר הלה' תגמלו זאת עם נבל ולא חכם שנפל ממעלתו באולתו וזה טעם אביך קנך כי קנהו לכבודו וילמדהו כאשר יפרש כמעשה האב עם הבן:


ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The rabbis, of blessed memory, say that the image of our father Jacob is engraved on the throne of glory.¹⁰⁰. Hence I.E.’s comment. See *Chullin* 91b. Also see *Bereshit Rabbah* 68:18. The latter is a great secret.¹⁰¹ *For the portion of the Lord is His people* is proof of this.¹⁰² This is a very great status. God did not do this for any nation. Scripture therefore states, *Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise*? (v. 6), that is, a people who have fallen from their status in their foolishness. Now, this God is your father, for he created you for His glory,¹⁰³ and as Scripture goes on to explain,¹⁰⁴ he taught you as a father teaches his son.

¹⁰² The children of Israel are under the direct providence of God.
¹⁰³ I.E.’s paraphrase of the last part of verse 5.
¹⁰⁴ In verse 10.

It has nothing to do with the word *bamot*, which means a high place. (with…his tomb) in *the wicked*¹³⁷. I.E. apparently quoted from memory.…*with…his tomb* (Is. 53:9) is not related to our word.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:13:4

FIELD. *Sadai* (field) is an adjective.¹³⁸ (fruitage). The ending *ai* usually indicates a plural. Compare, *nashai* (my wives); *benotai* (my daughters); *banai* (my sons). Hence I.E.’s comments. It follows the paradigm of *chakham* (wise).¹³⁹. The *yod* of *sadai* is in place of a *heh*.¹⁴⁰ is spelled with a *heh*. Hence I.E.’s comment. It is similar to the *vav* of *shalev*¹⁴¹ is in place of a *vav*, for the root of *shalev* is *shin, lamed, heh*. (at ease) in *I was at ease* (Job 16:12). The clause *ya’aloz sadai* (let the field exult) (Ps. 96:12) wherein *ya’aloz* is in the singular proves this.¹⁴² is singular, not plural.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:14:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:14:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:14:7)


ותי״‎ו **תשתה** לנכח והטעם כמדבר לחבירו כל כך הוא רב שתשת' חמר בכל עת. וי״‎א כי ענב לשון נקבה ואיננו כלום כי היה ראוי להיות התי״‎ו פתח עד שיצא לאחרים וי״‎א על לשון קהלה כי ישראל לשון זכר ולשון נקב' וזה קרוב מעט:


[THOU DRANKEST FOAMING WINE.]¹⁶¹. The *tav* of the word *tishteh* (thou drinkest) is a second person¹⁶² means you will drink. The word *tishteh* can also mean she will drink. Hence I.E.’s comment. prefix. Our verse, as it were, speaks like a person who tells his friend the land has so much wine that you will drink it at all times. Some say that *enav* (grape) is in the feminine.¹⁶³ is in the third person feminine. According to this interpretation our verse reads, the blood of the grape will give you wine to drink. However, what they say is worthless, for the *tav*¹⁶⁴. should have been vocalized with a *pattach*¹⁶⁵, not *tishteh. Tishteh* means she will drink; *tashteh*, she will cause you to drink. so that it would be a causative. Some say that *tishteh*¹⁶⁶ to be a third person feminine, meaning she will drink. speaks of the community,¹⁶⁷, she (Israel) will drink wine. for the word Israel is sometimes in the masculine and sometimes in the feminine. This interpretation is a bit closer to the correct meaning.

They are called *se’irim* because all who see them are terrified. Therefore Rabbi Isaac the son of Saul¹⁸⁷ who rests in Eden says that the word *se’arum* (dreaded) in *Which your fathers dreaded not*¹⁸⁸ is related to the word *se’irim*.¹⁸⁹ means dreaded and *se’irim* means those who terrify. The *lamed* of *la-shedim* (unto demons) pertains to *shedim* and also to another word.¹⁹⁰ of *lashedim* (unto demons) pertains to *shedim* and also to another word. *La-shedim lo eloha* (unto demons, no-gods) is to be read as if written *la-shedim u-le-lo eloha* (unto demons and unto no-gods).¹⁹¹ I believe that there is no need for this interpretation. On the contrary, the meaning of *la-shedim lo eloha* is clearly, unto demons who are no-gods. ###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:17:4)


**שערום.** פי' לא שערו מהם. מגזרת וישתער עליו כטעם תסמר שערת בשרי וקרוב הוא מגזרת סערה ואם הוא בסמ״‎ך וכמוהו בני יצאוני יצאו ממני חזקתני ותוכל חזקת ממני. והנה טעמו ולא פחדו מהם:


DREADED. *Se’arum* means they were not in dread of them. *Se’arum* is related to the word *ve-yista’er* (shall come like a whirlwind) in *shall come against him like a whirlwind* (Dan. 11:40). It is similar in meaning to *sa’ar* in *That made the hair* (sa’arat)¹⁹⁵ to the word *sa’ar* (hair). See Rashi, “*Se’arum* means they were not afraid of them, their hair (*sa’aratam*) did not stand up in fear of them. It is the nature of man’s hair to stand on end because of fear.” *of my flesh to stand up* (Job 4:15).¹⁹⁶ means, and will frighten. Similarly, the meaning of *se’arum* is, were not afraid of them. However, it appears that *se’arum* is related to the word *sa’arah* (storm) even though the latter is spelled with a *samekh*.¹⁹⁷ with a *sin*. *Se’arum* is similar to *yetza’uni* (are gone forth of me)¹⁹⁸ in *My children are gone forth of me* (Jer. 10:20) and in *chazaktani*¹⁹⁹ (Thou hast overcome me) in *Thou hast overcome me, and hast prevailed* (Jer. 20:7); that is, you are more powerful than me.²⁰⁰ and *chazaktani* are intransitive verbs with accusative suffixes. However, an intransitive verb cannot come with an accusative suffix. Thus these suffixes are not to be taken as accusatives. *Yetza’uni* is to be rendered, gone forth from me, and *chazaktani* is to be rendered, you are more powerful than me. The same is true with *se’arum*, which is an intransitive verb with an accusative. It literally means were in dread you. However, it is to be rendered as were in dread of you. Look, the meaning of *se’arum* is, they were not afraid of them.

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:18:2)


**תשי** כמו לא תנשה והנח הנעלם אחר התי״‎ו תחת הדגש שהוא אלף הבלוע והיו״‎ד תחת ה״‎א וכן אל תמחי ובאו שניהם מלעיל להפריש בין זכר לנקבה בפעלים שהאות האחרון ה״‎א נח והנכון בעיני כי היו״‎ד נוסף והוא על משפט אל תט מאמרי פי:


[THOU WAST UNMINDFUL.] The word *teshi* (thou wast unmindful) is related to the word *tinnasheh* (you will forget)²⁰⁷. in [the clause] you shall not forget.²⁰⁸. There is no such phrase in the Bible. The reference might be to Is. 44:21, which reads *lo tinnasheni* (do not forget me). The missing silent letter following the *tav*²⁰⁹ beneath the *tav*. I.E. refers to the *segol* as a missing silent letter because certain vowels are pronounced as if followed by an unsounded letter. *Kal* imperfect prefixes are usually vocalized with a *chirik*. Hence I.E.’s comment. is in place of the omitted *dagesh* which compensates for the first root letter, ²¹⁰, for the root of *teshi* is *nun, shin, heh*. When the *nun* is dropped it is usually compensated for with a *dagesh*. However, the *shin* of *teshi* does not have a *dagesh*. Hence I.E. points out that the *nun* is compensated by the change in vowels. and the *yod* is in place of the *heh*. Compare the word *temchi* (blot out)²¹¹ is vocalized with a *segol* rather than with a *chirik*, and the *yod* is in place of a *heh*. However, it should be noted that in *temchi* the *segol* does not take the place of any missing letter. See Filwarg. in *Neither blot out their sin* (Jer. 18:23). Both words²¹² and *temchi*. are accented penultimately in order to show a difference between the masculine and the feminine in verbs whose last letter is a silent *heh*.²¹³ and *temchi* can be either masculine or feminine depending on where the word is accented. If penultimately accented, it is masculine; if ultimately accented, it is feminine. However, it appears to me that the *yod*²¹⁴ and *temchi*. is superfluous.²¹⁵ and *temch*. It follows the same rule as *tet* (decline)²¹⁶ comes from the root *nun, tet, heh*. Words ending in a *heh* come in a shortened form. Thus *tet* is short for *titteh*. Similarly, *tesh* is short for *tisheh*, and *temch* for *timcheh. Teshi* is a variant of *tesh*, and *temchi* a variant of *temch*. does in *neither decline* (Prov. 4:5).

Some say that our verse is to be interpreted, *I will hide My face from them* because I see what they will ultimately do.²²³ means [because] I see what they will ultimately do. The word *emun* (faithfulness) is a noun. On the other hand, it might be an adjective²²⁷ meaning there is no faithful man among them, for we find *for the faithful fail* (Ps. 12:2)²²⁸ in which *faithful* is parallel to *godly* (*Ibid.*).²²⁹ *We* also find *that keepeth faithfulness* (emunim) (Is. 26:2).²³⁰ is a noun. We thus see that the word can be either a noun or an adjective.

AND THE DEVOURING OF THE FIERY BOLT. *Le-chume reshef* (the devouring of the fiery bolt) means consumed²⁴⁶ to *lechem* (bread). by birds.²⁴⁷ Compare, *As the birds* (bene reshef)²⁴⁸ *fly upward* (Job 5:7).²⁴⁹ It appears to me that Scripture mentions the four evil punishments. It means that the air will grow hot.²⁵¹

### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:26:1)


**אפאיהם.** יש אומרים שהם שלש מלות והנכון שאין לו ריע וטעמו כמו אשחיתם בעבור שיש אחריו אשביתה מאנוש זכרם והנה כולם ימותו ואילו הי' כדעת המדקדקים שהטעם אפיצם בכל פאה לא ידבק הטעם. ויש אומרים אחריבם באפי והנה טעמו אכריתם כמו אשביתם ויבא הטעם כפול וזה נכון לולי אל״‎ף אפיהם שהיה ראוי להיות אנפיהם והטעם אאנף בם והראשון נכון:


I WOULD MAKE AN END OF THEM. Some say that the word *afehem* (I would make an end of them) is a combination of three words.²⁶⁶, i.e. (anger, where, they), I said in my anger I will make them, as it were, not existent. So Rashi, based on the *Sifre*. Actually, it has no neighbor.²⁶⁷ Its meaning is, I will destroy them, for Scripture states afterwards, *I would make their memory cease from among* *m*en. Look, all of them will die.²⁶⁸. If the grammarians²⁶⁹ who say that *afehem* means I will scatter them to all the corners are right,²⁷⁰ to *pe’ah* (corner). then the idea expressed by the first part of the verse is not to be connected to that of the second.²⁷¹ Some say that the meaning of *afehem* is, I will destroy them in my anger.²⁷² to *af* (anger) from the root *alef, nun, feh*. According to this interpretation, *afehem* literally means I will place My anger on them. Behold, the meaning of *afehem* is,²⁷³ I will destroy them.²⁷⁴ as a compound of three words. *Afehem* is similar in meaning to *ashbitah* (I would make…cease). Scripture repeats itself.²⁷⁵ This interpretation²⁷⁶ to *af*. would be correct were it not for the *alef* of *afehem*,²⁷⁷ is spelled with an *alef* following the *feh*. If *afehem* was connected to the word *af*, then there is no way to explain the *alef* which follows the *heh*. for the word should have read *anfehem*,²⁷⁸ was connected to the word *af*, then it would be spelled with a *nun* (*anfehem*), for the root of *af* is *alef, nun, peh*. meaning I will be angry at them. The first interpretation²⁷⁹ as meaning I will destroy them. is correct.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:27:1)


**אגור.** אפחד מגזרת ויגר מואב והמתרגם אמר מגזרת אגרה בקציר והנכון שהוא מלשון תגרה והכתוב דבר כדרך בני אדם להבין השומעים:


I DREADED. *Agur* means I dreaded. It is related to the word *va-yagar* (was sore afraid) in *And Moab was sore afraid* (Num. 22:3). The Aramaic translation connects it to the word *agerah* (gathereth) in *And gatherest…in the harvest* (Prov. 6:8).²⁸⁰ Actually it is related to the word *tigrah* (fight).²⁸¹ (were it not that I dreaded the enemy’s provocation) as were it not that I had to fight against the enemy’s anger. Scripture speaks as people do so that those who hear will understand.²⁸²

When the word comes in the *pi’el* it means to estrange; when it comes in the *hifil* it means to recognize. *Yenakkeru* is similar²⁸⁶ to *va-yitnakker*²⁸⁷. (but made himself strange) in *but made himself strange unto them* (Gen. 42:7).

### Verse 28

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:28:1)


**כי גוי אובד עצות.** הנכון שזה הגוי הם צרי ישראל ומלת אבד שם התאר והיא סמוכה על כן נפתח הבי״‎ת וידוע כי מלת אבד מהפעלי' העומדי' רק פי' עצות שב אל אבד כמו נובלת עליה וכן ותאבדו דרך שהוא סמוך אל דרך והנה השכיל המתרגם שאמר מאבדי עצה:


FOR THEY ARE A NATION VOID OF COUNSEL. The reference is to the enemies of Israel. This is its correct interpretation.²⁸⁹ quotes Rabbi Judah as interpreting this verse as referring to Israel. Rabbi Nehemiah explains it as referring to Israel’s enemies. Hence I.E.’s comment. The word *ovad* (void) is an adjective.²⁹⁰ It is in the construct.²⁹¹ (counsel). It is therefore vocalized with a *pattach* beneath the *bet*.²⁹² in place of *oved*. It is known that the word *ovad* is an intransitive verb.²⁹³ (counsel). *Ovad etzot* (void of counsel) is not to be rendered, voids counsel. The correct interpretation of *ovad etzot* is that *etzot* (counsel) reverts to *ovad* (void).²⁹⁴ is to be rendered, void of counsel. It is similar to *novelet aleha* (whose leaf fadeth)²⁹⁵ is to be rendered, whose leaf fadeth, rather than fadeth its leaves, for *novelet* is an intransitive verb. (Is. 1:30). The same is true of *ve-tovedu derekh* (and ye perish in the way) (Ps. 2:12)²⁹⁶ (and ye perish in the way) is to be rendered, and you perish with regard to the way, not and you perish the way. wherein *tovedu* is connected to *derekh*. The Aramaic translator who rendered *ovad etzot* as *me’abbede etzah* (void of counsel) understood this.

²⁹⁴ In other words, ovad etzot

### Verse 31

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:31:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:31:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:31:1)


**כי לא כצורנו צורם.** דברי משה פירוש כי גוי אובד עצות והטעם כי צורנו מכרנו ואין להם צור כצורנו ולא הם טובים ממנו וכן הוא אומר ולא אויבינו פלילים וגו' כמו ולא למדתי חכמה וגו' וי״‎א שהוא כן ואויבינו יודו כן לכן איננו דבק עם מגפן סדום:


FOR THEIR ROCK IS NOT AS OUR ROCK. These are the words of Moses.³⁰⁵ Moses explains *for they*³⁰⁶ *are a nation void of counsel* (v. 28). It means that our Rock³⁰⁷ has handed us over, and the nations have no rock like our Rock, and they are no better than we³⁰⁸. are.³⁰⁹ means the nations do not realize that the God of Israel has delivered Israel into their hands and that their own gods had nothing to do with it. Scripture similarly states, and our enemies are not judges.³¹⁰ (not) in the first half of the verse also applies to the second half of the verse. I.E. reads *ve-oyevenu pelilim* (even our enemies themselves being judges) as *ve-oyevenu lo pelilim* (and our enemies are not judges); i.e., they did not execute judgment upon us, God did. Compare, *And I have not learned wisdom* (Prov. 30:3).³¹¹ (no or not) is carried over to the second part of the verse. The verse should be read: And I have not learned wisdom and I have no knowledge of the Holy One. Others say that the meaning of *Even our enemies themselves being judges* is as follows: our enemies admit this.³¹² It is therefore not connected to³¹³. *For their vine is of the vine of Sodom* (v. 32).³¹⁴ does not follow.

AND THERE IS NONE REMAINING, SHUT UP OR LEFT AT LARGE. When the captives are numerous, the captors take some of them and leave others, but in this case almost all are lost.³⁴⁶

### Verse 38

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:38:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:38:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:38:1)


**יאכלו.** כדברי האויבים שחשבו כי העולות מאכל לשם וכן בלשון רבים כדבריהם ע״‎כ כתוב אני אני הוא לבדי אחד ואין אלהים עמדי:


WHO DID EAT. Scripture employs the language of the enemies³⁴⁹ who thought that the burnt offerings serve as food for God. Scripture employs the plural as they do.³⁵⁰). The Torah therefore states, *I*, only *I, am He, And there is no god with Me* (v. 39).

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:38:2

**יין נסיכם.** כמו ונסכו יין ויהיו שני שמות י״‎א יין מלכם כמו נסיכי מדין כי המלאך היה נותן יין העולה והראשון קרוב אלי:


THE WINE OF THEIR DRINK-OFFERING. *Yen nesikham*³⁵¹. (the wine of their drink-offering) is similar to *venisko*³⁵². *yayin* (and the drink-offering thereof shall be of wine) (Lev. 23:13). They are two terms.³⁵³ and *nesekh*. Some say that *yen nesikham* (the wine of their drink-offering) means the wine of their king,³⁵⁴ means a prince or a king. for the kings used to donate the wine for the burnt offering. Compare, *nesikhe midian* (the princes of Midian) (Josh. 13:21).³⁵⁵. If it is not a scribal error, then I.E. quoted from memory and erred. The first interpretation appears correct to me.

### Verse 39

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:39:1

**אני אני.** פעמיים כמו אנכי אנכי או כי אני הוא ולא אשנה והוא הנכון כי אין עמו פועל אני הוא שהמתי את ישראל ואני אחיה אותם והנה הם לא נצולו ואין מציל אתכם מידי גם אתם מידי עד עשותי את המשפט בכם. ורבים אומרים כי מזה הכתוב נלמוד חיי העולם הבא והעד שאמר בתחל' אמית ואחר כך אחיה וכן ה' ממית ומחיה והעד ה' מוריד שאול ויעל ואחרים אמרו מפסוק ואך את דמכם לנפשותיכם גם וצדקה תהיה לנו כי היא חייך בעוה״‎ב ואורך ימיך בעולם הזה למען ייטב לך. ורבינו האי ז״‎ל אמר כי לא הוצרך הכתוב לפרש דבר העוה״‎ב כי היה ידוע בהעתק' ולפי דעתי שהתורה נתנה לכל לא לאחד לבדו ודבר העוה״‎ב לא יבינו א' מני אלף כי עמוק הוא ושכר העוה״‎ב תלוי בדבר הנשמה והנה הוא חלף עבודת הלב ועבודתו להתבונן מעשה השם כי הם הסולם לעלות בו אל מעלת דעת השם שהוא העיקר והנה גם התורה ביארה למשכיל דבר עץ החיים והנה יש כח לנצח הכרובים והאוכל מעץ החיים וחי לעולם כמלאכי השרת וכן במזמור לבני קרח שמעו זאת כל העמים והסוד אך אלהים יפדה נפשי מיד שאול כי יקחני סלה וכן אחר כבוד תקחני והנה עם שניהם לקיחה כאשר עם דבר חנוך ואליהו ואחר שאמר ויקר פדיון נפשם איך אמר יפדה נפשי והמשכיל יבין:


I, EVEN I.³⁶¹ The word *I* is written twice.³⁶² Compare, *I, even I*³⁶³ (Is. 51:12). On the other hand, its³⁶⁴ meaning might be, I am He, and I do not change.³⁶⁵ The latter is the correct interpretation, for God has no co-worker.³⁶⁶. I am He that put Israel to death, and I will bring them back to life. Look, they were not saved.³⁶⁷ There is none that can deliver you out of My hand, even you out of My hand,³⁶⁸ until I execute My judgment upon you. Many say that we can derive the existence of life in the future world from this verse.³⁶⁹ 91b; *Peshachim* 68a, and *Sifre* on this verse. They offer proof from the fact that Scripture first states, *I kill* and then, *I make alive*.³⁷⁰ refers to the same person. It similarly reads, *The Lord killeth, and maketh alive* (I Sam. 2:6). *He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up (Ibid.*) is proof.³⁷¹ *Others offer proof³⁷² from: And surely your blood of your lives (nafshotekhem)³⁷³ may be rendered, your souls.* will I require (Gen. 9:5).³⁷⁴ Also from And it shall be righteousness unto us (Deut. 6:25);³⁷⁵ implies a future world, for otherwise Scripture employs the present rather than the future tense. for that is thy life (Deut. 30:20) in the world to come,³⁷⁶ 40a. *and the length of thy days (Ibid.*) in this world;³⁷⁷ 40a. *that it may go well with thee* (Deut. 5:16).³⁷⁸ 40a. Rabbi Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Scripture had no need to state clearly that a future world exists because it was known by tradition. I believe that [Scripture does not speak of a future world] because the Torah was given to all. It was not given to an individual alone. The topic of the world to come is not comprehended by even one in a thousand, for it is very abstruse. The reward in the world to come is contingent on the nature of the soul.³⁷⁹ 1, Strickman translation, p. 22). The reward³⁸⁰ is given for the service of the heart.³⁸¹, Chapter 8, p. 100). The latter consists in comprehending the works of God,³⁸², Chapter 10, p. 143. See also Chapter 7, p. 107, “The intelligent person will…study the scienees…he will isolate himself for the purpose of studying and meditating upon God’s law and observing the Lord’s precepts…God’s right hand of bliss will be eternally upon his soul when it separates from the body.” for they are the ladder whereon one ascends to the level of understanding the knowledge of God, which is what is most important. Observe, the Torah itself explains to the intelligent the topic of the tree of life.³⁸³ Behold, there is a power by which one can overcome the cherubim.³⁸⁴ The one who eats from the tree of life³⁸⁵ gains eternal life like the ministering angels. The psalm of the sons of Korah similarly reads, *Hear this, all ye peoples…*(Ps. 49:2).³⁸⁶ The secret³⁸⁷ is *But God will redeem my soul from the power of the nether-world; For He shall receive* (take) *me. Selah* (Ps. 49:16).³⁸⁸ Scripture similarly states, *And afterward receive* (take) me *with glory* (Ps. 73:24). Both verses employ the word “taking” as Scripture does in the account of Enoch³⁸⁹ and Elijah.³⁹⁰ Now, since Scripture states, *But God will redeem my soul* [*from the power of the netherworld*] (Ps. 49:16), how could it say, *For too costly is the redemption of their soul* (Ps. 49:9)?³⁹¹ The intelligent will understand.³⁹²

**כי אשא אל שמים ידי.** שבועה בדבר קיים ואשא כמו וירם ימינו ושמאלו אל השמים ומלת אשא כדרך בן אדם להבין את השומעים:

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:43:1

**הרנינו גוים עמו.** אז ישבחוהו כאשר יקום השם דמם וי״‎א מגזרת ותעבור הרנה והטעם הכרוז והכריזו עליהם בכל מקום שיהיו:

Some say that the meaning of *harninu* (sing aloud) is similar to the word *rinnah* (cry) in *And there went a cry* (I Kings 22:36). It means the herald.⁴⁰⁵ Proclaim about them in every place where they are.⁴⁰⁶

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 32:43:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:43:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/32:43:2)


**וכפר אדמתו עמו.** י״‎א שהוא חסר וי״‎ו והטעם וכפר אדמתו ועמו ובדרש כי הארץ תכפר בעד כמו גם הוא נכון בטעם רק אינו מטעם המקום ועוד כי האדמה ל' נקבה והה״‎א העד הנאמן ותחתיו התי״‎ו והנה איננו וכפרה. ולפי דעתי שפירושו שהעם יכפר על האדמה כי כן מצאנו אבנים שחקו מים גם נמצא כפור בלא מלת על כמו וחטאת אותו וכפרתהו והטעם כי ישראל יעשו נקמה בגוים והם יכפרו על ארץ ישראל בעבור הדם ששופך בה כמו ולארץ לא יכופר והוא דבר בטעם המקום. או פירוש וכפר כמו וטהר וכמו וכפרתהו וכן אמר יחזקאל על סוף המלחמות וטהרו את הארץ והנה ישראל יטהרוה:


AND DOTH MAKE EXPIATION FOR THE LAND OF HIS PEOPLE. Some say that a *vav*⁴⁰⁷. is missing.⁴⁰⁸ (his people). Our verse should be interpreted as if written *ve-khipper admato ve-ammo* (and doth make expiation for His land and for His people). According to the midrash⁴⁰⁹ 111a. Rabbi Anan says: “Whoever is buried in the Land of Israel is considered to be buried beneath the altar.” the meaning of *ve-khipper admato ammo* (and doth make expiation for His land of His people) is that the land makes expiation for His people.⁴¹⁰ does not refer to God but to *admato* (His land). This interpretation is true in itself.⁴¹¹ However, it is not the meaning of the verse.⁴¹² Furthermore, the word *adamah* (land) is a feminine.⁴¹³ is a masculine. Hence it can not govern *admato*. The *heh* at its end⁴¹⁴ is the absolute form of the word *admato*. is proof of this. The *tav*⁴¹⁵. takes the place of the *heh*.⁴¹⁶. Now, Scripture does not read *vekhipperah* (and doth make expiation).⁴¹⁷ governed *admato* as the midrash says, then our verse would read, *ve-khipperah admato*. In my opinion the meaning of our clause is that the people will make expiation for the land,⁴¹⁸ governs *admato*. Our verse should be interpreted as if written, *ve-khipper ammo admato*. for we find Scripture stating, *avanim shachaku mayim* (The waters wear the stones) (Job 14:19).⁴¹⁹ (the waters wear the stones) literally reads, the stones wear the waters. This makes no sense. Hence we must rearrange the words in order to interpret the clause and interpret it as if written, *mayim shachaku avanim*. Similarly in our verse. The word *kippur* (expiate) is also found without the word *al* (for),⁴²⁰. This literally means and doth make expiation His land. This makes no sense. Our clause should read, *ve-khipper al admato* (and make expiation for his land). Hence I.E.’s comment. as in *ve-khippartahu* (and make atonement for it)⁴²¹ is a combination of *ve-khipparta oto* (literally, and you shall make atonement it). Scripture should have read, *ve-khipparta alav* (and you shall make atonement for it). We thus see that Scripture sometimes leaves out the word *al*. It assumes that the reader will supply it. in, *thus shalt thou purify it and make atonement for it* (Ezek. 43:20). The meaning of *ve-khipper admato ammo* is that Israel will execute vengeance upon the nations and they will make atonement for the Land of Israel because of the blood that was shed in it. Compare, *and no expiation can be made for the land* [*for the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it*] (Num. 35:33). This interpretation is in keeping with the meaning of the context.⁴²² On the other hand, the meaning of *ve-khipper* (and doth make expiation) is, and will purify, as in *ve-khippartahu* (and make atonement for it) (Ezek. 43:20). Ezekiel similarly said, regarding the end of the wars,⁴²³ *Thus shall they cleanse the land* (Ezek. 39:16). Israel will thus purify the land.⁴²⁴

**אש דת למו.** התורה שנתנה באש וברק ואמר כי טעם ה' מסיני בא דרך תפלה כאומר אתה שבאת בסיני והנחלת תורה יחי ראובן וזה רחוק כי היה ראוי להיות החיה ואל תמית. וחסרי אמונ' אמרו כי טעם משעיר על דת אדום. ופארן על דת ישמעאל ואלה תועים הלא ראו כי לא החל בתחלה כי אם לברך ישראל לבדם וכן כתוב אשר ברך משה איש האלהים את בני ישראל ואמר וזרח משעיר למו שפירושו להם כמו ואין למו מכשול. והנכון בעיני שהפרשה היא ברכה כלל לכל ישראל ואח״‎כ פרט לכל שבט ושבט ואחר כן כללם במקום אין כאל ישורון. והנה מצאנו שאמרה דבורה ה' בצאתך משעיר בצעדך משדה אדום והנה אין שדה אדום הר כאשר אמר הגאון כי שלשה הרים הם סמוכים או לנכח ובס' תהלות אלהים בצאתך לפני עמך בצעדך בישימון סלה ואחריו כתוב ארץ רעשה ובצעד השכינה בישימון לא היה יום מתן תורה. כי אחר מדבר פארן באו בישימון ואמר חבקוק אלוה מתימן יבוא שהוא מבני אדום תימן אומר כטעם משדה אדום. והנה הכל במלחמות ידבר והעד יקום אלהים יפוצו אויביו וכאשר יושיע השם את עבדיו ידמה הכתוב רדת עזר מהשם והארץ תמוג וההרי' ימסו והשמים ירעשו והעד בשירו' דוד ותגעש ותרעש הארץ. וטעם זה סיני פירשתיו במקומו. וכן הוא הפירוש השם בא והטעם הכבוד שנכנס בישראל ותחלת הכנסו מסיני וזרח משעיר והטעם כל השנים שהיו ישראל במדבר לא הראה השם גבורה בעמים עד בא ישראל אל שדה אדום וכן כתוב בהררם שעיר עד איל פארן והנה הם קרובים שעיר ופארן והטעם מפורש כי ממקום שעיר כאשר באו לשעיר אז זרח הכבוד לישראל והופיע מהר פארן והטעם כפול כי פה הראה יפעתו:


A FIERY LAW UNTO THEM. The Torah, which was given through fire and lightning.⁸ He⁹ says that the *Lord came…*is a prayer. It means, You who came to Sinai and bequeathed the Torah,¹⁰ *Let Reuben live* (v. 6). However, this interpretation is far-fetched, for Scripture should read, keep Reuben alive and do not put him to death.¹¹, the import of which is, may Reuben live, and not die. If Saadiah Gaon’s interpretation was correct the verse would read *hachayeh et re’uven ve-al tamito* (keep Reuben alive and do not put him to death). In other words, Scripture would have employed the imperative *hachayeh* (keep him alive) rather than the third person *yechi* (let him live). It similarly would have employed the second person *tamito* (you will put him to death) in place of the third person *yamut* (he will die). Those who lack faith say that *from Seir* refers to the religion of the Edomites,¹² and Paran refers to the faith of the Ishmaelites.¹³ However, these err. Do they not see that Moses commenced at first to bless Israel alone. Scripture thus reads, *wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel* (v. 1). Scripture goes on to say *ve-zarach mi-se’ir lamo*, the meaning of which is, And rose from Seir unto them.¹⁴ Compare, *lamo* (for them) in *And there is no stumbling for them* (Ps. 119:165).¹⁵ means unto them. It appears to me that this chapter is a general blessing to all of Israel.¹⁶ Moses then goes on to address each tribe and tribe individually.¹⁷ Then Moses includes them all in the verse which reads, *There is none unto God, O Jeshurun* (v. 26). Look,¹⁸ we find that Deborah said, *Lord, when Thou didst go forth out of Seir, When Thou didst march out of the field of Edom, The earth trembled* (Jud. 5:4). Clearly the field of Edom is not a mountain as the Gaon says,¹⁹) is parallel to Seir. If *sede edom* does not refer to a mountain neither does Seir. for the Gaon maintains that Sinai, Seir, and Paran are three mountains close to each other or facing each other. Also, the Book of Psalms states, *O God, when Thou wentest forth before thy people, When Thou didst march through the wilderness* (yeshimon); *Selah* (Ps. 68:8). Scripture then states, *The earth trembled* (Ps. 68:9).²⁰ not at Sinai. I.E. comments thus because someone might still insist on identifying the field of Edom with Mount Sinai. It should be noted that I.E. insists that the clause “the earth trembled” in Jud. 5:4 and the similar clause in Ps. 68:9 refer to the same event. See I.E. on Ps. 68:8. Now the Divine presence did not march through the wilderness (*yeshimon*) on the day that the Torah was given, for Israel came to the wilderness (*yeshimon*) after they had passed through the wilderness (*midbar*) of Paran.²¹ Furthermore, Habakkuk says, *God cometh from Teman* (Hab. 3:3). Teman was one of the sons of Edom, for we read, *Teman, Omar* (Gen. 36:11).²² *From Teman* means the same as *from the field of Edom*. Look, all the verses²³ speak of war. *Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered* (Ps. 68:2) is proof of this. Scripture describes God’s saving of His servants in terms of help coming down from heaven, the earth melting, the mountains dissolving, and the heavens quaking. *Then the earth did shake and quake* (Ps. 18:8) in David’s song is proof of this. I have explained the meaning of *even yon Sinai* (Ps. 68:9) in its place.²⁴) did. In other words, the phrase *zeh sinai* does not imply that what comes before (the earth trembled…) refers to the revelation at Sinai. The following is the explanation of our verse. *The Lord came* refers to the glory that entered into Israel. It first entered Israel at Sinai. *And rose from Seir* means that God did not show His might among the nations all the years that Israel was in the wilderness until Israel came to the field of Edom. Scripture similarly states, *in their mount Seir, unto El-paran* (Gen. 14:6). Seir and Paran are thus close to each other. The meaning of *And rose from Se’ir* is thus explained, for *mi-seir* means from the place of Seir; that is, when Israel came to Seir, God’s glory rose to Israel. *He shined forth from mount Paran* repeats the idea expressed by *and rose from Seir*. It means that God here²⁵ showed His shining.

**תכו.** בלא אח וי״‎א מל' מתוך כאילו הולכים בתוך רגלך ואחרים אומרים כי התי״‎ו במקום ה״‎א כתי״‎ו תרגלתי לאפרים כטעם אפילו שיוכו בשבילך לא יעזבו דבריך וזה רחוק. והנכון שהוא כמו נמשכו והטעם שילכו אל המקום ששם הארון שהוא הדום רגלי השם וזאת היא הברכ' שהשם יהיה חומת אש סביב ישראל ויהיה סגולתו והלוים יורו התורה תמיד:


AND THEY SIT DOWN. *Tukku* (sit down) has no brother.³⁸ Some say³⁹ that it is related to the word *mi-tokh* (from the midst of).⁴⁰. They, as it were, walk in the midst of Your feet. Others say that the *tav*⁴¹. is in place of a *heh*.⁴² is a variant of *hukku* (were beaten). It is like the *tav* of *tirgalti* (I taught)⁴³ is a variant of *hirgalti*. in *I taught Ephraim* (Hos. 11:3). This is the blessing:⁴⁵ May God be a wall of fire round about Israel.⁴⁶ May Israel be God’s treasure.⁴⁷ May the Levites always teach the Torah.⁴⁸

MOSES COMMANDED US A LAW. This is what they shall bear upon their lips and say from generation to generation: thus did we copy with our hands an inheritance from the mouth of Moses.⁴⁹ The *lamed* of *lanu* (us) applies to itself and also to another word.⁵⁰. *Morashah kehillat ya’akov* (an inheritance congregation of Jacob)⁵¹ literally means an inheritance congregation of Jacob. ### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 33:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/33:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/33:5:1)


**מלך.** הוא משה ששמעו ראשי עם התורה מפורשת מפיו והטעם כי הוא היה כמלך והתאספו אליו ראשי השבטים ויחזיק זה הפי' שאמר הכתוב כי התורה נתנה לכהנים שהם לפי דעתי כל קדושיו בידיך ואל כל זקני ישראל זהו בהתאסף ראשי עם גם שם כתוב הקהילו אלי כל ראשי שבטיכם. ויאמר רבי יהודה הלוי ז״‎ל כי המלך רמז לתורה וכן היה מפרש אין מלך בישראל:


A KING. The reference is to Moses, from whose mouth the heads of the people clearly heard the words of the Torah. The meaning of our verse is that Moses was the equivalent of a king, and the heads of the tribes were gathered unto him.⁵⁶ This interpretation is supported by Scripture’s statement that the Torah was given to the *kohanim*,⁵⁷ who, in my opinion, are meant by *All His holy ones-they are in Thy hand* (v. 3), and to *all the elders of Israel* (Deut. 31:9). This is what *When the heads of the people were gathered* refers to. Scripture also writes there, *Assemble unto me all the elders of your tribes* (Deut. 31:28). Rabbi Judah Ha-Levi, of blessed memory, says that the *king* alludes to the Torah. He similarly used to explain *there was no king in Israel* (Jud. 18:l).⁵⁸

**יחי ראובן.** הנה החל מהבכור כי כן המשפט ולא הזכיר שמעון בעבור בעל פעור כי העובדים היו שמעונים ומספרם לעד גם נשיאם נהרג או הלך על דרך יעקב שלא ברך שמעון ולוי ובעבור כבוד אהרן נתלה השבט ממנו ולא היה בשבט שמעון גדול כמותו. ואם יטעון טוען למה בירך ראובן. התשובה כי יעקב ברכו והברכ' היא אל תותר שיהיה כאחד מאחיו. ואחר ראובן הזכיר יהוד' שהוא בעל דגל והוא עולה בתחלה למלחמה ואחר כן לוי ואחריו בנימין בעבור היות הלוים דרים בירושלים שהיתה בין יהודה ובין בנימין כן כתוב. ואחר כן שבט יוסף שלא יאחרנו וכבר הקדים אחיו הקטן ואחר כן זבולון בעבור שהוא נלחם ואחר כן יששכר. וכאשר תמו בני הגבירות החל מגד שהוא עם דגל בני הגבירו' ואחר כן דן שהוא בעל דגל ואחר כן נפתלי כי הוא גדול מאשר:


LET REUBEN LIVE. Moses starts with the first-born, for this is the proper practice. He does not mention Simeon because of the incident of Baal-peor,⁵⁹ for those who served Baalpeor were from the tribe of Simeon.⁶⁰ Their number⁶¹ proves this.⁶² Also, their prince was killed.⁶³ It is also possible that Moses followed in the footsteps of Jacob,⁶⁴ who did not bless Simeon and Levi. The tribe of Levi was blessed out of respect for Aaron. Simeon had no one as great as Aaron.⁶⁵ Should one who disputes argue, “Why did Moses bless Reuben?”⁶⁶ The answer is that Jacob blessed Reuben. The blessing was *have not thou the excellency* (Gen. 49:4).⁶⁷ The meaning of the latter is that Reuben shall be like one of his brothers. Moses mentions Judah after Reuben⁶⁸ because he was in charge of a standard⁶⁹ and he was the first to lead in battle. Next Levi and then Benjamin are mentioned⁷⁰ because the Levites dwelled in Jerusalem, which was situated between Judah and Benjamin. Scripture clearly states this.⁷¹ Moses then mentions the tribe of Joseph so as not to delay naming him. He had already mentioned his younger brother.⁷² He next mentioned Zebulun because he waged war.⁷³ (Jud. 5:18). He then mentioned Issachar.⁷⁴ After Moses finished mentioning the children of the wives, he commenced with Gad,⁷⁵ who camped among the standard of the children of the wives.⁷⁶ Moses then mentions Dan, who was in charge of a standard.⁷⁷ He then mentioned Naphtali because he was older than Asher.⁷⁸

**רב לו.** יספיקו לו ידיו ואין לו צורך למי שיעזור אותו כי אם עזרת השם לבדו וי״‎א מל' מריבה והטעם ידיו יריבו בעדו ואחרים אמרו כמו וברקים רב מגזרת ורבו:


HIS HAND SHALL CONTEND FOR HIM. *Rav lo* (contend for him) means shall be sufficient for him⁹¹ means abundant. ¹²⁵ There is one moon. Hence I.E.’s comment.
¹²⁶ The moon reappears each month.
¹²⁷ There is thus a new moon each month. Hence one may speaks of “moons.”

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 33:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/33:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/33:16:4)


**תבואתה.** הברכה הזאת והתחברו שנים סימנין התי״‎ו והה״‎א כמו עזרתה ישועתה בצרתה ובעבור שהזכיר התבואה דמה השבט לשור ואמר בכור שורו כי יש לו כח רב כי הוא ראשית און:


LET THE BLESSING COME. *Tavotah* (let the blessing come)¹³² is the elongated or poetic form of the word *tavo*. refers to this blessing.¹³³ Two signs,¹³⁴ the *tav* and the *heh*, are joined together.¹³⁵ should have read *tavo’ah* or *tavo’at. Tavotah* is a combination of the two. Compare, *ezratah* (help) (Ps. 44:27);¹³⁶ is a combination of the two feminine forms *ezrat* and *ezrah*. *yeshu’atah* (salvation) (Ps. 3:3);¹³⁷ (salvation) is a combination of the two feminine forms *yeshu’ah* and *yeshu’at*. *ba-tzaratah* (in…distress) (Ps. 120:1).¹³⁸ is a combination of *tzarah* and *tzarat*. Moses compared the tribe of Joseph to a bullock because he earlier spoke of produce.¹³⁹ Moses referred to Joseph as *His firstling bullock* (v. 17) because a first-born bullock has great strength as it is the first of its father’s might.

¹³⁸ Tzaratah
¹³⁹ Bulls are used in plowing and for pulling carts loaded with produce.

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 33:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/33:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/33:19:1)

**ושפוני טמוני חול.** אין לו אח וטעמו כמו טמוני וכן אדמת עפר והטעם שיהא להם עושר רב עד שיטמנהו בחול ובעבור עשרם יבואו רובם אל הר השם לזבוח זבחי תודה לשם:

And because of their wealth, they will come in a multitude to the mountain of God to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving to the Lord.

**ויתא.** חסר אל״‎ף והטעם שבאו ראשי גד עם ישראל חלוצי צבא ומשה ראה זה בנבואה:


CAME. *Va-yeta* (came)¹⁵⁰. is missing an *alef*.¹⁵¹, for its root is *alef, tav, alef*. The meaning of our clause is that the heads of Gad came armed with the children of Israel.¹⁵² Moses prophetically saw this.

(Ps. 76:3) is proof of this. There are many such examples.¹⁷⁴ is used in the sense of protection. The meaning of our verse is: The eternal God is your covering.¹⁷⁵ Compare, *Even the Most High, thy habitation* (me’onekha)¹⁷⁶ (Ps. 91:9) and *Thou hast been our dwelling-place* (ma’on) (Ps. 90:1). The “place”¹⁷⁸).” is below.¹⁷⁹ refers to “up above” and *makom* to below. God is referred to as “The Place” because He is present in all places on the earth. ### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 34:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/34:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/34:6:1)


**ויקבר אותו.** הוא קבר עצמו שנכנס במערה בגיא וכן וירעו הרועים אותם ויראו שוטרי בני ישראל אותם ודע כי הר העברים שהוא הר נבו שהוא צלם ככב הוא בעצמו הגיא שהוא ראש הפסג' שהוא מול בית פעור והעד שאמר הכתוב כי נסע ישראל מבמו' אל הגיא אשר בשדה מואב ראש הפסגה וכתיב ויעל משה מערבות מואב אל הר נבו ראש הפסגה ושם מת ושם קבורתו וכתיב ונשב בגיא מול בית פעור והנה אחר שישבו ישראל בגיא אמר הכתוב ויסעו בני ישראל ויחנו בערבות מואב וכתוב אחר ויחנו בהרי העברים לפני נבו ויסעו מהרי העברים ויחנו בערבות מואב והנה דבר ברור כי במקום שמת משה שם קבורתו:


AND HE WAS BURIED.⁹ (literally, and he buried him). Moses buried himself.¹⁰ (and he buried him) is to be rendered, and he buried himself. I.E.’s point is that the pronoun *oto* (him) or *otam* (them) sometimes has the meaning of himself or themselves. He entered a cave in the valley. The same is true of *but the shepherds fed them* (otam),¹¹ (them) is to be rendered themselves. Our clause thus reads, but the shepherds fed themselves. and *fed not My sheep* (Ezek. 34:8) and, *And the officers of the children of Israel did see them*¹² (otam)¹³). (Ex. 5:19). Note,¹⁴); the valley (*gai*) which is over against Beth-peor (Deut. 34:6). I.E. goes on to explain that all of these terms refer to one and the same place. Mount Abarim is also known as Mount Nebo.¹⁵ Nebo is in the image of Mercury.¹⁶. According to I.E. the idol Nebo stood and was worshipped on Mount Abarim. Hence Mount Abarim was also known as Mount Nebo. Mount Abarim is also known as “the valley which is the top of Pisgah which is over against Beth-peor.”¹⁷ The fact that Scripture tells us that Israel journeyed *from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, by the top of Pisgah* (Num. 21:20) is proof of this.¹⁸) is to be identified with the top of Pisgah. Furthermore, Scripture writes, *And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah* (v. 1).¹⁹ Moses died there²⁰ and his grave is there.²¹ Scripture states,²² *So we abode in the valley over against Beth-peor (Deut. 3:29). Now, Scripture tells us that after Israel dwelt in the valley…the children of Israel journeyed, and pitched in the plains of Moab (Num. 22:1). Another verse states, And [Israel] pitched in the mountains of Abarim, in front of Nebo. And they journeyed from the mountains of Abarim, and pitched in the plains of Moab (Num. 33:47,48). Look, it is clear that Moses’ burial place was in the place where he died.²³ and Sotah* 13b.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 34:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/34:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/34:7:1)


**לחה.** הה״‎א תחת וי״‎ו כמו בתוך אהלה מגזרת לח כי היבשות תתגבר על הזקן:


HIS NATURAL FORCE. The *heh* of *lechoh* (his natural force) is in place of a *vav*.²⁶. Here it is indicated by a *heh*. Hence I.E.’s comment. It is like the *heh* of *oholoh* (his tent) (Gen. 9:21).²⁷. *Lechoh* is related to the word *lach* (moist, fresh).²⁸ means his moistness. Scripture notes this²⁹ because old people are overtaken by dryness.

²⁸ Thus lechoh

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Deuteronomy 34:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/34:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Deuteronomy/r/34:9:1)


**מלא** **רוח חכמה.** היא דוח ה' והעד כי סמך משה את ידיו עליו כי לא ימצא כמותו בישראל שישען עליו:


WAS FULL OF THE SPIRIT OF WISDOM. The reference is to the spirit of the Lord.³³ (Is. 11:2). It then goes on to explain that the spirit of the Lord is the spirit of wisdom and understanding (*Ibid.*). See I.E. on Ex. 31:3 (Vol. 2, pp. 645,646). *For Moses had laid his hands upon him* is proof of this,³⁴. for there was not found in Israel one such as Joshua for Moses to lean on.³⁵ to mean relied on him, i.e., took him for a disciple. Be that as it may, according to I.E, *For Moses had laid his hands upon him* does not mean that the placing of Moses’ hand on Joshua caused Joshua to be full of the spirit of wisdom but rather that Moses placed his hands on Joshua because Joshua was full of the spirit of God.

³⁵ Another term for “place his hands on him.” It is possible that I.E. interprets Moses had laid his hands upon him
